rules.title: About This Work
rules.body:
# A Higher Sanskrit Grammar

**Author:** @[moreśvara rāmacandra kāle]
**Original Publication:** 1894

---

This digital edition presents the complete text of _A Higher Sanskrit Grammar_ by M.R. Kale, a comprehensive treatise on Sanskrit grammar that has served generations of students and scholars since its first publication in 1894.

It is the best available grammar of the Sanskrit language in English written by a native grammarian. As such we hope to start with this work as a foundation for a more comprehensive modern grammar for the Sanskrit language that aspires to supercede the extant references (i.e. Macdonell, Whitney, etc.).

Those works are undoubtedly important to the modern English-speaking student of sanskrit, but they suffer from the 19th century condecension of their authors' era. One can recognize the monumental work of Whitney and Macdonell, but we hope to be able to remedy this by writing a modern grammar without the same flaws-- perhaps with flaws all our own. Please contribute to the project if you find such an error.

_The original work is in the public domain._

rules.title: Sanskrit Language and Devanāgarī Alphabet
rules.body:
Sanskrit, or the refined language, is the language of Devas or gods,[^1] and the alphabet in which it is written is called Devanāgarī, or that employed in the cities of gods.

(a) The correct name for the Sanskrit alphabet is Daivanāgarī sometimes abbreviated into Nāgarī. Perhaps in the word Devanāgarī we have a history of the times when the Aryans entered and settled in Northern India. The Aryans who were much fairer in colour than the aborigines of India are the Devas referred to in the name Devanāgarī (from @deva[दिव्] to shine, those of a brilliant complexion); and Nāgarī means the Aryan settlements within the precincts of which the sacred language was spoken.

(b) The Sanskrit language is generally written in different parts of the country in that alphabet which is used for the Vernacular (e.g. Bengālī, Marāṭhī &c.). That character, however, in which the earliest monuments are written (such as the inscriptions containing the edicts of Aśoka) and which is employed throughout Upper India is generally considered to be the real Devanāgarī.

---

[^1]: @deva[संस्कृतं नाम दैवी वागन्वाख्याता महर्षिभिः ।] Daṇḍin.

rules.title: Devanāgarī Alphabet Structure and Pāṇinian Classification
rules.body:
The Devanāgarī alphabet consists of *forty-two* letters or varṇas, *nine* vowels or swaras, and *thirty-three* consonants or vyañjanas.[^1]

(a) These express nearly every gradation of sound, and every letter stands for a particular and invariable sound.

**Note:**—This explains why there are no names, as in Greek, for the different letters of the alphabet.

---

[^1]: Thus given by Pāṇini:— Vowels:—@deva[अइउण् । ऋऌक् । एओङ् । ऐऔच् ।] Consonants:—@deva[हयवरट् । लण् । ञमङणनम् । झभञ् । घढधष् । जबगडदश् । खफछठथचटतव् । कपय् । शषसर् । हल् ।] The alphabet, it will be seen, is divided into 14 sections by Pāṇini, which are called Śivasūtrāṇi, or the sūtras revealed by Śiva. Each section ends with an indicatory letter called '@deva[इत्]' which is not to be counted among the letters of the alphabet. These "Its" serve an important purpose in Sanskrit grammar as they enable the grammarians to express several letters, or groups of letters, in a very convenient and condensed form. For any letter, with the following @deva[इत्] added to it, is not only expressive of itself but of all letters that intervene between it and this @deva[इत्]; e.g. @deva[अण्] means @deva[अ], @deva[इ], @deva[उ]; @deva[इक्] means @deva[इ], @deva[उ], @deva[ऋ], @deva[ऌ], &c. Similarly @deva[अल्] means technically the whole alphabet, @deva[अच्] any vowel, and @deva[हल्] any consonant; @deva[यण्] a semivowel, @deva[हश्] a soft consonant, @deva[खर्] a hard consonant, @deva[जश्] a soft unaspirate, @deva[झष्] a soft aspirate &c. Each of these significant terms is technically called a '@deva[प्रत्याहार]'. Since short vowels include the long and the protracted vowels (See @ref[3]. a.) another @deva[इत्], '@deva[त्]' is generally employed to mark a particular vowel: e.g. @deva[अ] means @deva[अ], @deva[आ] and @deva[आ३], but @deva[अत्] means @deva[अ] (of six kinds) only; so @deva[ईत्] means @deva[ई] and nothing else.

rules.title: Vowel Classification: Simple, Diphthongs, and Modifications
rules.body:
The nine primary vowels consist of five simple vowels viz. @deva[अ], @deva[इ], @deva[उ], @deva[ऋ] and @deva[ऌ], and four diphthongs viz. @deva[ए], @deva[ऐ], @deva[ओ] and @deva[औ].

(a) A vowel may be @deva[ह्रस्व] or short, @deva[दीर्घ] or long, and @deva[प्लुत] or protracted (also called prolated by some) according to the time required to pronounce it.[^1] The vowels are thus divided into—

(1) Short vowels—@deva[अ] @[a], @deva[इ] @[i], @deva[उ] @[u], @deva[ऋ] @[ṛ], @deva[ऌ] @[ḷ];

(2) Long vowels—@deva[आ] @[ā], @deva[ई] @[ī], @deva[ऊ] @[ū], @deva[ॠ] @[ṝ], @deva[ए] @[e], @deva[ऐ] @[ai], @deva[ओ] @[o], @deva[औ] @[au]; and

(3) Protracted vowels @deva[आ३] @[ā3], @deva[ई३] @[ī3], @deva[ऊ३] @[ū3], @deva[ॠ३] @[ṝ3], @deva[ऌ३] @[ḷ3], @deva[ए३] @[e3], @deva[ऐ३] @[ai3], @deva[ओ३] @[o3], and @deva[औ३] @[au3].

**N.B.** As the @deva[प्लुत] or protracted vowels are not commonly to be met with in classical Sanskrit, the vowels are usually given as thirteen, represented by the thirteen signs given above under (1) and (2).

(b) Each of these vowels may be again of two kinds, @deva[अनुनासिक] or nasalised, and @deva[अननुनासिक] or without a nasal sound.[^2]

(c) Vowels are also further discriminated into @deva[उदात्त] or acute, @deva[अनुदात्त] or grave, and @deva[स्वरित] or circumflex. @deva[उदात्त] is that which proceeds from the upper part of the vocal organs, @deva[अनुदात्त] that which proceeds from their lower part, while @deva[स्वरित] arises out of a mixture of these two.[^3] But these are ignored in classical Sanskrit. They are marked only in Vedic works: the Udātta is left unmarked; the Anudātta is marked with a horizontal line underneath; and Svarita has a perpendicular stroke above it. e. g. @deva[क्व१ वोऽश्वाः], &c. Ṛg. V. 61. 2 @deva[रथानां न पे२गाः ।] &c. Ṛg. X. 78. 4. @deva[शतचक्रं यो३ ह्यः] &c. Ṛg. X. 145. 4.

Thus there are eighteen different modifications of each of the vowels @deva[अ], @deva[इ], @deva[उ], @deva[ऋ], and twelve of @deva[ऌ], @deva[ए], @deva[ऐ], @deva[ओ] and @deva[औ]; for there is no long ḷ and the last four have not their corresponding short vowels.

---

[^1]: @deva[ऊकालोऽज्झ्रस्वदीर्घप्लुतः ।] Pāṇ. I. 2. 27. The crowing of the cock in the morning represents in its three stages these three kinds of vowels. The time required to pronounce a short vowel is called a @deva[मात्रा]. A long vowel has two mātrās and a Pluta vowel three.

[^2]: @deva[मुखनासिकावचनोऽनुनासिकः] Pāṇ. I. 1. 8.

[^3]: @deva[उच्चैरुदात्तः। नीचैरनुदात्तः। समाहारः स्वरितः।] — Pāṇ. I. 2. 29, 31.

rules.title: Consonant Classification: Sparśa, Antastha, and Ūṣman
rules.body:
The consonants are divided into @deva[स्पर्श] or mutes (those involving a complete closure or contact and not an approximate one of the organs of pronunciation), @deva[अन्तस्थ] (or intermediate, i.e. the Semivowels,) and @deva[ऊष्मन्] or sibilants.

These are represented by thirty-three syllabic signs arranged as below:—

**(a) Mutes:**

(1) @deva[कवर्ग] or the group @deva[कु]—@deva[क्] @[k], @deva[ख्] @[kh], @deva[ग्] @[g], @deva[घ्] @[gh], @deva[ङ्] @[ṅ].

(2) @deva[चवर्ग] or the group @deva[चु]—@deva[च्] @[c], @deva[छ्] @[ch], @deva[ज्] @[j], @deva[झ्] @[jh], @deva[ञ्] @[ñ].

(3) @deva[टवर्ग] or the group @deva[टु]—@deva[ट्] @[ṭ], @deva[ठ्] @[ṭh], @deva[ड्] @[ḍ], @deva[ढ्] @[ḍh], @deva[ण्] @[ṇ].

(4) @deva[तवर्ग] or the group @deva[तु]—@deva[त्] @[t], @deva[थ्] @[th], @deva[द्] @[d], @deva[ध्] @[dh], @deva[न्] @[n].

(5) @deva[पवर्ग] or the group @deva[पु]—@deva[प्] @[p], @deva[फ्] @[ph], @deva[ब्] @[b], @deva[भ्] @[bh], @deva[म्] @[m].

These are also called the five classes designated as @deva[कवर्ग], @deva[चवर्ग], @deva[टवर्ग], @deva[तवर्ग], and @deva[पवर्ग] respectively.

**(b) Semivowels**

@deva[य्] @[y], @deva[र्] @[r], @deva[ल्] @[l], @deva[व्] @[v].

**(c) Sibilants**

@deva[श्] @[ś], @deva[ष्] @[sh], @deva[स्] @[s].

**(d) Sonant Aspirate**

@deva[ह्] @[h].

Besides these we have two more characters occurring in the Veda, viz. @deva[ळ] and @deva[ळ्ह] (often substituted for @deva[ड] and @deva[ढ]; as @deva[ईळे] for @deva[ईडे], @deva[मीळ्हुषे] for @deva[मीढुषे] &c.). In Marāthi @deva[ळ] is generally substituted for the final @deva[ल] of Sanskrit words.

rules.title: Hard and Soft Consonants
rules.body: The first two letters of the five classes and the sibilants are called surds or hard consonants. The rest are called sonants or soft consonants.

rules.title: Nasal Sounds and Visarga
rules.body:
In addition to the characters given above there are in Sanskrit two nasal sounds:—the one called Anusvāra, is denoted by @deva[ं] i.e. a dot placed above the letter after which it is to be pronounced, e.g. @deva[कं]; the other, called Anunāsika is denoted by @deva[ँ] i.e. a dot within a semi-circle placed above the letter after which it is to be pronounced e.g. @deva[सँ].

(a) And a sort of hard breathing is known as Visarga (generally called Visarjanīya by Sanskrit grammarians). It is denoted by the sign @deva[ः] i.e. two vertical dots placed after the letter after which it is to be pronounced. In pronunciation it is a harder aspirate than @deva[ह]. The Visarga is not an original character but only a substitute for a final @deva[स्] @[s] or @deva[र्] @[r].

(b) Jihvāmūlīya (@deva[जिह्वामूलीय]) and Upadhmānīya (@deva[उपध्मानीय]) are terms given to a sort of Semi-Visarga, when pronounced before @deva[क्], @deva[ख्], and @deva[प्], @deva[फ्] respectively. It is written symbolically as @deva[ᳵ]. These may be regarded as the spirants of @deva[कवर्ग] and @deva[पवर्ग] respectively.

rules.title: Aspiration of Consonants: Alpa-prāṇa and Mahā-prāṇa
rules.body: Some consonants are pronounced with a slight aspiration and are designated as @deva[अल्पप्राण], while others which are pronounced with a stronger aspiration are called @deva[महाप्राण]. The first and third letters of each class, the nasals and the semi-vowels belong to the first class; the rest belong to the second class. For the sake of convenience the first and third letters of each class are sometimes called "unaspirates."

rules.title: Classification by Organs of Pronunciation
Homogeneous and Heterogeneous Letters: Savarṇa and Asavarṇa
rules.body:
Those letters are called @deva[सवर्ण] or homogeneous whose place of pronunciation is the mouth and the effort required to pronounce them is the same or equal.[^1] Letters which are not @deva[सवर्ण] or similar are called @deva[असवर्ण] or heterogeneous.

---

[^1]: @deva[तुल्यास्यप्रयत्नं सवर्णम्] — Pāṇ. I. 1. 9.

rules.title: Vowels and Consonants Defined
rules.body:
A *svara* or vowel is that which can be pronounced without the help of any other letter; a *vyañjana* or consonant is that which is pronounced with the help of a vowel. The consonants, therefore, are written with a slanting nether stroke to denote their imperfect character.

(a) Hence the consonants are given, in the system of Pāṇini, with an @deva[अ] added to them for the sake of pronunciation.

(b) As already remarked, there are no separate names for the letters of the Sanskrit alphabet, except the two mentioned before, viz. Anusvāra and Visarga, and Refa which is the name sometimes given to @deva[र]. The word @deva[कार] is therefore used as an affix to denote a particular letter; e.g. @deva[अकार] the letter '@deva[अ]', @deva[ककार] the letter '@deva[क]', &c.

rules.title: Definition of Akṣara (Syllable)
rules.body: A vowel by itself or a consonant, simple or conjunct, with a vowel added to it, is called an @deva[अक्षर] or a syllable.

rules.title: Vowel Signs and Conjunct Consonants
Punctuation and Orthographic Marks
rules.body:
As sandhi is of primary importance in Sanskrit, *virāma* or pause can be indicated only at the end of a sentence. The signs of punctuation, therefore, are only two, । and ॥. The former is used to mark the close of a sentence or the first half of a śloka or poetical stanza; the latter is employed to denote the close of a śloka.

(a) The sign called *Avagraha* (and which represents half @deva[अ] Ardhakāra) is generally employed to mark the elision of short @deva[अ] after @deva[ए] or @deva[ओ]; e.g. @deva[तेऽपि] (@deva[ते] + @deva[अपि]), @deva[कालोऽस्ति] (@deva[कालो] + @deva[अस्ति]). The double mark @deva[ऽऽ] is sometimes used to indicate the elision of @deva[आ] after initial long @deva[आ]; @deva[तथा] + @deva[आस्ते] = @deva[तथाऽऽस्ते].

(b) The mark @deva[०] is sometimes used to show that something is omitted, and which is to be understood from the context; e.g. @deva[अ०] may stand for @deva[अर्जुन], @deva[०प्रार्थी] for @deva[कवियशःप्रार्थी], &c.

rules.title: Prosodial Length of Short Vowels
rules.body: Short vowels when followed by a conjunct consonant are said to be prosodially long.

rules.title: Guṇa and Vṛddhi: Vowel Grades
rules.body:
The vowels @deva[अ], @deva[ए], @deva[ओ] and the syllables @deva[अर्] and @deva[अल्] are called Guṇa; the vowels @deva[आ], @deva[ऐ], @deva[औ] and the syllables @deva[आर्] and @deva[आल्] are called Vṛddhi.[^1] The Guṇa and Vṛddhi vowels and syllables that are substituted for the simple vowels will appear from the following table:

| Simple V. | @deva[अ] | @deva[इ] & @deva[ई] | @deva[उ] & @deva[ऊ] | @deva[ऋ] & @deva[ॠ] | @deva[ऌ] |
|-----------|----------|---------------------|---------------------|---------------------|----------|
| Guṇa | @deva[अ] | @deva[ए]            | @deva[ओ]            | @deva[अर्]          | @deva[अल्] |
| Vṛddhi | @deva[आ] | @deva[ऐ]            | @deva[औ]            | @deva[आर्]          | @deva[आल्] |

---

[^1]: @deva[वृद्धिरादैच्। अदेङ् गुणः। उरण् रपरः] Pāṇ. I, 1, 2; I, 51.

rules.title: Nasalization of Semivowels
rules.body: The three semivowels @deva[य्], @deva[ल्] and @deva[व्] are sometimes nasalised and then they are written with the @deva[अनुनासिक] sign over them, as @deva[य्ँ], @deva[ल्ँ], @deva[वँ].

rules.title: Numerical Figures in Sanskrit
rules.body:
The numerical figures in Sanskrit are:
    @deva[१, २, ३, ४, ५, ६, ७, ८, ९, ०]
    1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 0.

These are combined to express larger figures precisely in the same way as in English; @deva[१२५] 125, @deva[५४०] 540, &c.

rules.title: Definition of Sandhi and Saṃhitā
rules.body:
By Sandhi (from @deva[सम्] together, and @deva[धा] to join) is meant the coalescence of two letters coming in immediate contact with each other.[^1]

(a) Saṃhitā[^2] or sandhi is necessary in the case of the internal structure of a *pada*, prepositions and roots joined together and a compound word (@deva[समास]), while in that of a sentence i.e. in the case of the finals and initials of the different words in a sentence, it depends on the will of the writer.

---

[^1]: @deva[परः संनिकर्षः संहिता] — Pāṇ. I. 4. 109. Saṃhitā is the extreme contiguity of letters.

[^2]: @deva[संहितैकपदे नित्याऽनित्या धातुपसर्गयोः । नित्या समासे वाक्ये तु सा विवक्षामपेक्षते ॥] — Sid. Kau. This couplet gives the rule for the observation of Sandhi.

rules.title: Combination of Similar Vowels (Savarṇa Dīrgha)

derivations.gloss: the ṛkāra pronounced by the sacrificer (since there is no long

rules.body:
**I. SVARASANDHI, OR THE COMBINATION OF FINAL AND INITIAL VOWELS.**

If a simple vowel, short or long, be followed by a similar vowel, short or long, the substitute for them both is the similar long vowel; e.g.[^1] @deva[दैत्य] + @deva[अरिः] = @deva[दैत्यारिः]; @deva[अत्र] + @deva[आसीत्] = @deva[अत्रासीत्]; @deva[यदा] + @deva[अभवत्] = @deva[यदाभवत्]; @deva[विद्या] + @deva[आतुरः] = @deva[विद्यातुरः] eager to gain knowledge; @deva[इति] + @deva[इवः] = @deva[इतीवः] @deva[अपि] + @deva[ईक्षते] = @deva[अपीक्षते]; @deva[श्री] + @deva[ईशः] = @deva[श्रीशः]; @deva[भानु] + @deva[उदयः] = @deva[भानूदयः]; @deva[साधु] + @deva[ऊचुः] = @deva[साधूचुः]; @deva[चमू] + @deva[ऊर्जः] = @deva[चमूर्जः] the strength of the army; @deva[कर्तृ] + @deva[ऋजुः] = @deva[कर्तृजुः]; @deva[कृ] + @deva[ॠकारः] = @deva[कॄकारः]; @deva[होतृ] + @deva[ऌकारः] = @deva[होतॄकारः]; the ḷkāra pronounced by the sacrificer (since there is no long @deva[ऌ] long @deva[ॠ] is substituted for both).

(a) If @deva[ऋ] or @deva[ऌ] be followed by a short @deva[ऋ] or @deva[ऌ] short @deva[ऋ] or @deva[ऌ] is optionally substituted for both;[^2] @deva[होतृ] + @deva[ऋकारः] = @deva[होतृकारः], and also @deva[होतृऋकारः] (vide @ref[23]. sec. b.); so three forms altogether @deva[होतॄकारः] @deva[होतृकारः], and @deva[होतृऋकारः]; @deva[होतृ] + @deva[ऌकारः] = @deva[होतॢकारः]. and also @deva[होतृऌकारः].

---

[^1]: @deva[अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः ।] Pāṇ. VI. 1. 101.

[^2]: @deva[ऋति सवर्णे ऋ वा । ऌति सवर्णे ऌ वा ।] Vārtikas on the above.

rules.title: Guṇa Combination: @deva[अ]/@deva[आ] + @deva[इ]/@deva[उ]/@deva[ऋ]/@deva[ऌ]

derivations.gloss: chief guess (or this may be the acc

rules.body:
When @deva[अ] or @deva[आ] is followed by @deva[इ], @deva[उ], @deva[ऋ] or @deva[ऌ], short or long, the @deva[गुण] letter corresponding to the latter takes the place of both;[^1] e.g. @deva[उप] + @deva[इन्द्रः] = @deva[उपेन्द्रः] Vishṇu; @deva[परम] + @deva[ईश्वरः] = @deva[परमेश्वरः] the great lord; @deva[रमा] + @deva[इच्छा] = @deva[रमेच्छा], the wish of Ramā; @deva[यथा] + @deva[ईप्सितं] = @deva[यथेप्सितम्] according to wish or desire; @deva[हित] + @deva[उपदेशः] = @deva[हितोपदेशः] friendly instruction; @deva[कृष्ण] + @deva[ऊरुः] = @deva[कृष्णोरुः] Kṛshṇa's thigh; @deva[गङ्गा] + @deva[उदकं] = @deva[गङ्गोदकम्], @deva[महा] + @deva[ऊरुः] = @deva[महोरुः]. @deva[कृष्ण] + @deva[ऋद्धिः] = @deva[कृष्णर्द्धिः] Kṛshṇa's prosperity; @deva[महा] + @deva[ऋषिः] = @deva[महर्षिः], a great sage; @deva[तव] + @deva[ऌकारः] = @deva[तवल्कारः]. The ḷkāra pronounced by you.

**(a)** If a consonant be followed by homogeneous consonants, except the nasals, the semivowels and @deva[ह्], the first of them is optionally dropped;[^2] @deva[कृष्ण] + @deva[ऋद्धिः] = @deva[कृष्णर्द्धिः] by the general rule; then @deva[कृष्णर्] + @deva[द्] + @deva[ध्] + @deva[इः] = @deva[कृष्णर्धिः] by this rule, the @deva[द्] being dropped; and also a third form @deva[कृष्णर्द्द्धिः] (vide @ref[22], sec. d., below).

**(b)** A consonant of the first five classes except @deva[ञ्] coming after a semivowel is optionally doubled; so @deva[तवल्कारः] also becomes @deva[तवल्क्कारः], @deva[तवल्ल्कारः] and @deva[तवल्ल्क्कारः], 4 forms altogether.

**Exceptions:** Vṛddhi substitute takes place in the following cases:[^3]

**(a)** When a word ending in @deva[अ] is followed by @deva[ऊह], and @deva[प्र] by @deva[ऊह], @deva[ऊढ] and @deva[ऊढि]; e. g. @deva[प्रष्ठ] + @deva[ऊहः] = @deva[प्रष्ठौहः], chief guess (or this may be the acc. pl. of @deva[प्रष्ठवाह्] a young bull trained to the yoke); @deva[प्र] + @deva[ऊहः] = @deva[प्रौहः] principal reasoning. Similarly @deva[प्रौढः] full grown; @deva[प्रौढिः]; but @deva[प्रोढवान्] (as @deva[ऊढवान्] is not mentioned in the Sūtra).

**(b)** @deva[अक्ष] + @deva[ऊहिनी] = @deva[अक्षौहिणी] a complete army.[^4] (The change of @deva[न्] to @deva[ण्] will be explained further on).

**(c)** When @deva[स्व] is followed by @deva[ईर] and @deva[ईरिन्] both derived from @deva[ईर्] to go; e. g. @deva[स्व] + @deva[ईरः] = @deva[स्वैरः], one acting wilfully, self-willed; @deva[स्व] + @deva[ईरिणी] = @deva[स्वैरिणी], so @deva[स्वैरं], @deva[स्वैरी] (@deva[स्वेन ईरितुं शीलमस्य इति]).

**(d)** When @deva[अ] is followed by @deva[ऋतः] and there is an Inst. Tat.; as @deva[सुख] + @deva[ऋत] = @deva[सुखार्तः] blessed with happiness (@deva[सुखेन ऋतः]); but @deva[परमर्तः] very adorable (@deva[परमश्चासौ ऋतश्च]).

**(e)** When the word @deva[ऋण] comes after @deva[प्र], @deva[वत्सतर], @deva[कम्बल], @deva[वसन] and @deva[ऋण]; @deva[प्र] + @deva[ऋणं] = @deva[प्रार्णम्], principal debts, so @deva[वत्सतरार्णम्] debt for a calf; @deva[ऋणार्णम्] (a debt contracted to liquidate a previous debt); @deva[दशार्णः] (Name of a country; lit. the country with ten fortresses); also @deva[दशार्णा नदी] (lit. the river into which ten other rivers flow).

**(f)** When[^5] a preposition ending in @deva[अ] is followed by a root having an initial @deva[ऋ]; as @deva[उप] + @deva[ऋच्छति] = @deva[उपार्च्छति]; @deva[प्रार्च्छति]; but if the root be a denominative, the Vṛddhi is optional; @deva[प्र] + @deva[ऋषभीयति] = @deva[प्रर्षभीयति] or @deva[प्रार्षभीयति] acts like a bull; but @deva[उप] + @deva[ॠकारीयति] = @deva[उपर्कारीयति], as the @deva[ॠ] is long; also @deva[प्र]-@deva[ऌकारीयति] = @deva[प्रा]-@deva[प्रल्कारीयति] very much wishes for @deva[ऌ] lkāra; for @deva[ऌ] is grammatically considered to be similar to @deva[ऋ].

---

[^1]: @deva[आद्गुणः ।] Pāṇ. VI. 1. 86.

[^2]: @deva[झरो झरि सवर्णे] — Pāṇ. VIII. 4. 65.

[^3]: @deva[पत्येधत्यूठ्सु ।] Pāṇ. VI. 1. 89. The first part of the sūtra (viz. @deva[एत्येधति]) forms a counter-exception to @ref[21]. a (which see); @deva[प्रादूहोढोढ्येषैष्येषु]; '@deva[अक्षादूहिन्यामुपसंख्यानम्]' '@deva[स्वादीरेरिणोः]' '@deva[ऋते च तृतीयासमासे]' '@deva[प्रवत्सतरकम्बलवसनार्णदशानामृणे]', Vārtikas on the above Sūtra.

[^4]: Properly an army consisting of 21870 chariots, as many elephants, 65610 horse and 109350 foot. @deva[अक्षौहिण्याः प्रसंख्याता रथानां द्विजसत्तमाः । संख्या गणिततत्त्वज्ञैः सहस्राण्येकविंशतिः ॥ शतान्युपरि चैवाष्टौ तथा भूयश्च सप्ततिः । गजानां तु परीमाणमेतदेव विनिर्दिशेत् ॥ ज्ञेयं शत सहस्रं तु सहस्राणि नवैव तु । नराणामपि पञ्चाशच्छतानि त्रीणि चानघ ॥ पञ्चषष्टिः सहस्राणि तथाश्वानां शतानि च । दशोत्तराणि षट् प्राहुर्यथावदिह संख्यया ॥] Mahā-Bhār. Ad. P. II. 23-26.

[^5]: @deva[उपसर्गादृति धातौ] । Pāṇ. VI. 1. 91. @deva[वा सुप्यापिशलेः] । Pāṇ. VI. 1. 92.

rules.title: Vṛddhi Combination: @deva[अ]/@deva[आ] + @deva[ए]/@deva[ऐ]/@deva[ओ]/@deva[औ]

derivations.gloss: one who moves from one mansion to another, a woman of bad character
name of the celebrated author of the Mahābhāṣya (a vast commentary on the sūtras of Pāṇini)
an antelope with a spotted skin or a kind of bird

rules.body:
When @deva[अ] or @deva[आ] is followed by @deva[ए] or @deva[ऐ] and @deva[ओ] or @deva[औ], @deva[ऐ] and @deva[औ] are respectively substituted for both;[^1] @deva[कृष्ण] + @deva[एकत्वम्] = @deva[कृष्णैकत्वम्]; @deva[देव] + @deva[ऐश्वर्यं] = @deva[देवैश्वर्यम्] the majesty of god; @deva[सा] + @deva[एव] = @deva[सैव] she alone; @deva[भव] + @deva[ओषधं] = @deva[भवौषधम्] medicine against birth and re-birth; @deva[विद्या] + @deva[औत्सुक्यं] = @deva[विद्यौत्सुक्यम्] longing for knowledge.

**Exceptions:**

**(a)** If a preposition ending in @deva[अ] be followed by a root beginning with @deva[ए] or @deva[ओ], @deva[ए] or @deva[ओ] is substituted;[^2] @deva[प्र] + @deva[एजते] = @deva[प्रेजते] quakes very much; @deva[उप] + @deva[ओषति] = @deva[उपोषति] burns something near; but if the root be a denominative, vṛddhi is optional; @deva[उप] + @deva[एडकीयति] = @deva[उपेडकीयति] or @deva[उपैडकीयति]; @deva[प्र] + @deva[ओघीयति] = @deva[प्रोघीयति] or @deva[प्रौघीयति].

**Counter-exception:** If a form of the root @deva[इ] to go, or @deva[एध्] to grow, with an initial @deva[ए], comes after @deva[अ], and @deva[एष] or @deva[एष्य] derived from @deva[इष्] of the 4th, 6th or 9th conj., after @deva[प्र], vṛddhi takes place; @deva[उप] + @deva[एति] = @deva[उपैति]; @deva[उप] + @deva[एधते] = @deva[उपैधते]; (but @deva[उप] + @deva[इतः] = @deva[उपेतः]; @deva[अवेहि] know; from @deva[अव] + @deva[एहि] which is equal to @deva[अव] + @deva[आ] + @deva[इहि], and not @deva[अवैहि]; @deva[मा भवान् प्र] + @deva[इदिधत्] = @deva[प्रेदिधत्]); @deva[प्र] + @deva[एषः] = @deva[प्रैषः] sending or directing; @deva[प्र] + @deva[एष्यः] = @deva[प्रैष्यः] a servant. But @deva[प्रेषः], @deva[प्रेष्यः] (from @deva[ईष्]).

**(b)** When @deva[अ] is followed by @deva[एव] in an indefinite sense, @deva[ए] is substituted for both:[^3] @deva[क] + @deva[एव] = @deva[केव भोक्ष्यसे] where will you dine to-day? (The place being not definitely known); but @deva[तवैव] (why, I shall dine at your house).

**(c)** @deva[अ] followed by @deva[ओम्] and @deva[आ] (prep.) is dropped[^4] e. g. @deva[शिवाय] + @deva[ओं नमः] = @deva[शिवायों नमः]; @deva[शिव] + @deva[एहि] (@deva[आ] + @deva[इहि]) = @deva[शिवेहि].

**(d)** The vṛddhi is optional when the ending @deva[अ] of a word is followed by @deva[ओतु] a cat, or @deva[ओष्ठ] the lower lip, in a compound:[^5] @deva[स्थूल] + @deva[ओतुः] = @deva[स्थूलोतुः] or @deva[स्थूलौतुः]; @deva[बिम्बोष्ठः], @deva[बिम्बौष्ठः].

**(e)** The final vowel or the final consonant with the preceding vowel is dropped in the case of the following words when followed by certain words in a compound:[^6][^7] @deva[शक] the country of the Śakas + @deva[अन्धुः] a well = @deva[शकन्धुः]; @deva[कर्क] name of a country + @deva[अन्धुः] = @deva[कर्कन्धुः]; @deva[कुल] + @deva[अटा] = @deva[कुलटा] one who moves from one mansion to another, a woman of bad character; @deva[सीमन्] + @deva[अन्तः] = @deva[सीमन्तः] (the white line left by the parting of the hair on each side of the head); but @deva[सीमान्तः] when the meaning of the word is 'The last line or limit of a boundary.' @deva[मनस्] + @deva[ईषा] = @deva[मनीषा] wish; so @deva[लाङ्गलीषा] the pole of a plough; @deva[हलीषा]; @deva[पतन्] + @deva[अञ्जलिः] = @deva[पतञ्जलिः] name of the celebrated author of the Mahābhāṣya (a vast commentary on the sūtras of Pāṇini); lit. 'fit to be adored with joined hands; or according to tradition 'who fell down from the hands of a certain sage as he was offering water to the sun at the time of Sandhyā adoration.' @deva[सार] + @deva[अङ्गः] = @deva[सारङ्गः] an antelope with a spotted skin or a kind of bird; but @deva[साराङ्गः] one with a beautiful skin. This is an Ākṛtigaṇa i.e. words of similar formation and requiring grammatical explanation but not actually found in the gaṇa may be classed under it; e.g. @deva[मार्त] + @deva[अण्डः] = @deva[मार्तण्डः] (derived from @deva[मृताण्ड]) lit. born of a dead egg, the sun.

---

[^1]: @deva[वृद्धिरेचि] — Pāṇ. VI. 1. 88.

[^2]: @deva[एङि पररूपम्] । Pāṇ. VI. 1. 94.

[^3]: @deva[एवे चानियोगे] Vārtik.

[^4]: @deva[ओमाङोश्च] Pāṇ. VI. 1. 95.

[^5]: '@deva[ओत्वोष्ठयोः समासे वा ।]'

[^6]: @deva[शकन्ध्वादिषु पररूपं वाच्यम्] Vārt.

[^7]: And also in the case of an onomatopœic wording in @deva[अत्] followed by @deva[इति] e.g. @deva[पटत्] + @deva[इति] = @deva[पटिति]; but not in the case of a monosyllabic word @deva[श्रद्] + @deva[इति] = @deva[श्रदिति]; and when the word is repeated, only the @deva[त्] is optionally dropped, as @deva[पटत्पटत्] + @deva[इति] = @deva[पटत्पटेति] or @deva[पटत्पटदिति].

rules.title: Semi-vowel Substitution: @deva[इ]/@deva[उ]/@deva[ऋ]/@deva[ऌ] → @deva[य्]/@deva[व्]/@deva[र्]/@deva[ल्]
rules.body:
When @deva[इ], @deva[उ], @deva[ऋ] and @deva[ऌ], short or long, are followed by a dissimilar vowel, @deva[य्], @deva[व्], @deva[र्] and @deva[ल्] are respectively substituted for them[^1]; e. g. @deva[इति] + @deva[आह] = @deva[इत्याह], @deva[सुधी] + @deva[उपास्यः] = @deva[सुध्युपास्यः] adored by the wise; @deva[मधु] + @deva[अरिः] = @deva[मध्वरिः] the enemy of @deva[मधु] i. e. Vishṇu, @deva[धातृ] + @deva[अंशः] = @deva[धात्रंशः] a portion of the creator; @deva[ऌ] + @deva[आकृतिः] = @deva[लाकृतिः] a figure like that of @deva[ऌ] &c.

**Ob.**—Several of the above words may have more than one form when combined; e. g. @deva[सुधी] + @deva[उपास्यः] = @deva[सुध्य्] + @deva[उपास्यः] by the general rule:—

**N. B.** The following rules and the two (a), (b) given under @ref[20], though they properly form the subject of the next section, are given here to avoid confusion. Ordinary students may pass over these except sec. (b) of the present art.

**(a)** A consonant except @deva[ङ्], preceded by a vowel, is optionally doubled, if no vowel follows[^2]; @deva[सुध्य्] + @deva[उपास्यः] = @deva[सुध्युपास्यः] and @deva[सुध्ध्य्] + @deva[उपास्यः]:—

**(b)** When a consonant, except a nasal or a semivowel, is followed by a soft unaspirate or aspirate (3rd or 4th letter of a class) it is changed to the soft unaspirate (3rd letter) of its class[^3]; @deva[सुध्ध्य्] + @deva[उपास्यः] = @deva[सुद्ध्युपास्य]

**(c)** Semivowels, when preceded by a letter of the first five classes except @deva[ञ्] are optionally doubled[^4]; thus @deva[सुध्य्] + @deva[उपास्यः] = @deva[सुध्य्य्] + @deva[उपास्यः] and @deva[सुध्ध्य्य्] + @deva[उपास्यः]; @deva[सुद्ध्य्] + @deva[उपास्यः] = @deva[सुद्ध्य्य्] + @deva[उपास्यः] and @deva[सुद्ध्य्य्] + @deva[उपास्यः]। Thus there are four forms ultimately, viz. @deva[सुध्युपास्यः], @deva[सुद्ध्युपास्यः] and @deva[सुद्ध्य्युपास्यः]।

Similarly @deva[मधु] + @deva[अरिः] = @deva[मध्वरिः], @deva[मध्ध्वरिः], @deva[मद्ध्वरिः], and @deva[मद्ध्व्वरिः]; @deva[धातृ] + @deva[अंशः] = @deva[धात्रंशः] and @deva[धात्त्रंशः]. In @deva[ऌ] + @deva[आकृतिः] of course there is no possibility of any other form.

**(d)** A consonant except @deva[ङ्], coming after @deva[र्] or @deva[ह्] preceded by a vowel is optionally doubled[^5]; e. g. @deva[हरि] + @deva[अनुभवः] = @deva[हर्य्] + @deva[अनुभवः] = @deva[हर्यनुभवः] by the general rule; and optionally @deva[हर्य्य्] + @deva[अनुभवः] = @deva[हर्य्यनुभवः] (Hari's experience) by this rule; so @deva[न हि] + @deva[अस्ति] = @deva[न ह्यस्ति] and @deva[न ह्य्यस्ति]।

---

[^1]: @deva[इको यणचि] । Pāṇ. VI. 1. 77.

[^2]: @deva[अनचि च] । Pāṇ. VIII. 4. 47.

[^3]: @deva[झलां जश् झशि] । Pāṇ. 4. 53.

[^4]: @deva[यणो मयो द्वे वाच्ये] Vārt.

[^5]: @deva[अचो रहाभ्यां द्वे] । Pāṇ. VIII. 4. 46.

rules.title: Optional Non-combination of Final @deva[इ]/@deva[उ]/@deva[ऋ]/@deva[ऌ]
rules.body:
**(a)** @deva[इ], @deva[उ], @deva[ऋ] or @deva[ऌ], short or long, at the end of a word followed by a dissimilar vowel except in a compound, are optionally not combined, and when so they are shortened if long[^1] e.g. @deva[चक्री] + @deva[अत्र] = @deva[चक्र्यत्र], Vishṇu here, and @deva[चक्रि अत्र]; but @deva[वापी] + @deva[अश्वः] = @deva[वाप्यश्वः] a horse in a well, @deva[गौरी] + @deva[औ] (a term.) @deva[गौर्यौ].

**(b)** @deva[अ], @deva[इ], @deva[उ] and @deva[ऌ], short or long, at the end of a word followed by a short @deva[ऋ] are also optionally not combined, and when not combined are shortened if long[^2]; e.g. @deva[ब्रह्मा] + @deva[ऋषिः] = @deva[ब्रह्मर्षिः] A Brāhmaṇa saint, and @deva[ब्रह्म ऋषिः]; @deva[सप्तर्षीणाम्] of the seven sages, and @deva[सप्त ऋषीणाम्] (a comp. expression).

---

[^1]: @deva[इकोऽसवर्णे शाकल्यस्य ह्रस्वश्च ।]

[^2]: @deva[ऋत्यकः] Pāṇ. VII. 1. 127.

rules.title: Diphthong Transformation: @deva[ए]/@deva[ओ]/@deva[ऐ]/@deva[औ] → @deva[अय्]/@deva[अव्]/@deva[आय्]/@deva[आव्]

derivations.gloss: produced from a cow as milk, ghee &c

rules.body:
@deva[ए], @deva[ओ], @deva[ऐ] and @deva[औ], when followed by a vowel, are changed to @deva[अय्], @deva[अव्], @deva[आय्], and @deva[आव्] respectively[^1]; e.g. @deva[हरे] + @deva[ए] = @deva[हरये] for Hari; @deva[विष्णो] + @deva[ए] = @deva[विष्णवे] for Vishṇu; @deva[नै] + @deva[अकः] = @deva[नायकः] A leader; @deva[पौ] + @deva[अकः] = @deva[पावकः] the purifier i.e. fire.

**(a)** @deva[य्] or @deva[व्] at the end of a word and preceded by @deva[अ] or @deva[आ] is optionally dropped when followed by a vowel or a soft consonant[^2]; e.g. @deva[हरे] + @deva[एहि] = @deva[हरयेहि] or @deva[हर एहि]; @deva[विष्णो] + @deva[इह] = @deva[विष्णविह] or @deva[विष्ण इह]; @deva[श्रियै] + @deva[उद्यतः] = @deva[श्रियायुद्यतः] or @deva[श्रिया उद्यतः] intent on getting money; @deva[गुरौ] + @deva[उत्कः] = @deva[गुरावुत्कः] or @deva[गुरा उत्कः] longing to see the preceptor.

**Note:** Two vowels brought together by the disappearance of an intervening consonant or visarga do not coalesce.

**(b)** @deva[ओ] and @deva[औ], when followed by a termination beginning with @deva[य्], become @deva[अव्] and @deva[आव्] respectively[^3]; e.g. @deva[गो] + @deva[यं] = @deva[गव्यम्] produced from a cow as milk, ghee &c. @deva[नौ] + @deva[यं] = @deva[नाव्यम्] accessible by a boat, navigable.

**N.B.** This rule holds good, in the case of roots, only when the @deva[ओ] or @deva[औ] is brought in by virtue of a termination;[^4] e.g. @deva[लू] + @deva[यं] = @deva[लो] + @deva[यं] = @deva[लव्यम्] fit to be lopped off. @deva[अवश्यलु] + @deva[यं] = @deva[अवश्यलौ] + @deva[यं] = @deva[अवश्यलाव्यम्] which ought necessarily to be cut off.

**(c)** The @deva[ओ] of the word @deva[गो] is also changed to @deva[अव्] when followed by the word @deva[यूति] (in the Veda and) in ordinary language when it means a particular measure of length[^5]; e.g. @deva[गव्यूतिः] four miles.

**(d)** The @deva[ए] of the roots @deva[क्षि] and @deva[जि] is changed to @deva[अय्] when followed by the @deva[य] of the potential participle indicating capability[^6] e.g. @deva[क्षि] + @deva[य] = @deva[क्षे] + @deva[य] = @deva[क्षय्यं] what can be reduced; so @deva[जय्यं] what can be conquered; but @deva[क्षेतुं], @deva[जेतुं], @deva[योग्यं], @deva[क्षेयं] (what is fit to be removed but may not be so) @deva[पापं], @deva[जेयं] (what ought to be curbed but which it may not be always possible to curb as) @deva[मनः]।

---

[^1]: @deva[एचोऽयवायावः] — Pāṇ. VI. 1. 78.

[^2]: @deva[लोपः शाकल्यस्य] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 19.

[^3]: @deva[वान्तो यि प्रत्यये] । Pāṇ. VI. 1. 79.

[^4]: @deva[धातोस्तन्निमित्तस्यैव] । Pāṇ. VI. 1. 80.

[^5]: @deva[गोर्यूतौ छन्दस्युपसंख्यानम् । अध्वपरिमाणे च ।] Vārtikas.

[^6]: @deva[क्षय्यजय्यौ शक्यार्थे] । Pāṇ. VI. 1. 81.

rules.title: Merger of @deva[अ] into @deva[ए]/@deva[ओ] (Avagraha)
rules.body:
When @deva[ए] or @deva[ओ] at the end of a word is followed by @deva[अ] the latter merges into the former[^1] and the sign @deva[ऽ] is sometimes written in its place; e.g. @deva[हरे] + @deva[अव] = @deva[हरेऽव] protect, Oh Hari; @deva[विष्णो] + @deva[अव] = @deva[विष्णोऽव].

**(a)** If the word @deva[गो], ending in @deva[ओ], be followed by @deva[अ], the @deva[अ] is optionally retained, and if by a vowel, @deva[अव] is optionally substituted for @deva[ओ];[^2] @deva[गो] + @deva[अग्रम्] = @deva[गोग्रम्], @deva[गोअग्रम्] and @deva[गवाग्रम्] a multitude of cows or chief among cows; but if it be followed by @deva[इन्द्र] and @deva[अक्ष] it necessarily changes its @deva[ओ] to @deva[अव]; @deva[गो] + @deva[इन्द्रः] = @deva[गवेन्द्रः] an excellent bull; @deva[गवाक्षः] a lattice-window, similarly.

---

[^1]: @deva[एङः पदान्तादति] । Pāṇ. VI. 1. 109.

[^2]: @deva[सर्वत्र विभाषा गोः । अवङ् स्फोटायनस्य । इन्द्रे च ।] Pāṇ. VI. 1. 122-24.

rules.title: Pragṛhya: Exceptions to Sandhi
rules.body:
No *sandhi* is possible in the case of[^1]—

**I.** What are called the @deva[प्रगृह्य] exceptions; viz.—

**(a)** When a dual form (whether of a noun, pronoun or verb) ends in @deva[ई], @deva[ऊ], or @deva[ए];[^2] e.g. @deva[हरी एतौ]; @deva[विष्णू इमौ]; @deva[गङ्गे अमू]; @deva[पचेते इमौ].

**(b)** When @deva[ई] or @deva[ऊ] follows the @deva[म्] of the pronoun @deva[अदस्][^3] e. g. @deva[अमी ईशाः] these lords; @deva[अमू आसाते] the two sit down.

**Obs.** The @deva[ए] of the Vedic forms @deva[अस्मे] and @deva[युष्मे] also does not blend with a following vowel (@deva[शे] । Pāṇ. I. 1. 13.); e. g. @deva[अस्मे इन्द्राबृहस्पती] &c. Ṛg. IV. 49. 4. Similarly a Vaidic word having the sense of the loc. (but not ending in the termination of the loc.) remains unaffected by a following vowel; @deva[सोमो गौरी अधिश्रितः] &c. Ṛg. X. 12. 3. where @deva[गौरी] stands for @deva[गौर्याम्] the loc. term, being dropped by @deva[सुपां सुलुक्] Pāṇ. VII. 1. 30.

**(c)** Particles consisting of a single vowel, except @deva[आ] meaning 'a little, or a limit' exclusive or inclusive or used as a preposition, when followed by a vowel,[^4] e.g. @deva[इ इन्द्र] Oh Indra, @deva[उ उमेश], @deva[आ एवं नु मन्यसे] ah, you think so; but @deva[आ] + @deva[उष्णम्] = @deva[ओष्णम्] (a little warm) &c.

**(d)** When an indeclinable ends in @deva[ओ]; e.g. @deva[अहो ईशाः]; the final @deva[ओ] of a noun in the vocative case optionally combines when followed by @deva[इति]; e.g. @deva[विष्णो इति] = @deva[विष्णविति], and @deva[विष्णो इति]; also @deva[विष्ण इति] (see @ref[24] a.).

**N.B.** All these vowels which do not blend with others, and sometimes the words in which they occur are technically called @deva[प्रगृह्य].

**II.** and *pluta* vowels; e. g. @deva[एहि कृष्ण३ अत्र गौश्चरति] Come Kṛṣṇa; here is the cow grazing.

A vowel becomes pluta under the following circumstances:[^5]

**(1)** The last vowel of a sentence uttered in reply to a salutation from a male person other than a Śūdra when the name or the family is actually mentioned, e.g. @deva[भो आयुष्मानेधि देवदत्त३] live long, O Devadatta, which is said in reply to "@deva[अभिवादये देवदत्तोहम्]" I, Devadatta, bow to you; but the last @deva[इ] in "@deva[भो आयुष्मती भव गार्गि]" or in @deva[आयुष्मानेधि] is not pluta; for in the 1st we have the name of a female and in the 2nd no name at all.

But if the sentence end in the word @deva[भोः] or in the name of a Kshatriya or Vaishya the last vowel becomes optionally pluta e.g. @deva[आयुष्मान् एधि भोः] or @deva[भो३ः]; @deva[आयुष्मानेधीन्द्रवर्मन्] or @deva[वर्म३न्]; @deva[आयुष्मानेधीन्द्रपालित] or @deva[त३]।

**(2)** The final vowel of a sentence addressed from a distance to a person, and that of the particles @deva[हे] and @deva[है] used in such a sentence; e. g. @deva[सक्तून् पिब देवदत्त३]; @deva[हे राम]; @deva[राम]; @deva[हे३]।

---

[^1]: @deva[प्लुतप्रगृह्या अचि नित्यम्] Pāṇ. VI. 1. 125.

[^2]: @deva[ईदूदेद्द्विवचनं प्रगृह्यम्] ।

[^3]: @deva[अदसो मात्] । Pāṇ. I. 1. 11, 12.

[^4]: @deva[निपात एकाजनाङ् । ओत् । संबुद्धौ शाकल्यस्येतावनार्षे ।] Pāṇ. I. 14-16.

[^5]: @deva[वाक्यस्य टेः प्लुत उदात्तः । प्रत्यभिवादेऽशूद्रे ।] Pāṇ. VIII. 2. 82-83. @deva[स्त्रियां न । भोराजन्यविशां वेति वाच्यम् ।] Vārtikas on the latter sūtra. @deva[दूराद्धूते च । हैहेप्रयोगे हैहयोः ।] Pāṇ. VIII. 2. 84-85.

rules.title: Optional Transformation of @deva[उ] to @deva[व]
rules.body:
The particle @deva[उ], preceded by a letter of the first five classes except @deva[ञ्] and followed by any vowel, is optionally changed to @deva[व्][^1]; @deva[किमु उक्तं], @deva[किम्वुक्तम्] and @deva[किमु उक्तं] (by @ref[26] c.).

---

[^1]: @deva[मय उञो वो वा] । Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 33.

rules.title: Palatal and Lingual Assimilation
rules.body:
**II. HALSANDHI, OR THE COALESCENCE OF FINAL CONSONANTS WITH VOWELS AND CONSONANTS.**

When @deva[स्] or a consonant of the dental class comes in contact with:—

**(a)** @deva[श्] or a consonant of the palatal class, the corresponding letter of the latter class is substituted for the former, and @deva[श्] for @deva[स्];[^1] @deva[हरिस्] + @deva[शेते] = @deva[हरिश्शेते] Hari sleeps; @deva[रामः] + @deva[चिनोति] = @deva[रामश्चिनोति] Rāma collects: @deva[सत्] + @deva[चित्] = @deva[सच्चित्] Reality and knowledge; @deva[शार्ङ्गिन्] + @deva[जय] = @deva[शार्ङ्गिञ्जय] Be you victorious, Oh Kṛṣṇa.

**Exception:** (1) Dentals coming after @deva[श्] are not changed into the corresponding palatals: e.g. @deva[विश्नः] that which spreads lustre; @deva[प्रश्नः].

**(b)** @deva[ष्] or a consonant of the lingual class, @deva[ष्] is substituted for @deva[स्] and the corresponding letter of the latter class for the former; @deva[रामस्] + @deva[षष्ठः] = @deva[रामष्षष्ठः] Rāma who is sixth. @deva[रामस्] + @deva[टीकते] = @deva[रामष्टीकते] Rāma goes; @deva[तत्] + @deva[टीका] = @deva[तट्टीका] A commentary on that; @deva[चक्रिन्] + @deva[ढौकसे] = @deva[चक्रिण्ढौकसे] Oh Kṛṣṇa, thou goest; @deva[पेष्] + @deva[ता] = @deva[पेष्टा] one who pounds.

**Exception:**[^2] (1) If a letter of the lingual class coming at the end of a word be followed by @deva[स्] or a letter of the dental class, the @deva[स्] as well as the dentals except the @deva[न्] of @deva[नाम्], @deva[नवति] and @deva[नगरी] remain unaffected; @deva[षट्] + @deva[सन्तः] = @deva[षट्सन्तः] six good men; (see also @ref[39].); @deva[षट्] + @deva[ते] = @deva[षट्ते] these six; but @deva[ईट्टे] (since the @deva[ट्] of @deva[ईट्] is not at the end of a word) he praises. So @deva[षण्णवति] Ninety-six, @deva[षण्णगर्यः] six towns; but @deva[सर्पिस्] + @deva[तमम्] = @deva[सर्पिष्टमम्] abundance of ghee; as the exception excludes @deva[स्].

---

[^1]: @deva[स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः । शात् । ष्टुना ष्टुः ।] Pāṇ. VIII. 4, 40, 44, 41.

[^2]: @deva[न पदान्ताट्टोरनाम् ।] Pāṇ. VIII. 4. 42. @deva[अनाम्नवतिनगरीणामिति वाच्यम् ।] Vārt.

rules.title: No Lingual Substitution Before ष्
rules.body:
If a letter of the group @deva[त्] be followed by @deva[ष्] it does not substitute its corresponding lingual[^1]; @deva[सन्] + @deva[षष्ठः] = @deva[सन्षष्ठः] sixth good man.

---

[^1]: @deva[तोः षि] । Pāṇ. VIII. 4. 43.

rules.title: Nasal Substitution for Final Consonants
rules.body:
If a consonant, except @deva[र्] or @deva[ह्], coming at the end of a word, be followed by a nasal, the nasal of its class is optionally substituted for it[^1]; @deva[एतद्] + @deva[मुरारिः] = @deva[एतन्मुरारिः] and @deva[एतद्मुरारिः] (see @ref[22] sec. b.) this Murāri; @deva[षड्] + @deva[मासाः] = @deva[षण्मासाः] and @deva[षड्मासाः] six months.

**N.B.** If the nasal belong to a termination the change is necessary; @deva[तन्मात्रम्] that alone; @deva[चिन्मात्रं] mere knowledge. @deva[वाक्] + @deva[मय] = @deva[वाङ्मय]. The word @deva[ककुद्मत्] (see Rag. IV. 22.) is irregularly formed.

---

[^1]: @deva[यरोऽनुनासिकेऽनुनासिको वा ।] Pāṇ. VIII. 4. 45.

rules.title: Dental to Nasalised ल् Before ल्
rules.body:
A letter of the dental class, followed by @deva[ल्] is changed to @deva[ल्], the nasalised @deva[ल्ँ] taking the place of @deva[न्][^1]; @deva[तद्] + @deva[लयः] = @deva[तल्लयः] the destruction of that; @deva[विद्वान्] + @deva[लिखति] = @deva[विद्वाँल्लिखति] a learned man writes.

---

[^1]: @deva[तोर्लि] । Pāṇ. VIII. 4. 60.

rules.title: Change of @deva[स्] of @deva[स्था]/@deva[स्तम्भ्] to @deva[थ्] after @deva[उद्]
rules.body:
The @deva[स्] of @deva[स्था] and @deva[स्तम्भ्] is changed into @deva[थ्] when after the preposition @deva[उद्];[^1] @deva[उद्] + @deva[स्थानम्] = @deva[उद्] + @deva[थ्थानम्] = @deva[उद्थानम्] and @deva[उद्थ्थानम्] (see @ref[20]. a), and then @deva[उत्थानम्], @deva[उत्थ्थानम्] rising up; similarly @deva[उत्तम्भनम्] and @deva[उत्थ्तम्भनम्] upholding.

---

[^1]: @deva[उदः स्थास्तम्भोः पूर्वस्य] । Pāṇ. VIII. 4. 61.

rules.title: Optional Aspiration of ह् After a Class Letter
Final Consonant Devoicing and Softening
rules.body: Any consonant, except a nasal or a semi-vowel, is changed to the first of its class, when followed by a hard consonant, and to the first or third when followed by nothing; @deva[वाक्], @deva[वाग्].

rules.title: Optional Change of @deva[श] to @deva[छ]
@deva[म] to Anusvāra Conversion
rules.body:
@deva[म्] at the end of a word is changed into an Anusvāra when followed by a consonant;[^1] e.g. @deva[हरिम्] + @deva[वन्दे] = @deva[हरिं वन्दे] I salute Hari. But @deva[गम्] + @deva[य] + @deva[ते] = @deva[गम्यते] as @deva[म्] is not at the end of a word. The word @deva[सम्राट्] is an exception (see Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 25).

**(a)** @deva[म्] and @deva[न्], not at the end of a *pada*, are turned into an Anusvāra when followed by a consonant except a nasal or a semivowel or @deva[ह्]; @deva[आक्रम्] + @deva[स्यते] = @deva[आक्रंस्यते] he will overcome; @deva[यशान्] + @deva[सि] = @deva[यशांसि] (nom. pl. of @deva[यशस्] fame); but @deva[मन्यते] he thinks, as @deva[न्] is followed here by @deva[य] which is a semi-vowel; @deva[ग्रामान्] + @deva[गच्छति] = @deva[ग्रामान्गच्छति] as @deva[न्] is at the end of a *pada* (grammatical form).

**(b)** This change is optional in the case of @deva[म्] when @deva[ह्] followed by @deva[म्] comes after it; e. g. @deva[किम्] + @deva[ह्मलयति] = @deva[किंह्मलयति] and @deva[किम्ह्मलयति] what does he shake?; but if this @deva[ह्] be followed by @deva[न्], and if by @deva[य्], @deva[व्], @deva[ल्], the nasalised @deva[य्], @deva[व्], @deva[ल्], are optionally substituted for @deva[म्]: e. g. @deva[कि] + @deva[ह्नुते] = @deva[किंह्नुते] or @deva[किन्ह्नुते] what does he conceal? @deva[किम्] + @deva[ह्यः] = @deva[किंह्यः] and @deva[किय्ँह्यः] what! yesterday! so @deva[किंह्वलयति], @deva[किव्ँह्वलयति]; @deva[किंह्लादयति] and @deva[किल्ँह्लादयति]; but @deva[अहम्] + @deva[आगतः] = @deva[अहमागतः] I have come.

---

[^1]: @deva[मोऽनुस्वारः। नश्चापदान्तस्य झलि] — Pāṇ. VII. 3, 23, 24 and Pāṇ. VIII. 3, 27, I. 3. 10. (see sec. b).

rules.title: Anusvāra to Class Nasal Conversion
rules.body:
An Anusvāra followed by any consonant except @deva[श्], @deva[ष्], @deva[स्] or @deva[ह्] is changed to the nasal of the class to which the following letter belongs, necessarily when in the middle, and optionally when at the end of a word[^1]; e.g. @deva[अन्क्] + @deva[इतः] = @deva[अं] + @deva[क्] + @deva[इतः] (by the preceding rule and then) @deva[अङ्कितः] marked (by this); so @deva[अन्च्] + @deva[इतः] = @deva[अञ्चितः] honoured; @deva[कुण्ठित] obstructed; @deva[शान्तः] calmed; @deva[गुम्फितः] woven; @deva[त्वम्] + @deva[करोषि] = @deva[त्वं करोषि] or @deva[त्वङ्करोषि] thou doest; similarly @deva[संयन्ता] or @deva[सय्ँयन्ता] a restrainer; @deva[संवत्सरः] or @deva[सँव्वत्सरः] a year; @deva[यं लोकम्] or @deva[यल्ँलोकम्] to which people.

---

[^1]: @deva[अनुस्वारस्य ययि परसवर्णः । वा पदान्तस्य ।] Pāṇ. VIII. 4. 48-52.

rules.title: Optional @deva[क्]/@deva[ट्] Epenthesis and Aspiration
rules.body:
If @deva[ङ्] and @deva[ण्] be followed by a sibilant, @deva[क्] and @deva[ट्] respectively are suffixed to them optionally; and hard unaspirates are optionally changed into hard aspirates when followed by a sibilant;[^1] @deva[प्राङ्] + @deva[षष्ठः] = @deva[प्राङ्षष्ठः], @deva[प्राङ्क्षष्ठः], @deva[प्राङ्ख्षष्ठः]; the sixth man gone before; @deva[सुगण्] + @deva[षष्ठः] = @deva[सुगण्षष्ठः], @deva[सुगण्ट्षष्ठः], @deva[सुगण्ठ्षष्ठः], the sixth good counter.

---

[^1]: @deva[ङ्णोः कुक्टुक् शरि] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 28.

rules.title: Optional @deva[ध्] (@deva[त्]) Insertion between @deva[ड्]/@deva[न्] and @deva[स्]; Doubling
rules.body:
If @deva[ड्] or @deva[न्] at the end of a word be followed by @deva[स्], @deva[ध्] (changed to @deva[त्]) is optionally inserted between them;[^1] e. g. @deva[षड्] + @deva[सन्तः] = @deva[षड्सन्तः] or @deva[षड्] + @deva[ध्] + @deva[सन्तः] = @deva[षड्त्सन्तः] six good men; so @deva[सन्] + @deva[सः] = @deva[सन्सः] or @deva[सन्त्सः] that good man.

**(a)** @deva[ङ्], @deva[ण्] and @deva[न्] at the end of a word and preceded by a short vowel double themselves when followed by a vowel;[^2] e. g. @deva[प्रत्यङ्] + @deva[आत्मा] = @deva[प्रत्यङ्ङात्मा] the individual soul; so @deva[सुगण्णीशः] the best reckoner; @deva[सन्नच्युतः] good Achyuta.

---

[^1]: @deva[डः सि धुट्। नश्च] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 22, 32.

[^2]: @deva[ङमो ह्रस्वादचि ङमुण्नित्यम्] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 32.

rules.title: Complex Sandhi with @deva[न्] and @deva[श्]
rules.body:
**Ob.** If the ending @deva[न्] of a word be followed by @deva[श्], @deva[त्] is optionally inserted between them;[^1] e. g. @deva[सन्] + @deva[शंभुः] = @deva[सन्शंभुः] and @deva[सन्त्छंभुः] Śambhu existing for all times; and @deva[सन्त्शंभुः] = @deva[सन्त्शंभुः] and @deva[सन्त्छंभुः] (by @ref[35]); then by @ref[28] (a) @deva[न्] being changed to @deva[ञ्] (and @deva[त्] to @deva[च्]) @deva[सञ्शंभुः], @deva[सञ्च्शंभुः] and @deva[सञ्च्छंभुः] and finally by dropping @deva[च्] optionally (by @ref[20] a.) @deva[सञ्शंभुः], @deva[सञ्च्शंभुः] and @deva[सञ्छंभुः], @deva[सञ्च्छंभुः].

---

[^1]: @deva[शि तुक्] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 31.

rules.title: Retroflexion of @deva[न्] to @deva[ण्] after @deva[र्], @deva[ष्], @deva[ऋ] (Ṇatva)
rules.body:
@deva[न्] coming after @deva[र्], @deva[ष्], or @deva[ऋ] short or long, in the same word is changed to @deva[ण्] even though a vowel, a semi-vowel except @deva[ल्], a nasal, or a letter of the guttural or labial class or @deva[ह्] comes between @deva[र्], @deva[ष्] or @deva[ऋ] and @deva[न्];[^1] e. g. @deva[रामेन] = @deva[रामेण]; @deva[पूष्] + @deva[ना] = @deva[पूष्णा] by the sun, @deva[पितॄणाम्] &c.; but @deva[राम] + @deva[नाम] = @deva[राम नाम] (as these are two separate words). This change does not take place when @deva[न्] is at the end of a word[^2] @deva[रामान्].

---

[^1]: @deva[रषाभ्यां नो णः समानपदे। अट्कुप्वाङ्नुम्व्यवायेऽपि] — Pāṇ. VIII. 4. 1. 2.

[^2]: @deva[पदान्तस्य न] — Pāṇ. VIII. 4. 37.

rules.title: Retroflexion of @deva[स्] to @deva[ष्] after Vowels (Ṣatva)
rules.body:
@deva[स्] belonging to a substitute (@deva[आदेश]) or a termination (@deva[प्रत्यय]) and not at the end of a grammatical form is changed to @deva[ष्] when preceded by any vowel except @deva[अ] or @deva[आ], a semi-vowel, a letter of the guttural class or @deva[ह्];[^1] e. g. @deva[रामे] + @deva[सु] = @deva[रामेषु]; but @deva[रामस्य] as @deva[स्] is preceded by @deva[अ]. @deva[सुपीः] @deva[सुपिसौ] &c., as @deva[स्] belongs to the word @deva[सुपिस्]. This change takes place even if an *anuswāra* substituted for @deva[न्], a *visarga* or @deva[श्], @deva[ष्] or @deva[स्] intervene;[^2] e. g. @deva[धनून्] + @deva[सि] = @deva[धनूंषि] nom. pl. of @deva[धनुस्] neu. a bow. @deva[पिपठीष्] + @deva[सु] = @deva[पिपठीष्षु].

---

[^1]: @deva[अपदान्तस्य मूर्धन्यः। इण्कोः। आदेशप्रत्यययोः] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 55, 57, 59.

[^2]: @deva[नुम्विसर्जनीयशर्व्यवायेऽपि] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 58.

rules.title: Sandhi of @deva[सम्], @deva[पुम्], @deva[कान्] and Visarga before Sibilant @deva[स्]
rules.body:
The @deva[म्] of @deva[सम्] is changed to an Anuswāra and Visarga when followed by a form of the root @deva[कृ], the Anuswāra again is optionally changed to an Anunāsika; e. g. @deva[सम्] + @deva[कर्ता] = @deva[संस्कर्ता] and @deva[सँस्कर्ता]; @deva[स्] is affixed to the ending of the words @deva[सम्], @deva[पुम्] and @deva[कान्];[^1] so @deva[संस्कर्ता] and @deva[सँस्कर्ता].

*N. B.* The word @deva[संस्कर्ता] is capable of having 108 different forms as several *sūtras* are brought to bear upon it; but they are not given here as being tedious and of no material value.

Sections *a*, *b*, *c*, and *d* may be omitted by beginners.

**(a)** The @deva[म्] of @deva[पुम्] is optionally nasalised and has @deva[स्] added to it as above, when it is followed by a hard consonant except a sibilant, preceding a vowel, a semivowel, a nasal or @deva[ह्];[^2] @deva[पुम्] + @deva[कोकिलः] = @deva[पुम्] + @deva[स्] + @deva[कोकिलः] = @deva[पुंस्कोकिलः], @deva[पुँस्कोकिलः] a male *kokila* bird; so @deva[पुंस्पुत्र]; and @deva[पुँस्पुत्र]; the son, a grown up man; but @deva[पुंक्षीरम्] milk for a man; @deva[पुंदासः] a man-servant. Exception @deva[पुंख्यानम्] the account of a man.

**(b)** @deva[न्] at the end of a word (except @deva[प्रशान्]) followed by @deva[च्], @deva[छ्]; @deva[ट्], @deva[ठ्]; or @deva[त्], @deva[थ्] which is itself followed by a vowel, a semi-vowel, a nasal or @deva[ह्], undergoes the same changes;[^3] e. g. @deva[शार्ङ्गिन्] + @deva[छिन्द्धि] = @deva[शार्ङ्गिन्] + @deva[स्] + @deva[छिन्द्धि] = @deva[शार्ङ्गिन्] + @deva[श्] + @deva[छिन्द्धि] (by @ref[28], sec. *a*) @deva[शार्ङ्गिंश्छिन्द्धि] and @deva[शार्ङ्गिँश्छिन्द्धि] Oh Kṛṣṇa, cut off; similarly @deva[चक्रिन्] + @deva[त्रायस्व] = @deva[चक्रिंस्त्रायस्व] and @deva[चक्रिँस्त्रायस्व]; save, Oh Kṛṣṇa; but @deva[हन्ति] as the @deva[न्] is not at the end of a word. @deva[सन्त्सरुः] a fine handle of a sword. @deva[प्रशान्तनोति] a good man spreads.

**(c)** The @deva[न्] of @deva[नॄन्] when followed by @deva[प्] undergoes this change optionally; @deva[नॄन्] + @deva[पाहि] = @deva[नॄन्पाहि], @deva[नॄंःपाहि], and @deva[नॄँःपाहि].

**(d)** The @deva[न्] of @deva[कान्] followed by @deva[कान्] also undergoes this change optionally; @deva[कान्] + @deva[कान्] = @deva[कांस्कान्], @deva[काँस्कान्] to whom? @deva[स्] or @deva[ष्] is substituted for the visarga when the following sets are combined: @deva[कः] + @deva[कः] = @deva[कस्कः]; similarly @deva[कौतस्कुतः] wherefrom, @deva[भ्रातुष्पुत्रः], @deva[सद्यस्कालः] the present time; @deva[सर्पिष्कुण्डिका] a ghee-pot; @deva[धनुष्कपालम्] a bowstaff; @deva[यजुष्पात्रम्] a sacrificial vessel; @deva[अयस्कान्त] a magnet; @deva[तमस्काण्डः] great darkness; @deva[अयस्काण्डः]; @deva[भास्करः]; @deva[अहस्करः] the sun.

---

[^1]: @deva[संपुंकानां सो वक्तव्यः] — Vārt.

[^2]: @deva[पुमः खय्यम्परे] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 6. @deva[ख्यात्रादेशो न] — Vārt.

[^3]: @deva[नश्छव्यप्रशान्] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 7.

rules.title: Insertion of @deva[च्] before @deva[छ्]
Visargasandhi: @deva[स्] and @deva[र्] to Visarga
rules.body:
## Visargasandhi

@deva[स्] at the end of a word followed by any letter or not, the @deva[ष्] of @deva[सजुष्] and @deva[र्] followed by a hard consonant or by nothing, are changed to a *Visarga*; as @deva[रामः पठति] Rāma reads. @deva[पितर्] = @deva[पितः] oh father. @deva[भ्रातुः कन्यका] a brother's daughter.

rules.title: Visarga before Hard Consonants: @deva[स्], @deva[ष्]
rules.body:
Visarga, followed by @deva[च्], @deva[छ्], @deva[ट्], @deva[ठ्], and @deva[त्], @deva[थ्], themselves not followed by a sibilant, is changed to @deva[स्];[^1] e. g. @deva[विष्णुस्त्राता] Viṣṇu, the protector: @deva[हरिश्चरति], Hari walks: @deva[रामष्टीकते] Rāma goes; (Vide @ref[28].); but @deva[कः त्सरुः] (as the @deva[त्] is followed by @deva[स्]); and optionally when followed by @deva[श्], @deva[ष्] or @deva[स्];[^2] @deva[रामः स्थाता] or @deva[रामस्स्थाता] Rāma who would stand; @deva[हरिःशेते] or @deva[हरिश्शेते] &c.

**(a)** Visarga, not belonging to an indeclinable is changed to @deva[स्] when preceded by @deva[अ], and to @deva[ष्], when preceded by @deva[इ] or @deva[उ], short or long and followed by the terminations @deva[पाश], @deva[कल्प], @deva[क] and @deva[काम्य];[^3] e. g. @deva[पयस्पाशम्] bad milk; @deva[यशस्कल्पम्] little short of fame: @deva[यशस्कम्] with fame; @deva[यशस्काम्यति] he desires fame; but @deva[प्रातःकल्पम्] almost dawn (where @deva[प्रातः] is an indec.); @deva[सर्पिष्पाशम्] bad ghee, @deva[सर्पिष्कल्पम्], @deva[सर्पिष्कम्], @deva[सर्पिष्काम्यति]. If the visarga, however, is a substitute for a final @deva[र्], it is not changed to @deva[स्] before @deva[काम्य];[^4] @deva[गीः काम्यति] speech desires.

**(b)** The Visarga of @deva[नमः] and @deva[पुरः] when prefixed as indeclinables to verbs beginning with @deva[क्] or @deva[ख्] and @deva[प्] or @deva[फ्] is optionally changed to @deva[स्] in the case of the former and necessarily in that of the latter;[^5] e. g. @deva[नमस्करोति] or @deva[नमःकरोति], @deva[पुरस्करोति] puts in the front; but @deva[पुरः प्रवेष्टव्याः] towns fit to be entered (as @deva[पुर्] is a noun).

**(c)** Visarga, preceded by @deva[इ] or @deva[उ] and not belonging to a termination, is changed to @deva[ष्] except in the case of @deva[मुहुः]; often, if followed by a hard consonant of the guttural or the labial class;[^6] @deva[निः] + @deva[प्रत्यूह] = @deva[निष्प्रत्यूहम्] without obstacle. @deva[आविष्कृतम्] disclosed; @deva[दुष्कृतम्] a bad action; but @deva[मुहुः कृतम्]; @deva[आग्निः करोति] as the Visarga is substituted for @deva[स्] a term. so @deva[मातुः कृपा] and not @deva[मातुष्कृपा]. @deva[भ्रातुष्पुत्रः] is an exception.

**(d)** @deva[तिरस्][^7] optionally retains its @deva[स्] when followed by @deva[क्], @deva[ख्], @deva[प्] or @deva[फ्]; @deva[तिरः करोति] or @deva[तिरस्करोति] hides or scorns

@deva[द्विः], @deva[त्रिः] and @deva[चतुः]; all of them adverbs showing frequency, change their Visarga to @deva[ष्] optionally under the same circumstances;[^8] @deva[द्विष्करोति] or @deva[द्विःकरोति] does twice; but @deva[चतुष्कपालम्] having four parts (where @deva[चतुः] is not an adverb).

**(e)** The ending @deva[इः] or @deva[उः] of a word changes its visarga to @deva[ष्] optionally under the same circumstances when the presence of the following word is necessary for the completion of the sense;[^9] @deva[सर्पिष्करोति] or @deva[सर्पिःकरोति] turns into ghee; @deva[धनुष्करोति] or @deva[धनुःकरोति] makes a bow; but @deva[तिष्ठतु सर्पिः पिब स्वमुकदम्], as there is no connection here between the words @deva[सर्पिः] and @deva[पिब].

And necessarily when at the end of the first member of a compound; as @deva[सर्पिष्कुण्डिका] a pot for clarified butter; but @deva[परमसर्पिः कुण्डिका] a big ghee-pot (as the word @deva[सर्पिः] is an *uttara pada*).

**(f)** Visarga coming after the @deva[अ] of a word other than an indeclinable and forming the first member of a compound is changed to @deva[स्] when followed by a derivative of the roots @deva[कृ], @deva[कम्], and by @deva[कंस], @deva[कुंभ], @deva[पाश], @deva[कुशा] and @deva[कर्णी];[^10] e. g. @deva[अयस्कारः] an iron-smith; @deva[अयस्कामः] one who desires iron; @deva[अयस्कंसम्] an iron pot; @deva[अयस्पात्रम्]; @deva[अयस्कुशा] a bridle; @deva[अयस्कर्णी] a kind of iron pot; but @deva[गीःकारः] Bṛhaspati; @deva[स्वःकामः] one desiring heaven (where @deva[स्वर्] is an indec.); @deva[यशः करोति] (as there is no comp.); and @deva[परमयशःकारः] producing great fame (as the word @deva[यशस्] is not the first member of the com.).

**(g)** The words @deva[अधः] and @deva[शिरः] change their visarga to @deva[स्] when followed by @deva[पद] under the same circumstances as those mentioned above;[^11] @deva[अधस्पदम्], @deva[शिरस्पदम्] but @deva[अधःपदं] when there is no comp.; @deva[परमशिरः पदम्] (as @deva[शिर] is the latter member @deva[उत्तरपद]).

---

[^1]: @deva[विसर्जनीयस्य सः। शर्परे विसर्जनीयः] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 34-35.

[^2]: @deva[वा शरि] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 36.

[^3]: @deva[सोऽपदादौ] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 38. @deva[पाशकल्पकाम्येष्विति वाच्यम्। अनव्ययस्येति वाच्यम्] Vārtikas. @deva[इणः षः] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 39.

[^4]: @deva[काम्ये रोरेवेति वाच्यम्] — Vārt.

[^5]: @deva[नमस्पुरसोर्गत्योः] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 40.

[^6]: @deva[इदुपधस्य चाप्रत्ययस्य] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 41.

[^7]: @deva[तिरसोऽन्यतरस्याम्] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 42.

[^8]: @deva[द्विस्त्रिश्चतुरिति कृत्वोऽर्थे] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 43.

[^9]: @deva[इसुसोः सामर्थ्ये। नित्यं समासेऽनुत्तरपदस्थस्य] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 44-45.

[^10]: @deva[अतः कृकमिकंसकुम्भपात्रकुशाकर्णीष्वनव्ययस्य] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 46.

[^11]: @deva[अधःशिरसी पदे] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 47.

rules.title: Visarga after Short @deva[अ] changed to @deva[उ]
rules.body: Visarga (substituted for @deva[स्] and not @deva[र्]) preceded by short @deva[अ] and followed by short @deva[अ] or a soft consonant is changed to @deva[उ]; @deva[शिवः] + @deva[अर्च्यः] = @deva[शिव] + @deva[उ] + @deva[अर्च्यः] = @deva[शिवो] + @deva[अर्च्यः] = @deva[शिवोर्च्यः] Śiva is adorable; (see @ref[25]); @deva[देवः] + @deva[वन्द्यः] = @deva[देवो वन्द्य] God should be saluted; but @deva[तिष्ठतु पय अ३ग्निदत्त] (where the @deva[अ] after @deva[पयः] is *pluta*); @deva[प्रातः] + @deva[अत्र] = @deva[प्रातरत्र] (for here the visarga is substituted for @deva[र्]); so @deva[प्रातर्गच्छ] &c.

rules.title: Visarga after @deva[आ]: Dropping and @deva[य्]
rules.body: Visarga preceded by @deva[आ] is dropped necessarily when followed by a soft consonant, and optionally when followed by a vowel; it is also optionally dropped when preceded by @deva[अ] and followed by a vowel except @deva[अ]; when it is not dropped it is changed to @deva[य्] in both these cases; @deva[देवाः] + @deva[नम्याः] = @deva[देवा नम्याः]; @deva[देवा] + @deva[इह] = @deva[देवा इह], @deva[देवायिह]।

rules.title: Visarga to @deva[र्] after Other Vowels; @deva[अहन्]; @deva[र्]/@deva[ढ्] before @deva[र्]/@deva[ढ्]
rules.body:
**(a)** Visarga, preceded by any vowel except @deva[अ] or @deva[आ] and followed by a vowel or soft consonant, is changed to @deva[र्]; @deva[हरिः] + @deva[जयति] = @deva[हरिर्जयति] Hari conquers; so @deva[भानुरुदेति] the sun rises; @deva[गौरागच्छति] a cow or bull comes.

*Exception*:—The Visarga of the particles @deva[भोः], @deva[भगोः] and @deva[अघोः] obeys @ref[48]; e. g. @deva[भो] + @deva[अच्युत] = @deva[भो अच्युत] or @deva[भोयच्युत] Oh Achyuta; @deva[भगो नमस्ते] Bhago! a bow to thee; @deva[अघो याहि] Oh you go.

**(b)** The @deva[न्] of @deva[अहन्], not followed by a declensional termination, is always changed to @deva[र्] but if followed by @deva[पति][^1] and other words such as @deva[गिर्], @deva[धुर्] &c. the change is optional and if by @deva[रूप] and @deva[रात्रि], visarga is substituted for it; @deva[अहः], @deva[अहरहः] day by day; @deva[अहःपतिः] or @deva[अहर्पतिः] the lord of the day, the sun; @deva[गीर्पतिः] or @deva[गीष्पतिः] Bṛhaspati; @deva[धूर्पतिः] or @deva[धूष्पतिः] a leader; but @deva[अहोभ्याम्] Inst. dual; @deva[अहोरूपम्] the form of the day @deva[गतमहो रात्रिरेषा]; @deva[अहोरात्रः] day and night; @deva[अहोरथन्तरम्] a protection of Sāman to be chanted by day.

**(c)** @deva[र्] or @deva[ढ्] followed by @deva[र्] or @deva[ढ्] respectively is dropped,[^2] and the preceding @deva[अ], @deva[इ] or @deva[उ] if short is made long; @deva[पुनर्] + @deva[रमते] = @deva[पुना रमते] sports again; @deva[हरिः] + @deva[रम्य] = @deva[हरिर्] + @deva[रम्यः] = @deva[हरी रम्यः] Hari is graceful; but @deva[वृढ्] + @deva[ढः] = @deva[वृढः] (form @deva[वृह्] + @deva[त]) p. p. of @deva[वृह्] to grow.

---

[^1]: @deva[अहरादीनां पत्यादिषु वा रेफः] — Vārt.

[^2]: @deva[रारि। ढ्लोपे पूर्वस्य दीर्घोऽणः] — Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 14. VI. 3. 111.

rules.title: Dropping @deva[स्] of @deva[सः]/@deva[एषः]
rules.body:
**(a)** The @deva[स्] of the nom. sing. of @deva[तद्] and @deva[एतद्] *mas.* is dropped before a consonant when they do not end in @deva[क] or are not used in a negative Tatpurusha;[^1] *e. g.* @deva[स शंभुः], @deva[एष विष्णुः]; but @deva[एषको रुद्रः] this Rudra; @deva[असोऽशिवः] that is not Śiva (a neg. Tat.); @deva[एषोऽत्र].

**(b)** Sometimes in poetry the @deva[स्] of @deva[सः] and @deva[एषः] is considered as not existing when followed by a vowel other than @deva[अ], so that the two vowels may combine in order to meet the exigencies of the metre;[^2] *e. g.* @deva[सेमानविड्ढि प्रभृतिं य ईशिषे] &c. Ṛg. II. 24. 1.

@deva[सैष दाशरथी रामः सैष राजा युधिष्ठिरः।]
@deva[सैष कर्णो महात्यागी सैष भीमो महाबलः॥]

---

[^1]: @deva[एतत्तदोः सुलोपोऽकोरनञ्समासे हलि] — Pāṇ. VI. 1. 132.

[^2]: @deva[सोऽचि लोपे चेत्पादपूरणम्] — Pāṇ. VI. 1. 134.

rules.title: Chapter III. Subanta or Declension
rules.body:
## Chapter III. Subanta or Declension

In the present chapter *Declension* or the inflection of nouns, substantive and adjective, is considered.

rules.title: Definition of Prātipadika (Crude Form)
rules.body: The crude form of a noun (any declinable word) not yet inflected is technically called a Prātipadika (@deva[प्रातिपदिक]).

rules.title: Three Genders of Nouns
rules.body: A noun has three genders: masculine gender (mas.), a feminine gender (fem.), and the neuter (neu.). The question about the determination of the gender of nouns will be considered in a separate chapter.

rules.title: Three Numbers: Singular, Dual, Plural
rules.body:
There are three numbers:—Singular (sing.), dual (du.) and plural (pl.). The singular number denotes one, the dual two and the plural three or more.[^1]

---

[^1]: @deva[द्व्येकयोर्द्विवचनैकवचने। बहुषु बहुवचनम्] — Pāṇ. I. 4. 22. 21.

rules.title: Eight Cases in Sanskrit
rules.body:
There are eight cases in each number:—Nominative (Nom. or N.), Vocative (Voc. or V.), Accusative (Acc. or A.) Instrumental (Ins. or I.), Dative (Dat. or D.), Ablative (Abl. or Ab.), Genitive (Gen. or G.), and Locative (Loc or L.). These express nearly all relations between words in a sentence.

**N. B.** These genders, numbers and cases will, for the sake of convenience, be denoted by their abbreviations enclosed into brackets after each.

rules.title: Sup: Technical Term for Case Terminations
rules.body:
Sup (@deva[सुप्])[^1] is the technical term for a case termination in Sanskrit. Declension consists in adding the case termination to the crude form or base.

---

[^1]: The general terminations as given by Pāṇini are—@deva[स्वौजसमौट्छष्टाभ्याम्भिस्ङेभ्याम्भ्यस्ङसिभ्याम्भ्यस्ङसोसाम्ङ्योस्सुप्] IV. 1. 2. i. e. Nom. @deva[सु औ जस्]; Acc. @deva[अम् औट् शस्]; Ins. @deva[टा भ्याम् भिस्]; Dat. @deva[ङे भ्याम् भ्यस्]; Ab. @deva[ङसि भ्याम् भ्यस्]; Gen. @deva[ङस् ओस् आम्]; Loc. @deva[ङि ओस् सुप्]. Some of these terminations, as in common with Pāṇini's system of nomenclature, have certain *Its* (servile letters) added or prefixed to them; *e. g.* @deva[उ] in @deva[सु], @deva[ज्] in @deva[जस्] &c. It will be easily seen that the term @deva[सुप्] is obtained by taking the first letter and the last *It* in the sūtra.

rules.body:
The following are the normal case-terminations:—

| | Mas. and Fem. | | | Neu. | | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| | Sing. | Dual | Plural | Sing. | Dual | Plural |
| N. V. | @deva[स्] | @deva[औ] | @deva[अस्] | N. A. @deva[म्] | @deva[ई] | @deva[इ] |
| A. | @deva[अम्] | ,, | ,, | V. | ,, | ,, |

rules.title: Vocative Case Explained
rules.body: The Vocative is considered to be a different aspect of the nom. and is identical with it in the dual and plural. It is, therefore, supposed to have no separate terminations of its own. In the sing. it sometimes coincides with the original stem, sometimes with the nom., at others, it differs from both.

rules.title: Two Classes of Declension
rules.body:
## Declension of Nouns and Adjectives

Declension is for the sake of convenience divided into two classes:—

I. BASES ENDING IN VOWELS.

II. BASES ENDING IN CONSONANTS.

rules.title: Declension of Adjectives; Vowel Bases
rules.body:
The declension of adjectives does not, in general, differ from that of substantives. It will not, therefore, be given here separately; the points of difference only will be noted.

## SECTION I.

## I. BASES ENDING IN VOWELS.

**Note:**—The variations and modifications, which the general terminations given above undergo when applied to several of the vowel bases, are so numerous, that it has been thought advisable not to notice them here, as being tedious, but simply to give the forms and leave the students to find them out for themselves. Every word declined here should be considered a model and words alike in form should be declined similarly to it.

rules.body:

rules.title: General Rule for @deva[अ]-Stems with Special Note on @deva[अह्]
rules.body:
Decline all nouns ending in @deva[अ] mas. and neu. similarly.

**(a)** The Loc. sing. of words ending in @deva[अह्] (substituted for @deva[अहन्] a day, at the end of a Tat. comp.) is optionally formed like that of nouns ending in @deva[न्]; e. g. @deva[व्यह्] has @deva[व्यहे], @deva[व्यहि] or @deva[व्यहनि]. So @deva[व्यहे], @deva[व्यहि] or @deva[व्यहनि] &c. see p. 73.

rules.title: Declension of @deva[आ]-Stems Masculine: @deva[गोपा] Paradigm
rules.body:

rules.title: @deva[आ]-Stem Compounds from Roots vs. Non-Root Compounds
rules.body:
Decline similarly @deva[विश्वपा] the protector of the world, @deva[शंखध्मा] a conch-shell-blower, @deva[सोमपा] one who quaffs the soma-juice, @deva[धूम्रपा] one who inhales smoke, @deva[बलदा] strength-giver, or Indra, and other comp. nouns derived from roots ending in @deva[आ].

**(a)** If the latter member be not a root the final @deva[आ] is not dropped; e. g. @deva[हाहा] name of a Gandharva, Acc. plu. @deva[हाहान्]; D. Ab. G. and L. sing. @deva[हाहै], @deva[हाहाः], @deva[हाहाः] and @deva[हाहे] respectively. The rest like @deva[गोपा].

rules.body: **Irregular bases:**—The Voc. sing. of @deva[अम्बा], @deva[अल्ला] and @deva[अक्का], all meaning 'a mother', is @deva[अम्ब], @deva[अल्ल] and @deva[अक्क] respectively.

rules.body: Several adjectives ending in @deva[अ] follow the declension of pronouns, for which see the chap. on pronouns.

rules.title: Compounds with @deva[पति] and @deva[प्रियत्रि]
rules.body: Compound nouns ending with @deva[पति] such as @deva[भूपति] &c. are declined like @deva[हरि] regularly. @deva[प्रियत्रि] (@deva[प्रियाः त्रयः यस्य यस्या वा]) is declined like @deva[हरि] mas. & @deva[मति] fem.; the Gen. plu. is optionally like that of @deva[त्रि]; @deva[परमत्रीणाम्], or @deva[°त्रयाणाम्].

rules.title: Patronymics: @deva[औडुलोमि] and @deva[गार्ग्य]
rules.body:
**Obs.** **(a)** @deva[औडुलोमि] a descendant of Uduloman (@deva[उडुलोम्नः अपत्यं पुमान्]) is declined like @deva[हरि] in the sing. and dual and like @deva[राम] in the plural, the original word @deva[उडुलोम] being substituted;[^1]

N. @deva[औडुलोमिः औडुलोमी], @deva[उडुलोमाः] &c.

**(b)** Words of similar derivation (see Pāṇ. II. 4. 62. 63. 65. 66 and IV. 1. 105) also substitute their originals in the plural, e. g. @deva[गर्गस्य अपत्यं गार्ग्यः] N. @deva[गार्ग्यः गार्ग्यौ गार्गाः] &c.

---

[^1]: From @deva[उडुलोमन्] name of a sage, + @deva[इञ्] (@deva[इ]) added @deva[अपत्यार्थे] by '@deva[बाह्वादिभ्यश्च]' Pāṇ. IV. 1. 96, the final @deva[न्] being dropped (Pāṇ. VI. 4. 144).

rules.title: Root Nouns in @deva[ई] and @deva[ऊ]: Multiple Paradigms
rules.body:
**§ 77.** Root nouns in @deva[ई] or @deva[ऊ] M. F. N.

Rule of *Sandhi*:—**(a)** The ending @deva[इ] or @deva[उ], short or long, of nouns derived from roots with the affix @deva[क्विप्] (o) and of @deva[भ्रू], is changed to @deva[इय्] or @deva[उव्] before the vowel terminations[^1]; the fem. nouns of this description are optionally declined like @deva[नदी] in the Da. Ab. Gen. and Loc. singulars and the Gen. plu.

**(b)** But if the ending @deva[इ] or @deva[उ] of a many-voweled noun having a root at the end be not preceded by a radical conjunct consonant or the root noun has a preposition termed @deva[गति] (e. g. as added to the root) or a word governed by the root preceding it, it is changed to @deva[य्] or @deva[व्], except in the case of @deva[सुधी] and nouns ending in @deva[भ्रू].[^2]

[^5]: @deva[ह्रस्वो नपुंसके प्रातिपदिकस्य] । Pāṇ. I. 2. 47. A *prātipadika* ending in a long vowel has a short vowel substituted for it when becoming neu.

rules.title: Agent Nouns in @deva[तृ]: @deva[धातृ] Paradigm
rules.body:
Nouns ending in @deva[ऋ] *mas. fem.* and *neu.*

Nouns derived from roots with the affix @deva[तृ] (@deva[तृच्] and @deva[तृन्] Pāṇ. III. 1. 133. and 2. 135), such as @deva[कर्तृ] a maker, &c. and the words @deva[स्वसृ] f, @deva[नप्तृ], @deva[नेष्टृ], @deva[क्षत्तृ], @deva[होतृ], @deva[पोतृ], and @deva[प्रशास्तृ] as also @deva[उद्गातृ][^1] change their @deva[ऋ] to @deva[आ] in the Nom. sing. and to @deva[आर्] in the first five inflections. The @deva[ऋ] is lengthened in the Acc. and Gen. pl. and changed to @deva[उर्] before the Ab. and Gen. sing.; the Voc. sing. ends in @deva[अर्].

@deva[धातृ] mas. the creator.

| N. | @deva[धाता] | @deva[धातारौ] | @deva[धातारः] |
| V. | @deva[धातः (र्)] | ,, | ,, |

| I. | @deva[धात्रा] | @deva[धातृभ्याम्] | @deva[धातृभिः] |

Decline similarly @deva[कर्तृ], @deva[नेतृ], @deva[नप्तृ], @deva[शास्तृ], @deva[उद्गातृ] &c.

@deva[धातृ] neu.

| | Sing. | Dual | Plural |
|---|---|---|---|

| V. | @deva[धात-तृ] | ,, | ,, |
| A. | @deva[धातृ] | ,, | ,, |

[^1]: @deva[अप्तृन्तृच्स्वसृनप्तृनेष्टृत्वष्टृक्षतृपोतृप्रशास्तॄणाम्] । Pāṇ. VI. 4. 11. @deva[उद्गातृशब्दस्य भवत्येव समर्थसूत्रे] '@deva[उद्गातारः]' @deva[इति भाष्यप्रयोगात्] । Sid. Kau.

rules.title: Kinship Terms in @deva[तृ]: @deva[पितृ] and @deva[मातृ]
rules.body:
Nouns expressive of relationship like @deva[पितृ] m. a father, @deva[मातृ] f. a mother, @deva[देवृ] m. a husband's brother, &c. with the exception of @deva[नप्तृ] a grandson, @deva[भर्तृ] a husband and @deva[स्वसृ] a sister, as also the words @deva[शंस्तृ] one who praises (Un. II. 92), @deva[नृ] a man (Un. II. 98) and @deva[सव्येष्टृ] a charioteer, do not change their @deva[ऋ] to @deva[आर्] in the N. dual and plural and Acc. sing. and dual; e. g.

@deva[पितृ]

| | Sing. | Dual | Plural |
|---|---|---|---|
| N. | @deva[पिता] | @deva[पितरौ] | @deva[पितरः] |
| V. | @deva[पितः (र्)] | ,, | ,, |
| A. | @deva[पितरम्] | ,, | @deva[पितॄन्] |

The rest like @deva[धातृ].

Decline similarly @deva[भ्रातृ], @deva[जामातृ], @deva[देवृ], @deva[शंस्तृ], @deva[सव्येष्टृ] and… @deva[नृ]. The Gen. plu. of @deva[नृ] is @deva[नृणाम्] or @deva[नॄणाम्][^1]

@deva[मातृ]

| | Sing. | Dual | Plural |
|---|---|---|---|
| N. | @deva[माता] | @deva[मातरौ] | @deva[मातरः] |
| V. | @deva[मातः (र्)] | ,, | ,, |
| A. | @deva[मातरम्] | ,, | @deva[मातॄः] |

The rest like @deva[स्वसृ].

Decline similarly @deva[यातृ] a husband's brother's wife, @deva[दुहितृ] a daughter, and @deva[ननान्दृ] or @deva[ननन्दृ][^2] a husband's sister.

---

[^1]: @deva[नृ च] । Pāṇ. VI. 4. 9. @deva[नृ इत्येतस्य नामि वा दीर्घः स्यात्] । Sid. Kau.

[^2]: @deva[नञि च नन्देः] । Un. II. 97 @deva[न नन्दति ननान्दा । इह वृद्धिर्नानुवर्तते इत्येके ।] '@deva[ननान्दा तु स्वसा पत्युर्ननन्दा नन्दिनी च सा]' @deva[इति शब्दार्णवः] । Sid. Kau.

rules.body:
The word @deva[क्रोष्टु] a jackal, is declined like a word ending in @deva[ऋ] necessary in the first five inflections and optionally before the vowel terminations beginning with the Inst. sing. except that of the Gen. plu.[^1] e. g.

**Obs.**—The word @deva[प्रियक्रोष्टु] *neu.* is declined like @deva[मधु] and optionally like @deva[क्रोष्टु] *mas.* before the vowel terminations from the I. sing.; e. g. D. sing. @deva[प्रियक्रोष्ट्रे-ष्टवे-ष्टुने].

---

[^1]: @deva[तृज्वत्क्रोष्टुः । विभाषा तृतीयादिष्वचि] । Pāṇ. VII. 1. 95, 97.

rules.title: Imitative @deva[ॠ] and @deva[ऌ] Stems: @deva[कॄ], @deva[गम्ऌ]
rules.body:
Words ending in @deva[ॠ] and @deva[ऌ].

There are no words ending in @deva[ॠ] or @deva[ऌ]; therefore, the imitative sounds of the roots @deva[कॄ] and @deva[तॄ] and @deva[गम्ऌ] and @deva[शक्ऌ] are taken to show what the forms of such words will be, if there be need to use such words.

@deva[कॄ] *m.*

| | Sing. | Dual | Plural |

| A. | @deva[किरम्], @deva[कॄम्] | ,, | @deva[किरः], @deva[कॄन्] |
| I. | @deva[किरा], @deva[क्रा] | @deva[कीर्भ्याम्], @deva[कॄभ्याम्] | @deva[कीर्भिः], @deva[कॄभिः] |
| D. | @deva[किरे], @deva[क्रे] | ,, | @deva[कीर्भ्यः], @deva[कॄभ्यः] |

| G. | ,, | @deva[किरोः], @deva[क्रोः] | @deva[किराम्], @deva[क्राम्] |

| N. | @deva[गमा] | @deva[गमलौ] | @deva[गमलः] |
| V. | @deva[गमल्] | ,, | ,, |
| A. | @deva[गमलम्] | ,, | @deva[गमॄन्] |
| I. | @deva[गम्ला] | @deva[गम्ऌभ्याम्] | @deva[गम्ऌभिः] |
| D. | @deva[गम्ले] | ,, | @deva[गम्ऌभ्यः] |
| Ab. | @deva[गमुल्] | ,, | ,, |
| G. | ,, | @deva[गम्लोः] | @deva[गमॄणाम्] |
| L. | @deva[गमलि] | ,, | @deva[गम्ऌषु] |

rules.title: Diphthong Stems @deva[ए] and @deva[ऐ]: @deva[से] and @deva[रै]
rules.body:
Words ending in @deva[ए] and @deva[ऐ].

Here simply the terminations should be added and *Sandhi* rules observed.

@deva[से] (@deva[सह इना कामेन वर्ततेऽसौ])

| | Sing. | Dual | Plural |
|---|---|---|---|
| N. | @deva[सेः] | @deva[सयौ] | @deva[सयः] |
| V. | @deva[से][^1] | ,, | ,, |
| A. | @deva[सयम्] | ,, | ,, |
| I. | @deva[सया] | @deva[सेभ्याम्] | @deva[सेभिः] |
| D. | @deva[सये] | ,, | @deva[सेभ्यः] |
| Ab. | @deva[सेः] | ,, | ,, |
| G. | ,, | @deva[सयोः] | @deva[सयाम्] |
| L. | @deva[सयि] | ,, | @deva[सेषु] |

Decline similarly @deva[स्मृते] (@deva[स्मृतः तत् इ. येन]) one who has thought of *Kāma*.

@deva[रै] *m. f.* wealth.

| | Sing. | Dual | Plural |
|---|---|---|---|
| N. V. | @deva[राः] | @deva[रायौ] | @deva[रायः] |
| A. | @deva[रायम्] | ,, | ,, |
| I. | @deva[राया] | @deva[राभ्याम्] | @deva[राभिः] |
| D. | @deva[राये] | ,, | @deva[राभ्यः] |
| Ab. | @deva[रायः] | ,, | ,, |
| G. | ,, | @deva[रायोः] | @deva[रायाम्] |
| L. | @deva[रायि] | ,, | @deva[रासु] |

The neu. @deva[प्ररै] (@deva[प्रकृष्टा रै यस्य]) changed to @deva[प्ररि] (by @deva[एच इग्घ्रस्वादेशे] Pāṇ. I. 1. 48. and I. 2. 47.) should be declined like @deva[वारि] except before the consonantal terminations, when it should be declined like @deva[रै] *m. f.*

| | Sing. | Dual | Plural |
|---|---|---|---|
| N. A. | @deva[प्ररि] | @deva[प्ररिणी] | @deva[प्ररीणि] |
| I. | @deva[प्ररिणा] | @deva[प्रराभ्याम्] | @deva[प्रराभिः] &c. |

---

[^1]: The Kau. does not specially mention this form. Just as it stops after giving the Nom. forms in the case of words like @deva[रै], @deva[गो], @deva[स्मृतो] &c., so does it do in the case of @deva[से] also, implying thereby that the Voc. forms of @deva[से] are also like the Nom. ones. But the Sutra @deva[एङ्ह्रस्वात्संबुद्धेः] Pāṇ. VI. 1. 69 (@deva[एङन्तात् ह्रस्वान्ताच्च अङ्गात् हल् लुप्यते सम्बुद्धेः चेत्]) (Kau.) seems to apply in the present case and by dropping the final @deva[स्] we get the form @deva[से].

rules.title: Diphthong Stems @deva[ओ] and @deva[औ]: @deva[गो] and @deva[ग्लौ]
rules.body:
## Words ending in @deva[ओ] and @deva[औ].

Vṛddhi (@deva[औ]) is substituted for the @deva[ओ] of words ending in @deva[ओ] in the first five inflections except the Acc. sing.; @deva[आ] is substituted for @deva[ओ] in the Acc. sing. and plural.[^1] Nouns ending in @deva[औ] are regularly declined.

rules.title: Introduction to Consonant-Ending Bases
rules.body:
## SECTION II.

## BASES ENDING IN CONSONANTS.

Bases ending in any of the first four letters of a class, and in @deva[ण्], @deva[र्], @deva[ल्], @deva[श्], @deva[ष्], @deva[स्] and @deva[ह्]. The declension of these bases consists, for the most part, in adding the general case terminations and observing the rules of sandhi.

rules.title: General Rules for Consonant-Ending Bases
rules.body:
**(a)** As a general rule the @deva[स्] of the nom. singular is dropped. If there be a conjunct consonant at the end of a word the first consonant only is retained.

**(b)** The final letter is changed to the first or third of its class when followed by nothing, to the third when followed by a soft consonant and first when followed by a hard consonant and remains unchanged before a vowel termination.

**(c)** @deva[न्] is prefixed to the @deva[इ] of the N. & Acc. plural in the case of neuter nouns ending in a consonant except a nasal or a semi-vowel; but not in the case of a noun derived from the frequentative base.
