**(c)**[^3] A word that has fewer syllables should be placed first and in case there are more words than one having an equal number of syllables, the one that has more short syllables should be placed first; e. g. @deva[शिवकेशवौ], @deva[ग्रीष्मवसन्तौ], @deva[कुशकाशम्], &c.; the names of seasons and stars, under this latter circumstance, should be arranged according to their astronomical order; as @deva[हेमन्तशिशिरवसन्ताः], @deva[कृत्तिकारोहिण्यौ], &c. Also a word of more important significance should precede others; as @deva[तापसपर्वतौ].

**(d)**[^4] Names of the four castes of men should be arranged according to their order, beginning from the highest and so should be the names of brothers beginning from the eldest; e. g. @deva[ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविट्शूद्राः]; @deva[युधिष्ठिरार्जुनौ].

---

[^1]: @deva[द्वंद्वे घि ।] Pāṇ. II. 2. 32. @deva[अनेकप्राप्तावेकत्र नियमोऽनियमः शेषे ।] Vārt.

[^2]: @deva[अजाद्यदन्तम् ।] Pāṇ. II. 2. 33.

[^3]: @deva[अल्पाच्तरम् ।] Pāṇ. II. 2. 34. @deva[लघ्वक्षरं पूर्वम् । ऋतुनक्षत्राणां समानाक्षराणामानुपूर्व्येण । अभ्यर्हितं च ।] Vārt.

[^4]: @deva[वर्णानामानुपूर्व्येण । भ्रातुर्ज्यायसः ।] Vārtikas on the above Sūtra.

rules.title: @deva[राजदन्तादि] and @deva[धर्मादि]: Reverse Order Exceptions
rules.body:
In the case of words of the @deva[राजदन्तादि] class that which ought to be placed first is placed last; while in the case of words of the @deva[धर्मादि] group (a sub-division of @deva[राजदन्तादि]) the rule is observed optionally;[^1] @deva[शूद्रार्यम्] a Śudra and an Arya, @deva[धर्मश्च अर्थश्च धर्मार्थौ] or @deva[अर्थधर्मौ]; so @deva[अर्थशब्दौ] or @deva[शब्दार्थौ], @deva[अर्थकामौ] or @deva[कामार्थौ], &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[राजदन्तादिषु परम् ।] Pāṇ. II. 2. 31. @deva[धर्मादिष्वनियमः ।] Vārt.

rules.title: Definition of Tatpurusha Compound
rules.body:
## II. TATPURUSHA OR THE DETERMINATIVE COMPOUNDS.

When a compound consists of two members and the first determines the sense of the other, that is called Tatpurusha.

rules.title: Six Varieties of Tatpurusha
rules.body: According to the grammatical nature of the first or attributive member the Tatpurusha is divided into six varieties:-(1) Tatpurusha proper or the Inflectional, (2) Nañ or the Negative Tatpurusha, (3) Karmadhāraya or the Appositional including 'Dwigu', (4-5) Prādi and Gati or the Prepositional compounds, and (6) Upapada. These are either nouns, adjectives or adverbs.

rules.title: Shortening of Feminine Vowels in Compounds
rules.body:
The final vowel of a feminine noun ending in any of the affixes @deva[आ], @deva[ई] or @deva[ऊ] and forming the second member of a compound used adjectively is shortened; the @deva[ओ] of @deva[गो] is changed to @deva[उ] under the same circumstances;[^1] e. g. @deva[प्राप्त + जीविका = प्राप्तजीविकः] (Tat.), @deva[अतिमालः] (Tat.); @deva[पञ्चगुः] something bought for five cows; @deva[बह्व्यो नाड्यो यस्मिन् बहुनाडिः] many-veined @deva[देहः] (Bah.); @deva[चित्रा गावो यस्य चित्रगुः] having variegated cows, &c.; but @deva[कल्याणपञ्चमीकः] as the @deva[ई] is not final.

**(a)** If the final @deva[ई] or @deva[ऊ] be not a fem. termination, it remains unchanged; @deva[सुष्ठु धीः सा सुधीः], @deva[बहुतन्त्रीर्धमनी].

---

[^1]: @deva[गोस्त्रियोरुपसर्जनस्य ।] Pāṇ. I. 2. 48.

rules.title: First Variety: Inflectional Tatpurusha
rules.body:
## 1 Tatpurusha.

The first variety consists of such Tatpurusha compounds as have the attributive member in any one of the oblique cases when dissolved. There are six sub-varieties of this corresponding to the six oblique cases.

rules.title: Accusative Tatpurusha
rules.body:
**(a)** A noun in the Accusative case is compounded with @deva[श्रित], @deva[अतीत], @deva[पतित], @deva[गत], @deva[अत्यस्त], @deva[प्राप्त], @deva[आपन्न], @deva[गमी], @deva[बुभुक्षु], and others;[^1] as @deva[कृष्णं श्रितः कृष्णश्रितः] one who has resorted to Kṛishṇa (as his refuge); @deva[दुःखमतीतः दुःखातीतः] one who has overcome pain; @deva[सुखं आपन्नः सुखापन्नः] one who has obtained happiness, @deva[ग्रामं गमी ग्रामगमी] going to a village, a passenger; @deva[अन्नं बुभुक्षुः अन्नबुभुक्षुः] &c.

**N. B.** @deva[प्राप्त] and @deva[आपन्न] may also be placed first; as @deva[प्राप्तो जीविकां प्राप्तजीविकः] or @deva[जीविकाप्राप्तः] one who has obtained livelihood; similarly @deva[आपन्नजीविकः] or @deva[जीविकापन्नः]; @deva[प्राप्तजीविका स्त्री], &c.

**(b)** A word expressive of the duration of an action or state is compounded with another expressive of the action or state, in the Accusative case;[^2] e. g. @deva[मुहूर्तं सुखं मुहूर्तसुखम्] 'happiness lasting for a moment'; @deva[संवत्सरं वासः संवत्सरवासः] 'residence for a year' &c.

**(c)** The word @deva[खट्वा] forms an Accusative Tatpurusha with a p. p. participle when censure is implied or contempt is to be shown;[^3] as @deva[खट्वाम् आरूढः खट्वारूढः] 'a silly fool'. cf. Bhatti. V. 10

**(d)** Sometimes a preposition or a word denoting a period of time may take the place of the Accusative;[^4] as @deva[सामिकृतं] 'half done;' @deva[मासप्रमितः] (@deva[प्रतिपच्चन्द्रः]) 'what marks the commencement of a month as the new moon.'

---

[^1]: @deva[द्वितीया श्रितातीतपतितगतात्यस्तप्राप्तापन्नैः ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 24. @deva[गम्यादीनामुपसंख्यानम् ।] Vārtika.

[^2]: @deva[अत्यन्तसंयोगे च ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 29.

[^3]: @deva[खट्वाक्षेपे ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 26.

[^4]: @deva[साभि । कालाः ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 27, 28.

rules.title: Instrumental Tatpurusha
rules.body:
A noun in the Instrumental may be compounded—

**(a)**[^1] with another expressive of an effect produced by what is denoted by the noun in the Instrumental case, and with @deva[अर्थ], as @deva[शङ्कुलया खण्डः शङ्कुलाखण्डः] severed by means of a knife; @deva[धान्येन अर्थः धान्यार्थः] wealth obtained by means of grain.

**(b)**[^2] with verbal derivatives when the Instrumental has the sense of the agent or the instrument or means of the action; as @deva[हरिणा त्रातः हरित्रातः] saved by Hari; @deva[नखैर्भिन्नः नखभिन्नः] torn with the nails &c.

**(c)** with the words[^3] @deva[पूर्व], @deva[सदृश], @deva[सम], @deva[ऊन] and words having the sense of @deva[ऊन], @deva[कलह], @deva[निपुण], @deva[मिश्र], @deva[श्लक्ष्ण] and @deva[अवर]; as @deva[मासेन पूर्वः मासपूर्वः]; @deva[मात्रा सदृशः मातृसदृशः] like his mother; @deva[पितृसमः] equal to his father; @deva[माषेण ऊनं माषोनं]; so @deva[माषविकल] (less by one māsha, a particular weight); @deva[वाचा कलहः वाक्कलहः] a quarrel (in words); @deva[आचारनिपुणः]; @deva[गुडमिश्रः]; @deva[आचारश्लक्ष्णः] 'thin by the discharge of religious duties'; @deva[मासेन अवरः मासावरः] 'younger by a month.'

**(d)**[^4] With another noun signifying an article of food or something eatable, the noun in the Instrumental case denoting some kind of condiment used to season it or another article of food mixed with it; as @deva[दध्ना ओदनः दध्योदनः] rice mixed with curds; @deva[गुडेन धानाः गुडधानाः] fried rice mixed with treacle.

**(e)** Sometimes @deva[स्वयं] may take the place of the Instrumental as @deva[स्वयंकृतः] done by one's self.

---

[^1]: @deva[तृतीया तत्कृतार्थेन गुणवचनेन ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 30.

[^2]: @deva[कर्तृकरणे कृता बहुलम् ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 32.

[^3]: @deva[पूर्वसदृशसमोनार्थकलहनिपुणमिश्रश्लक्ष्णैः ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 31.

[^4]: @deva[अन्नेन व्यञ्जनम् । भक्ष्येण मिश्रीकरणम् ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 34. 35.

rules.title: Aluk of Instrumental: Retaining Case Endings
rules.body:
Instances of the Aluk of the Instrumental[^1] (i. e. in which the noun in the Inst. does not drop its case term.)—@deva[अञ्जसा कृतम् अञ्जसाकृतम्] 'done honestly'; @deva[ओजसाकृतम्] 'done with might'; @deva[पुंसानुजः] 'one having an elder brother'; @deva[जनुषान्धः] 'blind from birth'; @deva[मनसागुप्ता], @deva[मनसाज्ञायी], when proper names, otherwise @deva[मनोगुप्ता], @deva[मनोज्ञायी], &c. @deva[आत्मन्] followed by an ordinal number retains its case ending; as @deva[आत्मना पञ्चम आत्मनापञ्चमः ।]

---

[^1]: @deva[ओजःसहोम्भस्तमसस्तृतीयाया ।] Pāṇ. VI. 3. 3. @deva[अञ्जस उपसंख्यानम् ।] Vārt.

rules.title: Dative Tatpurusha
rules.body:
A noun in the Dative is compounded[^1]—

**(a)** with another expressive of the material of which the thing expressed by the noun in the Dative case is made; as @deva[यूपाय दारु यूपदारु], 'wood for a sacrificial post.'

**(b)** and with the words @deva[अर्थ], @deva[बलि], @deva[हित], @deva[सुख] and @deva[रक्षित]. The compound with @deva[अर्थ] is a nityasamāsa and takes the gender and number of the noun it qualifies; @deva[द्विजाय अयं द्विजार्थः सूपः] broth for a Brāhmana; @deva[द्विजाय इयं द्विजार्था यवागूः] (water-gruel) @deva[द्विजाय इदं द्विजार्थं पयः]; @deva[भूतेभ्यो बलिः भूतबलिः] an offering to the bhūtas (certain created beings); @deva[गवे हितं गोहितम्] good for a cow; @deva[गवे सुखं गोसुखम्]; @deva[गवे रक्षितं गोरक्षितम्].

---

[^1]: @deva[चतुर्थी तदर्थार्थबलिहितसुखरक्षितैः ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 36.

rules.title: Aluk of Dative: Retaining Case Endings
rules.body: Instances of the Aluk of the Dat. @deva[परस्मैपदम्], @deva[परस्मैभाषा]; @deva[आत्मनेपदम्], @deva[आत्मनेभाषा].

rules.title: Ablative Tatpurusha
rules.body:
A noun in the Ablative case is compounded[^1]—

**(a)** with words expressive of fear or rather with the words @deva[भय], @deva[भीत], @deva[भीति] and @deva[भीः]; as @deva[चौराद् भयं चौरभयम्] fear from a thief; @deva[वृकाद् भीतः वृकभीतः] afraid of a wolf, &c.

**(b)** in a few cases with the words @deva[अपेत], @deva[अपोढ], @deva[मुक्त], @deva[पतित], and @deva[अपत्रस्त];[^2] as @deva[सुखादपेतः सुखापेतः] deprived of happiness; @deva[कल्पनाया अपोढः कल्पनापोढः] 'transcending thought' or 'a fool;' @deva[चक्रमुक्तः], @deva[स्वर्गपतितः] 'fallen from heaven, as a sinner'; @deva[तरङ्गापत्रस्तः] 'afraid of waves'.

**(c)** in the case of the words @deva[स्तोक] a little, @deva[अन्तिक] near, @deva[दूर] after, and words having the sense of these, and @deva[कृच्छ्र] a difficulty, there is an Aluk of the Ablative;[^3] as @deva[स्तोकाद् मुक्तः स्तोकान्मुक्तः]; @deva[अल्पान्मुक्तः]; @deva[अन्तिकादागतः]; @deva[अभ्याशादागतः]; @deva[दूरादागतः]; @deva[विप्रकृष्टादागतः]; @deva[कृच्छ्रादागतः ।]

---

[^1]: @deva[पञ्चमी भयेन ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 37. @deva[भयभीतभीतिभीभिरिति वाच्यम् ।] Vārtika.

[^2]: @deva[अपेतापोढमुक्तपतितापत्रस्तैरल्पशः ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 38.

[^3]: @deva[स्तोकान्तिकदूरार्थकृच्छ्राणि क्तेन ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 39.

rules.title: Genitive Tatpurusha: General Rule
rules.body: A noun in the Genitive may, as a general rule, be compounded with any other noun; @deva[राज्ञः पुरुषः राजपुरुषः] the king's man ( an officer or a servant ).

rules.title: Restrictions on Genitive Compounds
rules.body:
**(a)** It is not compounded with verbal derivatives[^1] ending in @deva[तृ] and @deva[अक] and denoting the agent of the action; @deva[अपां स्रष्टा] and not @deva[अप्स्रष्टा]; @deva[घटस्य कर्ता], @deva[ओदनस्य पाचकः] &c.; but @deva[इक्षूणां भक्षणम् इक्षुभक्षिका] as the @deva[अक] here does not denote the agent.

**Exception**[^2]:—But a compound is allowed in the case of the words @deva[याजक] one who employs as sacrificing priests, @deva[पूजक], @deva[परिचारक], @deva[परिवेषक] a waiter at meals, @deva[स्नापक] a servant who bathes his master or brings bathing water for him, @deva[अध्यापक], @deva[उत्सादक] one who destroys, @deva[होतृ], @deva[भर्तृ], when it does not mean 'a holder,' and others not very important: @deva[ब्राह्मणयाजकः], @deva[देवपूजकः], @deva[राजपरिचारकः] &c.; @deva[अग्निहोता], @deva[भूमर्ता], &c. but @deva[वज्रस्य भर्ता] 'the thunder-bolt-bearer'.

**(b)**[^3] A specific Genitive (i. e. from which a singling out is made) is not compounded with any other words, as @deva[नृणां द्विजः श्रेष्ठः]

**(c)**[^4] A noun in the Genitive is not compounded with ordinal numbers, words denoting qualities, words implying satisfaction, present participles, past participles meaning 'honoured or approved of' or showing the place of the act, verbal indeclinables and verbal nouns ending in @deva[तव्य]; e. g. @deva[सतां षष्ठः], @deva[ब्राह्मणस्य शुक्लाः] (@deva[दन्ताः]); @deva[काकस्य कार्ष्ण्यम्]; @deva[फलानां सुहितः] 'satisfied with fruits' (an Inst. Tat. is, of course, allowed in these cases); @deva[द्विजस्य कुर्वन् कुर्वाणो वा किंकरः], @deva[सतां मतः] esteemed by the good; @deva[राज्ञां पूजितः]; @deva[इदमेषां आसितं] (place of sitting) @deva[गतं भुक्तं वा]; @deva[ब्राह्मणस्य कृत्वा], @deva[नरस्य कर्तव्यम्] &c.

**N. B.** Compounds like @deva[राजपूजितः], @deva[राजमतः], &c. ought to be considered as Instrumental Tatpurushas.

**Exceptions.**

**(1)** If the word denoting a quality ends in @deva[तर] it does combine with a noun in the Genitive, and the @deva[तर] is dropped; @deva[सर्वेषां श्वेततरः सर्वश्वेतः] whiter than all others; similarly @deva[सर्वेषां महत्तरः सर्वमहान्] &c.

**(2)**[^5] The words @deva[द्वितीय], @deva[तृतीय], @deva[चतुर्थ] and @deva[तुर्य] are compounded with nouns signifying the whole of which they are parts, and are optionally placed first, @deva[द्वितीयं भिक्षायाः द्वितीयभिक्षा], @deva[भिक्षाद्वितीयम्] half of the quantity of alms; but @deva[द्वितीयं भिक्षायाः] (begging alms a second time) @deva[भिक्षुकस्य].

**Note.**—Compounds like @deva[द्वितीयभिक्षा], @deva[पूर्वकायः] (see further on) &c. are not strictly Gen. Tat. as the case of the first word determines the name, but mere Tat.; some call these Nom. Tat. (@deva[प्रथामतत्पुरुष]).

**(a)**[^6] A noun in the Genitive, used as an object in a sentence, when the agent and object of the action denoted by the nouns formed by kṛit affixes are both used, is not compounded; as @deva[आश्चर्यो गवां दोहोऽगोपेन] 'the milking of cows by one, not a cowherd, is a wonder.'

---

[^1]: @deva[तृजकाभ्यां कर्तरि ।] Pāṇ. II. 2. 15.

[^2]: @deva[याजकादिभिश्च ।] Pāṇ. II. 2. 9.

[^3]: @deva[न निर्धारणे ।] Pāṇ. II. 2. 10.

[^4]: @deva[पूरणगुणसुहितार्थसद्व्ययतव्यसमानाधिकरणेन । क्तेन च पूजायाम् अधिकरणवाचिना च ।] Pāṇ. II. 2. 11-13. The prohibition with respect to a word expressive of a quality (@deva[गुण]) is not obligatory, remarks Dikshita; as Pāṇ. himself uses such compounds as @deva[संज्ञाप्रमाणत्व] &c. Hence compounds like @deva[अर्थगौरवम्], @deva[बुद्धिमान्यम्], &c. are justified (@deva[अनित्योयं गुणेन निषेधः तदशिष्यं संज्ञाप्रमाणत्वादित्यादिनिर्देशात् । तेनार्थगौरवं बुद्धिमान्यमित्यादि सिद्धम् ।]).

[^5]: @deva[द्वितीयतृतीयचतुर्थतुर्याण्यन्यतरस्याम् ।] Pāṇ. II. 2. 3.

[^6]: @deva[कर्मणि च ।] Pāṇ. II. 2. 14.

rules.title: Genitive Compounds with @deva[पूर्व], @deva[अपर], @deva[अधर], @deva[उत्तर], @deva[अर्ध]
rules.body:
[^1]@deva[पूर्व], @deva[अपर], @deva[अधर], @deva[उत्तर] and @deva[अर्ध] n. are compounded with nouns in the Genitive expressive of the whole and are placed first; e. g. @deva[पूर्वं कायस्य पूर्वकायः] the forepart of the body; @deva[अपरकायः] @deva[अधरकायः] &c. @deva[अर्धं पिप्पल्याः अर्धपिप्पली]; but @deva[ग्रामार्धः] as (@deva[अर्ध] is mas. here).

**N. B.** In order that the above rule should hold the noun expressive of the whole must denote a single object; hence @deva[पूर्वः] the first @deva[छात्राणां] among pupils, @deva[अर्धं पिप्पलीनाम्] half of a number of pippalis &c. and not @deva[पूर्वछात्रः] &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[पूर्वापराधरोत्तरमेकदेशिनैकाधिकरणे । अर्धं नपुंसकम् ।] Pāṇ. II. 2. 1, 2.

rules.title: Parts Compounded with Time Periods
rules.body: A word expressive of a part is compounded with another signifying a period of time and is placed first; @deva[मध्यं अह्नः] @deva[मध्याह्नः] mid-day; @deva[सायाह्नः]; @deva[मध्यरात्रं] &c.

rules.title: Time Elapsed Since Occurrence
rules.body:
[^1]A word expressive of a period of time that has passed since a certain occurrence is compounded with another expressive of the occurrence; as @deva[मासो जातस्त यस्य स मासजातः] 'one since whose birth a month has elapsed'; so @deva[द्व्यहजातः]; @deva[संवत्सरमृतः] &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[कालाः परिमाणिना ।] Pāṇ. II. 2. 5.

rules.title: Aluk of Genitive: Retaining Case Endings
rules.body:
[^1]Instances of the Aluk of the Gen. The noun in the Genitive may retain its case ending—

**(a)** when reproach is to be implied; as @deva[चौरस्यकुलम्], but @deva[ब्राह्मणकुलम्]. Also when @deva[देवानां] is followed by @deva[प्रिय] and the whole means a fool; otherwise @deva[देवप्रियः].

**(b)** when the words @deva[वाच्], @deva[दिश्] and @deva[पश्यत्] are followed by @deva[युक्ति], @deva[दण्ड] and @deva[हर] respectively; as @deva[वाचोयुक्तिः] 'skilful speech;' @deva[दिशोदण्डः] 'a particular appearance of stars in the shape of a staff in the sky,' @deva[पश्यतोहरः] 'one who robs another in his very presence while he is looking on,' hence 'a goldsmith, a rogue.'

**(c)** in the following cases:—@deva[दिवोदासः] 'a king of Kāshi,' @deva[दिवस्पतिः] 'Indra,' @deva[वाचस्पतिः] lord of speech, Brihaspati; @deva[शुनःशेपः], @deva[शुनःपुच्छः] and @deva[शुनोलाङ्गूलः] 'sons of Ajigarta.'

**(d)** and optionally when followed by @deva[पुत्र] and censure is implied; @deva[दास्याः पुत्रः] or @deva[दासीपुत्रः] a bastard, a knave; but @deva[ब्राह्मणीपुत्रः].

**(e)**[^2] When a word ending in @deva[ऋ] is compounded with another and there is the relation by blood or some kind of learning, the aluk is necessary; and optional when it is followed by @deva[स्वसृ] and @deva[पति]. The initial @deva[स] of @deva[स्वसृ] is optionally changed to @deva[ष] when preceded by @deva[मातृ] or @deva[पितृ] and when there is aluk, and necessarily when there is no aluk in a compound; e. g. @deva[होतुःपुत्रः], @deva[होतुरन्तेवासी], a pupil of the hotri; @deva[मातुःस्वसा], or @deva[मातुःष्वसा] and @deva[मातृष्वसा]; so @deva[पितुःस्वसा], &c. (but @deva[मातुः स्वसा], @deva[पितुः स्वसा] when uncompounded); @deva[स्वसृपतिः] or @deva[स्वसुःपतिः]; but @deva[होतृधनम्].

---

[^1]: @deva[षष्ठ्या आक्रोशे ।] Pāṇ. VI. 3. 21. @deva[देवानांप्रिय इति च मूर्खे । वाग्दिक्पश्यद्भ्यो युक्तिदण्डहरेषु । शेपपुच्छलाङ्गूलेषु शुनः । दिवश्च दासे ।] Vārtikas. '@deva[पुत्रेन्यतरस्याम्]' Pāṇ. VI. 3. 22.

[^2]: @deva[ऋतो विद्यायोनिसम्बन्धेभ्यः । विभाषा स्वसृपत्योः ।] Pāṇ. VI. 3. 23. 24; @deva[मातुःपितृभ्यामन्यतरस्याम् । मातृपितृभ्यां स्वसा ।] Pāṇ. VIII. 3. 84, 85.

rules.title: Locative Tatpurusha
rules.body:
A noun in the Locative is compounded—

**(a)**[^1] with @deva[शौण्ड], @deva[धूर्त], @deva[कितव] a rogue, @deva[प्रवीण], @deva[संवीत] adorned, invested with, @deva[अन्तर], @deva[आधि], @deva[पटु], @deva[पण्डित], @deva[कुशल], @deva[चपल], @deva[निपुण], @deva[सिद्ध], @deva[शुष्क], @deva[पक्व], and @deva[बन्ध]; as @deva[अक्षेषु शौण्डः अक्षशौण्डः] skilled in dice; @deva[ईश्वरे अधि ईश्वराधीनः] dependent on God (when compounded the affix @deva[ख] i. e. @deva[ईन] is compulsory; so the compounded form is always with @deva[अधीन]); @deva[आतपशुष्कः] dried in the sun; @deva[स्थालीपक्वः] cooked in a pot; @deva[चक्रबन्धः] a kind of poetic composition; &c.

**(b)**[^2] with words meaning a 'crow' when contempt is implied; @deva[तीर्थे ध्वाङ्क्ष इव तीर्थध्वाङ्क्षः] said in contempt of one who is very greedy; so @deva[तीर्थकाकः]; similarly @deva[नगरकाकः]—@deva[वायसः] &c. &c.

There are a few Loc. Tat. compounds given in the list @deva[पात्रेसमितादि] having a similar sense; e. g. @deva[कूपे मण्डूक इव कूपमण्डूकः] a well-abiding frog i. e. one who knows nothing of the world outside the pale of his own village; so @deva[कुंभ-उदपान-मण्डूकः]; @deva[उदुम्बरकृमिः-मशकः] lit. an insect in the fruit of the Udumbara tree; metaphorically it means the same as @deva[कूपमण्डूकः]; @deva[कूपकच्छपः] &c. In some cases there is an aluk of the Loc.; as @deva[गेहेशूरः] 'a boasting coward', @deva[गेहेव्याडः] 'a braggadocio'; @deva[गेहेनर्दी] 'a house-hero', 'a carpet knight', @deva[पात्रेकुशलः] 'clever in eating only' i. e. 'a good-for-nothing fellow'; @deva[पात्रेसमिताः]; @deva[गोष्ठेशूरः]; @deva[गोष्ठेविजयी]; @deva[गेहेधृष्टः], &c.

**Note:**—Words of this class do not enter into further combination with other words.

**(c)**[^3] with another, when they both imply a name (@deva[संज्ञा]); there is an aluk of the Loc. term when the noun ends in a consonant or @deva[अ]; as @deva[अरण्येतिलकाः] lit. 'wild sesamum yielding no oil, hence anything not answering to one's expectations;' similarly @deva[वनेकसेरुकाः]; @deva[स्वचिसारः] 'a bamboo' (also @deva[त्वक्सारः], vide Si. IV. 61.). These compounds are nitya (obligatory) as remarked by Bhaṭṭoji (@deva[वाक्येन संज्ञानवगमान्नित्यसमासोयम्]).

**(d)** with potential p. participles in @deva[य] implying an obligation; @deva[मासेदेयं] (@deva[ऋणम्]); @deva[पूर्वाह्णगेयं] (@deva[साम]); the aluk by @ref[217] (b) below.

**(e)**[^4] with p. p. participles when it expresses a part of the day or night; @deva[तत्र] may take the place of the Loc.; as @deva[पूर्वाह्णे कृतं पूर्वाह्णकृतम्]; @deva[अपररात्रकृतम्]: @deva[तत्रभुक्तम्] &c; but @deva[अह्नि दृष्टं]; and with the p. p. participles when reproach is implied, with an aluk of the Loc.; as '@deva[अवतसेनकुलस्थितं तवैतत्]' 'this thy action is similar to that of a mungoose on the hot ground.' @deva[अवतसेनकुलस्थितं] is used to express the inconstancy of a person.

---

[^1]: @deva[सप्तमी शौण्डैः । सिद्धशुष्कपक्वबन्धैश्च ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 40, 41.

[^2]: @deva[ध्वाङ्क्षेण क्षेपे । पात्रेसमितादयश्च ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 42, 48. @deva[चकारोऽवधारणार्थः । तेनैषां समासान्तरे घटकतया प्रवेशो न ।] Sid. Kau.

[^3]: @deva[संज्ञायाम् । हलदन्तात्सप्तम्याः संज्ञायाम् । गवियुधिभ्यां स्थिरः ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 44. VI. 3. 9. VIII. 3. 9. 5.

[^4]: @deva[क्तेनाहोरात्रावयवाः । तत्र । क्षेपे ।] Pāṇ. II. 2. 45-47.

rules.title: Additional Aluk Cases of Locative
rules.body:
Additional instances of the aluk of the Loc.

**(a)** Aluk is necessary in the case of the words—(1) @deva[गो] and @deva[युध्] followed by @deva[स्थिर], as @deva[गविष्ठिरः], stationary in the sky, @deva[युधिष्ठिरः] firm in battle; (2) @deva[हृद्] and @deva[दिव्] followed by @deva[स्पृश्]; @deva[हृदिस्पृक्], @deva[दिविस्पृक्] (@deva[हृदयं दिवं च स्पृशतीति]); (3) @deva[अन्त] and @deva[मध्य] followed by @deva[गुरु]; @deva[मध्येगुरुः], @deva[अन्तेगुरुः] and (4) words expressive of parts of the body except @deva[मूर्धन्] and @deva[मस्तक] and not followed by @deva[काम]; @deva[कण्ठेकालः], @deva[उरसिलोमा] (having the hair on the breast: Bah.), but @deva[मूर्ध-मस्तक-शिखः], @deva[मुखे कामो अस्य मुखकामः].

**(b)**[^1] When a noun in the Loc. is compounded with a verbal derivative and the whole is a name, aluk takes place in most cases; e. g. @deva[स्तम्बेरमः] (@deva[स्तम्बे] a kind of grass @deva[रमते असौ]) an elephant; @deva[कर्णेजपः] one who whispers into the ear, a spy; @deva[खेचरः] a heavenly being; @deva[पंकेरुहं] a lotus; @deva[कुशेशयम्], @deva[जलेशयः] a fish; but @deva[कुरुचरः], @deva[सरसिजं] or @deva[सरोजम्] &c.

**(c)** There is optional aluk of the Loc. of a word expressive of time when compounded with @deva[काल] and words ending in the affixed @deva[तर], @deva[तम] and @deva[तन]; @deva[पूर्वाह्ण-ह्णे-काले]; @deva[पूर्वाह्ण-ह्णे-तरे] &c. @deva[पूर्वाह्ण-ह्णे तने].

**(d)**[^2] When the compound is not a name, aluk is necessary when @deva[ज] comes after @deva[प्रावृद्], @deva[शरद्], @deva[काल] and @deva[दिव्]; and optional when it comes after @deva[वर्ष], @deva[क्षर], @deva[शर] and @deva[वर]; as @deva[प्रावृषि-शरदि-काले-दिवि-जः]; @deva[वर्षेजः] or @deva[वर्षजः] produced in the rainy season, &c.

**Exceptions**[^3]:—No aluk takes place in the case of verbal derivatives ending in @deva[इन्] and the words @deva[सिद्ध], @deva[बद्ध], and @deva[स्थ] in the ordinary language; as @deva[स्थण्डिलशायी] 'an ascetic,' @deva[साङ्काश्यसिद्धः]; @deva[चक्रबद्धः]; @deva[समस्थः]; but @deva[कृष्णोऽस्याखरेष्ठः] &c.

**(e)**[^4] When a noun in the Loc. case ending in @deva[अ] or a consonant and not denoting time is compounded with @deva[शय], @deva[वास] and @deva[वासिन्] and with @deva[बन्ध] aluk is optional; @deva[खे-खशयः], @deva[ग्रामे-मवासः], @deva[ग्रामे-मवासी], @deva[हस्ते-स्तबन्धः], but @deva[भूमिशयः], @deva[गुप्तिबन्धः] &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[तत्पुरुषे कृति बहुलम् ।] Pāṇ. VI. 3. 14.

[^2]: @deva[प्रावृद्शरद्कालदिवां जे । विभाषा वर्षक्षरशरवरात् ।] Pāṇ. VI. 3. 15. 16.

[^3]: @deva[नेन्सिद्धबध्नातिषु च । स्थे च भाषायाम् ।] Pāṇ. VI. 3. 19. 20.

[^4]: @deva[बन्धे च विभाषा । शयवासवासिष्वकालात् ।] Pāṇ. VI. 3. 13. 18.

rules.title: Nañ or Negative Tatpurusha: Definition
rules.body:
## 2. Nañ or the Negative Tatpurusha.

**(a)** The negative particle @deva[न] changed to @deva[अ] before a consonant and @deva[अन्] before a vowel, may be compounded with any noun to form the Negative-Tatpurusha;[^1] as @deva[न ब्राह्मणः अब्राह्मणः], one not a Brāhmaṇa; @deva[न अश्वः अनश्वः], @deva[असत्], non-existent, or not good, &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[नञ् ।] Pāṇ. II. 2. 6. @deva[न लोपो नञः । तस्मान्नुडचि ।] Pāṇ. VI. 3, 73. 74.

rules.title: Exceptions to @deva[न] → @deva[अ]/@deva[अन्] Change
rules.body:
The @deva[न] is not changed to @deva[अ] or @deva[अन्] in the following cases[^1]:—@deva[नभ्राट्] 'that which does not shine,' 'a cloud;' @deva[नपात्] (pre. p.) 'one who does not protect;' @deva[नवेदाः] 'one who does not know;' @deva[नासत्याः] [ @deva[न सत्याः असत्याः न असत्याः नासत्याः][^2] ] the two Aswins, the physicians of the gods. @deva[नमुचिः] [ @deva[न मुञ्चतीति] ] name of a demon slain by Indra; @deva[नकुलः] [ @deva[न कुलमस्य], for the mungoose is supposed to belong to no particular species of animals ]; @deva[नखं] [ @deva[न खमस्य] that which leaves no cavity, or does not go to heaven being burnt down with the dead body ]; @deva[नपुंसकं] [ @deva[न स्त्री पुमान्] ]; @deva[नक्षत्रं] [ @deva[न क्षरतीति] ] that which does not move from its proper place, hence a star; @deva[नक्रः] [ @deva[न क्रामतीति] that which does not go far off from water ]; @deva[नाकः] [ @deva[न कं अकं न अकं अस्मिन्] ]; @deva[नग] when it does not qualify an animal retains its @deva[न] optionally as @deva[नगः] or @deva[अगः] 'a mountain or a tree;' but @deva[अगः वृषलः] 'a Sudra that cannot move.'

**N. B.** It should be noted that some of these are Bahuvrihi compounds.

---

[^1]: @deva[नभ्राण्नपान्नवेदानासत्यानमुचिनकुलनखनपुंसकनक्षत्रनक्रनाकेषु प्रकृत्या ।] Pāṇ. VI. 3. 75. @deva[नगोऽप्राणिष्वन्यतरस्याम् ।] Pāṇ. VI. 3. 77.

[^2]: @deva[अत्र बहुवचनमविवक्षितं] (is not the point) @deva[तेन 'नासत्यावश्विनौ दस्रौ' इति सिद्धम् ।] Tatvabodhinī.

rules.title: Definition of Karmadhāraya
rules.body:
## 3. KARMADHĀ'RAYA OR THE APPOSITIONAL COMPOUNDS.

Panini defines a 'Karmadhāraya' as @deva[समानाधिकरणः तत्पुरुषः][^1] or Tatpurusha both the members of which are in the same case relation i. e. have the same case when dissolved.

**N. B.** The difference between the Tatpurusha proper and Karmadhāraya is this:—In the case of the former the attributive member has one of the oblique cases when dissolved, while in the case of the latter it is in apposition to the other member. It may thus be a noun or an adjective qualifying the other member.

---

[^1]: @deva[तत्पुरुषः समानाधिकरणः कर्मधारयः ।] Pāṇ. I. 2. 42.

rules.title: Karmadhāraya with Standards of Comparison
rules.body:
**(a)**[^1] A word expressive of the standard of comparison (@deva[उपमान]) may be compounded in a Karmadhāraya with another denoting the common quality or ground of comparison; as @deva[घन इव श्यामः घनश्यामः] dark like a cloud. Such compounds are called @deva[उपमानपूर्वपदकर्मधारय].

**(b)**[^2] Similarly a noun denoting the person or thing compared (@deva[उपमेय]) may be compounded with words indicative of excellence, such as @deva[व्याघ्र],[^3] @deva[सिंह], @deva[चन्द्र], @deva[कमल], &c. no mention of the common attribute (of similarity) being made; as @deva[पुरुषो व्याघ्र एव पुरुषव्याघ्रः] a man like a tiger (i. e. as bold as a tiger); @deva[मुखं चन्द्र इव मुखचन्द्रः] a moon-like face i. e. as delightful as the moon; @deva[मुखं कमलमिव मुखकमलम्] &c.; these are called @deva[उपमानोत्तरपदकर्मधारय].

**Note. 1.**—The difference between the two is this:—In the former the common quality of comparison is actually expressed; while in the latter it is left to be understood; in fact if it be expressed there can be no compound; as @deva[पुरुषः व्याघ्र इव शूरः ।]

**Note. 2.**—The above Karmadhārayas may be dissolved as @deva[मुखमेव चन्द्रः मुखचन्द्रः], @deva[मुखमेव कमलं मुखकमलम्], &c. Dissolved in either way there will be no difference in the formation of the compounds; but there will be difference both in the meaning and in the metaphor. In one case prominence will be given to @deva[चन्द्र] or the moon and the figure will be 'upamā (a simile),' while in the other to @deva[मुख] or the face in which case the figure will be 'Rūpaka.'[^4] Compounds like @deva[पाद एवपद्मं पादपद्मम्], @deva[विद्या एव धनं विद्याधनं], &c. are termed @deva[अवधारणापूर्वपदकर्मधारय]s.

---

[^1]: @deva[उपमानानि सामान्यवचनैः ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 55.

[^2]: @deva[उपमितं व्याघ्रादिभिः सामान्याप्रयोगे ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 56.

[^3]: All these words are included under what is called the group of @deva[व्याघ्र]. The more important of these words are @deva[व्याघ्र], @deva[सिंह], @deva[ऋक्ष], @deva[ऋषभ], @deva[चन्दन], @deva[वृक], @deva[वृष], @deva[वराह], @deva[हस्तिन्], @deva[रुरु], @deva[पृषत्], @deva[पुण्डरीक], &c.; @deva[चन्द्र], @deva[पद्म], @deva[कमल], @deva[किसलय], &c.; cf. @deva[स्युरुत्तरपदे व्याघ्रपुंगवर्षभकुञ्जराः । सिंहशार्दूलनागाद्याः पुंसि श्रेष्ठार्थगोचराः ॥] Amara III. 1. 59.

[^4]: So when the common attribute is applicable in its expressed (@deva[वाच्य]) sense to the @deva[उपमेय] as in @deva[मुखपद्मं सहास्यं] dissolve the comp. as @deva[मुखं पद्ममिव] and when to the @deva[उपमान] as in @deva[मुखपद्मं विकसितं] dissolve as @deva[मुखमेव पद्मम्].

rules.title: Adjective-Noun Compounds (@deva[विशेषणपूर्वपदकर्मधारय])
rules.body:
An adjective may be compounded with the noun it qualifies in most cases[^1] as @deva[नीलं च तदुत्पलं च नीलोत्पलं], a blue lotus &c.; @deva[कृष्णश्चासौ सर्पश्च कृष्णसर्पः] where the comp. is necessary; but @deva[जामदग्न्यो रामः ।] Such compounds are called @deva[विशेषणपूर्वपदकर्मधारय]s.

As a general rule in such compounds the qualifying word is placed first; but there are several exceptions which are given below.

**(a)**[^2] The qualified word is placed first and is always of the mas. gender if it denotes a class or species, when compounded with certain adjectives; e. g. @deva[इभयुवतिः] 'a young female elephant', @deva[अग्निस्तोकः] 'a small fire', @deva[उदश्वित्कतिपयम्] 'butter-milk mixed with a little water', @deva[गोगृष्टिः] 'a cow that has brought forth a calf for the first time', @deva[गोधेनुः] 'a milch-cow (@deva[नवप्रसूतिका])'; @deva[गोवशा] 'a barren cow', @deva[गोवेहत्] (@deva[गर्भघातिनी गौः]), @deva[गोबष्कयणी] 'a cow whose calf is one year old,' @deva[कठश्रोत्रियः] 'an agnihotrin Brāhmaṇa of the Kaṭha branch of the Yajurveda,' @deva[कठाध्यापकः] 'a teacher of the Kaṭha branch,'[^3] @deva[गो-मतल्लिका-मचर्चिका-प्रकाण्डं] (also mas. according to some)—@deva[उद्धः] (@deva[गवोद्ध])-@deva[तल्लज] 'an excellent cow'. The last mentioned five words, all of which denote excellence, retain their own gender invariably; as @deva[ब्राह्मणमतल्लिका] 'an eminent Brāhmaṇa' &c.; but @deva[कुमारी मतल्लिका], as no class is meant here.

**(b)**[^4] The words @deva[कडार], @deva[खञ्ज], @deva[खोड] lame, @deva[काण], @deva[कुण्ठ] blunt, dull, @deva[खलति] bald-headed, @deva[गौर], @deva[वृद्ध], @deva[भिक्षुक] @deva[पिंग], @deva[पिंगल], @deva[तनु], @deva[जरठ] hard, stiff, @deva[बधिर], @deva[कुब्ज] and @deva[वर्बर], may optionally precede the words in apposition to them; as @deva[जैमिनिकडारः] or @deva[कडारजैमिनिः] Jaimini who is turned tawny on account of his having practised penance in the sun,' &c.

**(c)**[^5] Words expressive of the persons or things condemned or reproached are placed first; as @deva[वैयाकरणखसूचिः] 'a bad grammarian,' 'one who has forgotten his grammar and therefore can make no use of his knowledge;' (@deva[पृष्टः सन् प्रश्नं विस्मारयितुं खं सूचयति अभ्यासवैधुर्यात्स एकमुच्यते ।] Tatv.); so @deva[मीमांसकादुर्दुरूढः] 'a mīmāṃsaka who is a sceptic' or 'an unbeliever'; except in the case of the words @deva[पाप], @deva[अणक] and @deva[किम्]; as @deva[पापनापितः] 'a bad barber,' @deva[अणककुलालः] 'a mean, silly potter,' @deva[कुत्सितः राजा किराजः], @deva[किंसखा] (@deva[कुत्सितः सखा]), &c.

**(d)**[^6] Words in apposition to @deva[वृन्दारक], @deva[नाग] and @deva[कुञ्जर] are also placed first; e. g. @deva[नृपवृन्दारकः] 'an eminent king,' @deva[तापसकुञ्जरः], @deva[पुरुषनागः], &c.

**(e)**[^7] @deva[कतर] and @deva[कतम] are compounded only when they ask a question with reference to a class (@deva[जाति] family), and are placed first; e. g. @deva[कतर-कतम-कठः] 'which Brāhmaṇa of the Kaṭha branch'? @deva[कतर-कतम-कलापः] 'which Brāhmaṇa of the Kalāpa branch'? But @deva[कतरः पुत्रः] 'which son'?

**(f)**[^8] The word @deva[कुमार] (and also @deva[कुमारी] changed to @deva[कुमार]) is placed first when compounded with one of the words @deva[श्रमणा], @deva[प्रव्रजिता], @deva[कुलटा], @deva[गर्भिणी], @deva[तापसी], @deva[दासी], @deva[अध्यापक], @deva[पण्डित], @deva[पटु], @deva[मृदु], @deva[कुशल], @deva[चपल] and @deva[निपुण]; as @deva[कुमारश्रमणा] 'a female mendicant,' @deva[कुमारप्रव्रजिता] 'a young female ascetic'; @deva[कुमारमृदुः-द्वी] 'a delicate boy or girl,' @deva[कुमारगर्भिणी], @deva[कुमाराध्यापकः], &c.

**(g)**[^9] The words @deva[एक], @deva[सर्व], @deva[जरद्], @deva[पुराण], @deva[नव] and @deva[केवल]; and the words @deva[पूर्व], @deva[अपर], @deva[चरम], @deva[जघन्य] 'hindmost,' @deva[समान], @deva[मध्य], @deva[मध्यम] and @deva[वीर] are always placed first in a Karmadhāraya compound. @deva[अपर] when followed by @deva[अर्ध] is changed to @deva[पश्च]; as @deva[एकनाथः] 'sole master or lord', @deva[सर्वशैलाः], @deva[जरद्वैयायिकः] 'an old logician,' @deva[पुराणमीमांसकाः] 'old mīmāṃsā philosophers,' @deva[नवपाठकाः], @deva[पूर्ववैयाकरणाः] 'the old grammarians,' @deva[अपराध्यापकः] @deva[अपरश्चासौ अर्धश्च पश्चार्धः] 'the hinder part or side of the body;' @deva[चरमराजः] 'the last king,' @deva[समानाधिकरणम्] 'being in the same category or predicament'; @deva[वीरैकः] 'a sole warrior i. e. an eminent warrior', &c. The form @deva[एकवीर] (found used by great writers) also may be defended.[^10]

**(h)**[^11] The words @deva[सत्], @deva[महत्], @deva[परम], @deva[उत्तम] and @deva[उत्कृष्ट] are compounded with another noun when they are used as terms of praise or excellence; @deva[सद्वैद्यः] 'an excellent physician' @deva[महावैयाकरणः] &c. but @deva[उत्कृष्टो गौः] where @deva[उत्कृष्ट] means 'uplifted, or 'drawn out of.'

---

[^1]: @deva[विशेषणं विशेष्येण बहुलम् ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 57.

[^2]: @deva[पोटायुवतिस्तोककतिपयगृष्टिधेनुवशावेहद्बष्कयणीप्रवक्तृश्रोत्रियाध्यापकधूर्तैर्जातिः । पुंवत्कर्मधारयजातीयदेशीयेषु ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 65. VI. 3. 42.

[^3]: @deva[प्रशंसावचनैश्च ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 66 (@deva[मतल्लिकादयो नियतलिङ्गा न तु विशेष्यनिघ्नाः ।] Sid. Kau). @deva[मतल्लिकामचर्चिकाप्रकाण्डमुद्धतल्लजौ । प्रशस्तवाचकान्यमूनि ।] Amara.

[^4]: @deva[कडाराः कर्मधारये ।] Pāṇ. II. 2. 38.

[^5]: @deva[कुत्सितानि कुत्सनैः । पापाणके कुत्सितैः ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 53. 54. @deva[किं क्षेपे ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 64.

[^6]: @deva[वृन्दारकनागकुञ्जरैः पूज्यमानम् ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 62.

[^7]: @deva[कतरकतमौ जातिपरिप्रश्ने] Pāṇ. II. 1. 63.

[^8]: @deva[कुमारः श्रमणादिभिः ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 70.

[^9]: @deva[पूर्वकालैकसर्वजरत्पुराणनवकेवलाः समानाधिकरणेन ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 49. @deva[पूर्वापरप्रथमचरमजघन्यसमानमध्यमध्यमवीराश्च ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 58. @deva[अपरस्यार्धे पश्चभावो वक्तव्यः ।] Vārt.

[^10]: @deva[कथमेकवीर इति । पूर्वकालैकेति बाधित्वा परत्वादनेन समास वीरैक इति हि स्यात् । बहुलग्रहणाद्भविष्यति ।] How do you justify the form @deva[एकवीर]? For the Sūtra @deva[पूर्वापर] &c. being a subsequent one ought to have preference over the preceding Sūtra @deva[पूर्वकालैक] &c. and we should have @deva[वीरैकः] We reply.—The form may be justified by supposing that the rule operates in most cases only (@deva[बहुलग्रहणात्] and not in a few).

[^11]: @deva[सन्महत्परमोत्तमोत्कृष्टाः पूज्यमानैः ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 61.

rules.title: Quarters and Numerals in Karmadhāraya
rules.body:
Names of quarters and numerals form a Karm. compound with any @deva[सुबन्त] (a declinable word) but only when the whole compound is an appellation;[^1] e. g. @deva[सप्तर्षयः] 'Name of a constellation of stars,' 'Ursa Major;' @deva[पञ्चजनाः][^2] &c., @deva[पूर्वेषुकामशमी] 'Name of a town in the east;' @deva[उत्तरा वृक्षाः] 'Northern trees; @deva[पञ्च ब्राह्मणाः] &c. The compound is forbidden in other cases.

**(a)**[^3] But words denoting a cardinal point or numerals may be compounded with any other noun when a Taddhita termination is to be affixed to the compound so formed (or it conveys in addition to its sense as a Karm. a derivative meaning such as is usually denoted by a Tad. aff.) or when the compound itself becomes the first member of another compound or when the compound forms a proper name; @deva[पूर्वा शाला पूर्वशाला]; @deva[पूर्वस्यां शालायां भवः पौर्वशालः] 'being in the eastern hall' from @deva[पूर्वशाला+अ] (i. e. Tad. aff. @deva[ञ] added by @deva[दिक्पूर्वपदादसंज्ञायां ञः] Pāṇ. IV. 2. 107); so @deva[षष्+मातृ=षण्मातृ] 'six mothers'+Tad. @deva[अ]=@deva[षाण्मातुरः] the son of six mothers; @deva[पूर्वा शाला प्रिया यस्य स पूर्वशालाप्रियः] where @deva[पूर्वशाला] is a @deva[पूर्वपद] and not used independently; @deva[उत्तरध्रुवः], @deva[दक्षिणध्रुवः] &c. which are names.

---

[^1]: @deva[दिक्संख्ये संज्ञायाम् ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 61.

[^2]: These are gods, men, Gandharvas, serpents, and Pitṛis, according to some; and Brāhmaṇas, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, Śūdras and Nishādhas or barbarians, according to others. (Vide Shankarāchārya on Brah. Sū. I. 4. 11.-13.)

[^3]: @deva[तद्धितार्थोत्तरपदसमाहारे च ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 51.

rules.title: @deva[कु] Particle in Karmadhāraya
rules.body:
The particle @deva[कु] forms a Karm. compound with any other word, @deva[कुपुरुषः] (@deva[कुत्सितः पुरुषः]) a bad man; @deva[कुपुत्रः] &c.

**(a)**[^1] @deva[कु] is changed to (1) @deva[कत्] when followed by a noun with an initial vowel in a Tat. by @deva[त्रि] and the nouns @deva[रथ] and @deva[वद] and by @deva[तृण] 'denoting a species;' @deva[कुत्सितोऽश्वः कदश्वः] 'bad horse;' so @deva[कदन्नं] 'coarse food;' but @deva[कूष्ट्रः] 'having bad camels' (a Bah. comp.) @deva[राजा]; @deva[कुत्सिताः त्रयः कत्रयः] 'three inferior things;' @deva[कत्रथः] 'a bad chariot,' @deva[कद्वदः] 'speaking ill, a bad speaker,' @deva[कत्तृणम्] 'a kind of fragrant grass.'

(2) To @deva[का] when followed by @deva[पथिन्] and @deva[अक्ष] and when meaning 'a little,' and optionally when prefixed to @deva[पुरुष]; @deva[कापथम्], @deva[काक्षः] 'a sidelong look or a frown of displeasure;' see Bh. V. 54 (@deva[अक्षशब्देन तत्पुरुषः अक्षिशब्देन बहुव्रीहिर्वा] Sid. Kau.). @deva[ईषज्जलं काजलं] 'a little water,' @deva[ईषत्पुरुषः कापुरुषः], but @deva[कुत्सितःपुरुषः कुपुरुषः] or @deva[कपुरुषः].

(3) And to @deva[का] or @deva[कव] when followed by @deva[उष्ण]; @deva[कोष्णं], @deva[कवोष्णं] and @deva[कदुष्णं] by (1), all meaning 'luke-warm'.

---

[^1]: @deva[कोः कत्तत्पुरुषेऽचि ।] ('@deva[त्रौ च]' Vārt:) @deva[रथवदयोश्च । तृणे च जातौ । कापथ्यक्षयोः । ईषदर्थे । विभाषा पुरुषे । कवं चोष्णे ।] Pāṇ. VI. 3. 101-107.

rules.title: Two Adjectives and Other Special Karmadhāraya Cases
rules.body:
Two adjectives may also be compounded into what is called the @deva[विशेषणोभयपदकर्मधारयः] as @deva[शुक्लकृष्णः], @deva[कृष्णसारंगः].

**(a).**[^1] Two participles expressive of two consecutive actions of the same individual may be compounded together, the one expressive of the previous action being placed first; @deva[आदौ स्नातः पश्चादनुलिप्तः स्नातानुलिप्तः] 'first bathed and then anointed'; similarly @deva[पीतोद्गीर्णम्] 'first drunk and afterwards vomited out', @deva[पीतप्रतिबद्धः], @deva[गृहीतप्रतिमुक्तः] (Rag. II. 1. IV. 43), &c.

**(b).** In the case of the two sets of words given above (@ref[222] g.) forming compounds with one another those beginning with @deva[पूर्व] are placed first. In the case of @deva[एक] compounded with @deva[वीर] it may precede or follow it; as @deva[वीरैकः] or @deva[एकवीरः]; the former, however, is preferable. In the case of the first set of words viz. @deva[एक]......@deva[केवल] the one succeeding precedes the one preceding when compounded together; as @deva[पुराणजरत्], @deva[केवलपुराणम्], &c.

**(c)**[^2] A past participle is compounded with another with the negative particle prefixed to it; '@deva[कृताकृतम्],' what is done and not done, i. e. 'partially done'.

**(d).**[^3] The word @deva[युवन्] (m. f.) enters into a Karm. comp. with the words @deva[खलति], @deva[पलित], @deva[वलित] having wrinkles, and @deva[जरती], and is placed first; i. e. @deva[युवा+खलतिः युवखलतिः] 'a young bald-headed man';-@deva[ती] 'a young bald-headed woman'; @deva[युवजरती] 'a young woman looking old'; @deva[युवपलितः] 'a young man whose hair is grey', &c.

---

[^1]: See Pāṇ. II. 1. 49. (@deva[पूर्वकाल-पूर्वत्वस्य ससंबन्धिकत्वात्पूर्वकालोऽपरकालेन समस्यते ।] Tatv. quoted above)

[^2]: @deva[केन नञ्विशिष्टेनानञ् ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 60.

[^3]: @deva[युवाखलतिपलितवलितजरतीभिः ।] Pāṇ. II. 67.

rules.title: @deva[ईषत्] 'Little' in Compounds
rules.body:
The word @deva[ईषत्] 'little' is compounded with any other word except a verbal derivative, and even with a verbal derivative when it expresses a quality;[^1] as @deva[ईषत्पिङ्गलः] 'a little brown', @deva[ईषद्रक्तम्] 'reddish,' &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[ईषदकृता ।] Pāṇ. II. 2. 7. @deva[ईषद्गुणवचनेनेति वाच्यम् ।] Vārt.

rules.title: Compounds with @deva[तव्य], @deva[अनीय], @deva[य], @deva[तुल्य]
rules.body:
Words ending in the terminations @deva[तव्य], @deva[अनीय], @deva[य] and @deva[तुल्य] and words having a similar meaning, may be compounded with any subanta not importing a particular kind;[^1] e. g. @deva[भोज्योष्णम्] 'any hot eatable,' @deva[तुल्यश्वेतः] 'of a similar white colour,' @deva[सदृशश्वेतः], &c.; but @deva[भोज्यः ओदनः] as the latter word refers to a kind of food here.

---

[^1]: @deva[कृत्यतुल्याख्या अजात्या ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 68.

rules.title: Irregular Compounds: @deva[मयूरव्यंसकादि] Class
rules.body:
The following are the more important of the compounds given by Pāṇ. as irregular under the class @deva[मयूरव्यंसकादि][^1]—@deva[मयूरश्चासौ व्यंसकश्च मयूरव्यंसकः] 'a cunning peacock', so @deva[छात्रव्यंसकः]; @deva[उदक् च अवाक् च उच्चावचम्], so @deva[उच्चनीचम्] 'high and low', 'great and small', @deva[निश्चितं च प्रचितं च निश्चप्रचम्], @deva[नास्ति किंचन यस्य अकिंचनः]; @deva[नास्ति कुतो भयं यस्य स अकुतोभयः]; @deva[अन्यो राजा राजान्तरम्], @deva[अन्यो ग्रामः ग्रामान्तरम्], @deva[चिदेव चिन्मात्रं] (these are nitya-samāsas). @deva[अश्नीत पिबत इत्येवं सततं यत्राभिधीयते सा अश्नीतपिबता] that in which are constantly uttered the words 'eat and drink', so @deva[पचतभृज्जता], @deva[खादतमोदता]; @deva[अहं अहं इति यस्यां क्रियायामभिधीयते सा अहमहमिका], that in which are uttered the words 'I alone; I alone;' hence hard competition, &c. @deva[अहं पूर्वं अहं पूर्वमिति यस्यां क्रियायामभिधीयते सा अहंपूर्विका]; so @deva[आहोपुरुषिका] 'great self-conceit or pride' (Bhatti. V. 27); 'vaunting', (Bv. I. 84) &c. Also @deva[कान्दिशीक] 'put to flight,' @deva[यदृच्छा] 'accident,' &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[मयूरव्यंसकादयश्च ।] Pāṇ. II. 1, 72.

rules.title: Madhyamapadālopi: Dropping Middle Member
rules.body:
In some Karmadhāraya compounds the last member of the first word which is itself a compound word is dropped;[^1] e. g. @deva[शाकप्रियः पार्थिवः शाकपार्थिवः] 'a king who likes vegetables', @deva[देवपूजको ब्राह्मणः देवब्राह्मणः] &c. These compounds, though they should be properly called "*Uttamapadalopi*" are popularly designated "*Madhyamapadalopi*". Any compound requiring a similar explanation is classed under this group (@deva[शाकपार्थिवादि]) which is an @deva[आकृतिगण].

---

[^1]: @deva[शाकपार्थिवादीनां सिद्धये उत्तरपदलोपस्योपसंख्यानम् ।] Vārt on Pāṇ. II. 1. 60.

rules.title: Definition of Dwigu
rules.body:
## DWIGU OR NUMERAL APPOSITIONAL COMPOUNDS.

When the first member of a Karmadhāraya compound is a numeral it is called 'Dwigu'.[^1]

---

[^1]: @deva[संख्यापूर्वो द्विगुः ।] Pāṇ. II. 1. 52.

rules.title: Formation Conditions for Dwigu
rules.body:
A Dwigu compound is possible (a) under the circumstances mentioned in @ref[223] (a) i. e.—

(1) when a Taddhita affix is to be added to the compound so formed; @deva[षण्णां मातृणामपत्यं षाण्मातुरः] 'the son of six mothers, Kārtikeya' (vide Ku. IX); @deva[पञ्चकपालः] &c; or (2) when the compound itself becomes the first member of another compound, as @deva[पञ्चगावः धनं यस्य असौ पञ्चगवधनः], @deva[पञ्चनावप्रियः] &c.

(b) And when the compound denotes an aggregate; in this case it is singular;[^1] as @deva[त्रयाणां भुवनानां समाहारः त्रिभुवनम्] the three worlds (taken collectively); as @deva[पञ्चपात्रम्], @deva[पञ्चगवम्], &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[द्विगुरेकवचनम् ।] Pāṇ. II. 4. 1.

rules.title: Prādi: Prepositional Compounds
rules.body:
## PREPOSITIONAL COMPOUNDS.
## 4. Pradi.

Those Tatpurusha compounds whose first member is a preposition are termed Prādi by Sanskrit grammarians;[^1] some of these prepositions combine with a following noun in the Nom., with a noun in the Acc. &c.; e. g. @deva[प्रगतः आचार्यः प्राचार्यः] 'an eminent teacher', @deva[संगतः अध्वानं समध्वः] 'taken to a path-way' (vide Bhatti. III. 45). @deva[प्रकृष्टो वातः प्रवातः] 'strong or excessive wind,' &c.; @deva[अतिक्रान्तो मालां अतिमालः] 'excelling a garland' (in fragrance or beauty), @deva[अतिक्रान्तो रथं रथिनं वा अतिरथः] 'a chariot-warrior who has no rival or equal'; so @deva[अतिमात्र] 'exceeding measure,' @deva[अतिसर्व] &c. @deva[अवक्रुष्टः कोकिलया अवकोकिलः] 'attracted by the cuckoo;' @deva[परिग्लानः अध्ययनात् पर्यध्ययनः] 'tired of studying;' @deva[निष्क्रान्तः कौशाम्ब्याः निष्कौशाम्बिः] 'gone out of Kauśāmbi;' so @deva[निर्लुब्ध] &c. A compound with prepositions which govern cases (@deva[कर्मप्रवचनीय]) is forbidden; @deva[वृक्षं प्रति].

---

[^1]: @deva[कुगतिप्रादयः ।] Pāṇ. II. 2. 18. @deva[प्रादयो गताद्यर्थे प्रथमया । अत्यादयः क्रान्ताद्यर्थे द्वितीयया । अवादयः क्रुष्टाद्यर्थे तृतीयया । पर्यादयो ग्लानाद्यर्थे चतुर्थ्या । निरादयः क्रान्ताद्यर्थे पञ्चम्या । कर्मप्रवचनीयानां प्रतिषेधः ।] Vārtikas.

rules.title: Gati: Compounds with Indeclinables
rules.body:
## 5 Gati.

Compounds of the following words with verbal indeclinables are called Gati.

**(a)**[^1] The particles @deva[ऊरी], @deva[उररी], @deva[वौषट्], @deva[वषट्], @deva[स्वाहा], @deva[स्वधा], @deva[प्रादुः], @deva[आविस्] and @deva[श्रत्] and the word @deva[कारिका] meaning an action; as @deva[ऊरीकृत्य], @deva[उररीकृत्य] 'having accepted; @deva[वषट्कृत्य] 'having uttered the word *Vashaṭ*;' @deva[प्रादुर्भूय], @deva[कारिकाकृत्य] 'having done the act.'

**(b)**[^2] Onomatopoetic words not followed by @deva[इति], as @deva[खाट्कृत्य]; but @deva[खाडिति कृत्वा] (@deva[निरटीवत्]).

**(c)**[^3] The words @deva[सत्] and @deva[असत्] showing respect and disrespect respectively, the prepositions @deva[अलं] in the sense of 'adorning,' @deva[पुरः], @deva[अदः], @deva[अन्तः], @deva[कणे], @deva[मनः], @deva[अस्तं], @deva[अच्छ], and @deva[तिरः]; as @deva[अलंकृत्य] 'having adorned', but @deva[अलं कृत्वा] doing enough (@deva[पर्याप्तमित्यर्थः] Sid. Kau.); @deva[पुरस्कृत्य] 'placing in the front'; @deva[अदःकृत्य] (@deva[अदःकृतम्]) @deva[अन्तर्हत्य] (@deva[मध्ये हत्वा] Sid. Kau.); @deva[कणेहत्य], as @deva[कणेहत्य पयः पिबति] 'he drinks milk to his heart's content'; @deva[अच्छोद्य] 'having gone up to and spoken' (@deva[अभिमुखं गत्वा उक्त्वा च इत्यर्थः] Sid. Kau.); @deva[तिरोभूय], @deva[मनोहत्य] (till disgust is produced); @deva[अस्तंगत्य], @deva[अच्छगत्य] 'going towards.'

**(d)**[^4] The words @deva[हस्ते], @deva[पाणौ] and @deva[प्राध्वं]; as @deva[हस्तेकृत्य], @deva[पाणौकृत्य] 'having married'; @deva[प्राध्वंकृत्य] 'having forced to yield.'

**(e)**[^5] The particles @deva[उपाजे], @deva[अन्वाजे], @deva[साक्षात्], @deva[मिथ्या], @deva[अमा], @deva[प्रादुः], @deva[आविः] and @deva[नमस्], the words @deva[मनसि], @deva[उरसि] (except when there is the sense of juxtaposition or extreme contact), @deva[मध्ये], and the word @deva[पदे] form compounds with verbal indeclinables optionally; @deva[उपाजेकृत्य], @deva[उपाजे कृत्वा], @deva[अन्वाजेकृत्य] @deva[अन्वाजे कृत्वा] 'giving strength to the weak' [@deva[दुर्बलस्य बलमाधाय इत्यर्थः] Sid. Kau.]; @deva[साक्षात्कृत्य-त्वा], @deva[लवणंकृत्य-त्वा], @deva[उरसिकृत्य-त्वा] (having accepted) @deva[मनसिकृत्य कृत्वा]; but @deva[उरसि कृत्वा पाणिं शेते]; @deva[मध्येकृत्य-त्वा], @deva[पदेकृत्य], @deva[पदे कृत्वा], &c.

**(f)** These compounds are also formed with nouns derived from roots for their second members; e. g. @deva[अस्तमयः] 'setting of the sun,' @deva[पुरस्कारः] 'reception, showing respect,' @deva[तिरस्कारः], @deva[सत्कारः], @deva[अलंकृतिः], &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[ऊर्यादिच्विडाचश्च ।] Pāṇ. I. 4. 61. @deva[कारिकाशब्दस्योपसंख्यानम् ।] Vārtikas.

[^2]: @deva[अनुकरणं चानितिपरम् ।] Pāṇ. I. 4. 62.

[^3]: Pāṇ. I. 4. 63-71.

[^4]: Pāṇ. I. 4. 77-78.

[^5]: Pāṇ. I. 4. 73-76. (@deva[अनत्याधान उरसिमनसी ।]).

rules.title: @deva[च्वि] Formations as Prepositional Compounds
rules.body: The @deva[च्वि] formations (see Chap. XI.) are also classed as prepositional Tatpurusha compounds; as @deva[शुक्लीकृत्य] having turned white what was not so before.

rules.title: Upapada Compounds: Definition
rules.body:
## 6. UPAPADA COMPOUNDS.

When the second member of a Tat. Comp. is a root-noun derived from a root which takes a particular Kṛit affix by virtue of the presence of the first member, it is called an Upapada Tat.; as @deva[कुम्भं करोतीति कुम्भकारः] 'a potter;' so @deva[साम गायतीति सामगः] 'one who chants a verse of the Sāman Veda;' @deva[मांसं कामयती मांसकामा] 'desirous of meat'; similarly @deva[अश्वक्रीती] (@deva[अश्वेन क्रीता]) 'bought for a horse', @deva[कच्छपी] 'a female tortoise,' &c. The noun prefixed to the last member, such as @deva[कुम्भ], is called an *upapada*.[^1]

**N. B.** The latter member of such compounds must neither be the conjugated form of a root nor a separate verbal derivative i. e. formed independently of the last member; e. g. @deva[पयोधर] is not an Upapada Tat., as the word @deva[धर] can be independently formed; it is a Gen. Tat. @deva[धरतीति धरः पयसां धरः पयोधरः] 'a cloud' or 'the female breast.'

---

[^1]: @deva[तत्रोपपदं सप्तमीस्थम् ।] Pāṇ. III. 1. 92. @deva[सप्तम्यन्ते पदे कर्मणीत्यादौ वाच्यत्वेन स्थितं कुम्भादि तद्वाचकं पदमुपपदसंज्ञं स्यात् ।] Sid. Kau.

rules.title: Upapada with Namul and Indeclinables
rules.body: Sometimes the second member of an Upapada Tat. may be a *Namulanta* or the verbal indeclinable in @deva[अम्]; as @deva[स्वादुंकारं भुङ्क्ते] 'he eats having sweetened the food;' @deva[अग्रेभोजं] 'having dined first;' sometimes this compound is optional. @deva[मूलकोपदंशं] or @deva[मूलकेन उपदंशं भुङ्क्ते] 'he eats the condiment with a raddish,' &c.

rules.title: Upapadas with @deva[त्वा]/@deva[य] Indeclinables
rules.body: Some *upapadas* such as @deva[उच्चैः], @deva[नीचैः], @deva[तिर्यक्], @deva[मुखतः], &c. also optionally form compounds with the verbal indeclinable in @deva[त्वा] (changeable to @deva[य]); as @deva[उच्चैःकृत्य] (or @deva[उच्चैः कृत्वा]), @deva[तिर्यक्कृत्य], @deva[मुखतोभूय], @deva[नानाकृत्य], @deva[एकधाभूय], &c. For further particulars vide the Chapter on verbal derivatives.

rules.title: @deva[अङ्गुलि] → @deva[अङ्गुल] in Compounds
rules.body:
## GENERAL RULES APPLICABLE TO THE TATPURUSHA COMPOUNDS.

The word @deva[अङ्गुलि] at the end of a Tatpurusha compound changes its final to @deva[अ] when preceded by a numeral or an indeclinable,[^1] as @deva[द्वे अङ्गुली प्रमाणमस्य द्व्यङ्गुलं दारु] 'a piece of wood measuring two fingers,' @deva[निर्गतमङ्गुलिभ्यो निरङ्गुलम्] &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[तत्पुरुषस्याङ्गुलेः संख्याव्ययादेः ।] Pāṇ. V. 4. 86.

rules.title: Vowel Dropping and @deva[अ] Addition in Compounds
rules.body:
The following words, when at the end of a Tatpurusha, drop the final vowel, together with the following consonant if there be any, and add @deva[अ] under the circumstances mentioned:—

**(a)**[^1] @deva[रात्रि] when preceded by a numeral, an indeclinable, a word expressive of a part of the whole, such as @deva[पूर्व], @deva[अपर], &c., or by the words @deva[सर्व], @deva[संख्यात] and @deva[पुण्य]; as @deva[द्वयोः रात्र्योः समाहारः द्विरात्रम्] an aggregate of two nights (Dwi.); @deva[अतिक्रान्तो रात्रिमतिरात्रः] that has passed a night, the dead of night; @deva[पूर्वं रात्रेः पूर्वरात्रः] the first part of the night; @deva[सर्वा रात्रिः सर्वरात्रः], @deva[संख्याता रात्रिः संख्यातरात्रः], @deva[पुण्यरात्रः] an auspicious night.

The same happens when @deva[रात्रि] is preceded by @deva[अहन्] in a Dwandwa; as @deva[अहश्च रात्रिश्च अहोरात्रः].

**(b)**[^2] @deva[राजन्], @deva[अहन्] and @deva[सखि]; as @deva[परमः राजा परमराजः] a great king; @deva[मद्राणां राजा मद्रराजः], @deva[उत्तमं अहः उत्तमाहः] an excellent day, @deva[एकं च तदहः एकाहः]; @deva[द्वयोरह्नोः समाहारः द्व्यहः], so @deva[त्र्यहः], @deva[सप्ताहः], &c. @deva[पुण्यं अहः पुण्याहं] a holy day, @deva[सुदिनाहं], (vide @ref[245], b.), @deva[कृष्णस्य सखा कृष्णसखः] &c.

**(c) Exceptions**[^3]—@deva[अहन्] when preceded by an indeclinable, or a word denoting a part of the whole, or by @deva[सर्व] or by a numeral with a Taddhita affix added to the whole compound, becomes @deva[अह्न]; as @deva[अतिक्रान्तमहः] exceeding a day (in duration) @deva[अत्यह्नः], @deva[पूर्वाह्नः] forenoon, @deva[सर्वाह्नः] the whole day, @deva[संख्याताह्नः], @deva[द्वयोरह्नोः भवः द्व्यह्नः] (@deva[-ह्ना] fem.), @deva[द्व्यह्नप्रियः] &c.; with @deva[संख्यात] the change is optional; as @deva[संख्याताह्नः], or @deva[हः].

**N. B.** The[^4] @deva[न्] of the substitute is changed to @deva[ण्] when preceded by @deva[र्] belonging to the first member ending in @deva[अ]; as @deva[सर्वाह्णः]; but @deva[परागतं अहः पराह्नः] (as @deva[परा] ends in @deva[आ]).

**(d)**[^5] @deva[तक्षन्] when preceded by @deva[ग्राम] or @deva[कौट], and @deva[श्वन्] by @deva[अति] or an inanimate object with which it is compounded; e. g. @deva[ग्रामस्य तक्षा ग्रामतक्षः] 'a village carpenter i. e. one not very skilful;' @deva[कुट्यां भवः कौट] (@deva[स्वतन्त्रः]) @deva[स चासौ तक्षा च कौटतक्षः] 'an independent carpenter'; @deva[अतिश्वः] [@deva[वराहः]] 'fleeter than a dog'; @deva[अतिश्वी] (worse than a dog's life) @deva[सेवा]; @deva[आकर्षः श्वा इव आकर्षश्वः] 'a dog like i. e. bad or unlucky throw of dice;' but @deva[वानरश्वा] 'a monkey like a dog'.

**(e)**[^6] @deva[सक्थि] when preceded by @deva[उत्तर], @deva[मृग] or @deva[पूर्व] or by a word denoting an inanimate object with which it is compounded; @deva[उत्तरसक्थम्] 'the upper part of the thigh', @deva[मृगसक्थम्] 'the thigh of a deer,' @deva[पूर्वसक्थम्], @deva[फलकामिव सक्थि फलकसक्थम्] 'a thigh like a board'.

**(f)** A numeral when compounded in a Tat. @deva[निर्गतानि त्रिंशतः निस्त्रिंशानि वर्षाणि] (@deva[चैत्रस्य]) more than thirty; @deva[निर्गतः त्रिंशतांगुलिभ्यः निस्त्रिंशः खड्गः] a sword more than thirty fingers in length.

---

[^1]: @deva[अहः सर्वैकदेशसंख्यातपुण्याच्च रात्रेः ।] Pāṇ. V. 4. 87.

[^2]: @deva[राजाहःसखिभ्यष्टच् ।] Pāṇ. V. 4. 91.

[^3]: @deva[अह्नोऽह्न एतेभ्यः ।] Pāṇ. V. 4. 88.

[^4]: @deva[अह्नोऽदन्तात् ।] Pāṇ. VIII. 4. 7.

[^5]: @deva[ग्रामकौटाभ्यां च तक्षण् । अतेः शुनः । उपमानादप्राणिषु ।] Pāṇ. V. 4. 96-97.

[^6]: @deva[उत्तरमृगपूर्वाच्च सक्थ्नः ।] Pāṇ. V. 4. 98.

rules.title: Addition of @deva[अ] to Final Member
rules.body:
The following words have an @deva[अ] added to them when at the end of a Tatpurusha compound:—

**(a)** @deva[गो] except when a Tad. aff. is added and then dropped;[^1] e. g. @deva[परमगवः] an excellent bull, @deva[पञ्चगव]-(a collection of five cows) @deva[धनः], but @deva[द्विगुः] exchanged or bartered for two cows.

**(b)**[^2] @deva[उरस्] meaning 'chief or eminent'. @deva[अश्वानां उर इव अश्वोरसम्] 'the chief of horses i. e. an excellent horse.'

**(c)**[^3] The words @deva[अनस्] @deva[अश्मन्], @deva[अयस्] and @deva[सरस्] when they denote a class or form names; @deva[उपानसम्] (@deva[उपगतं अनः]) 'a cart-load,' @deva[महानसः] 'a kitchen'; @deva[अमृताश्मः] 'a kind of stone like the moon-stone' [in this case the final @deva[अन्] is dropped]; @deva[कालायसम्] 'black iron', @deva[मण्डूकसरसम्] 'a lake full of frogs'; @deva[जलसरसम्] 'a lake of that name.'

**(d)**[^4] @deva[नौ] at the end of a Dwigu, except when the Tad. affix is dropped), as @deva[द्वाभ्यां नौभ्यामागतः द्विनावरूप्यः] (when the aff. is not dropped), @deva[द्विनावम्] 'a collection of two boats', so @deva[त्रिनावम्] &c; but @deva[पञ्चभिः नौभिः क्रीतः पञ्चनौः], also when it is preceded by @deva[अर्ध]; as @deva[नावः अर्धम् अर्धनावम्] the *neuter* is irregular (@deva[लोकात्] Sid. Kau).

**(e)**[^5] @deva[खारी] (a measure of corn) under similar circumstances takes the @deva[अ] optionally, the final @deva[ई] being dropped before it; @deva[द्विखारम्-रिः], @deva[अर्धखारम्-रि].

**(f)**[^6] @deva[अञ्जलि], preceded by @deva[द्वि] or @deva[त्रि] in a Dwigu, optionally takes @deva[अ], except when the Tad. aff. is dropped, before which the final @deva[इ] is dropped; @deva[द्व्यञ्जलं-लि] 'two handfuls'; but @deva[द्वाभ्यामञ्जलिभ्यां क्रीतः द्व्यञ्जलिः ।]

---

[^1]: @deva[गोरतद्धितलुकि ।] Pāṇ. V. 4. 92.

[^2]: @deva[अग्राख्यायामुरसः ।] Pāṇ. V. 4. 93.

[^3]: @deva[अनोश्मायः सरसां जातिसंज्ञयोः ।] Pāṇ. V. 4. 94.

[^4]: @deva[नावो द्विगोः । अर्धाच्च ।] Pāṇ. V. 4. 99. 100.

[^5]: @deva[खार्याः प्राचाम् ।] Pāṇ. V. 4. 101.

[^6]: @deva[द्वित्रिभ्यामञ्जलेः ।] Pāṇ. V. 4. 102.

rules.title: Dropping @deva[न्] from @deva[ब्रह्मन्]
rules.body:
The @deva[न्] of @deva[ब्रह्मन्] is optionally dropped when preceded by @deva[कु] and @deva[महत्];[^1] @deva[कुब्रह्मा-ह्मः] a bad Brāhmaṇa, @deva[महाब्रह्मा-ह्मः]. The @deva[न्] is dropped necessarily when the compound implies the country in which the Brāhmaṇa dwells; e. g. @deva[सुराष्ट्रब्रह्मा] a Brāhmaṇa dwelling in Surāshṭra.

---

[^1]: @deva[ब्रह्मणो जानपदाख्यायाम् । कुमहद्भ्यामन्यतरस्याम् ।] Pāṇ. V. 4. 104. 105.

rules.title: @deva[महत्] → @deva[महा] in Compounds
rules.body:
The word @deva[महत्] is changed to @deva[महा] when it forms the first member of a Karmadhāraya or a Bahuvrīhi compound, or when the termination @deva[जातीय] follows,[^1] as @deva[महादेवः] the great god, @deva[महाबाहुः] a great arm (Tat.) or one having a great arm (Bah.); @deva[महाजातीयः]; but @deva[महतः सेवा महत्सेवा] (Gen. Tat.).

**Exception:**—When it is followed by @deva[घास], @deva[कर] and @deva[विशिष्ट] the change takes place necessarily; @deva[महतो महत्या वा करः महाकरः]; similarly @deva[महाघासः], @deva[महाविशिष्टः].

---

[^1]: @deva[आन्महतः समानाधिकरणजातीययोः ।] Pāṇ. VI. 3. 46. and the Vārtikas on it.

rules.title: @deva[अष्टन्] → @deva[अष्टा] before @deva[कपाल] and @deva[गो]
Exceptions for Negative Tatpurusha
rules.body:
All the rules given above for the change of the finals of the Tat. compounds do not hold good in the case of the Neg. Tat.;[^1] e. g. @deva[न राजा अराजा] one not a king; @deva[न सखा असखा], &c.

**(a)** But in the case of the word @deva[पथिन्] the final @deva[इन्] is optionally dropped and @deva[अ] added; @deva[अपथं] or @deva[अपंथाः] 'absence of a road'. @deva[पथिन्] when so modified in a Tat. is neu.;[^2] (but @deva[अपथः देशः]).

---

[^1]: @deva[नञस्तत्पुरुषात् । पथो विभाषा ।] Pāṇ. V. 4. 71, 72.

[^2]: @deva[अपथं नपुंसकम् ।] Pāṇ. II. 4. 3.

rules.title: Gender Rules for Tatpurusha Compounds
rules.body:
## GENDERS OF TATPURUSHA COMPOUNDS.

As a general rule a Tatpurusha compound follows the gender of the final noun.[^1]

**Exceptions:**[^2]

**(a)** Compounds with @deva[प्राप्त] and @deva[आपन्न] for their first member and the Prādi compounds follow the gender of the words they qualify; @deva[प्राप्तजीविकः नरः], @deva[प्राप्तजीविका स्त्री], @deva[निष्कौशाम्बिः पुरुषः] &c.

**(b)** A Tatpurusha ending in @deva[रात्र], @deva[अह्न] and @deva[अह] is *masculine*, except when @deva[रात्र] is preceded by a numeral and @deva[अह] by @deva[पुण्य] and @deva[सुदिन]; e. g. @deva[पूर्वरात्रः], @deva[मध्याह्नः], @deva[सप्ताहः], @deva[नवरात्रम्], @deva[गणरात्रम्], @deva[पुण्याहम्], @deva[सुदिनाहम्]; also that ending in @deva[पथ] (substituted for @deva[पथिन्], vide @ref[280]) preceded by a numeral or an indeclinable; as @deva[त्रयाणां पन्थाः त्रिपथम्], @deva[विरूपः पन्थाः विपथम्], a bad or a wrong way; but @deva[सुपन्थाः], @deva[अतिपन्थाः] as they do not end in @deva[पथ]; (see @ref[285])

**(c)**[^3] A collective Dwigu is *neu.*; but that ending in @deva[अ] is generally *feminine*, and that ending in @deva[आ] is optionally so in which case it takes the termination @deva[ई]; @deva[पञ्चगवं] a collection of five cows; @deva[त्रयाणां लोकानां समाहारः त्रिलोकी]; but @deva[पञ्चपात्रम्], @deva[त्रिभुवनम्], @deva[चतुर्युगम्] &c.; @deva[पञ्चानां खट्वानां समाहारः पञ्चखट्वी], @deva[पञ्चखट्वम्]. The @deva[न्] of final @deva[अन्] is dropped and the Dwigu is optionally *feminine* @deva[पञ्चतक्षी-क्षम्], (fr. @deva[पञ्च + तक्षन्] a carpenter).

**(d)**[^4] A Tatpurusha ending in @deva[उपज्ञा] and @deva[उपक्रम] is of the *neuter* gender, when the idea of @deva[प्राथम्य] 'being the first' of what is known or commenced (introduced) is meant to be expressed; @deva[पाणिनेरुपज्ञा पाणिन्युपज्ञं ग्रन्थः] the work (grammar) first taught or composed by Pāṇini. @deva[नन्दोपक्रमं द्रोणः] the *droṇa* (a measure of corn) first brought into use in the reign of King Nanda.

**(e)**[^5] A Tatpurusha ending in @deva[छाया] is *neuter* when the objects casting the shade are many; @deva[इक्षूणां इक्षुच्छायम्].

**(f)**[^6] A Tatpurusha having for its first member a synonym of @deva[राजन्] (and not @deva[राजन्] itself) or the words @deva[रक्षस्], @deva[पिशाच] &c. and @deva[सभा] for its latter member is *neuter*; as @deva[इनसभम्], @deva[ईश्वरसभम्], a king's council; but @deva[राजसभा]; @deva[रक्षःसभम्], @deva[पिशाचसभम्]; also that ending in @deva[सभा] when it means 'a multitude'; as @deva[स्त्रीसभम्] 'an assembly of women'; but @deva[धर्मसभा] in the sense of @deva[धर्मशाला].

**(g)**[^7] A Tatpurusha ending in @deva[सेना], @deva[सुरा], @deva[छाया], @deva[शाला] and @deva[निशा] is optionally *neuter*; @deva[ब्राह्मणसेना-नम्], @deva[यवसुरा-रम्] malt liquor, beer, @deva[कुड्यच्छाया-यम्], the shadow of a wall; @deva[गोशाला-लम्], @deva[श्वनिशा-शम्] (the 14th day of the dark half of a month, so called because certain dogs observe a fast on this night, according to the Sābarabhāṣya).

**N. B.** These rules hold good in the case of Tat. alone; so @deva[दृढसेनो राजा] (Bah.); @deva[असेना] (Neg. Tat.), @deva[परमसेना] (Karm.).

---

[^1]: @deva[परवल्लिङ्गं द्वन्द्वतत्पुरुषयोः ।] Pāṇ. II. 4. 26.

[^2]: @deva[द्विगुप्राप्तापन्नालंपूर्वगतिसमासेषु ।] Vārt. @deva[रात्राह्नाहाः पुंसि ।] Pāṇ. II. 4. 29. @deva[संख्यापूर्वं रात्रं क्लीबम् ।] Sid. Kau. @deva[पुण्यसुदिनाभ्यामह्नः क्लीबतेष्टा । पथः संख्याऽव्ययादेः ।] Vārtikas.

[^3]: @deva[स नपुंसकम् ।] Pāṇ. II. 4. 17. @deva[आकारान्तोत्तरपदो द्विगुः स्त्रियामिष्टः । आवन्तो वा । अनो नलोपश्च वा द्विगुः स्त्रियाम् । पात्राद्यन्तस्य न ।] Vārtikas on *ibid.*

[^4]: @deva[उपज्ञोपक्रमं तदाद्याचिख्यासायाम् ।] Pāṇ. II. 4. 21. @deva[उपज्ञा ज्ञानमाद्यं स्यात् ज्ञात्वारंभ उपक्रमः ।] Amara.

[^5]: @deva[छाया बाहुल्ये ।] Pāṇ. II. 4. 22.

[^6]: @deva[सभा राजाऽमनुष्यपूर्वा ।] Pāṇ. II. 4. 23. @deva[पर्यायस्यैवेष्यते ।] Vārt. @deva[अशाला च ।] Pāṇ. II. 4. 24. @deva[अमनुष्यशब्दो रूढ्या रक्षः पिशाचादीनाह ।] Sid. Kau.

[^7]: @deva[विभाषा सेनासुराच्छायाशालानिशानाम् ।] Pāṇ. II. 4. 25.

rules.title: Definition and Nature of Bahuvrīhi
rules.body:
## III. BAHUVRĪHI OR THE ATTRIBUTIVE COMPOUNDS.

A Bahuvrīhi compound consists of two or more nouns in apposition to each other the attributive member being placed first and denotes or refers to something else than what is expressed by its members.[^1] It generally attributes that which is expressed by its second member, determined or modified by what is denoted by its first member, to something denoted by neither of the two; e. g. @deva[महाबाहुः] 'one whose arm is great;' @deva[पीताम्बरः] 'one whose garment is yellow.' When dissolved it must have the pronoun @deva[यत्] in any one of the oblique cases; as @deva[महान् बाहुः यस्य स महाबाहुः] [@deva[नलः]]; @deva[पीतं अम्बरं यस्य स पीताम्बरः] [@deva[हरिः]]. A Bahuvrīhi compound partakes of the nature of an adjective and assumes the gender of the substantive it qualifies.

**Note**—In English such compounds are by no means rare; cf. high-souled, good-natured, narrow-minded &c.

**N. B.** The difference between a Karm. and Bah. comp. is this:—In the former, one of the member alone is in apposition to the substantive it qualifies, while in the latter the whole compound is an adjective. In the former the sense is complete in the comp. itself; in the latter it is not so; e. g. @deva[घनश्यामः नलः], here one of the members viz. @deva[श्यामः] is in apposition to @deva[नलः] and therefore the comp. is a Karm. @deva[गंभीरनादः] as a Karm. simply means @deva[गंभीरश्चासौ नादः] 'a deep sound,' and the sense is complete; as a Bah. it is equivalent to @deva[गंभीरः नादः यस्य] 'some one whose sound is deep'; here the sense is not complete unless it is known whose sound is meant.

---

[^1]: @deva[अनेकमन्यपदार्थे ।] Pāṇ. II. 2. 24. @deva[समस्यमानपदातिरिक्तस्य पदस्यार्थे इत्यर्थः ।] Tb.

rules.title: @deva[समानाधिकरण] and @deva[व्यधिकरण] Bahuvrīhi
rules.body:
Bahuvrīhi compounds are divided into two classes, @deva[समानाधिकरणबहुव्रीहि] and @deva[व्यधिकरणबहुव्रीहि].[^1]

**(a)** That is a Samānādhikaraṇa Bah. in which both the members are in apposition to each other i. e. have the same case relation when dissolved. There are six kinds of this according as the @deva[यत्] is in any one of the six oblique cases; e. g. @deva[प्राप्तं उदकं यं असौ प्राप्तोदको ग्रामः]; @deva[ऊढः रथः येन असौ ऊढरथः अनड्वान्], @deva[उपहृतः पशुः यस्मै सः उपहृतपशुः रुद्रः], @deva[उद्धृतः ओदनः यस्याः सा उद्धृतोदना स्थाली], @deva[पीतं अम्बरं अस्य स पीताम्बरो हरिः], @deva[वीराः पुरुषाः यस्मिन् स वीरपुरुषो ग्रामः ।]

---

[^1]: Strictly speaking this is not a division of the Bah. but an exception to the general rule. We have given it as a separate division to avoid confusion.

rules.title: Vyadhikaraṇa Bahuvrīhi
rules.body:
A Vyadhikaraṇa Bah. is that whose members are not in apposition to each other i. e. are in different cases when dissolved. A Vyadhikaraṇa Bah. is not allowed in any case except in the Genitive and the Locative;[^1] as @deva[चक्रं पाणौ यस्य स चक्रपाणिः हरिः], @deva[चन्द्रस्य इव कान्तिर्यस्य स चन्द्रकान्तिः];[^2] so @deva[पद्मगन्धिः], @deva[शस्त्रपाणिः], &c. @deva[शशी शेखरे यस्य असौ शशिशेखरः] &c.; but @deva[पञ्चभिर्भुक्तमस्य पञ्चभुक्तः] is not allowed.

---

[^1]: @deva[सप्तमीविशेषणे बहुव्रीहौ ।] Pāṇ. II. 2. 35. In a Bah. the noun in the Loc. and an adjectival word are placed first; @deva[अत एव ज्ञापकाद् व्यधिकरणपदो बहुव्रीहिः ।] Sid. Kau.

[^2]: This is allowed by the Vārt. '@deva[सप्तम्युपमानपूर्वपदस्योत्तरपदलोपश्च वक्तव्यः ।]' In a Bah. comp. the word following a noun in the Loc. or an *upamānapada* (a noun denoting a standard of comparison) is dropped; so this ought to be properly analysed as @deva[चन्द्रस्य कान्तिः चन्द्रकान्तिः चन्द्रकान्तिरिव कान्तिर्यस्य असौ चन्द्रकान्तिः ।] But later grammarians, such as Vāmana, Bhaṭṭoji &c., have rejected this Vārt. altogether as of no practical value.

rules.title: @deva[तद्गुणसंविज्ञान] and @deva[अतद्गुणसंविज्ञान] Bahuvrīhi
rules.body: **Obs.**—The Bah. compounds are also further divided into two kinds; @deva[तद्गुणसंविज्ञानबहुव्रीहिः] and @deva[अतद्गुणसंविज्ञानबहुव्रीहिः]. That in which the sense of the attributive member is also present is called *Tadguṇasaṃvijñāna*. @deva[पीताम्बरं हरिमाह्वय] is an instance of the first; here such a @deva[हरि] is meant as has the yellow silk garment actually on. @deva[चित्रगुं गोपं आनय] is of the other; here what is meant is herdsman only and not his variegated cows.

rules.title: Negative Particles and Prepositions in Bahuvrīhi
rules.body:
The negative particle @deva[अ] or @deva[अन्] and prepositions, may, sometimes, form Bah. compounds with substantives; the verbal derivatives used to express their sense may be optionally retained;[^1] @deva[अविद्यमानः पुत्रः यस्य स अपुत्रः]; @deva[प्रपतितानि पर्णानि यस्य स प्रपर्णः] a tree with its leaves dropped; @deva[निर्गता घृणा यस्य स निर्घृणः] ruthless; @deva[उद्गता कन्धरा यस्य स उत्कन्धरः] with the neck uplifted; @deva[विगतं जीवितं यस्य स विजीवितः] dead &c. Also @deva[अविद्यमानपुत्रः], @deva[प्रपतितपर्णः] &c.; @deva[अस्ति क्षीरं यस्याः सा अस्तिक्षीरा गौः] a milk-cow (where @deva[अस्ति] is an indeclinable meaning 'having').

---

[^1]: @deva[प्रादिभ्यो धातुजस्य वाच्यो वा चोत्तरपदलोपः । नञोऽस्त्यर्थानां वाच्यो वा चोत्तरपदलोपः ।] Vārtikas on Pāṇ. II. 2. 24.

rules.title: @deva[सह] Compounds in Bahuvrīhi
rules.body:
The particle @deva[सह] may be compounded with a noun in the Instrumental case in a Bahuvrīhi when there is equal participation in some action; in this case @deva[सह] optionally becomes @deva[स];[^1] as @deva[पुत्रेण सह सहपुत्रः] or @deva[सपुत्रः].

**(a)** @deva[सह] remains unchanged when the compound involves a blessing but is necessarily changed to @deva[स] when followed by @deva[गो] a cow, @deva[वत्स] a calf, or @deva[हल] a plough, even when a blessing is pronounced; as @deva[स्वस्ति राज्ञे सहपुत्राय], @deva[सहामात्याय], &c.; @deva[सगवे], @deva[सवत्साय], @deva[सहलाय].

---

[^1]: @deva[तेन सहेति तुल्ययोगे ।] Pāṇ. II. 2. 28. @deva[वोपसर्जनस्य । प्रकृत्याशिषि ।] Pāṇ. VI. 3. 82-83. @deva[अगोवत्सहलेष्विति वाच्यम् ।] Vārt. The restriction @deva[तुल्ययोगे] is not universal as there are instances in which there is no equal participation; e. g. @deva[सकर्मक], @deva[सलोमक], @deva[सपक्षक] &c.; hence the Vṛittikāra remarks—'@deva[प्रायिकं तुल्ययोगे इति विशेषणमन्यत्रापि समासो दृश्यते ।]' Dīkshita also says @deva[तुल्ययोगवचनं प्रायिकम् ।]

rules.title: Numeral and Indeclinable Bahuvrīhi Compounds
rules.body:
A compound of an indeclinable or a numeral or of @deva[आसस], @deva[अदूर] or @deva[अधिक] with a numeral is a Bahuvrīhi.[^1] In the formation of such compounds the final vowel except that of @deva[बहु] and @deva[गण], or the final consonant with the preceding vowel of the latter numeral and the @deva[अति] of @deva[विंशति][^2] are dropped and @deva[अ] added; @deva[दशानां समीपे ये सन्ति ते उपदशाः] 'about ten' i. e. nine or eleven; @deva[द्वौ वा त्रयो वा द्वित्राः] 'two or three'; @deva[द्वे वा त्रीणि वा द्वित्राणि]; @deva[द्विः आवृत्ता दश द्विदशाः] 'ten repeated twice i. e. twenty'; so @deva[त्रिदशाः] &c.; @deva[विंशतेः आसन्नाः आसन्नविंशाः] 'nearly twenty', @deva[त्रिंशतः अदूराः अदूरत्रिंशाः] 'not far from thirty', @deva[अधिकचत्वारिंशाः] 'more than forty'; but @deva[उपबहवः], @deva[उपगणाः].[^3] @deva[चतुर्] preceded by @deva[उप] or @deva[त्रि] does not drop any letter but simply has an @deva[अ] added to it; @deva[त्रयो वा चत्वारो वा त्रिचतुराः], @deva[चतुर्णां समीपे ये सन्ति ते उपचतुराः].

---

[^1]: @deva[संख्ययाव्ययासन्नदूराधिकसंख्याः संख्येये ।] Pāṇ. II. 2. 25.

[^2]: @deva[बहुव्रीहौ संख्येये डजबहुगणात् । तिविंशतेर्डिति ।] Pāṇ. V. 4. 75; VI. 4. 142. @deva[त्र्युपाभ्यां चतुरोऽजिष्यते ।] Vārt. under Pāṇ. V. 4. 77. (see art. @ref[284]).

[^3]: @deva[अत्र स्वरे विशेषः ।] Sid. Kau. (for the form is the same in both cases.)

rules.title: Directional Bahuvrīhi Compounds
rules.body:
Names of directions may form a Bahuvrīhi compound and signify the point of direction between them;[^1] @deva[दक्षिणस्याः पूर्वस्याश्च दिशोऽन्तरालं दक्षिणपूर्वा]; so @deva[उत्तरपूर्वा], &c. But if the words so compounded are not the names of quarters, no compound is possible; as @deva[ऐन्द्र्याश्च कौबेर्याश्चान्तरालं दिक्] the point between the East and the North, and not @deva[ऐन्द्रीकौबेरी] as these are not the names of the Eastern and Northern quarters.

---

[^1]: @deva[दिङ्नामान्यन्तराले ।] Pāṇ. II. 2. 26.

rules.title: Phonological Changes at End of Bahuvrīhi
rules.body:
The following words drop their final vowel or the final consonant with the preceding vowel and take @deva[अ] when at the end of a Bah. compound:—

**(a)**[^1] @deva[अक्षि] and @deva[सक्थि] 'both meaning parts of the body'; @deva[जलजवत् अक्षिणी यस्य स जलजाक्षः] 'one whose eyes are like lotuses'; @deva[दीर्घे सक्थिनी यस्य स दीर्घसक्थः] 'one having long thighs', 'spindlelegged'; @deva[कमले इव अक्षिणी यस्याः सा कमलाक्षी] (@deva[स्त्री]); but @deva[दीर्घसक्थि शकटम्] 'a cart with long poles'; @deva[स्थूलाक्षा वेणुयष्टिः] 'a bamboo stick with big eyelike holes'; (where @deva[अ] is added by @ref[282] (c) and hence the *feminine* ends in @deva[आ]; see N. B. For @deva[सक्थि] see also (e) below.

**N. B.** The *fem.* of Bah. compounds ending in @deva[अक्ष] is formed by adding @deva[आ] when it qualifies an inanimate object.

**(b)**[^2] @deva[अङ्गुलि], when the compound is an attribute of @deva[दारु]; @deva[पञ्च अङ्गुलयो यस्य तत्पञ्चाङ्गुलं दारु] (@deva[अङ्गुलिसदृशावयवं धान्यादिविक्षेपणकाष्ठम्]); but @deva[पञ्चाङ्गुलिः हस्तः] the hand having five fingers.

**(c)**[^3] The words @deva[मूर्धन्] preceded by @deva[द्वि] or @deva[त्रि], @deva[लोमन्] preceded by @deva[अन्तर्] and @deva[बहिः], and @deva[नेतृ] used in apposition to the name of a constellation of stars; @deva[द्वौ मूर्धानौ यस्य स द्विमूर्धः] two-headed; @deva[त्रिमूर्धः]; but @deva[दशमूर्धा]; @deva[अन्तर्लोमः]; @deva[बहिर्लोमः]; @deva[मृगो नेता यासां ताः मृगनेत्रा रात्रयः] 'nights of which the *Mṛiga* constellation is the leader' i. e. 'whose position in the heavens marks their advance;' so @deva[पुष्यनेत्राः] &c.

**(d)**[^4] *Feminine* words ending in a termination showing 'a complement of,' and the word @deva[प्रमाणी]; e. g. @deva[कल्याणी पञ्चमी यासां रात्रीणां ताः कल्याणीपञ्चमा रात्रयः]; 'nights whose complement is an auspicious fifth night.' @deva[स्त्री प्रमाणी यस्य असौ स्त्रीप्रमाणः] 'one whose authority is a woman.'

**(e)**[^5] @deva[हलि] and @deva[सक्थि] optionally become @deva[हल] and @deva[सक्थ] when preceded by @deva[अ], @deva[दुस्] or @deva[सु]; @deva[अहलः-लिः] having no plough; @deva[असक्थः-] 'one who has no thighs,' @deva[दुःसक्थः-क्थिः] 'one having deformed thighs'; @deva[सुसक्थः-क्थिः]; &c. @deva[शक्ति] is another reading for @deva[सक्थि] in the sūtra; so @deva[अशक्तः-क्तिः], &c.

**(f)**[^6] @deva[प्रजा] and @deva[मेधा] under similar circumstances drop their @deva[आ] and add @deva[अस्]; as @deva[अविद्यमाना प्रजा यस्य असौ अप्रजाः]; having no progeny, @deva[दुष्टा प्रजा यस्य स दुष्प्रजाः], having bad progeny, @deva[शोभना मेधा यस्य स सुमेधाः] of good intellect; similarly @deva[दुर्मेधाः], @deva[अमेधाः].

---

[^1]: @deva[बहुव्रीहौ सक्थ्यक्ष्णोः स्वाङ्गात्षच् ।] Pāṇ. V. 4. 113.

[^2]: @deva[अङ्गुलेर्दारुणि ।] Pāṇ. V. 4. 114.

[^3]: @deva[द्वित्रिभ्यां ष मूर्ध्नः । अन्तर्बहिर्भ्यां च लोम्नः ।] Pāṇ. V. 4. 115, 117. @deva[नेतुर्नक्षत्रे अब्वक्तव्यः ।] Vārt.

[^4]: @deva[अप्पूरणीप्रमाण्योः ।] Pāṇ. V. 4. 116.

[^5]: @deva[नञ्दुःसुभ्यो हलिसक्थ्योरन्यतरस्याम् ।] Pāṇ. V. 4. 121. @deva[शक्त्योरिति पाठान्तरम् ।] Sid. Kau.

[^6]: @deva[नित्यमसिच् प्रजामेधयोः ।] Pāṇ. V. 4. 122.

rules.title: Transformations of @deva[धर्म], @deva[धनुष्], @deva[जम्भ], and @deva[ईर्म]
rules.body:
**(a)**[^1] @deva[धर्म] when preceded by a single member in a Bahuvrīhi becomes @deva[धर्मन्]; @deva[कल्याणं धर्मः यस्य स कल्याणधर्मा]; similarly @deva[समानधर्मा] (see Māl. Māḍ. Act. I. Intro.); but @deva[परमः स्वः धर्मः यस्य स परमस्वधर्मः]; @deva[परमस्वधर्मा] may also be correct if @deva[परमस्व] be regarded as one word compounded in a Karmadhāraya. @deva[संदिग्धसाध्यधर्मा], @deva[निवृत्तिधर्मा], @deva[अनुच्छित्तिधर्मा] are to be similarly explained.

**(b)** @deva[धनुष्] at the end of a Bah. becomes @deva[धन्वन्]; as @deva[अधिज्यं धनुर्यस्य सः अधिज्यधन्वा] 'one whose bow is strung'; so @deva[शार्ङ्गधन्वा] (@deva[शृङ्गस्य इदं शार्ङ्गं]) 'one whose bow is made of horn'; i. e. the god Vishṇu. This change is optional when the whole compound is a name; @deva[शतधन्वा-नुः].

**(c)** Similarly @deva[जम्भ] 'a tooth', 'food, &c. becomes @deva[जम्भन्] when preceded by @deva[सु], @deva[हरित], @deva[तृण] or @deva[सोम]; as @deva[शोभनः जम्भः अस्य सुजम्भा] one having beautiful teeth; similarly @deva[हरितजम्भा] m.; @deva[तृणं भक्ष्यं यस्य, तृणमिव दन्ता यस्येति वा तृणजम्भा], @deva[सोमजम्भा] 'one whose food is the holy *soma* juice'; but @deva[पतितजम्भः].

**(d)** The word @deva[ईर्म] n. a wound, preceded by @deva[दक्षिण] becomes @deva[ईर्मन्] when the wound is inflicted by a hunter; @deva[दक्षिणे ईर्म यस्य दक्षिणेर्मा मृगः] a stag wounded on the right side by a hunter. See Bhaṭṭi. IV. 44.

---

[^1]: @deva[धर्मादनिच् केवलात् ।] Pāṇ. V. 4. 124. @deva[धनुषश्च । वा संज्ञायाम् । जम्भा सुहरिततृणसोमेभ्यः । दक्षिणेर्मा लुब्धयोगे ।] Pāṇ. V. 4. 132, 133, 125, 126.

rules.title: Transformations of @deva[जानु], @deva[जाया], @deva[गन्ध], and @deva[नासिका]
rules.body:
At the end of a Bah. compound—

**(a)**[^1] @deva[जानु] is changed to @deva[ज्ञु] necessarily when preceded by @deva[प्र] or @deva[सम्] and optionally when preceded by @deva[ऊर्ध्व]; @deva[प्रगते जानुनी यस्य स प्रज्ञुः] 'one having the knees wide apart' i. e. 'bandylegged'; @deva[संज्ञुः] 'one having well-turned or beautiful knees'; @deva[ऊर्ध्वजानुः-ज्ञुः]; 'long-shanked'.

**(b)**[^2] @deva[जाया] becomes @deva[जानि]; @deva[युवती जाया यस्य स युवजानिः] 'one whose wife is young;' @deva[भूजानिः] lit. one whose wife is the earth; i. e. 'a king', &c.

**(c)**[^3] @deva[गन्ध] becomes @deva[गन्धि] when preceded by @deva[उत्], @deva[पूति] or @deva[सु]; @deva[उद्गतः गन्धः यस्य स उद्गन्धिः] 'whose smell is spread above,' @deva[पूतिगन्धिः] 'having a repulsive smell', @deva[सुगन्धिः]. This change of @deva[गन्ध] is possible only when the smell referred to is inseparably connected with (looks like a part and parcel of) the object denoted by the other member; as @deva[सुगन्धि पुष्पं, सलिलं च] (which receives its odour from the lotuses &c. growing in it); @deva[सुगन्धिवायुः]; but @deva[शोभना गन्धा अस्य सुगन्ध आपणिकः] 'a perfumer dealing in sweet smells.' @deva[गन्ध] is also changed to @deva[गन्धि][^4] when it means 'a particle of', 'a little of,' or when the compound involves comparison; as @deva[सूपस्य गन्धः यस्मिन् तत् सूपगन्धि भोजनम्]; so @deva[घृतगन्धि] a dinner in which there is a scanty supply of ghee, &c.; @deva[पद्मस्य इव गन्धः यस्य तत् पद्मगन्धि] 'that which has the smell of a lotus.'

**(d)**[^5] @deva[नासिका] becomes @deva[नस] when it is preceded by a preposition or when the compound is used as a distinguishing name and it is preceded by any word except @deva[स्थूल]; @deva[उन्नता नासिका यस्य स उन्नसः] 'one having a prominent nose,' @deva[प्रणसः] 'one having a good nose,' @deva[द्रुरिव नासिका यस्य द्रुणसः][^6] 'one whose nose is like a tree,' 'large-nosed;' but @deva[स्थूलनासिकः]. @deva[नस] becomes @deva[नस्] optionally when preceded by @deva[खुर] or @deva[खर]; as @deva[खुरणसः] or @deva[खुरणाः] 'having a nose like a horse's hoof i. e. flat;' @deva[खरणसः-णाः] 'sharp-nosed.' @deva[नासिका] when preceded by @deva[वि] becomes @deva[ग्र] or @deva[ख्य]; as @deva[विगता नासिका यस्य स विग्रः] or @deva[विख्यः] 'one having a deformed nose.'

---

[^1]: @deva[प्रसंभ्यां जानुनोर्ज्ञुः । ऊर्ध्वाद्विभाषा ।] Pāṇ. V. 4. 129, 130.

[^2]: @deva[जायाया निङ् ।] Pāṇ. V. 4. 134. @deva[लोपो व्योर्वलि ।] Pāṇ. VI. 1. 66. @deva[जाया] at the end of a Bah. substitutes @deva[नि] for its final @deva[आ]. The preceding @deva[य्] or @deva[व्] is dropped before a consonant except @deva[य्].

[^3]: @deva[गन्धस्येदुत्पूतिसुसुरभिभ्यः ।] Pāṇ. V. 4. 135. @deva[गन्धस्येत्वे तदेकान्तग्रहणम् ।] Vārt. There is a difference of opinion among critics as to the meaning of the Vārt. @deva[गन्धस्य] &c. Some hold that the smell must be the natural property of a thing to necessitate the final @deva[इ]. Cf. Jayamaṅgala on Bhaṭṭi. @deva[आघ्रायि वान्गन्धवहः सुगन्धः] &c. II. 10, and Mallinātha on Rag. IV. 45. But the view of such eminent grammarians as Kaiyaṭa, Bhaṭṭoji, Nagesha, &c. is as given above.

[^4]: @deva[अल्पाख्यायाम् । उपमानाच्च ।] Pāṇ. V. 4. 136-137.

[^5]: @deva[अत्र नासिकायाः संज्ञायां नसं चास्थूलात् । उपसर्गाच्च ।] Pāṇ. V. 4. 118. 119. @deva[वेर्ग्रो वक्तव्यः । ख्यश्च ।] Vārtikas.

[^6]: @deva[पूर्वपदात्संज्ञायामगः । उपसर्गाद्बहुलम् ।] Pāṇ. VIII. 4. 3. 28.

rules.title: Loss of Final Vowel: @deva[पाद], @deva[दन्त], @deva[ककुद्], @deva[काकुद]
rules.body:
The following words lose their final vowel when at the end of a Bahuvrīhi:—

**(a)**[^1] The word @deva[पाद] when it is preceded by a numeral or @deva[सु] or when the compound involves comparison and it is not preceded by a word of the @deva[हस्त्यादि] group (@deva[हस्तिन्], @deva[अज], @deva[कुसूल], @deva[अश्व], @deva[कपोत], @deva[जाल], @deva[गण्ड], @deva[दासी], @deva[गणिका] and some others). @deva[द्वौ पादौ यस्य द्विपात्] a biped; @deva[सुपात्] fair-footed; (@deva[व्याघ्रस्य इव पादौ यस्य],) &c. but @deva[हस्तिपादः], @deva[कुसूलपादः], &c.
