A Bah.[^1] ending in @deva[पाद्] ( substituted for @deva[पाद] ) optionally forms its *fem.* in @deva[ई] before which it is changed to @deva[पद्]; @deva[व्याघ्रस्य इव पादौ यस्याः सा व्याघ्रपाद्-पदी], @deva[द्विपाद्-पदी] and in @deva[आ] when @deva[पाद्] means 'a foot of a Vedic verse'; @deva[द्विपदा ऋक्], @deva[एकपदा] &c.

**(a)** But if @deva[पाद्] be preceded by one of the words @deva[कुम्भ], @deva[शूल], @deva[तृण], @deva[हंस], @deva[काक], @deva[कृष्ण], @deva[सूकर], &c. the *fem.* is necessarily formed in @deva[ई], @deva[पाद्] changing into @deva[पद्] as before; @deva[कुम्भपदी] 'a woman whose feet are as big as a pitcher.'

**(b)** In other cases the *fem.* of *prâtipadikas* ending in @deva[पाद्] is formed by adding @deva[आ]; @deva[हस्तिपादा], @deva[अजपादा], &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[पादोऽन्यतरस्याम्] । @deva[टाबृचि] । Pân. IV. 1. 8, 9.

rules.title: Feminine of Dwigu Compounds
rules.body:
[^1] A Dwigu ending in @deva[अ] forms its *fem.* in @deva[ई]; as @deva[त्रिलोकी]; but if the ending word be one of those included in the Ajâdi group ( see foot-note on p. 108 ) its *fem.* is formed in @deva[आ]; @deva[त्रिफला], @deva[त्र्यनीका] ( consisting of three battalions ) @deva[सेना], &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[द्विगोः] । @deva[अपरिमाणविस्ताचितकम्बल्येभ्यो न तद्धितलुकि] । Pân. IV. 1. 21. 22.

rules.title: Dwigu with Measurement Words
rules.body:
**(a)** A Dwigu ending in @deva[काण्ड][^1] ( a particular measure ) and qualifying a word denoting 'a field' has its *fem.* formed by the addition of @deva[आ], but when a Taddhita affix has been first added to it and then dropped; as @deva[द्वे काण्डे प्रमाणं यस्याः असौ द्विकाण्ड+मात्रा=द्विकाण्डा क्षेत्रभक्ति] 'a piece of land 30 hands in extent'; but @deva[द्विकाण्डी रज्जुः] 'a rope, 30 hands in length'; also when the ending word is one that does not denote a measure, except the words @deva[विस्त] 'a tola', @deva[आचित] 'the load of a cart,' and @deva[कंबल्य] ( a weight equal to 3⅓ tolas ); @deva[पञ्चभिरश्वैः क्रीता पञ्चाश्वा], @deva[द्वौ विस्तौ पचतीति द्विविस्ता स्थाली]; so @deva[द्व्याचिता], @deva[द्विकंबल्या].

**(b)**[^2] When the word @deva[पुरुष] expressive of measurement ends a Dwigu and the Taddhita affix is added and dropped as before, its *fem.* is formed both in @deva[आ] and @deva[ई]; @deva[द्वौ पुरुषौ प्रमाणं अस्याः द्विपुरुषा-षी परिखा] 'a ditch two purushas ( 13 feet ) in depth'.

---

[^1]: @deva[काण्डान्तात्क्षेत्रे] । Pân. IV. 1. 23.

[^2]: @deva[पुरुषात्प्रमाणेऽन्यतरस्याम्] । Pân. IV. 1. 24.

rules.title: Feminine of Participles and Adjectives
rules.body: Participles ( those of the Pres. and Fut. ) of Parasm. roots take @deva[ई] in the *fem.*, @deva[न्] being inserted before @deva[त्] as in the Nom. or Acc. dual of the *Neu.* ( see @ref[116] ) and so do adjectives ending in a consonant; @deva[पचन्ती]; @deva[याती-न्ती], @deva[शासती], @deva[ददती], @deva[दीव्यन्ती], @deva[महती], &c.

rules.title: Introduction to Kṛit and Taddhita Affixes
rules.body:
# Chapter IX. Secondary Nominal Bases Derived by the Addition of the Taddhita or Secondary Affixes

The terminations used to form derivative bases, in Sanskrit are distinguished into two classes, (1) *Krit* ( @deva[कृत्] ) or Primary Affixes and (2) *Taddhita* ( @deva[तद्धित] ) or Secondary affixes. Krit are those affixes that are added to verbs, and the Nominal Bases formed by their means are called PRIMARY NOMINAL BASES; while TADDHITA affixes are those that are added to substantives, primary or derived from roots, and the bases formed with them are called SECONDARY NOMINAL BASES ( vide @ref[179] ).

rules.title: Scope of Chapter on Taddhita Affixes
rules.body: In this chapter we will treat of the more general secondary nominal bases formed by means of the Taddhita affixes, reserving for a future chapter the formation of the primary nominal bases derived by means of the Kṛit affixes from roots.

rules.title: General Rules for Taddhita Affixes
rules.body:
The Taddhita affixes are added in various senses. They occasion various changes in the words to which they are added. The following general observations should be paid attention to.

**(a)** As a general rule the first vowel of a word takes its Vriddhi substitute before the terminations @deva[अ], @deva[य], @deva[इक], @deva[ईन], @deva[एय], @deva[त्य]. &c.; as @deva[अश्वपति + अ = आश्वपति + अ].

**(b)** Before terminations beginning with a vowel or @deva[य] (1) the final @deva[अ], @deva[आ], @deva[इ], and @deva[ई] are rejected; (2) @deva[उ] and @deva[ऊ] take their Guṇa substitute; (3) @deva[ओ] and @deva[औ] obey the ordinary rules of sandhi; @deva[आश्वपति + अ = आश्वपत] 'belonging to Asvapati,' &c. *m. n.*; @deva[मनु + अ = मानवः] 'a descendant of Manu'; @deva[गो + य = गव्यं] 'belonging to a cow', so @deva[नाव्यं] fr. @deva[नौ] &c.

**(c)** In the case of derivatives from compound words sometimes the initial vowel of the second word takes its Vriddhi substitute, and sometimes the Vriddhi is double; @deva[पूर्ववार्षिक] 'belonging to the last year'; similarly @deva[सुपांचालकः] &c. @deva[सौहार्दं] fr. @deva[सुहृद्], @deva[सौभाग्य] from @deva[सुभग], &c. When these terminations are added to a Dwa. comp. both the words of which are the names of deities, Vriddhi is substituted for the initial vowel of both; @deva[आग्निमारुतं कर्म] 'a sacrifice offered to Agni and the Marut deities,' &c.

**(d)** If the initial vowel of a word be preceded by the @deva[य्] and @deva[व्] of a preposition the @deva[य्] or @deva[व्] is first changed to @deva[इय्] or @deva[उव्] before Vriddhi substitute can take place; as @deva[व्याकरण+अ=वियाकरण+अ=वैयाकरणः]; @deva[स्वश्व+अ=सुवश्व+अ=सौवश्व]; similarly @deva[सौवस्तिक] from @deva[स्वस्ति], @deva[सौवर] fr. @deva[स्वर], &c.

**(e)** Before consonantal Tad. affixes, a final @deva[न्] is generally rejected; the final @deva[न्] with the preceding vowel is sometimes dropped before vowel terminations and before such as begin with @deva[य]; @deva[युवन्-युवत्वं], @deva[राजन्-राजकं], &c. @deva[आत्मन्-आत्म्य-आत्मीय]. There are various exceptions to this latter part of the rule; *e. g.* @deva[राजन्य] fr @deva[राजन्] &c.

*N. B.*—Other changes the student will easily note from the instances given.

rules.title: List of Common Taddhita Affixes - Section I: Miscellaneous Affixes
rules.body:
The following is a list of such of the Taddhita affixes as are commonly to be met with.

## Section I. Miscellaneous Affixes

### @deva[अ]

is added in the sense of:—

**(1)** 'the son of'; as @deva[उपगोः अपत्यं पुमान् औपगवः] 'the son of Upagu'; so @deva[वासुदेवः] from @deva[वसुदेव]; @deva[पर्वतस्य अपत्यं स्त्री पार्वती] 'the daughter of the mountain,' &c.

**(2)** 'the descendant of'; as @deva[उत्सस्य गोत्रापत्यं पुमान् औत्सः] 'a descendant of Utsa', @deva[उत्सस्य गोत्रापत्यं स्त्री औत्सी] 'a female descendant of Utsa', ( vide @ref[311], @ref[313] );

**(3)** 'dyed with,' @deva[हरिद्रया रक्तं हारिद्रं वसनं] 'a garment dyed with turmeric';

**(4)** 'made of,' @deva[देवदारोर्विकारः दैवदारवः] 'made of the fir tree;'

**(5)** 'belonging to,' &c; @deva[देवस्य अयं दैवः] 'belonging to a god;' @deva[शर्कराया इदं शार्करं] 'of sand'; @deva[ऊर्णाया इदं और्णं वस्त्रं] 'a woolen garment,' @deva[ग्रैष्मः] 'belonging to the sultry season'; @deva[नैशः] 'nocturnal;' @deva[सांवत्सरः] 'yearly' &c.; when added to @deva[हेमन्त] the final @deva[त] is dropped, @deva[हैमनः] 'autumnal,' ( vide Sis. VI. 65; Kir. XVII. 12 ). @deva[हैमन्तः] means 'agreeable in the autumnal season;'

**(6)** 'lord of'; @deva[पृथिव्या ईश्वरः पार्थिवः] 'the lord of the earth'; @deva[पञ्चालानां स्वामी पाञ्चालः] 'the king of the Panchâlas'; @deva[ऐक्ष्वाकः][^1] 'the king of the Ikshvâku race',

**(7)** 'a collection of'; @deva[काकानां समूहः काकं]; @deva[बकानां समूहः बाकं] 'a flock of cranes'; similarly @deva[मायूरं] from @deva[मयूर] 'a peacock,' @deva[कापोतं] from @deva[कपोत] 'a pigeon', @deva[भिक्षाणां समूहो भैक्षम्]; @deva[गर्भिणीनां समूहो गार्भिणम्] &c.

**(8)** 'knowing or studying'; @deva[व्याकरणं अधीते वेद वा वैयाकरणः] 'one who studies grammar, grammarian', &c.

**(9)** and to form abstract nouns; @deva[मुनेः भावः मौनं] 'silence', @deva[युवन् यौवनं] 'youth;' @deva[सुहृद्-सौहार्दं] 'friendship'; @deva[पृथोर्भावः पार्थवं] 'greatness, width,' &c.

### @deva[अक]

forms derivatives with various significations:—

**(1)** @deva[उष्ट्रे भवः औष्ट्रकः] 'produced from or relating to a camel,' @deva[ग्रीष्मे भवः ग्रैष्मकः] 'produced in the hot season,'

**(2)** @deva[कुलालेन कृतं कौलालकं] 'made by a potter,' @deva[ब्रह्मणा कृतं ब्राह्मकं] 'made by Brahman,'

**(3)** @deva[आरण्यकः] 'a forester,' 'a wild man',

**(4)** @deva[राज्ञां योग्यं राजन्यकं] 'a place fit for kings to live in'; @deva[मानुष्यकं] 'a country fit for men to live in' @deva[कुरुषु जातः कौरवकः] ( also @deva[कौरवः][^2] ) 'an inhabitant of Kuru'; @deva[युगन्धरेषु जातः यौगन्धरकः] ( also @deva[यौगन्धरः][^2] ) 'inhabiting Yugandhara';

**(6)** @deva[पथि जातं पन्थकं] 'grown on a way';

**(7)** @deva[पन्थानं गच्छतीति पथिकः] 'a traveller';

**(8)** @deva[पूर्वाह्णे भवः पूर्वाह्णिकः] 'happening in the forenoon'; similarly @deva[अपराह्णिकः] 'happening in the afternoon';

**(9)** @deva[पुरुष] in different senses; @deva[पौरुषेयः] 'man-slaughter', 'human work', 'derived from or incidental to man, composed or propounded by man'; and

**(10)** to @deva[पथिन्], @deva[अतिथि], @deva[वसति] and @deva[स्वपति] in the sense of 'useful in, good for'; @deva[पथि साधु पाथेयं] 'what is useful on the way', i. e. 'provisions for a journey'; @deva[अतिथिषु साधुः आतिथेयः] 'attentive to guests, hospitable'; @deva[वसतौ साधुः वासतेयः] 'hospitable',—@deva[यी रात्रिः]; @deva[स्वपते आगतं स्वपतेयं] ( @deva[धनं] ) 'wealth, property'; vide Kir. XIV. 8.

### @deva[क] ( @deva[कन्] )

—is affixed

**(1)** to words expressive of countries in the sense of 'born or produced in'; @deva[मद्रकः] 'born or produced in the Madra country';

**(2)** to @deva[पीत] in the sense of 'dyed with'; @deva[पीतकः] 'dyed yellow',

**(3)** in the sense of 'belonging to'; @deva[मत्कः], @deva[त्वत्कः], &c.

**(4)** 'bought for' @deva[पञ्चकः] 'bought for five rupees';

**(5)** in the sense of 'acting' @deva[शीतकः] 'one who is cold' i. e. 'slow in action,' 'a dilatory or lazy man;' @deva[उष्णकः] 'an active man';

**(6. 7. 8.)** to express pity or diminution, or depreciation—@deva[पुत्रकः] 'poor son', @deva[देवदत्तकः] 'unhappy Devadatta'; @deva[ह्रस्वो वृक्षो वृक्षकः], 'a small or stunted tree'; @deva[अश्वकः] a bad horse, a hack; @deva[शूद्रकः] 'a wicked Sudra,'

**(9)** and sometimes with no signification; @deva[अविकः] i. e. @deva[अविः] 'a ram' @deva[मणिकः] 'a jewel', @deva[बालकः] 'a young boy'; &c.

### @deva[कट] ( @deva[कटच्] )

—is affixed

**(1)** to words denoting names of beasts, in the sense of 'a collection of'; @deva[अविकटं] 'a flock of sheep' &c.

**(2)** and in various senses to the prepositions @deva[सं], @deva[प्र], @deva[वि], @deva[नि] and @deva[उत्]; @deva[संकट] 'narrow, impassable, crowded' &c.; @deva[प्रकट] 'manifest,; @deva[विकट] 'huge, fierce, large', &c; @deva[निकट] 'near, close to' &c.; @deva[उत्कट] 'large, excessive, powerful' &c.

### @deva[कट्या]

—@deva[रथकट्या] 'a number of chariots'

### @deva[कल्प], @deva[देश्य] and @deva[देशीय] ( @deva[कल्पप्], @deva[देश्य], @deva[देशीयर्], )

—are added to express 'equality with, little inferiority to'; @deva[विदुषः ईषन्न्यून], @deva[विद्वत्कल्पः—देश्यः—देशीयः] 'almost learned'; @deva[कुमारकल्पः] 'nearly equal to Kumâra in valour'; @deva[कविकल्पः], @deva[मृतकल्प] 'nearly dead', &c.; these are also added to verbs; @deva[पचतिकल्पं] 'cooks tolerably well'.

### @deva[चण] ( @deva[चणप्] ), @deva[चुञ्चु] ( @deva[चुञ्चुप्] )

are added in the sense of 'reputed or remarkable for'; as @deva[विद्यया वित्तः–विद्याचणः] 'remarkable or known for one's knowledge'; @deva[अस्त्रचुञ्चुः]–'renowned for his skill in the use of weapons' ( vide Bhaṭṭi II. 32. )

### @deva[तन] ( @deva[ट्यु], @deva[ट्युल्] )

—is added to adverbs of time in the senses of relating or belonging to,' @deva[सायं भवः सायंतनः], @deva[अद्यतनः], @deva[ह्यस्तनः], @deva[प्राह्णेतन], @deva[दिवातनः], @deva[दोषातनः], @deva[चिरंतनः], @deva[सनातनः],—to @deva[प्र]; as @deva[प्रतनः] old,—to the word @deva[नव] changed to @deva[नू]; @deva[नूतनः].

### @deva[तर] ( @deva[तरप्] )

—expresses diminution; @deva[गोणीतरा] 'a small sack,' @deva[वत्सतरः] 'a young calf', &c.

### @deva[त्न]

—is similarly added to @deva[चिर], @deva[परुत्] 'last year', @deva[परारि] 'the year before the last', @deva[प्र] and @deva[नव]; @deva[चिरत्नं], @deva[परुत्नं], @deva[परारित्नं], @deva[प्रत्नं] and @deva[नूत्नं].

### @deva[ता] ( @deva[तल्] )

—forms abstract nouns @deva[स्त्रीता], @deva[पुंस्ता], @deva[समता], &c.; added to @deva[ग्राम], @deva[जन], @deva[बन्धु], @deva[सहाय], and @deva[गज] it has the sense of 'a collection of;' @deva[ग्रामता], @deva[जनता], @deva[बन्धुता], &c.

### @deva[तिथ]

—@deva[बहुतिथ] 'manifold'.

### @deva[त्य] ( @deva[त्यक्] )

—is added in the sense of 'living in, belonging to,' &c. to the words @deva[दक्षिणा], @deva[पश्चात्], @deva[पुरस्], @deva[अमा], @deva[इह], @deva[क्व], @deva[ह्यस्], @deva[श्वस्], and indeclinables ending in @deva[तस्]; @deva[दाक्षिणात्यः] a southerner, @deva[पाश्चात्यः], @deva[पौरस्त्यः], an inhabitant of the east; @deva[अमात्य], one who accompanies a king, a minister, @deva[इहत्यः], @deva[क्वत्यः], @deva[ह्यस्त्य], @deva[ततस्त्यः] &c ; also to the preposition @deva[नि], @deva[नित्यः] 'eternal'.

### @deva[त्यक] ( @deva[त्यकन्] )

is added to @deva[उप] and @deva[अधि]; @deva[उपत्यका] land at the foot of a mountain, @deva[अधित्यका] 'a table-land.'

### @deva[त्रा]

—is affixed to @deva[गो] only: @deva[गवां समूहो गोत्रा] *f.* 'a herd of kine'.

### @deva[त्व]

—forms abstract nouns; @deva[गोत्वं].

### @deva[दघ्न], @deva[द्वयस] and @deva[मात्र][^11] ( @deva[दघ्नच्], @deva[द्वयसच्], @deva[मात्रच्], )

are added in the sense of 'measuring as much as'; @deva[जानु प्रमाणं अस्य जानुदघ्नं–द्वयसं–मात्रं उदकं] 'water reaching as far as the knee', &c.

### @deva[ण] and @deva[न] ( @deva[नञ्], @deva[स्नञ्] )[^12]

—are added to @deva[स्त्री] and @deva[पुंस्] respectively in different senses:—@deva[स्त्रैण] 'womanly, *feminine*, suited to women, ( *n* ) womenhood' &c ; @deva[पौंस्न] 'manly, heroic, fit for a man, ( *n.* ) manhood, virility'.

### @deva[पाश]

—is added as a depreciatory termination; @deva[भिषक्पाशः] 'a bad doctor, a quack'; @deva[वैयाकरणपाशः] &c ; added to @deva[केश] it has the sense of 'a collection of', as @deva[केशपाशः] ( @deva[दक्ष] and @deva[हस्त] are also added to @deva[केश] in the same sense ).

### @deva[मय] ( @deva[मयट्] )

—is added in the sense of ( 1 )[^13] 'made of'; @deva[मृदः विकारः मृन्मयं] 'made of earth,' @deva[काष्ठमयं] 'made of wood' &c.; and ( 2 ) in that of profusion or excess' @deva[घृतं प्रचुरं] @deva[यस्मिन् घृतमयो यज्ञः] 'a sacrifice consisting for the most part of clarified butter,' @deva[अन्नमयः] &c. It is not added to words denoting 'an article of food or a covering'; *e. g.* @deva[मौद्गः सूपः].

### @deva[य] ( @deva[यत्], @deva[यञ्], @deva[ण्य] )

—is added to nouns with different meanings:—( 1 ) @deva[गवां समूहो गव्या] *f.* 'a herd of cattle.' @deva[वातानां समूहो वात्या], so @deva[खल्या], @deva[रथ्या], ( @deva[रथानां समूह] ), @deva[पाश्या], @deva[धूम्या], 'a dense mass of smoke,' @deva[तृण्या], @deva[नड्या], &c ( 2 ) @deva[सभायां साधुः सभ्यः] a 'courtier'; ( 3 ) @deva[सतीर्थ्या] 'disciples of the same preceptor,' @deva[सोदर्य], @deva[समानोदर्य] 'a brother of whole blood'; ( 4 ) forms abstract nouns @deva[राज्य], @deva[सैनापत्यं], @deva[पौरोहित्यं], @deva[सारथ्यं], @deva[आस्तिक्यं], &c.; it is added—( 5 ) to the words @deva[राजन्] and @deva[मनु] in the sense of 'born of the race of.' @deva[राजन्य] 'a man of the Kshatriya class,' @deva[मनोर्जात]. @deva[मनुष्य]. ( in this case @deva[ष्] is inserted ) 'a man;'—( 6 ) to @deva[श्वशुर] in the sense of 'the son of,' @deva[श्वाशुर्यः], ( 7 ) to @deva[कुल]; @deva[कुल्य]–'of noble descent;' ( 8 ) to @deva[वायु], @deva[ऋतु], @deva[पितृ], and @deva[उषस्] in the sense of 'having any of these for one's presiding or tutelary deity,' &c. @deva[वायुः देवता अस्य वायव्यं अस्त्रं] 'a missile having Vâyu for its presiding deity,' @deva[ऋतव्यः] 'worshipping the Seasons ( as divinities ),' @deva[पित्र्य]. 'sacred to the manes, offered to the manes'; @deva[उषस्यः] 'sacred to the Dawn;'—( 9 ) to @deva[दण्ड] and words included under the @deva[दण्डादि] group in the sense of 'deserving or meriting'; @deva[दण्ड्य] 'deserving punishment,' @deva[वध्यं] 'fit to be killed,; @deva[अर्घ्य] 'deserving worship,' &c. In the derivatives given hereafter @deva[य] should be considered as added in the sense attached to each word;—@deva[स्तेय] 'theft' from @deva[स्तेन], @deva[उरस्य] 'born of the breast' ( also @deva[औरसः] fr. @deva[उरस् + अ] ); @deva[दन्त्यं] 'wholesome to the teeth' ( in this sense it is added to words denoting the limbs of the body; as @deva[कण्ठ्य] 'good for the neck,' &c. ); @deva[शुनं-शुन्यं] 'fit for a dog' fr. @deva[श्वन्]; @deva[नाभ्यं] fit for being the central part of a wheel' fr. @deva[नाभि] 'the nave of a wheel;' @deva[नस्य] 'fit for the nose' from @deva[नासिका]; @deva[रथ्य] 'drawing a chariot, a horse,' @deva[युग्य] 'harnessed to the yoke, a bull'; @deva[वयस्य] 'of equal age, a friend'; @deva[तुल्य] 'what is weighed in a balance and found equal', hence 'equal,' fr. @deva[तुला]; @deva[न्याय्य] ( @deva[न्यायादनपेतं] ) just; @deva[पथ्यं] ( @deva[पथि साधु] ) 'wholesome;' @deva[हृद्यं] ( @deva[हृदि स्पृश्यते मनोज्ञत्वात्] ) 'agreeable to the heart', @deva[धन्यः] ( @deva[धनं लब्धा] ) obtaining wealth, @deva[धर्म्यं] ( @deva[धर्मादनपेतं लब्धा वा] ) 'consistent with *dharma*', or 'obtained justly'; @deva[जन्यं] 'talk of the people,' @deva[वश्य] 'capable of being controlled, obedient', &c. @deva[द्रव्य] ( @deva[द्रोर्विकार] ) 'wooden or of a tree,; @deva[मूल्यं] ( @deva[मूलेनानाम्यं] Pâṇ. IV. 4. 49. ) 'price'; &c @deva[यशस्यः] ( @deva[यशसा युतः] ) 'glorious, leading to glory'; ( @deva[नाव्यं नावा तार्ये] ) 'fit to be crossed over in a boat'; @deva[धुर्यः] ( @deva[धुरं वहतीति] 'a horse or bullock yoked to the pole of a carriage'; @deva[गव्यं] ( @deva[गवे हितं] ) 'proper or fit for a cow, got from a cow'; &c.

### @deva[र]

—**(1)** is added to @deva[कुटी], @deva[शमी] and @deva[शुण्ड], as a diminutive term.; @deva[ह्रस्वा कुटी-कुटीर] *m. n.* 'a small hut,' @deva[शमीरः] a small S'ami tree', @deva[शुण्डारः] 'the trunk of a young elephant'.

### @deva[शंकट] and @deva[शाल]

—are affixed to @deva[वि] in the sense of 'largeness,' @deva[विशकट] 'great, large'; @deva[विशाल] 'extensive,' 'spacious,' &c.

---

[^1]: For the declension of such words vide @ref[74]. a., b.

[^2]: @deva[विभाषा कुरुयुगन्धराभ्याम्] । Pāṇ. IV. 2. 30.

[^3]: Vide supra. @ref[306]. a. These are generally *fem.* There are exceptions, as @deva[देवासुरम्] 'the enmity between the gods and demons' &c.

[^4]: In this sense it is added to a few words only.

[^5]: These are @deva[अश्व], @deva[अश्वत्थ], @deva[रथ], @deva[जाल], @deva[न्यास], and @deva[पाद].

[^6]: @deva[भस्त्रा], @deva[भट], @deva[भरण], @deva[शीर्ष-षे-भार], @deva[अंस-से-भार], &c.

[^7]: Pân. V. 2. 23. and Sid. Kau.

[^8]: @deva[तत्तु हैयंगवीनं यद् ह्योगोदोहोद्भवं घृतम्] । Amara.

[^9]: @deva[शुभ्र], @deva[पुर], @deva[ब्रह्मकृत], @deva[रोहिणी], @deva[रुक्मिणी], @deva[धर्मिणी], @deva[विमातृ], @deva[विधवा], @deva[शुक], @deva[विश्], @deva[शकुनि], @deva[शुक्र], @deva[बन्धकी], &c.

[^10]: @deva[कत्रि], @deva[पुष्कर], @deva[पुष्कल], @deva[कुम्भी], @deva[कुण्डिन], @deva[ग्राम], &c.

[^11]: @deva[प्रमाणे द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रचः] । Pâṇ. V. 2. 37.

[^12]: @deva[स्त्रीपुंसाभ्यां नञ्स्नञौ भवनात्] । Pâṇ. VI. 1. 87.

[^13]: @deva[मयड् वा एतयोर्भाषायामभक्ष्याच्छादनयोः] Pâṇ IV. 3. 143.

rules.title: Possession Affixes (मत्वर्थीय) - Section II (अ to मतुप्)
म → व in मत् (मतुप्)
rules.body:
( *a* ) The @deva[म] of the termination @deva[मत्] is changed to @deva[व] when affixed to words ending in @deva[म्] or @deva[अ], short or long, or having either for their penultimate;[^1] @deva[किंवत्] from @deva[किम्], @deva[विद्यावत्], @deva[लक्ष्मीवत्], @deva[यशस्वत्], @deva[भास्वत्], &c.;[^2] @deva[राजन्+वत्=राजन्वत्]; as @deva[राजन्वान् देशः] 'a country having a good or just king'; ( *cf.* Rag. VI. 22. )=@deva[राजवत्]; as @deva[राजवान् देशः] 'a country governed by a king'; @deva[उदक+वत्=उदन्वत्] *m.* 'the sea'; @deva[उदकवत्] as @deva[उदकवान्] ( @deva[घटः] 'a jar' ) containing water.

Exceptions:—@deva[म] is not changed to @deva[व] in the case of the words @deva[यव], @deva[दल्मि], @deva[ऊर्मि], @deva[भूमि], @deva[कृमि], @deva[क्रुञ्चा], @deva[वशा], @deva[द्राक्षा], @deva[भ्रजि], @deva[व्रजि], @deva[ध्वजि], @deva[नजि], @deva[हरित्], @deva[ककुद्], @deva[गरुत्], @deva[इक्षु], @deva[द्रु] and @deva[मधु], as @deva[यवमान्], @deva[ऊर्मिमान्], &c.

( *b* )[^3] @deva[मत्] also becomes @deva[वत्] when added to words ending in any of the first four letters of a class; @deva[विद्युत्वान्], @deva[तडित्वान्] *m.* 'possessing lightning' *i. e.* 'a cloud', &c. The @deva[त्] of @deva[विद्युत्] &c. is not changed to @deva[द्] as it is not at the end of a @deva[पद्].

( *c* ) and when the whole expresses a @deva[संज्ञा] ( a name ); @deva[अहीवती], @deva[मुनीवती] &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः] । Pâṇ. VIII. 2. 9.

[^2]: @deva[राजन्वान्सौराज्ये] । Pâṇ. VIII. 2. 14. @deva[राजवानन्यत्र] । Sid. Kau.

[^3]: @deva[झयः] । @deva[संज्ञायाम्] । Pâṇ. VIII. 2. 10. 11.

rules.title: Possession Affixes (य, युस्, र, ल …) and Section III: Affixes forming Adverbs (अक, एन, तस्, वत्, शस्, च्वि, सात्)
Introduction to Gender
rules.body:
# Chapter X. Gender

No definite rules can be laid down for the determination of the gender of words in Sanskrit. It can best be studied from the dictionary or from usage. The following hints, however, may be useful to the student in the majority of cases.

rules.title: Masculine Words: Verbal Derivatives
rules.body:
## 1. Masculine Words

Verbal derivatives formed by the affixes @deva[अ] and @deva[न], and @deva[इ] added to the roots @deva[दा] and @deva[धा]; *e. g.* @deva[पाकः], @deva[त्यागः], @deva[करः], @deva[गरः] any beverage or drink, poison, @deva[गोचरः] range, scope, @deva[यज्ञः], @deva[विघ्नः], @deva[आधिः] mental pain or anguish, @deva[निधिः] a treasure, &c.

**Exceptions:**—@deva[याञ्चा] *fem.* and @deva[भय], @deva[लिङ्ग], and @deva[भग] all *neu.*

rules.title: Masculine Words Ending in उ and Specific Penultimates
rules.body:
Words ending in @deva[उ] and those having @deva[क्], @deva[ट्], @deva[ण्], @deva[थ्], @deva[न्], @deva[भ्], @deva[म्], @deva[य्], @deva[र्], or @deva[स्], for their penultimate; as @deva[प्रभुः], @deva[भानुः], @deva[इक्षुः], @deva[स्तबकः] 'a bunch of flowers' &c; @deva[घटः], @deva[पाषाणः], @deva[शोथः] 'a swelling', @deva[फेनः], @deva[दीपः], @deva[स्तम्भः], @deva[सोमः], @deva[समयः], @deva[क्षुरः] a razor, @deva[अङ्कुरः], @deva[वृषः], @deva[वायसः] &c.

**Exceptions:**—Words ending in—

**(*a*)** @deva[उ]—@deva[धेनु], @deva[रज्जु] ( except when it ends a compound, in which case it is both *mas.* and *fem.* ) @deva[कुहु]—@deva[हू] 'the last day of a lunar month on which the moon is invisible,' @deva[सरयु] 'name of a river,' @deva[तनु], @deva[करेणु] and @deva[प्रियंगु] 'a kind of creeper,' which are all *fem.*; @deva[श्मश्रु], @deva[जानु], @deva[वसु] 'wealth,' @deva[अश्रु], @deva[जतु] 'lac,' @deva[त्रपु] 'tin or lead', @deva[तालु], @deva[दारु], @deva[मधु] 'honey,' @deva[स्वादु] 'relish', @deva[वस्तु] and @deva[मस्तु] 'sour cream', which are all *neuter.*

rules.title: Definition of Avyaya (Indeclinable)
rules.body:
# Chapter XI. Avyayas or Indeclinables

That is an *Avyaya* whose form remaining the same in all the genders, numbers and cases, undergoes no change.[^1] The Avyayas may be divided into simple and compound ones. The latter are treated of in the chapter on compounds (Avyayībhāvas and a few Bahuvrīhis and Tatpurusha).

[^1]: @deva[सदृशं त्रिषु लिङ्गेषु सर्वासु च विभक्तिषु । वचनेषु च सर्वेषु यन्न व्येति तदव्ययम् ॥] @deva[स्वरादिनिपातमव्ययम्] । Pāṇ. I. 1. 37.

rules.title: Five Categories of Indeclinables
rules.body:
## Five Categories of Indeclinables

The indeclinables comprise (I) Prepositions, (II) Adverbs, (III) Particles, (IV) Conjunctions, and (V) Interjections.

rules.title: Nouns with Single Inflection Treated as Indeclinables
rules.body:
## Nouns with Single Inflection Treated as Indeclinables

Besides these there are in Sanskrit a few nouns having one inflection only which are treated as indeclinable (nipātas), e. g. @deva[अन्यत्] another (reason), @deva[अस्तम्] setting, @deva[अस्ति] that exists, @deva[ओम्] the well-known sacred syllable om, @deva[चनस्] satisfaction, food, @deva[चाटु] coaxing, @deva[नमस्] a bow, @deva[नास्ति] non-existence, @deva[भूर्] the earth, @deva[भुवर्] the sky, @deva[वदि] the dark fortnight, @deva[शम्] happiness, @deva[शुदि] or @deva[सुदि] the bright fortnight, @deva[संवत्] a year, @deva[स्वाहा] food offered to gods, @deva[स्वधा] food offered to the manes, @deva[स्वर्] heaven, @deva[स्वस्ति] happiness &c.

rules.title: Definition and Function of Prepositions (Upasarga)
rules.body:
## I. PREPOSITIONS

## Definition and Function of Prepositions (Upasarga)

A preposition, styled 'Upasarga or Gati,' in Sanskrit is an indeclinable word, having an independent meaning and prefixed to verbs and also to their derivatives. These prepositions modify, intensify and sometimes totally alter the senses of roots[^1]; e. g. @deva[प्रहृ] 'to strike,' @deva[आहृ] 'to eat, to perform as a sacrifice,' @deva[संहृ] 'to contract,' @deva[विहृ] 'to sport,' @deva[परिहृ] 'to avoid, &c.' Sometimes they are prefixed without any alteration in the sense.

[^1]: @deva[धात्वर्थं बाधते कश्चित्कश्चित्तमनुवर्तते । तमेव विशिनष्ट्यन्य उपसर्गगतिस्त्रिधा ॥] Cf. also Sid. Kau. @deva[उपसर्गेण धात्वर्थो बलादन्यत्र नीयते । प्रहाराहारसंहारविहारपरिहारवत् ॥] Some think that prepositions have no meaning of their own, but they simply bring to light when prefixed to roots their hidden senses. (cf. Śiś. X. 15).

rules.title: List of Common Sanskrit Prepositions
rules.body:
## List of Common Sanskrit Prepositions

§ 366. The following are the prepositions (upasargas) commonly prefixed to roots:—

### @deva[अति]

'beyond, over'; @deva[अतिक्रमः] 'overstepping' or 'going beyond,' @deva[अतिसर्जन] 'a gift, &c.'

### @deva[अधि]

'over, above, &c.;' @deva[अधिगमः] 'going up, acquisition,' @deva[अधिकार] 'high office or power,' @deva[अधिक्षेपः] 'censure,' &c.

### @deva[अनु]

'after, behind, along, &c.' @deva[अनुक्रमणं] 'following,' @deva[अनुकृतिः] 'imitation,' @deva[अनुग्रहः] 'favour,' &c.

### @deva[अप]

'away from, away.' @deva[अपनयनं] 'the act of taking away,' @deva[अपहृ] 'to plunder, seize' &c., @deva[अपकारः] 'harm, wrong' &c.

### @deva[अपि] (sometimes @deva[पि])

'near to,' 'over,' 'taking to,' &c.; @deva[अपिगम्] 'to be resolved into or reduced to,'[^1] @deva[अपिधानं] or @deva[पिधानं] 'a covering,' @deva[अप्ययः] 'destruction,' &c.

This prep. is more commonly used as an independent adverb having a cumulative force in classical Sanskrit.

### @deva[अभि]

'towards, near to,' &c.; @deva[अभिगम्] 'to go towards,' @deva[अभिजनः] 'noble descent or family,' @deva[अभिमानः] 'self-respect,' @deva[अभिभू] 'to defeat,' &c.

### @deva[अव] (sometimes @deva[व]; see @deva[अपि] and ft. note)

'away, down,' &c. @deva[अव]—or @deva[वगाह्] 'to plunge into,' @deva[अवतारः] 'descent,' @deva[अवगीत] 'reproached,' @deva[अवमन्] to disrespect,' &c.

### @deva[आ]

'up to, towards, all round, a little,' &c.; @deva[आच्छाद्] 'to cover all round,' @deva[आकारः] 'form or shape (within due bounds),' @deva[आकाशः] 'that which shines all round' i. e. 'the ether'; @deva[आकम्प्] 'to shake a little,' &c.

### @deva[उत्]—@deva[द्]

'upon,' &c.; @deva[उद्गम्] 'to go up,' @deva[उद्यमः] 'industry,' @deva[उत्सर्गः] 'pouring out, hence a gift, a general rule,' &c.

### @deva[उप]

'near to, towards, by the side of,' &c.; @deva[उपया] 'to go near to,' @deva[उपकृति] f. 'an obligation,' @deva[उपरति] f. 'death,' @deva[उपस्थानं] 'praise, worship,' @deva[उपमिति] f. 'comparison,' &c.

### @deva[दुस्]—@deva[र्]

'bad, hard to be done,' &c.; @deva[दुराचारः] 'bad conduct,' @deva[दुष्कर] 'hard to be done,' @deva[दुःसह] 'difficult to be borne,' &c.

### @deva[नि]

'in, into, great, opposed to,' &c.; @deva[निकृ] 'to insult,' @deva[निकेत] 'a house,' @deva[निचय] 'a heap, a great collection,' @deva[निपीत] 'drunk in,' @deva[निदेश] 'a command,' &c.

### @deva[निस्]—@deva[र्]

'out of, away from, without,' &c.; @deva[निःसृ] 'to issue out,' @deva[निर्गम] 'a passage out,' @deva[निर्दोषः] 'out of i. e. free from blame,' @deva[निः शङ्क] 'without doubt,' &c.

### @deva[परा]

'away, back, opposed to,' &c.; @deva[पराकृ] 'to reject, to despise,' @deva[पराक्रम] 'to act bravely,' @deva[परागत] 'gone away,' @deva[पराञ्च्] 'turn back,' @deva[पराजय] 'what is opposed to victory; defeat,' &c.

### @deva[परि]

'all round, about,' &c.; @deva[परिधा] 'to place all round i. e. to put on or wear,' @deva[परिधिः] 'a wall &c. that surrounds,' @deva[परिणामः] 'ripening, maturity,' @deva[परिगणना] 'counting all round, i. e. a complete enumeration,' &c.

### @deva[प्रति]

'towards, back, in return, in opposition to,' &c.; @deva[प्रतिगम्] 'to go towards,' @deva[प्रतिभाषण] 'a speech in return, an answer,' @deva[प्रति—ती—कारः] 'an act in opposition to i. e. a remedy' &c.

### @deva[वि]

'apart, separate from, reverse to,' &c.; @deva[विचल्] 'to move apart,' @deva[वियुज्] 'to be separated,' @deva[विक्री] opp. of @deva[क्री] 'to sell,' 'to buy' &c.; sometimes this has an intensive force.

### @deva[सम्]

'together with, excellent, full,' &c. @deva[संगम्], 'to be united,' @deva[संस्कारः] 'perfection,' @deva[संस्कृति] 'refinement,' @deva[संहारः] 'destruction, contraction,' &c.

### @deva[सु]

'well, thoroughly,' &c. (in this sense it is opposed to @deva[दुस्]); @deva[सुकृतं] 'done well,' @deva[सुशासित] 'thoroughly trained, well governed,' &c. It is also used in the sense of 'very, excessively;' @deva[सुमहत्] 'very great.'

[^1]: Cf. @deva[कारणेन अपिगच्छत् कारणं], &c. Shārīra Bhāshya. According to the grammarian Bhāguri the prepositions @deva[अपि] and @deva[अव] may optionally lose their @deva[अ]—@deva[वष्टि भागुरिरल्लोपमवाप्योरुपसर्गयोः] । (Sid. Kau.)

rules.title: Combination of Multiple Prepositions
rules.body: § 367. Two or more of these prepositions may also be combined and prefixed; e. g. @deva[अभिनिविश्] 'to enter into with resolution,' @deva[समुपागम्] 'to come in close contact with,' &c.

rules.title: Verb Ellipsis After Prepositions in Compounds
rules.body: § 368. When used in a compound the verb may be omitted after the prepositions @deva[अति], @deva[अधि], @deva[अनु], @deva[अप], @deva[अव], @deva[अभि], @deva[उप], @deva[परि] and @deva[प्रति]; @deva[अतिक्रान्तो मालां अतिमालः] &c. Vide @ref[232].

rules.title: Other Words Used Prepositionally (Gati)
rules.body:
## Other Words Used Prepositionally (Gati)

§ 369. There are several other words, also styled Gati by Sanskrit grammarians, used prepositionally. These are prefixed to certain roots only. We give the more important of them below.

(a) @deva[अच्छ][^1] 'towards' is prefixed to @deva[वद्] and to roots implying motion; @deva[अच्छगम्य]—@deva[गत्य] 'going near,' @deva[अच्छपतत्] 'flying towards,' @deva[अच्छोद्य] 'having spoken to.'

(b) (1) @deva[अन्वाजे] 'giving strength to the weak,' @deva[अलं] in the sense of 'decorating,' @deva[ऊरी], @deva[उररी], @deva[ऊररी] all implying 'assent, acceptance or promise,' @deva[खात्] and similar imitative sounds, @deva[असत्] and @deva[सत्] in the sense of 'dishonouring or honouring;' @deva[प्राध्वं] denoting 'fastening,' &c. are prefixed to @deva[कृ]; @deva[अन्वाजेकरणम्], @deva[ऊरीकरणम्], @deva[असत्कारः], @deva[सत्कृत्य], @deva[खात्कृत्य], @deva[प्राध्वंकरणम्], &c.

(2) @deva[नमः], @deva[प्रादुः], @deva[मिथ्या], @deva[वशे], @deva[साक्षात्] and some other words may be optionally prefixed to @deva[कृ] or remain separate; @deva[नमस्कारः], @deva[वशेकृ] or @deva[वशे कृ] 'to bring under subjection,' @deva[साक्षात् कृ] or @deva[साक्षात्कृ] 'to make manifest,' &c.

(c) @deva[अन्तर्] is prefixed to roots meaning 'to go,' @deva[धा], @deva[भू], and similar roots; @deva[अन्तरित्य] 'having disappeared,' @deva[अन्तर्धानं] 'disappearance,' @deva[अन्तर्भूत], &c.

(d) @deva[अस्तम्] is prefixed to roots implying motion; @deva[अस्तमयः] 'setting,' @deva[अस्तंगत] 'set,' @deva[अस्तंनी] 'to cause to set, to lead to destruction,' &c.

(e) @deva[आविः], and @deva[प्रादुः] are prefixed to @deva[कृ], @deva[अस्] and @deva[भू] and @deva[तिरस्] to @deva[भू], @deva[धा] and similar roots, and optionally to @deva[कृ], @deva[आविष्करणं], @deva[आविर्भवनं] 'manifestation,' @deva[प्रादुर्]—@deva[आविर्भूत] 'manifested,' &c.; @deva[तिरोभूय] 'vanishing out of sight,' @deva[तिरोधानं] 'disappearance,' &c.

(f) @deva[पुरः] is prefixed to @deva[कृ], @deva[भू], @deva[गम्] &c.; @deva[पुरस्कृत] 'placed before, headed by,' @deva[पुरोगत] 'gone in the front,' &c.

[^1]: @deva[अच्छगत्यर्थवदेषु] । Pāṇ. 1. 4. 69.

rules.title: Nouns as Gati with Chvi-Derivatives
rules.body: § 370. Several nouns, substantive and adjective, may be prefixed to the roots @deva[कृ], @deva[भू], and @deva[अस्] to form what are called in Sanskrit 'chvi-derivatives' (vide chap. IX. Sec. III.) @deva[कृष्णकरणम्] = @deva[कृष्णीकरणम्], @deva[घन] = @deva[भूत] = @deva[घनीभूतः]. Such nouns are also termed 'Gati.'

rules.title: Taddhita Affix -sāt Used Prepositionally
rules.body: § 371. Like prepositions may be further used the words to which the Taddhita affix @deva[सात्] is affixed, @deva[अग्निसात्कृ] 'to consign to flames;' @deva[भस्मसात्कृत] 'reduced to ashes,' @deva[राजसात्कृता] 'made over to the king.' &c. (vide p. 216.)

rules.title: Formation of Adverbs from Various Cases
rules.body:
## II. ADVERBS

§ 372. Adverbs are either primitive or derived from nouns, pronouns or numerals. As adverbs may also be further used the Acc. sing. neu. of nouns and adjectives; and sometimes the sing. of other cases also; @deva[सत्यम्] 'truthfully,' @deva[मृदु] 'softly,' @deva[सुखम्] 'happily,' @deva[लघु] 'quickly,' @deva[निर्भरम्], @deva[अवश्यम्], @deva[अत्यन्तम्], @deva[बलवत्] 'strongly,' @deva[भूयः], 'again' &c.; @deva[दुःखेन] 'painfully,' @deva[सुखेन], @deva[धर्मेण] 'virtuously, justly,' @deva[दक्षिणेन], @deva[उत्तरेण], @deva[अशेषेण], @deva[चिरेण] 'after a long time,' @deva[क्षणेन] &c.; @deva[चिराय], @deva[चिररात्राय] 'for a long time,' @deva[अर्थाय] 'for the sake of,' @deva[बलात्] 'forcibly,' @deva[हर्षात्], @deva[शोकात्], @deva[दूरात्], @deva[तस्मात्], @deva[कस्मात्] &c.; @deva[चिरात्] 'for a long time,' @deva[दूरात्], @deva[उत्तरात्] &c.; @deva[स्थाने] 'properly,' @deva[दूरे], @deva[प्रभाते], @deva[प्राह्णे], @deva[अग्रे], @deva[एकपदे] 'at once,' @deva[सपदि], @deva[ऋते], @deva[समीपे], @deva[अभ्यासे] 'near,' &c.

N. B. Adverbs formed from pronouns and numerals are given in their proper places; while those formed from nouns are given in Chapter IX.

rules.title: Alphabetical List of Sanskrit Adverbs
rules.body:

rules.title: Particles as Expletives and Intensives
rules.body:
## III. PARTICLES

§ 374. The particles are either used as expletives or intensives; some of these are @deva[किल], @deva[खलु], @deva[च], @deva[तु], @deva[नु], @deva[वै], @deva[हि], &c.

rules.title: Particles Used with Certain Words
Principal Conjunctions in Sanskrit
rules.body:
## IV. CONJUNCTIONS

§ 376. The following are the principal conjunctions in Sanskrit:—

(a) Copulative @deva[अथ], @deva[अथो], @deva[उत], @deva[च], @deva[किंच], &c.

(b) Disjunctive @deva[वा], @deva[वा]...@deva[वा], &c.

(c) Adversative @deva[अथवा], @deva[तु], @deva[किंतु], @deva[किंवा], &c.

(d) Conditional @deva[चेत्], @deva[यदि], @deva[यदापि], @deva[नेत्], @deva[नोचेत्], @deva[वेट्] (used in sacrificial ceremonies), &c.

(e) Causal @deva[हि], @deva[तत्], @deva[तेन], &c.

(f) Interrogative @deva[आहो] @deva[अहोस्वित्], @deva[उत], @deva[उताहो], @deva[किं], @deva[किन्नु], @deva[किमुत], @deva[किंस्वित्], @deva[ननु], @deva[नवा], @deva[नु], &c.

(g) Affirmatives and negatives @deva[अङ्ग], @deva[अथ किम्], @deva[आम्], @deva[अद्धा] &c.

(h) Conjunctions of time @deva[यावत्]—@deva[तावत्], @deva[यदा], @deva[तदा] &c.

(i) @deva[अथ] and @deva[इति] are used to mark the beginning and the close of a work respectively.

rules.title: Interjections Expressing Emotions
rules.body:
## V. INTERJECTIONS

§ 377. "The interjection is not properly a part of speech, as it does not enter into the construction of sentences. It is a sudden exclamation prompted by some strong feeling or emotion. There are various utterances suited to the different emotions of the mind":—*Prof. Bain.*

(a) These are—@deva[आ], @deva[इ], @deva[उ], @deva[ए], @deva[ऐ], @deva[ओ], @deva[अह], @deva[अहह], @deva[अहो], @deva[बत], @deva[ह], @deva[हा], @deva[हाहा], &c. expressive of wonder, grief or regret, &c.

(b) @deva[किम्], @deva[धिक्] &c. expressive of contempt.

(c) @deva[हा], @deva[बत], &c. expressing sorrow, dejection, &c.

(d) @deva[हा], @deva[हाहा], @deva[हन्त] showing grief.

(e) @deva[आ], @deva[हम्], @deva[हुम्], &c. expressive of anger, contempt, &c.

(f) @deva[हन्त], &c. expressing joy.

(g) There are some interjections used to call attention. Of these,

(1) some show respect; such as @deva[अङ्ग], @deva[अये], @deva[अहो], @deva[अहो], @deva[बत], @deva[उ], @deva[ए], @deva[ओ], @deva[प्याट्], @deva[भोः], @deva[हंहो], @deva[हे], @deva[है], @deva[हो], &c.

(2) and others, disrespect or contempt; as @deva[अङ्ग], @deva[अरे], @deva[अवे], @deva[रे], @deva[रेरे], @deva[अरेरे] &c.

(3) The exclamations @deva[श्रौषट्], @deva[वौषट्] and @deva[वषट्] are used when offering oblations to gods or manes; and

(4) @deva[स्वाहा] and @deva[स्वधा] when offering oblations to gods and manes respectively.

rules.title: Introduction to Verbs: Types, Tenses, Moods, and Voices
rules.body:
# Chapter XII. Conjugation of Verbs

§ 378. There are in Sanskrit—

(a) Two kinds of verbs, Primitive and Derivative.

(b) Six Tenses (@deva[कालाः]) and four Moods (@deva[अर्थाः]) which are as follow:—[^1]

| TENSES | TECHNICAL NAME | MOODS | TECHNICAL NAME |
|---|---|---|---|
| @deva[वर्तमानः] or Present | @deva[लट्] | @deva[आज्ञा] or Imperative | @deva[लोट्] |
| @deva[भूतः] or Aorist | @deva[लुङ्] | @deva[विधि] or Potential | @deva[विधिलिङ्] |
| @deva[अनद्यतनभूतः] or Imperfect | @deva[लङ्] | @deva[आशीः] or Benedictive | @deva[आशीर्लिङ्] |
| @deva[परोक्षभूतः] or Perfect | @deva[लिट्] | @deva[संकेत] or Conditional | @deva[लृङ्] |
| @deva[अनद्यतनभविष्यन्] or 1st Future | @deva[लुट्] | | |
| @deva[भविष्यन्] or 2nd Future | @deva[लृट्] | | |

@deva[लेट्] or the Subjunctive is used only in the Veda and is therefore termed 'The Vedic Subjunctive.'

Note:—The ten tenses and moods are technically called the ten Lakaras in Sanskrit grammars.

(c) Three Voices (@deva[प्रयोगाः]), the Active Voice (@deva[कर्तरीप्र०]) as @deva[रामः सत्यं भाषते]. the Passive Voice (@deva[कर्मणीप्र०]), as @deva[हरिणा फलं भक्ष्यते], and the Impersonal Construction (@deva[भावेप्र०]) @deva[रामेण गम्यते].

(d) Two sets of personal terminations, the one called 'Parasmaipada,' the other 'Ātmanepada.' Some roots take exclusively the Par. terminations and some the Ātm. ones; while there are others which take either. Several roots again, though Parasmaipadi, become Ātmanepadi and *vice versa*, when preceded by certain prepositions or in particular senses. These will be considered in a separate chapter.

[^1]: These technical names are given in the following Kārikā.

@deva[लट् वर्तमाने लेट् वेदे भूते लुङ्लङ्लिटस्तथा । विध्याशिषोस्तु लिङ्लोटौ लुट् लृट् लृङ् च भविष्यति ॥]

This terminology of Pāṇini, it will be seen, is artificial. Other grammarians use different names. The ten Lakaras of Pāṇini are according to their nomenclature, as follow.—@deva[भवति] (@deva[वृत्तिः]), @deva[अद्यतनी], @deva[ह्यस्तनी], @deva[परोक्षा], @deva[श्वस्तनी], @deva[भविष्यन्ती], @deva[पञ्चमी], @deva[सप्तमी], @deva[क्रियातिपत्ति] and @deva[आशीः]—'Apte's Guide'.

rules.title: Primitive and Derivative Verbs
rules.body: § 379. Primitive verbs or roots are those which originally exist in the language, while derivative verbs are those which may be derived from a parent stock—a root or a noun.

rules.title: Tenses, Moods and Voices of Every Verb
rules.body:
§ 380. Every verb, in Sanskrit, whether primitive or derivative, may be conjugated in the ten tenses and moods given above.

(a) Transitive verbs are conjugated in the Active and Passive voices and intransitive verbs in the active and the Impersonal form.

rules.title: Number and Person in Verbs
rules.body: § 381. In each tense and mood there are three numbers, singular, dual and plural, with three persons in each.

rules.title: Special vs. General Lakāras and Verb Bases
rules.body:
In four of the tenses and moods given above, viz. the Present, the Imperfect, the Imperative and the Potential, the verbs undergo peculiar modifications (@deva[विकरण]) and these are therefore called Conjugational (@deva[सार्वधातुक])[^1] or special tenses and moods; and the remaining Non-Conjugational (@deva[आर्धधातुक]) or general. In the former the characteristic marks and terminations of each are mostly added to a special base formed from the roots in various ways, while in the latter they are combined with the roots itself.

(a) The base (@deva[अङ्ग]) of a root is that form which it assumes before the personal terminations.

[^1]: Strictly the term Sārvadhātuka (belonging to the form of the verbal base) is given by Pāṇini to the terminations of all the tenses and moods, except those of the Perfect and the Benedictive, and to the affixes distinguished by an indicatory ś (@deva[शित्]) i. e. the various conjugational signs of the 9 classes (except that of the eighth), and the terminations of the Present Participle Pars. and Atm. All other verbal affixes i. e. the conjugational signs of the 8th and 10th classes, the affixes added to form the causal base and a few denominatives, the affixes @deva[स्य], @deva[ता], @deva[स], and @deva[य] added to the bases of the two futures, the Desiderative and the Aor., and the Passive and the Frequentative respectively, and those forming the Past Participle (Act. and Pass.), the infinitive and the verbal indeclinables, and some others are called Ardhadhātuka.

rules.title: Parasmaipada vs. Ātmanepada Usage
rules.body:
When a root is capable of taking either pada, the Parasmaipada (lit. word for another) should be used when the fruit or result of the action of the verb accrues to any other person or thing than the agent, and the Ātmanepada (lit. word for self) when it refers to the agent. Thus @deva[देवदत्तः यजति] will mean 'Devadatta sacrifices for another (his Yajamāna);' while @deva[देवदत्तः यजते] will mean 'Devadatta sacrifices for himself.'

## SECTION I. ACTIVE VOICE

## I. CONJUGATIONAL OR SPECIAL TENSES AND MOODS.

**PRESENT, IMPERFECT, IMPERATIVE and POTENTIAL.**

rules.title: Ten Conjugational Classes
rules.body: With reference to the various moods the verbs are divided into ten conjugational classes by Sanskrit grammarians, each class being denominated after the root which begins it viz. (1) @deva[भ्वादि] (2) @deva[अदादि], (3) @deva[जुहोत्यादि], (4) @deva[दिवादि], (5) @deva[स्वादि], (6) @deva[तुदादि], (7) @deva[रुधादि], (8) @deva[तनादि] (9) @deva[क्र्यादि] and (10) @deva[चुरादि].

rules.title: Primitive vs. Derivative Roots
rules.body: The roots contained in the first nine classes and a few of the tenth are primitive roots, while almost all roots of the tenth class, the Causals, Desideratives, Frequentatives, Denominatives, and the roots @deva[गुप्], @deva[धूप्], @deva[विच्छ्], @deva[पण्], @deva[पन्], @deva[ऋत्], and @deva[कम्], are comprised under the head of Derivative roots.

rules.title: Two Groups of Conjugational Classes
rules.body:
These ten classes may again be conveniently divided into two groups, the first comprising the 1st, 4th, 6th and 10th classes, and the second the remaining. In the first the base ends in @deva[अ] and remains unchanged throughout; while in the second it does not end in @deva[अ] and is changeable.

## I. GROUP 1. ROOTS WITH UNCHANGEABLE BASES

(1st, 4th, 6th and 10th classes).

| 3. | @deva[ईत्] | @deva[ईताम्] | @deva[ईयुः] | @deva[ईत] | @deva[ईयाताम्] | @deva[ईरन्] |

**Note:**—Terminations beginning with vowels may be called Vowel terminations; those beginning with consonants, consonantal terminations.

**Formation of the base of the roots of the first group:**—

rules.title: First Class (@deva[भ्वादि]): Addition of @deva[अ] (@deva[शप्])
Fourth Class (@deva[दिवादि]): Addition of @deva[य] (@deva[श्यन्])
rules.body: @deva[य] (@deva[श्यन्]) is added on to the final of a root of the Fourth or @deva[दिवादि] class before the terminations; the radical vowel remains unchanged; e. g. @deva[कुप्+ति=कुप्+य+ति=कुप्यति].

rules.title: Sixth Class (@deva[तुदादि]): Addition of @deva[अ] with Vowel Changes
rules.body: @deva[अ] is added on to the roots of the sixth or @deva[तुदादि] class before which the penultimate vowel remains unchanged, and the final @deva[इ], @deva[उ], short or long, @deva[ऋ] and @deva[ॠ] are changed to @deva[इय्], @deva[उव्], @deva[रिय्] and @deva[इर्] respectively; e. g. @deva[क्षिप्+ति=क्षिप्+अ+ति=क्षिपति]; @deva[धु+ति=धुव्+अ+ति=धुवति]; @deva[रि+अ+ति=रियति]; @deva[मृ+अ+ते=म्रियते]; @deva[गॄ+अ+ति=गिर्+अ+ति=गिरति], &c.

rules.title: Tenth Class (@deva[चुरादि]): Addition of @deva[अय] with Vṛddhi
rules.body:
Roots of the tenth or @deva[चुरादि] class[^1] add @deva[अय] before the personal terminations. Before @deva[अय] (1) the penultimate short vowel (except @deva[अ]) takes the Guṇa substitute; and the final vowel and the penultimate @deva[अ] not prosodially long, take their Vṛddhi substitute; e. g. @deva[चुर्+ति=चुर्+अय+ति=चोर्+अय+ति=चोरयति]; @deva[भू+अय+ति=भौ+अय+ति=भाव्+अय+ति=भावयति]; @deva[तड्+अय+ति=ताड्+अय+ति=ताडयति]; but @deva[दण्ड्+अय+ति=दण्डयति], &c.

[^1]: This class contains a few primitive verbs, almost all the roots belonging to it being derivative; besides, all Causals and some Nominal verbs may be regarded as belonging to this class.

rules.title: Lengthening of @deva[अ] and Elision Before Terminations
rules.body:
(a)[^1] The preceding @deva[अ] is lengthened before a conjugational termination beginning with a semivowel, a nasal or @deva[झ्] or @deva[भ्]; e. g. @deva[नयामि] &c.

(b) The final @deva[अ] is dropped before terminations beginning with @deva[अ]; @deva[नय+अन्ति=नयन्ति], &c.

The augment @deva[अ] is prefixed to roots in this tense. rules.title: Changes of Long @deva[ऋ] to @deva[इर्] or @deva[उर्]
rules.body:
The[^1] @deva[ॠ] (long) of a root, penultimate or final, when it does not take Guṇa or Vṛddhi, is changed to @deva[इर्], and to @deva[उर्] if a labial or @deva[व्] precedes; and the @deva[इ] or @deva[उ] is lengthened when @deva[इर्] or @deva[उर्] is followed by a consonant; e. g. @deva[जॄ] 4. P. 'to become old,' @deva[जीर्यति], @deva[अजीर्यत्], &c.; @deva[कॄ] 6. P. @deva[किरति], @deva[अकिरत्], &c.; here @deva[कि] does not become long as @deva[किर्] is followed by @deva[अ]; @deva[कृत्] 10. P. A. @deva[कीर्तयति-ते], @deva[अकीर्तयत्-त], &c.

[^1]: @deva[ऋत इद्धातोः] । @deva[उरण् रपरः] । Pāṇ. VII. 1. 100, I. 1. 51. @deva[हलि च] Pāṇ. VII. 2. 77.

rules.title: Lengthening of Penultimate Vowels and Irregular First Class Roots
rules.body:
The penultimate @deva[इ], @deva[उ], @deva[ऋ] or @deva[ऌ] of a root, followed by @deva[र्] or @deva[व्] is lengthened when a consonant follows;[^1] e. g. @deva[उर्द्] 1. A. to measure, to play, @deva[ऊर्दते]; similarly @deva[कुर्द्], @deva[खुर्द्], @deva[गुर्द्] all A. and meaning to play, @deva[हुर्छ्], to act dishonestly, to be crooked, @deva[मुर्छ्] to faint; @deva[स्फुर्छ्] to spread, to forget; @deva[स्फुर्ज्] to thunder, to shine; @deva[उर्व्], @deva[तुर्व्], @deva[थुर्व्], @deva[दुर्व्], @deva[धुर्व्] all meaning to kill, @deva[गुर्व्] to try, @deva[मुर्व्], &c., all Parasm. and belonging to the 1st class, lengthen their penultimate vowel; @deva[दिव्] 4. P. @deva[दीव्यति]; similarly @deva[सिव्] has @deva[सीव्यति], @deva[ष्ठिव्], @deva[ष्ठीव्यति], &c.

rules.title: Seven Roots Forming Bases Like Desiderative
rules.body: The following seven roots form their bases like the Desiderative in the senses indicated. These are:—@deva[कित्] to administer medicine, to treat as a patient, @deva[चिकित्सति-ते]; @deva[गुप्] to censure, @deva[जुगुप्सते]; @deva[तिज्] to bear, to forgive, @deva[तितिक्षते]; @deva[बध्] to abhor, to act loathsomely, @deva[बीभत्सते]; @deva[दान्] to make straight, @deva[दीदांसति-ते]; @deva[मान्] to reason, to think, @deva[मीमांसते]; @deva[शान्] to sharpen, @deva[शीशांसति-ते]. But @deva[कित्] to desire @deva[केतति]; to dwell, @deva[केतयति]; @deva[दान्] to cut @deva[दानयति-ते] &c.

rules.title: Roots Adding Penultimate Nasal and Irregular Fourth Class Roots
rules.body:
There are a few roots which add a penultimate nasal in the Special Tenses and Moods necessarily; e. g. @deva[भिद्] to cut @deva[भिन्दति], @deva[अह्] to go @deva[अंहते], @deva[पिड्] to roll into a ball @deva[पिण्डते], @deva[शुठ्] to purify, to go @deva[शुंठति] &c.; and a few more which do so optionally; e. g. @deva[दृह्] to be firm @deva[दर्हति]-@deva[दृंहति]; @deva[म्रुच्] or @deva[म्लुच्] to go @deva[म्रोचयति]-@deva[म्रुंचति], @deva[म्लोचयति]-@deva[म्लुंचति]; @deva[लुच्] to pluck @deva[लोचति], @deva[लुञ्चति] all P.; @deva[गुज्] A. to hum @deva[गोजते], @deva[गुञ्जते]; @deva[गृज्] P. to roar @deva[गर्जति], @deva[गृंजति] and others less important.

rules.title: Tenth Class Roots Preserving Vowel Unchanged
rules.body: The following roots of the 10th class preserve their vowel unchanged; @deva[अघ्] to sin, @deva[कथ्] to tell, @deva[क्षप्] to send, to pass; @deva[गण्] to count, @deva[गल्] U. to filter, A. to throw, @deva[वर्] to choose or seek, to get, @deva[ध्वन्] to sound, @deva[मह्] to honour, @deva[रच्] to compose, @deva[रस्] to taste, @deva[रह्] to forsake, @deva[शठ्] to speak ill of, deceive, @deva[रट्] to scream, @deva[पट्] to weave, (but @deva[पाटयति] when it means to tear &c.), @deva[स्तन्] to thunder, @deva[गद्] to sound, @deva[पत्] to go, @deva[कल्] to count, @deva[स्वर्] to sound, @deva[पद्] A. to go, @deva[अंस्] to divide, @deva[वट्] to separate, @deva[लज्] to shine, @deva[कर्ण्] to bore, @deva[छद्] to conceal, @deva[चप्] to cheat, @deva[वस्] to dwell, @deva[श्रथ्] or @deva[श्लथ्] to be weak or lax, @deva[व्यय्] to give, to spend, @deva[स्पृह्] to desire, @deva[मृग्] to seek, @deva[मृष्] to bear, @deva[कृप्] to pity, to be weak, @deva[कुण्], @deva[गुण्] to converse with, @deva[ग्रह्] A. to take (also @deva[ग्राहयति] when caus. of @deva[ग्रह्]), @deva[कुह्] A. to astonish, to deceive, @deva[पुट्] to bind or string together, @deva[स्फुट्] to become manifest, @deva[सुख्] to make happy, and others less common.

rules.title: Tenth Class Roots Exclusively Taking Ātmanepada
rules.body: Some roots of the 10th class exclusively take the Ātmanepada i. e. even when the fruit of the action expressed by them does not accrue to the agent. These are:—@deva[अर्थ्] to request, to desire, @deva[कुह्] to astonish, to deceive, @deva[चित्] to be conscious of, to think, @deva[दंश्] to bite, @deva[दंस्] (or @deva[दस्] according to some) to see, to bite, @deva[डप्] or @deva[डिप्] to accumulate, @deva[तन्त्र्] to support a family, @deva[मन्त्र्] to counsel secretly, @deva[मृग्] to search, to hunt, to seek, @deva[स्पृश्] to take, to string together, @deva[तर्ज्] and @deva[भर्त्स्] to reprove, @deva[बस्त्] and @deva[गन्ध्] to injure, to hurt, @deva[विष्क्] to kill (@deva[हिष्क्] according to some), @deva[निष्क्] to measure, @deva[लल्] to desire, @deva[कण्] to contract, @deva[तुण्] to fill, @deva[भ्रूण्] to fear, @deva[शल्] to praise, @deva[यक्ष्] to worship, @deva[स्यम्] to guess, @deva[गुर्] to strike, @deva[सम्] to look at, to inspect, @deva[कुत्स्] to reproach, @deva[त्रुट्] (according to some @deva[कुट्]) to cut, @deva[गल्] to drop down, @deva[भल्] to see, to expound, @deva[कूट्] to abstain from giving, to muddle, @deva[कुट्] to cut, @deva[वञ्च्] to deceive, @deva[वृष्] to have the power of generation, to be eminent, @deva[मुद्] to gratify, @deva[दिन्] to bewail, @deva[गृ] to know, @deva[विद्] to know, to be conscious of, @deva[मन्] to stop, @deva[यु] to censure, and @deva[कुस्म्] to smile improperly.

rules.title: Roots Belonging to Both First and Tenth Classes - Introduction to Group II
rules.body:
The following roots belong to the 1st and the 10th classes:—

@deva[युज्], @deva[पृच्] to unite, to restrain, @deva[अर्च्] to worship, @deva[ईर्] to throw, @deva[ली] to melt @deva[वृज्] to abandon, to avoid, @deva[वृ] to cover, @deva[जृ], @deva[ज्रि] to grow old, @deva[रिच्] to separate, to join, @deva[शिष्] to leave a residue, @deva[तप्] to burn, @deva[तृप्] to be pleased or satisfied, @deva[छृद्] to kindle, @deva[चृप्], @deva[छृप्], @deva[दृप्] to kindle, @deva[दृभ्] to fear, @deva[श्रथ्] to release, to kill, @deva[मी] to go, @deva[ग्रन्थ्] to string together, @deva[शीक्], @deva[चीक्] to endure, @deva[अर्द्] to kill, @deva[हिंस्] to kill, @deva[अर्ह्] to worship, @deva[सद्] with @deva[आ] to go, to assail, @deva[शुन्ध्] to purify, to cleanse, @deva[छद्] to cover, @deva[जुष्] to satisfy, to guess, to kill, @deva[प्री] to please, @deva[श्रन्थ्], @deva[ग्रन्थ्] to compose, arrange, @deva[आप्] to obtain, @deva[तन्] to confide, to stretch, @deva[चन्] to confide, to hurt, @deva[वद्] to inform, @deva[वच्] to speak, @deva[मान्] to honour, worship, @deva[भू] Â. to obtain (@deva[भवति] also according to some), @deva[गर्ह्] to censure, @deva[मार्ग्] to seek, @deva[कण्ठ्] to grieve, to remember with regret, @deva[मृज्] to clean, @deva[मृष्] to endure, @deva[धृष्] to brave, to overcome, @deva[जस्] to hurt, to injure, @deva[दिव्] 10 A. 1. P. to torment, to beg, @deva[घुष्] to aver, and some others.

---

## II. GROUP II.

## ROOTS WITH CHANGEABLE BASES.

(2nd, 3rd, 5th, 7th, 8th, and 9th Classes.)

rules.title: Personal Terminations for Group II (Changeable Bases)
rules.body:
Terminations:—

Parasmaipada.

The terminations of the Present, the Imperfect and the Imperative are the same as those of the first group, the termination of the 2nd per. sing. of the Imperative is @deva[हि]. The terminations of the Potential are as follow:—

Potential

| 2. | @deva[यास्] | @deva[यातम्] | @deva[यात] |
| 3. | @deva[यात्] | @deva[याताम्] | @deva[युस्] |

Ātmanepada.

Present

| 2. | @deva[से] | @deva[आथे] | @deva[ध्वे] |
| 3. | @deva[ते] | @deva[आते] | @deva[अते] |

Imperfect

rules.title: Strong and Weak Terminations for Group II
rules.body:
The base of the roots of the 2nd group of Conjugational classes undergoes many modifications with regard to which the terminations are divided into sets, one set is called 'strong', the other 'weak.' The base taking the strong terminations may be called 'The strong base;' and that taking the weak ones 'The weak base'.

(a) The strong terminations are:—

The singulars of all persons of the Present and the Imperfect, the third person singular and all numbers of the first person of the Imperative, in the Parasmaipada, and all numbers of the first person of the Imperative in the Ātmanepada.

(b) The rest are weak.

rules.title: Guṇa Substitution Before Strong Terminations - Fifth, Eighth, and Ninth Classes
rules.body:
Before strong terminations the penultimate short and the final vowel of the base take their Guṇa substitute.

Fifth, Eighth and Ninth classes

rules.title: Addition of @deva[नु] and @deva[उ] in Fifth and Eighth Classes
rules.body:
@deva[नु] and @deva[उ] are added on to the roots of the 5th and 8th classes respectively before the terminations.[^1]

[^1]: @deva[स्वादिभ्यः श्नुः] । @deva[तनादिकृञ्भ्य उः] । Pāṇ. III. 1. 73, 79.

rules.title: Rules for Final @deva[उ] of @deva[नु] and @deva[उ] Bases
rules.body: The final @deva[उ] of the base is optionally dropped before @deva[व्] and @deva[म्] if it be not preceded by a conjunct consonant. It is changed to @deva[उव्] before a weak termination beginning with a vowel, if preceded by a conjunct consonant and to @deva[व्] in other cases. The @deva[हि] of the Imperative 2nd per. sing. is dropped after @deva[उ] not preceded by a conjunct consonant.

rules.title: Insertion of @deva[ना] in Ninth Class
rules.body:
In the ninth class @deva[ना] is inserted between the root and the terminations. @deva[ना] becomes @deva[न्] before the weak terminations beginning with a vowel, and @deva[नी] before the weak terminations beginning with a consonant.[^1]

[^1]: @deva[क्र्यादिभ्यः श्ना] । Pāṇ. III. 1. 81.

rules.title: Fifth and Eighth Class Paradigms
rules.body:
(a) The penultimate nasal of a root is dropped before @deva[ना] &c. as @deva[ग्रथ्नामि], @deva[ग्रथ्नीवः], @deva[ग्रथ्नीमः] &c. from @deva[ग्रन्थ्] 'to put together.'

(b) In the case of roots ending in a consonant, the imperative second person singular termination is @deva[आन] instead of @deva[हि]; as @deva[मुषाण] from @deva[मुष्] 'to steal'.

---

rules.title: @deva[क्षुभ्] and the @deva[न्/ण्] of @deva[ना]

**IRREGULAR SPECIAL BASES OF THE NINTH CLASS.**

In the case of the root @deva[क्षुभ्] the @deva[न्] of @deva[ना] is not changed to @deva[ण्]; as @deva[क्षुभ्नाति], @deva[क्षुभ्नीतः], @deva[क्षुभ्नन्ति], &c.

rules.title: Special Sandhi Rules for Group II - Nine Rules
rules.body:
**Second, Third and Seventh Classes.**

Special rules of Sandhi of the finals of roots and the initial letters of terminations:—

(1) The ending @deva[उ] of a root takes its Vṛddhi substitute when followed by a consonantal strong termination; as @deva[नु+मि=नौमि].

(2) The final @deva[इ] or @deva[उ], short or long, of a root is changed to @deva[इय्] or @deva[उव्] before a vowel weak termination.

(3) The ending @deva[ह्] of roots is changed to @deva[ढ्] when followed by any consonant, except a nasal or a semivowel, or by nothing; and that of roots beginning with @deva[द्] to @deva[घ्] under the same circumstances.

(4) The initial @deva[त्] or @deva[थ्] of a termination is changed to @deva[ध्] after a soft aspirate (4th letter of a class).

(5) @deva[ढ्] or @deva[ष्] followed by @deva[स्] is changed to @deva[क्].

(6) @deva[न्] and @deva[म्] when followed by a consonant are changed to the nasal of the class to which the following consonant belongs, and to an *anusvāra* when followed by @deva[श्], @deva[ष्], @deva[स्] or @deva[ह्].

(7) The ending @deva[इ] of a root, short or long, not preceded by a conjunct consonant is changed to @deva[य्] before vowel weak terminations, when the base consists of more than one syllable.

(8) The ending @deva[द्] of a root is optionally changed to @deva[र्] or Visarga in the Imperfect second pers. sing. and the ending @deva[स्] to @deva[त्] or @deva[द्] before the termination @deva[त्] and optionally before @deva[स्].

(9) When a conjunct consonant having @deva[स्] or @deva[क्] for its first member is at the end of a word or is followed by a consonant except a nasal or a semivowel, the @deva[स्] or @deva[क्] is dropped.

N. B.—The usual Sandhi rules i. e. those given in the 2nd and 3rd Chapters should be observed.

rules.title: Second Person Singular Imperative Termination @deva[धि]
rules.body:
(1)[^1] The second person sing. termination of the Parasm. Imperative is @deva[धि] when the base ends in any consonant except a nasal or a semivowel; also in the case of the root @deva[हु] 3 P. 'to sacrifice.'

[^1]: @deva[हुझल्भ्यो हेर्धिः ।] Pāṇ. VI. 4 101

rules.title: Dropping of @deva[स्] and @deva[त्] in Imperfect; Second Class
rules.body: The @deva[स्] and @deva[त्] of the Imperfect 2nd and 3rd per. sing. are dropped after a consonant.

rules.title: Direct Addition of Terminations in Second Class
rules.body:
**Second (or @deva[अदादि]) Class.**

In this class the terminations are directly added to the root.

rules.title: Highly Irregular Verb @deva[अस्] (to be)
rules.body:
@deva[अस्] P. (Â.[^1] rare) 'to be'—drops its @deva[अ] before weak terminations and @deva[स्] before a termination beginning with @deva[स्] and @deva[ध्व]. Before 2 and 3 Imperf. it takes the augment @deva[ई]. It is irregular in many respects.

**Present.**

| | P. | | | Â. | | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| | S. | D. | P. | S. | D. | P. |
| 1. | @deva[अस्मि] | @deva[स्वः] | @deva[स्मः] | @deva[हे] | @deva[स्वहे] | @deva[स्महे] |
| 2. | @deva[असि] | @deva[स्थः] | @deva[स्थ] | @deva[से] | @deva[साथे] | @deva[ध्वे] |
| 3. | @deva[अस्ति] | @deva[स्तः] | @deva[सन्ति] | @deva[स्ते] | @deva[साते] | @deva[सते] |

**Imperfect.**

| | Par. | | | Ātm. | | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| | S. | D. | P. | S. | D. | P. |
| 1. | @deva[आसम्] | @deva[आस्व] | @deva[आस्म] | @deva[आसि] | @deva[आस्वहि] | @deva[आस्महि] |
| 2. | @deva[आसीः] | @deva[आस्तम्] | @deva[आस्त] | @deva[आस्थाः] | @deva[आसाथाम्] | @deva[आध्वम्] |
| 3. | @deva[आसीत्] | @deva[आस्ताम्] | @deva[आसन्] | @deva[आस्त] | @deva[आसाताम्] | @deva[आसत] |

**Imperative.**

| | Par. | | | Ātm. | | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| | S. | D. | P. | S. | D. | P. |
| 1. | @deva[असानि] | @deva[असाव] | @deva[असाम] | @deva[असै] | @deva[असावहै] | @deva[असामहै] |
| 2. | @deva[एधि] | @deva[स्तम्] | @deva[स्त] | @deva[स्व] | @deva[साथाम्] | @deva[ध्वम्] |
| 3. | @deva[अस्तु] | @deva[स्ताम्] | @deva[सन्तु] | @deva[स्ताम्] | @deva[साताम्] | @deva[सताम्] |

**Potential.**

| | Par. | | | Ātm. | | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| | S. | D. | P. | S. | D. | P. |
| 1. | @deva[स्याम्] | @deva[स्याव] | @deva[स्याम] | @deva[सीय] | @deva[सीवहि] | @deva[सीमहि] |
| 2. | @deva[स्याः] | @deva[स्यातम्] | @deva[स्यात] | @deva[सीथाः] | @deva[सीयाथाम्] | @deva[सीध्वम्] |
| 3. | @deva[स्यात्] | @deva[स्याताम्] | @deva[स्युः] | @deva[सीत] | @deva[सीयाताम्] | @deva[सीरन्] |

[^1]: @deva[अस्] is Ātmanepadi in a few cases. Cf. Bhaṭṭikāvya II. 35 '@deva[अन्यो व्यतिस्ते तु ममापि धर्मः]' &c. where it implies @deva[कर्मव्यतिहार] or an exchange of duty.

rules.title: Irregular Forms of @deva[इ] (to go) and @deva[अधि] with @deva[इ]
rules.body:
The @deva[इ] of the root @deva[इ] P.[^1] 'to go' is changed to @deva[य्] before a weak vowel termination; @deva[एति] @deva[इतः] @deva[यन्ति] 3 pers. Pre.; @deva[आयम्] @deva[ऐव] @deva[ऐम] 1st Pers. Imperf., @deva[ऐः] 2 sing. Imperf.; @deva[अयानि], @deva[इहि], @deva[एतु] 1. 2. 3. sings. Imp.; @deva[यन्तु] 3 pl. Imp.

@deva[इ] with @deva[अधि] Â.[^2] 'to study.' &c. is regularly conjugated; as

**Present.**

| | Ātm. | | |
|---|---|---|---|
| | S. | D. | P. |
| 1. | @deva[अधीये] | @deva[अधीवहे] | @deva[अधीमहे] |
| 2. | @deva[अधीषे] | @deva[अधीयाथे] | @deva[अधीध्वे] |
| 3. | @deva[अधीते] | @deva[अधीयाते] | @deva[अधीयते] |

**Imperfect.**

| | Ātm. | | |
|---|---|---|---|
| | S. | D. | P. |
| 1. | @deva[अध्यैयि] | @deva[अध्यैवहि] | @deva[अध्यैमहि] |
| 2. | @deva[अध्यैथाः] | @deva[अध्यैयाथाम्] | @deva[अध्यैध्वम्] |
| 3. | @deva[अध्यैत] | @deva[अध्यैयाताम्] | @deva[अध्यैयत] |

**Imperative.**

| | Ātm. | | |
|---|---|---|---|
| | S. | D. | P. |
| 1. | @deva[अध्ययै] | @deva[अध्ययावहै] | @deva[अध्ययामहै] |
| 2. | @deva[अधीष्व] | @deva[अधीयाथाम्] | @deva[अधीध्वम्] |
| 3. | @deva[अधीताम्] | @deva[अधीयाताम्] | @deva[अधीयताम्] |

**Potential.**

| | Ātm. | | |
|---|---|---|---|
| | S. | D. | P. |
| 1. | @deva[अधीयीय] | @deva[अधीयीवहि] | @deva[अधीयीमहि] |
| 2. | @deva[अधीयीथाः] | @deva[अधीयीयाथाम्] | @deva[अधीयीध्वम्] |
| 3. | @deva[अधीयीत] | @deva[अधीयीयाताम्] | @deva[अधीयीरन्] |

[^1]: @deva[ई] P. 'to go' is conjugated regularly like @deva[वी]—@deva[एति] @deva[ईतः] @deva[इयन्ति] 3rd Pers. Pre.; @deva[ईहि] 2 sing. Imp. @deva[इयन्तु] 3 plural Imp.
[^2]: @deva[इ] with @deva[अधि] P. 'to remember' should be conjugated like @deva[इ], @deva[अधियन्ति] 3rd pl. Pre. Some think that it is to be conjugated like @deva[इ] in the Non-conjugational tenses only. According to them the third pers. plu. will be @deva[अधीयन्ति]. The line of Bhaṭṭi '@deva[सतीतयो राघवयोरधीयन्]' III. 18 &c. is quoted in support of this opinion. @deva[केचित्तु आर्धधातुकाधिकारोक्तस्यैवातिदेशमाहुः । तन्मते यण्न ।] Sid. Kau.

rules.title: Third Class Formation: Reduplication and @deva[न्] Dropping
rules.body:
## THIRD OR @deva[जुहोत्यादि] CLASS.

(a) The base is formed by reduplication of the root.

(b) The third personal plural termination loses its @deva[न्].

(c) The Imperfect third person plural termination is @deva[उस्] (P.), before which the final @deva[आ] of roots is dropped and the final @deva[इ], @deva[उ] and @deva[ऋ], short or long, are guṇated.

**Rules of Reduplication:—**

rules.title: Reduplication - First Vowel with Initial Consonant
rules.body:
The first vowel of a root together with the initial consonant, if any, is reduplicated i. e. doubled; as @deva[पत्]=@deva[पपत्], @deva[उख्]—@deva[उउख्], &c. after reduplication.

**Note**—The first syllable of a reduplicated root is called 'the reduplicative syllable;' e. g. the first @deva[प] in @deva[पपत्], or first @deva[उ] in @deva[उउख्].

rules.title: Reduplication of Conjunct Consonants
rules.body:
If a conjunct consonant begins a root, the first consonant only with the following vowel is reduplicated; e. g. @deva[प्रच्छ्]–@deva[पप्रच्छ्].

(a) If the first member of a conjunct consonant, however, be a sibilant (@deva[श्], @deva[ष्] or @deva[स्]) and the second a hard consonant, the hard consonant is reduplicated. @deva[स्पर्ध्]–@deva[पस्पर्ध्], @deva[श्चुत्]–@deva[चुश्चुत्]; but @deva[स्वन्]–@deva[सस्वन्] &c.

rules.title: Aspirates Become Unaspirates in Reduplicative Syllable
rules.body: A radical aspirate (2nd or 4th letter of a class) is changed to its corresponding unaspirate in the reduplicative syllable; as @deva[छिद्]–@deva[चिच्छिद्], @deva[धु]–@deva[दुधु], @deva[भुज्]–@deva[बुभुज्], &c.

rules.title: Gutturals to Palatals and @deva[ह्] to @deva[ज्] in Reduplicative Syllable
rules.body: The guttural of the reduplicative syllable is changed to the corresponding palatal (subject to the above rule) and @deva[ह्] to @deva[ज्]; e. g. @deva[कम्]-@deva[ककम्]-@deva[चकम्], @deva[खन्]-@deva[खखन्]-@deva[कखन्]=@deva[चखन्], @deva[हु]-@deva[जुहु] &c.

rules.title: Long Vowels Shortened and @deva[ऋ] to @deva[अ] in Reduplicative Syllable
rules.body: A radical long vowel becomes short and @deva[ऋ] is changed to @deva[अ] in the reduplicative syllable; as @deva[धा]-@deva[दधा], @deva[नी]-@deva[निनी], @deva[कृ]-@deva[चकृ] &c.

rules.title: Penultimate Vowel Changes and Third Class Paradigms
rules.body:
The penultimate @deva[ए] or @deva[ऐ] and @deva[ओ] or @deva[औ] become @deva[इ] and @deva[उ] respectively in the reduplicative syllable; @deva[सेव्]-@deva[सिषेव्], @deva[ढौक्]—@deva[डुढौक्], &c.

rules.title: Roots @deva[मा], @deva[हा], @deva[भृ], @deva[पृ] with @deva[इ] in Reduplicative Syllable
rules.body:
## IRREGULAR BASES:—

The vowel of the roots @deva[मा], @deva[हा] 'to go,' @deva[भृ], @deva[पृ] or @deva[पॄ] 'to fill' and @deva[ऋ] is changed to @deva[इ] in the reduplicative syllable.

rules.title: @deva[निज्], @deva[विज्], @deva[विष्] with Guṇa in Reduplicative Syllable
rules.body: The @deva[इ] of the reduplicative syllable of @deva[निज्], @deva[विज्] and @deva[विष्], takes its Guṇa substitute before all terminations and the radical @deva[इ] is not guṇated before vowel strong terminations.

rules.title: @deva[दा] and @deva[धा] Dropping @deva[आ] After Reduplication
rules.body: @deva[दा] and @deva[धा] drop their @deva[आ] after reduplication before weak terminations; @deva[दध्] becomes @deva[धद्] before @deva[स्], @deva[ध्व], @deva[त] and @deva[थ]. The Par. Imperative 2 per. singulars are @deva[देहि] and @deva[धेहि] respectively.

rules.title: @deva[भी] and the Forms @deva[मिमी], @deva[जिही]
rules.body:
@deva[भी] optionally shortens its vowel before consonantal weak terminations.

(a) @deva[मा] and @deva[हा] 'to go' assume the forms @deva[मिम्] and @deva[जिह्] before vowel terminations and @deva[मिमी] and @deva[जिही] before consonantal terminations.

rules.title: Complete Third Class Paradigms; @deva[हा] (to abandon)
rules.body:
@deva[हा] 'to abandon' assumes the forms @deva[जहि] or @deva[जही] before consonantal weak terminations except in the Pot. and @deva[जह्] before vowel terminations and those of the Pot. The Imp. 2 sing. forms are @deva[जहाहि], @deva[जहिहि] and @deva[जहीहि].

rules.title: Seventh Class Formation: Insertion of @deva[न] and @deva[न्]
rules.body:
## Seventh or @deva[रुधादि] Class.

In this class the base is formed by inserting @deva[न] between the radical vowel and the final consonant before the strong and @deva[न्] before the weak terminations.

rules.title: Complete Seventh Class Paradigms
rules.body:
(a) The original nasal of a root is dropped.

(b) In the case of the root @deva[तृह्], @deva[न] is changed to @deva[ने] before consonantal strong terminations.
