| @deva[स्रिव्] | 'to go, to become dry.' | @deva[स्रुत] | @deva[स्त्यै] | with @deva[प्र] | @deva[प्रस्तीत] or @deva[प्रस्तीम] 'sounded.' |
| @deva[ह्लाद्] | 'to delight' | @deva[ह्लन्न] | @deva[स्ना] | with @deva[नि] | @deva[निष्णात] 'clever.' |
| @deva[श्रा] | to cook (also @deva[श्रप्] cau. of @deva[श्रा]) | @deva[शृत] 'boiled' (when it qualifies @deva[क्षीर] or @deva[हविः]) else @deva[श्राण], @deva[श्रपित]. |  | with @deva[नदी] | @deva[नदीष्ण], 'skilful, experienced, clever.' (lit. one who knows the dangerous spots in a river); but @deva[निस्नात], @deva[नदीस्नात] in other cases. |
| @deva[स्तंभ्] | with @deva[प्रति] and @deva[नि] | @deva[प्रतिस्तब्ध], @deva[निस्तब्ध] (here the @deva[स्] is not changed to @deva[ष्]). |  |  |  |
| @deva[स्फाय्] | 'to grow' | @deva[स्फीत] |  |  |  |

rules.title: Roots @deva[सु] and @deva[यज्] Taking Affix @deva[वत्] in Active Sense
rules.body: (a) The roots @deva[सु] and @deva[यज्] take the affix @deva[वत्] like @deva[त] in an active sense; @deva[सुन्वन्] 'one who extracted Soma juice,' @deva[यज्वन्] 'one who has offered a sacrifice;' @deva[अत्] is added to @deva[जॄ] optionally in the same sense; @deva[जीर्ण] or @deva[जरन्] 'one who has become old' (also @deva[जीर्णवत्]).

rules.title: Declension of Participles in @deva[त] or @deva[न] and Note on Passive Force
rules.body:
The participles in @deva[त] or @deva[न] follow the Declension of nouns in @deva[अ].

The P. P. participles have not always a passive force:—

rules.title: Affix @deva[त] Showing Place of Habitual Action
rules.body:
The affix @deva[त][^1] added to roots having the sense of 'sitting or going, or eating' shows the place where the action takes place; @deva[इदं मुकुन्दस्य आसितं] 'this is the place where Mukunda to sit;' @deva[इदं यातं रमापतेः] 'this is the path by which the husband of Ramā used to pass;' @deva[भुक्तं एतत् अनंतस्य] 'this is the place where Ananta took his food,' &c.

[^1]: @deva[अधिकरणे च ध्रौव्यगतिप्रत्यवसानार्थेभ्यः ।] Pāṇ. III. 4, 48.

rules.title: Past Passive Participles with Active Sense
rules.body: The P. P. Participles of roots implying motion, of intransitive roots, and of the roots @deva[श्लिष्], @deva[शी], @deva[स्था], @deva[आस्], @deva[वस्] 'to dwell,' @deva[जन्], @deva[रुह्], and @deva[जॄ] 4. cl. have an active sense; @deva[गतोऽहं मद्रपुरम्] 'I went to Madras;' @deva[म्लानो बालः] 'the boy has become languid,' @deva[लक्ष्मीमाश्लिष्टो हरिः] 'Hari embraced Lakshmī;' @deva[शेषमधिशयितः] 'slept on Sesha;' @deva[वैकुंठमधिष्ठितः] 'dwelt in Vaikuntha;' @deva[शिवमुपासितः] 'served Shiva,' @deva[हरिदिनमुपोषितः] 'observed a fast on the day sacred to Hari,' @deva[राममनुजातः] 'was born after Rāma;' @deva[गरुडमारूढः] sat on Garuda; @deva[विश्वमनुजीर्णः] 'grew old after the world.'

rules.title: Past Passive Participles as Neuter Abstract Nouns
rules.body: P. P. Participles have sometimes the sense of neuter abstract nouns; as @deva[जल्पितं] 'speech', @deva[शयितं] 'sleep', @deva[हसितं] 'laughing,' similarly @deva[स्थितं], @deva[गतं], etc.; See Bhaṭṭ. VII. 125.

rules.title: Past Passive Participles with Present Tense Sense
rules.body: The P. P. Participles of roots meaning 'to think or to wish,' 'to know,' 'to adore,' and of the roots @deva[इन्ध्], @deva[भी] etc. have the sense of the present Tense; @deva[राज्ञः मतः] 'he is honoured by the king,' @deva[सतां पूजितः इद्धः अग्निः] 'the fire is kindled,' so @deva[भीतः] etc

rules.title: Formation of Past Active Participles
rules.body:
## (d) Past Active Participles.

Past Active participles are derived from the P. Passive Participles in @deva[त] or @deva[न] by adding to them the affix @deva[वत्]; e. g.

| Roots. | P. P. Ptc. | P. Ac. Ptc. | | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| @deva[भू] to be | @deva[भूत] | @deva[भूतवत्] | one or that | has been |
| @deva[कृ] to do | @deva[कृत] | @deva[कृतवत्] | ,, ,, | done |
| @deva[कॄ] to scatter | @deva[कीर्ण] | @deva[कीर्णवत्] | ,, ,, | scattered |
| @deva[छिद्] to cut | @deva[छिन्न] | @deva[छिन्नवत्] | ,, ,, | cut |
| etc. | etc. | etc. | | etc. |

rules.title: Formation of Future Tense Participles
rules.body:
## (e) Participle of the Future Tense.

The Participle of the Simple Future, Active as well as Passive, is formed from the third person singular form of the Second Future of a root. The Parasm. Ptc. is formed simply by dropping the final @deva[इ], and the Ātm. and the Passive one by substituting @deva[मान] for the final @deva[ते]; e. g.

**Participles.**

| Roots. | Par. | Ātm. | Passive. |
|---|---|---|---|
| @deva[दा]— | @deva[दास्यत्] | @deva[दास्यमान] | @deva[दास्यमान] or @deva[दायिष्यमाण] |
| @deva[भू]— | @deva[भविष्यत्] | @deva[भविष्यमाण] | @deva[भविष्यमाण] or @deva[भाविष्यमाण] |

---

| Roots. | Par. | Ātm. | Passive. |
|---|---|---|---|
| @deva[चुर्]—@deva[चोरयिष्यत्] | | @deva[चोरयिष्यमाण] | @deva[चोरयिष्यमाण] or @deva[चोरिष्यमाण] |
| @deva[गम्]—@deva[गमिष्यत्] | | @deva[संगमिष्यमाण] | @deva[गामिष्यमाण] |
| @deva[जि]—@deva[जेष्यत्] | | @deva[विजेष्यमाण] | @deva[जेष्यमाण], @deva[जायिष्यमाण] |
| @deva[कृ]—@deva[करिष्यत्] | | @deva[करिष्यमाण] | @deva[कारिष्यमाण], @deva[कारिष्यमाण] |
| @deva[श्रु]—@deva[श्रोष्यत्] | | @deva[संश्रोष्यमाण] | @deva[श्रोष्यमाण], @deva[श्राविष्यमाण] |
| @deva[एध्]—A. | | @deva[एधिष्यमाण] | @deva[एधिष्यमाण] |
| @deva[तुद्]—@deva[तोत्स्यत्] | | @deva[तोत्स्यमान] | @deva[तोत्स्यमान] |

Similarly @deva[पिपठिष्] Desi. Base of @deva[पठ्]—@deva[पिपठिष्यत्], @deva[पिपठिष्यमाण] &c.: @deva[बोभू] Fre. B. of @deva[भू]—@deva[बोभविष्यत्], @deva[बोभविष्यमाण], &c.

rules.title: Declension of Future Participles
rules.body: These Participles are declined like words ending in @deva[त्] and @deva[अ].

rules.title: Introduction to Potential Participles
rules.body:
## (f) Potential Participles (and Verbal Adjectives).

The Potential Participle is formed by means of the affixes @deva[तव्य][^1], @deva[अनीय], @deva[त] and rarely @deva[एलिम], added to a root or derivative verb. This is Passive when the verb is transitive and impersonal when the verb is intransitive. It is also used like an adjective when denoting fitness, &c.

[^1]: @deva[तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः ।] Pāṇ. III. 1. 96. @deva[केलिमर उपसंख्यानम् ।] Vārtika.

rules.title: Formation of Participles in @deva[तव्य] and @deva[अनीय]
rules.body:
## (1) Participles in @deva[तव्य] and @deva[अनीय].

The affixes @deva[तव्य] or @deva[अनीय] are added to roots or derivative bases in the sense of 'must be fit to be,' &c. Before these the ending vowel and the penultimate short of a root take their Guṇa substitute. Before @deva[तव्य] Seṭ roots take @deva[इ], Aniṭ roots do not, and Veṭ roots take it optionally. Before @deva[अनीय] penultimate @deva[ऋ] is always changed to @deva[अर्] and not to @deva[र्] (as it sometimes does); e. g.

| Roots. | | Pot. Ptc. |
|---|---|---|
| @deva[दा]— | @deva[दातव्य], @deva[दानीय] | what must or ought to be given. |
| @deva[चि]— | @deva[चेतव्य], @deva[चयनीय] | what must or ought to be searched into, &c. |
| @deva[नी]— | @deva[नेतव्य], @deva[नयनीय] | ,, ,, carried. |
| @deva[श्रु]— | @deva[श्रोतव्य], @deva[श्रवणीय] | ,, ,, heard. |
| @deva[भू]— | @deva[भवितव्य], @deva[भवनीय] | ,, ,, been. |
| @deva[कृ]— | @deva[कर्तव्य], @deva[करणीय] | ,, ,, done. |
| @deva[बुध्]— | @deva[बोधितव्य], @deva[बोधनीय], @deva[बोद्धव्य] | ,, ,, known. |
| @deva[मुच्]— | @deva[मोक्तव्य], @deva[मोचनीय] | ,, ,, released. |
| @deva[मृज्]— | @deva[मार्ष्टव्य][^1], @deva[मार्जनीय] | ,, ,, wiped. |
| @deva[सृज्]— | @deva[स्रष्टव्य], @deva[सर्जनीय] | ,, ,, created. |
| @deva[भ्रस्ज्]— | @deva[भर्ष्टव्य], @deva[भर्जनीय], @deva[भ्रष्टव्य], @deva[भ्रज्जनीय] | ,, ,, fried. |
| @deva[भिद्]— | @deva[भेत्तव्य], @deva[भेदनीय] | ,, ,, split. |
| @deva[निन्द्]— | @deva[निन्दितव्य], @deva[निन्दनीय] | ,, ,, censured. |
| @deva[गुह्]— | @deva[गोढव्य], @deva[गूहनीय], @deva[गूहितव्य][^2] | ,, ,, concealed. |

[^1]: The @deva[ऋ] of @deva[मृज्] is changed to @deva[आर्] against § 712.

[^2]: The @deva[उ] of @deva[गुह्] is lengthened instead of being Guṇated before a strong termination beginning with a vowel.

rules.title: Participles in @deva[अनीय] for Causals, Frequentatives, and Desideratives
rules.body:
The final @deva[अय] of roots of the tenth class and of causals, the final @deva[अ] of Ātm. Freq. Bases, when the @deva[य] is preceded by a vowel and the whole @deva[य] when it is preceded by a consonant, are dropped before @deva[अनीय]. To Desiderative bases it is added without any change; e. g.

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| @deva[कथ्]— | @deva[कथनीय] | what must, or ought to be told. |
| @deva[चुर्]— | @deva[चोरणीय] | ,, ,, stolen. |
| @deva[बोधय] cau. of @deva[बुध्]— | @deva[बोधनीय] | ,, ,, made to know. |
| @deva[बोबुध्य] Ātm. Freq. Base of ,, | @deva[बोबुधनीय] | ,, ,, known frequently. |
| @deva[बोभूय]—Ātm. freq. Base of @deva[भू]— | @deva[बोभूयनीय] | what must or ought to be frequently. |
| @deva[बुबोधिष्] Desi. Base of @deva[बुध्] | @deva[बुबोधिषणीय] | ,, ,, desired to know. |

rules.title: Affix @deva[य] (@deva[यत्]) for Vowel-Ending Roots
rules.body:
## (2) Participles in @deva[य] (@deva[यत्], @deva[क्यप्] and @deva[ण्यत्]).

**By means of @deva[यत्] (@deva[य]).**

The affix @deva[य] (@deva[यत्])[^1] is added on to roots ending in a vowel in the sense of 'fit for, or fit to be, or ought to be.' Before this @deva[य] the radical vowel undergoes Guṇa substitute and final @deva[आ] (@deva[ए], @deva[ऐ] and @deva[ओ] changeable to @deva[आ]) is changed to @deva[ए].

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| @deva[दा]— | @deva[देय] | what is fit or ought to be given. |
| @deva[धे]— | @deva[धेय] | ,, ,, sucked. |
| @deva[गै]— | @deva[गेय] | ,, ,, sung. |
| @deva[छो]— | @deva[छेय] | ,, ,, cut. |
| @deva[चि]— | @deva[चेय] | ,, ,, collected. |
| @deva[नी]— | @deva[नेय] | ,, ,, led or carried. |

[^1]: @deva[अचो यत् ।] Pāṇ. III. 1. 97.

rules.title: Affix @deva[य] for Roots with Penultimate @deva[अ] and Labial Ending
rules.body:
Roots having @deva[अ] for their penultimate and ending in a consonant of the labial class take the affix @deva[य]; @deva[शप्]—@deva[शप्य]; @deva[लभ्]—@deva[लभ्य]; @deva[रम्]—@deva[रम्य], &c.

(a) When @deva[लभ्] is preceded by @deva[आ], @deva[न्] (changed to @deva[म्]) is inserted between @deva[ल] and @deva[भ्]; @deva[आलभ्]—@deva[आलंभ्य] 'what ought or is fit to be killed;' @deva[न्] is also inserted when @deva[लभ्] is preceded by @deva[उप] if the meaning be 'to praise;' @deva[उपलंभ्यः साधुः] 'a Sādhu ought to be praised;' but @deva[उपलभ्यं धनं] 'wealth ought to be acquired.'

rules.title: Specific Roots Taking Affix @deva[य]
rules.body: The roots @deva[तक्] 'to laugh at,' @deva[शस्] 'to kill,' @deva[चत्] to 'look for, to ask,' @deva[यत्] 'to strive,' @deva[जन्], @deva[शक्] and @deva[सह्] take the affix @deva[य]; @deva[तक्यं] 'what is fit to be laughed at,' @deva[शस्यं] 'what ought to be killed;' &c.

rules.title: @deva[गद्], @deva[मद्], @deva[चर्], @deva[यम्] Taking @deva[य] Without Preposition
rules.body: The roots @deva[गद्], @deva[मद्], @deva[चर्] and @deva[यम्], take the affix @deva[य] when not preceded by a preposition; @deva[गद्]—@deva[गद्य] 'what ought to be spoken or told;' @deva[मद्य], @deva[चर्य], @deva[यम्य]. @deva[चर्] with @deva[आ] may take this affix, if it does not mean 'a preceptor;' in which case it takes the affix @deva[ण्यत्] (@deva[य]) @deva[आचर्यो देशः] 'a country fit to be gone to, but @deva[आचार्यः] 'a preceptor.'

rules.title: @deva[वद्], @deva[पण्], and @deva[वृ] Taking @deva[य] with Semantic Conditions
rules.body: The roots @deva[वद्] implying reproach, @deva[पण्] meaning 'to transact business,' and @deva[वृ] 9 Ātm. not denoting limit or restraint, take the suffix @deva[य]; as @deva[अवद्यं पापं] 'sin is reprehensible or merits condemnation;' but @deva[अनुद्यं] (@deva[अन्+वद्+क्यप्] i. e. @deva[य]) @deva[गुरुनाम] 'the name of a preceptor ought not to be uttered (out of respect),' @deva[पण्या गौः] 'a cow is saleable;' but @deva[पाण्यः] (@deva[पण्+ण्यत्] i. e. @deva[य]) @deva[ब्राह्मणः] 'a Brāhmaṇa deserving praise;' @deva[वर्य] 'that can be chosen or sought after;' as @deva[शतेन वर्या कन्या] 'hundred men (i. e. any one) can seek the hand of a girl;' but @deva[वृत्या] (@deva[वृ+क्यप्] i. e. @deva[य]) @deva[कन्या] 'to be married by a particular man.'

rules.title: @deva[वह्] and @deva[ऋ] Taking @deva[य] in Specific Senses
rules.body: The root @deva[वह्] not denoting an instrument for carrying, and @deva[ऋ] in the sense of 'a master or a Vaishya' take @deva[य]; @deva[वह्यं] 'a carriage or a vehicle;' but @deva[वाह्य] (@deva[वह्+ण्यत्]) 'what can be borne;' @deva[अर्यः] 'a master or a Vaishya;' but @deva[आर्य] (@deva[ऋ+ण्यत्]) 'fit to be approached or adored.'

rules.title: @deva[सृ] with @deva[उप] Taking @deva[य] for Conception Sense
rules.body: @deva[सृ] with @deva[उप] in the sense of 'being conceived' takes the affix @deva[य]; as @deva[उपसर्या गौः गर्भाधानार्थं वृषभेण उपगन्तुं योग्येत्यर्थः]. (Sid. Kau.) but @deva[उपसार्या] (@deva[उपसृ+ण्यत्]) @deva[काशी प्राप्तव्या इत्यर्थः] (Sid. Kau.).

rules.title: @deva[जॄ] Taking @deva[य] with Negative Particle
rules.body: @deva[जॄ] takes this affix with the negative particle prefixed to it and forms @deva[अजर्य] 'what cannot grow old' but this must qualify @deva[संगतं] 'friendship;' cf. @deva[तेन संगतमार्येण रामाचर्यं कुरु द्रुतम् ।] Bhaṭṭi. VI. 53. In @deva[मृगैरजर्यं जरसोपदिष्टमदेहबन्धाय पुनर्बबन्ध ।] Rag. XVIII. 7, the word @deva[संगत] must be considered as understood. If it does not qualify @deva[संगत], it will take the affix @deva[तृ]; as @deva[अजरिता कम्बल].

rules.title: @deva[हन्] Taking @deva[यत्] or @deva[ण्यत्] Optionally
rules.body: @deva[हन्] takes the affix @deva[यत्] optionally, before which @deva[वध्] is substituted for it; @deva[हन्+य=वध्य]='what ought to be killed;' it optionally takes @deva[ण्यत्], in which case @deva[घात्] is substituted for it; @deva[घात्यः].

rules.title: Roots Taking Affix @deva[क्यप्] (@deva[य])
rules.body:
**By means of the affix @deva[क्यप्] (@deva[य])**

The roots @deva[इ] 1. 2. P. 'to go,' @deva[स्तु], @deva[शास्], @deva[वृ] 5. P. A., @deva[दृ], @deva[जुष्], and roots having @deva[ऋ] short for their penultimate, except @deva[कॢप्] and @deva[चृत्], take the affix @deva[क्यप्] (@deva[य]) in the same sense as @deva[यत्]. When a root ends in a short vowel, @deva[त्] is inserted between the final vowel and the affix @deva[य]; e. g. @deva[इ]—@deva[इत्य] 'worthy of being approached;' @deva[स्तुत्य] 'deserving praise;' @deva[शास्]—@deva[शिष्य] 'fit to be instructed;' @deva[वृत्]—@deva[वृत्य]; @deva[दृ]—@deva[आदृत्य]; @deva[जुष्]—@deva[जुष्य] 'worthy of being served;' @deva[वृत्]—@deva[वृत्य]; @deva[वृध्]—@deva[वृध्य] 'fit to be increased as wealth, &c.' but @deva[कल्प्य] (@deva[कॢप्+यत्]) 'able;' @deva[चृत्]—@deva[चर्त्य] (@deva[चृत्+ण्यत्]) 'that ought to be teased or hurt.'

rules.title: @deva[शंस्], @deva[दुह्], @deva[गुह्] Taking @deva[क्यप्] Optionally According to Vāmana
rules.body: According to Vāmana, the roots @deva[शंस्], @deva[दुह्] and @deva[गुह्] take this affix optionally; @deva[शंस्]—@deva[शस्य] 'praiseworthy;' @deva[दुह्]—@deva[दुह्य], @deva[गुह्]—@deva[गुह्य]; optionally they take the affix @deva[ण्यत्] (to be given hereafter); @deva[शंस्य], @deva[दोह्य], @deva[गोह्य].

rules.title: @deva[मृज्] Taking @deva[क्यप्] or @deva[ण्यत्] Optionally
rules.body: @deva[मृज्] also takes this affix optionally; @deva[मृज्य] 'what is fit or ought to be cleansed;' optionally it takes @deva[ण्यत्] before which the final @deva[ज्] is changed to @deva[ग्]; @deva[मार्ग्य].

rules.title: @deva[भू] and @deva[वद्] with Subanta Taking @deva[क्यप्]
rules.body:
(a) @deva[भू] when it has a Subanta prefixed to it and is without a preposition takes the affix @deva[क्यप्] impersonally; @deva[ब्रह्मणो भावः] @deva[ब्रह्मभूयं] 'identity with Brahman.' When no Subanta is used prepositionally with it, it takes the affix @deva[यत्]; @deva[भव्य] or @deva[प्रभव्य].

(a) @deva[वद्] under similar circumstances takes either @deva[क्यप्] or @deva[ण्यत्] in a passive sense or impersonally; @deva[ब्रह्मोद्यं] or @deva[ब्रह्मवद्यं] 'expounding the Veda' (@deva[ब्रह्म वेदः तस्य वदनं] Sid. Kau.).

rules.title: @deva[खन्] Taking @deva[क्यप्] with @deva[न्] Dropping and @deva[ई] Addition
rules.body: @deva[खन्] takes this affix, but drops its @deva[न्] and adds @deva[ई] to its penultimate vowel; @deva[खन्+य=ख+य=ख+ई+य=खेय] 'what is fit or ought to be dug or excavated.'

rules.title: @deva[भृ] 1. cl. Taking @deva[क्यप्] When Not Forming a Name
rules.body:
@deva[भृ] 1. cl. takes this affix when the participle so derived does not form a name; @deva[भृत्याः] 'those who ought to be nourished or maintained, hence servants,' &c; but @deva[भार्याः] (@deva[भृ+ण्यत्]) 'a class of Kshatriyas;' when @deva[सम्] precedes @deva[भृ], @deva[क्यप्] and @deva[ण्यत्] are added optionally @deva[संभृत्याः] or @deva[संभार्याः].

*N. B.* The word @deva[भार्या] meaning 'a wife' ought to be derived from @deva[भृ] of the 3rd class and affix @deva[ण्यत्].

rules.title: Seven Irregular Words with @deva[क्यप्]
rules.body:
The following seven words are irregularly formed with the affix @deva[क्यप्] in the sense given in each case[^1]—@deva[राजसूयः] (@deva[राजन्+सू+क्यप्]) @deva[राजा सोतव्यः अभिषवद्वारा निष्पादयितव्यः ।] @deva[यद्वा लतात्मकः सोमः राजा स सूयते कण्ड्यते अत्र इत्यादिकरणे क्यप् । निपादनादीर्घः]; also @deva[राजसूयम्]; @deva[सूर्यः] (@deva[सृ+क्यप्], or @deva[सू] 6 P. 'to incite,' 'to impel' + @deva[क्यप्]) @deva[सरति आकाशे । कर्तरि क्यप्, निपातनादूत्वं । यद्वा षू प्रेरणे तुदादिः; सुवति कर्माणि लोकं प्रेरयतीति क्यपो रुट् ।] @deva[मृषोद्य] 'falsehood' (from @deva[मृषा+वद्+क्यप्]); @deva[रोचते इति रुच्यः]; @deva[कुप्यं] (any base metal) fr. @deva[गुप्+क्यप् । गुपेरादेः कुत्वं च संज्ञायाम् । सुवर्णरजतभिन्नं धनं कुप्यम् ।] Cf. Kir. I. 35, Manu. VII. 96. @deva[गुप्] in other cases takes the affix @deva[ण्यत्]; @deva[गोप्यं] 'what ought to be concealed' @deva[कृष्टे स्वयमेव पच्यन्ते कृष्टपच्याः कर्मकर्तरि । शुद्धे तु कर्मणि कृष्णपाक्याः ।] 'growing in cultivated ground;' @deva[न व्यथते अव्यथ्यः] 'not feeling pain.'[^2]

[^1]: @deva[राजसूयसूर्यमृषोद्यरुच्यकुप्यकृष्टपच्याव्यथ्याः ।] Pāṇ. III. I. 114. Vide Sid. Kau. on the same.

[^2]: Cf. @deva[मित्रो जनान्यातयति ब्रुवाणो], &c. Rig III 59. 1.

rules.title: River Names and Constellation Names with @deva[क्यप्]
rules.body:
(a) The following two words which are the names of two rivers are derived by means of this affix; @deva[भिनत्ति कूलं भिद्यः] from @deva[भिद्+क्यप्]; @deva[उज्झत्युदकं उज्झ्यः], @deva[उज्झ्+क्यप्]; see Rag. XI. 8. In other cases these roots take the affix @deva[तृ]; @deva[भेत्ता], @deva[उज्झिता].

(b) Similarly the words @deva[पुष्यः] and @deva[सिध्यः]; both the names of the constellation Pushya, are derived from @deva[पुष्] and @deva[सिध्] respectively with the affix @deva[क्यप्]; @deva[पुष्यन्त्यस्मिन्नर्थाः पुष्यः], @deva[सिध्यन्त्यस्मिन् सिध्यः].

rules.title: @deva[पू], @deva[नी], @deva[जि] with @deva[वि] Taking @deva[क्यप्] in Specific Contexts
rules.body: The roots @deva[पू], @deva[नी] and @deva[जि], preceded by @deva[वि], take this affix, when they are connected with the words @deva[मुञ्ज], @deva[कल्क] and @deva[हल] respectively, @deva[विपूयो मुञ्जः] 'The Munja grass to be prepared for weaving into a rope' (@deva[मुञ्जादिकरणाय शोधयितव्य इत्यर्थः] Sid. Kau.); @deva[विनीयः कल्कः] 'sin which ought to be destroyed;' @deva[विजित्यो हलिः] 'The plough to be pulled with great force,' @deva[बलेन कृष्टव्यः], in other cases these take the affix @deva[यत्]; @deva[विपत्य], @deva[विनेय], @deva[जेय].

rules.title: Words Derived from @deva[ग्रह्] with @deva[क्यप्]
rules.body: The following words are derived from the root @deva[ग्रह्] with the affix @deva[क्यप्]:—@deva[अवगृह्यं], @deva[प्रगृह्यं], @deva[पदं] 'two technical terms in grammar;' @deva[गृह्यकाः] 'birds restrained from free motion, such as parrots, &c.;' '@deva[पञ्जरादिबन्धेन परतन्त्रीकृता इत्यर्थः ।] Sid. Kau. @deva[ग्रामगृह्या सेना] 'an army stationed outside a village'; @deva[आर्यैर्गृह्यते आर्यगृह्यः तत्पक्षाश्रित इत्यर्थः] (Sid. Kau.) 'siding with the noble.' See Rag. II. 43.

rules.title: @deva[कृ] and @deva[वृ] Taking Both @deva[क्यप्] and @deva[ण्यत्]
rules.body: The roots @deva[कृ] and @deva[वृ] take both @deva[क्यप्] and @deva[ण्यत्]; @deva[कृत्य], @deva[कार्य]; @deva[वृत्य], @deva[वर्य] 'what ought to be chosen, best,' &c.

rules.title: @deva[युज्] Taking @deva[क्यप्] with Final Consonant Change
rules.body: @deva[युज्] in the sense of 'to be harnessed' takes the affix @deva[क्यप्] and changes its final to @deva[ग्]; @deva[युग्यः गौः] 'a bull to be harnessed to the yoke;' in other senses it takes the affix @deva[ण्यत्]—@deva[योज्य].

rules.title: Affix @deva[ण्यत्] (@deva[य]) for @deva[ऋ]-Ending and Consonant-Ending Roots
@deva[वस्] with @deva[अमा] Taking @deva[ण्यत्] and @deva[सृज्] with Special Prefixes
rules.body:
The root @deva[वस्] when preceded by @deva[अमा] 'with' takes the affix @deva[ण्यत्] before which the penultimate @deva[अ] is optionally changed to Vṛiddhi; @deva[अमा सह वसतोऽस्यां चन्द्रार्कौ] @deva[अमावस्या] or @deva[वास्या] 'the day on which the sun and the moon are with each other i. e. are in conjunction.'

(a) @deva[सृज्] when preceded by @deva[पाणि] or the preposition @deva[समव] takes the affix @deva[ण्यत्]; as @deva[पाणिभ्यां सृज्यते पाणिसर्ग्या रज्जुः]; similarly @deva[समवसर्ग्या].

rules.title: Roots Not Changing @deva[च्] or @deva[ज्] Before @deva[ण्यत्]
rules.body:
(a) The roots @deva[यज्], @deva[याच्], @deva[रुच्], @deva[प्रवच्], @deva[त्यज्], and @deva[पच्] do not change their @deva[च्] or @deva[ज्] to @deva[क्] or @deva[ग्] before @deva[ण्यत्]; @deva[याज्यम्], @deva[याच्यम्]; @deva[रोच्यम्], @deva[प्रवाच्यम्] (@deva[ग्रन्थविशेषः]), @deva[अर्च्य], @deva[त्याज्य], @deva[पाच्य].

(b) @deva[वच्] does not change its @deva[च्] to @deva[क्] before @deva[ण्यत्] when the meaning is 'what ought to be spoken out, speech,' @deva[वाच्यं]; but @deva[वाक्यं]; a sentence.'

(c) @deva[वञ्च्] when it means 'to go' does not change @deva[च्] its to @deva[क्]; @deva[वञ्च्यम्]; when it means 'to bend' the @deva[च्] is changed to @deva[क्]; @deva[वङ्क्यं काष्ठम्].

(d) @deva[युज्] when it is preceded by @deva[प्र] and @deva[नि], takes the affix @deva[ण्यत्] in the sense of 'what is possible or capable of;' and does not change its @deva[ज्] to @deva[ग्]; @deva[प्रयोक्तुं शक्य प्रयोज्यः], @deva[नियोक्तुं शक्यः नियोज्यः भृत्यः ।]

(e) @deva[भुज्] has @deva[भोज्यं] meaning 'food,' and @deva[भोग्यं] 'what is fit to be enjoyed.'

rules.title: Affix @deva[ण्यत्] for @deva[उ]-Ending Roots and Selected Labial-Ending Roots
rules.body:
Roots ending in @deva[उ], short or long, take the affix @deva[ण्यत्] in the sense of 'what ought or must necessarily be done;' @deva[लू]—@deva[लाव्यं] 'what must necessarily be cut off;' @deva[पाव्यं] 'what must necessarily be purified;' @deva[सू] with @deva[आ]—@deva[आसाव्यं], @deva[यु] 'to mix,' @deva[याव्य], &c.

(a) The roots @deva[वप्], @deva[रप्], @deva[लप्], @deva[भप्] and @deva[चप्] also do the same; @deva[वाप्यं] 'what must necessarily be sown;' @deva[राप्यम्], 'what must be spoken of distinctly;' @deva[लाप्यम्], @deva[भाप्यम्], @deva[चाप्यम्].

rules.title: Irregular Words Derived with Affix @deva[ण्यत्]
rules.body: The following words are irregularly derived by means of the affix @deva[ण्यत्]; @deva[आनाय्यः] 'what ought to be brought from the Gārhapatya i. e. the Dakshināgni;' (fr. @deva[नी] with @deva[आ]) @deva[दक्षिणाग्निविशेष एवेदम् । स हि गार्हपत्यादानीयतेऽनित्यश्च सततमज्वलनात् ।] (Sid. Kau.;) but @deva[आनेय] in other cases; as 'a jar,' @deva[प्रणाय्यः] (fr. @deva[नी] with @deva[प्र]) @deva[चोरः प्रीत्यनर्ह इत्यर्थः] (Sid. Kau); 'disgusted with worldly pleasures;' as @deva[प्रणाय्योन्तेवासी विरक्त इत्यर्थः ।] but @deva[प्रणेय] in other cases.

rules.title: Further Irregular Words with Affix @deva[ण्यत्]
rules.body: @deva[मीयते अनेन इति माय्यं] 'a measure' (fr. @deva[मा]); @deva[सम्यङ् नीयते होमार्थमग्निं प्रति इति सान्नाय्यं] (from. @deva[नी] with @deva[सम्]) @deva[हविर्विशेषः] 'a kind of offering (See Śis XI. 41)'; @deva[निचीयतेऽस्मिन्धान्यादिकं निकाय्यः निवासः] (fr @deva[चि] with @deva[नि]); @deva[धीयते अनया समिदिति धाय्या] (fr. @deva[धा]) @deva[ऋक्]; @deva[कुण्डेन पीयते] (@deva[अस्मिन् सोमः]) @deva[कुण्डपाय्यः क्रतुः]; @deva[संचीयतेऽसौ संचाय्यः] (a sacrifice); @deva[परिचाय्यः], @deva[उपचाय्यः], @deva[समूह्यः] (particular places for depositing the sacrificial fire); @deva[परिचेयम्], @deva[उपेचयम्], @deva[संवाह्यम्] in other cases; @deva[चीयतेऽसौ चित्यः अग्निः]; @deva[अग्नेः चयनं अग्निचित्या].

rules.title: Potential Participles with @deva[यत्], @deva[अनीय] and @deva[ण्यत्] in Active Sense
rules.body: The roots @deva[भू] and @deva[गै] take the affix @deva[यत्]; @deva[वच्] and @deva[स्था] take @deva[अनीय]; and @deva[जन्], @deva[प्लु] and @deva[पत्] take @deva[ण्यत्], in an active sense; @deva[भवतीति भव्यः] (also @deva[भव्यमनेन]); @deva[गायतीति गेयः] 'one who sings' (also @deva[गेयं साम अनेन]); @deva[प्रवचनीयः] 'one who speaks' @deva[उपस्थानीय] 'one who stands by'. @deva[जन्यः], @deva[प्लाव्यः], @deva[पात्यः].

rules.title: Affix @deva[एलिम] for Transitive Roots
rules.body:
## (3) By means of @deva[केलिमर्] (@deva[एलिम]).

A few transitive roots take the affix @deva[एलिम] having the same force as the affix @deva[य]; @deva[पचेलिम] fr. @deva[पच्], 'fit to ripen or to be cooked; as @deva[पचेलिमा माषाः]; @deva[भिदेलिमाः] (fr. @deva[भिद्]) @deva[सरलाः] 'the pine trees ought to be felled;' &c.

rules.title: Declension of Potential Participles
rules.body: The declension of these Participles follows that of nouns ending in @deva[अ].

rules.title: Introduction to Indeclinable Past Participles (Gerunds)
rules.body:
## II. INDECLINABLE PARTICIPLES.

## (a) Indeclinable Past Participles.

The Indeclinable Past Participles are of the nature of gerunds. They fall under two heads:—(1) Those derived by affixing @deva[त्वा] to the simple root, and (2) Those derived by means of @deva[य] affixed to the root compounded with prepositions or words used prepositionally; @deva[गम्]—@deva[गत्वा] 'having gone;' @deva[भू] with @deva[अनु]—@deva[अनुभूय] 'having experienced;' &c.

rules.title: Gerund Formation with @deva[त्वा]
rules.body:
## I. Indeclinable Participles formed with @deva[त्वा].

The indeclinable Past Participle or gerund in @deva[त्वा] is formed of all roots or derivative verbal bases to which no preposition (nor a prepositional word) is prefixed. The affix @deva[त्वा] is of the same nature as the @deva[त] of the Past Passive Participle, so that all the changes that take place before @deva[त] generally also take place before @deva[त्वा]. In other words from the P. P. Ptc. of a root, separate the @deva[त] or @deva[न] from it, add @deva[त्वा] instead, and this will be the form of the gerund in @deva[त्वा] e. g.

| Roots | | P. P. Ptc. | Ind. P. Ptc. |
|---|---|---|---|
| @deva[ज्ञा] | to know | @deva[ज्ञात] | @deva[ज्ञात्वा] |
| @deva[दा] | to give | @deva[दत्त] | @deva[दत्त्वा] |
| @deva[स्था] | to stand | @deva[स्थित] | @deva[स्थित्वा] |
| @deva[हा] | to go | @deva[हान] | @deva[हात्वा] |
| @deva[हा] | to abandon | @deva[हीन] | @deva[हीत्वा] |
| @deva[धा] | to place | @deva[हित] | @deva[हित्वा] |
| @deva[जि] | to conquer | @deva[जित] | @deva[जित्वा] |
| @deva[पू] | to purify | @deva[पवित] or @deva[पूत] | @deva[पवित्वा] or @deva[पूत्वा] |
| @deva[भू] | to be | @deva[भूत] | @deva[भूत्वा] |
| @deva[कृ] | to do | @deva[कृत] | @deva[कृत्वा] |
| @deva[तृ] | to cross | @deva[तीर्ण] | @deva[तीर्त्वा] |
| @deva[पॄ] | to fill | @deva[पूर्ण] | @deva[पूर्त्वा] |
| @deva[त्रै] | to protect | @deva[त्रात] | @deva[त्रात्वा] |
| @deva[मुच्] | to release | @deva[मुक्त] | @deva[मुक्त्वा] |
| @deva[अद्] | to eat | @deva[जग्ध] | @deva[जग्ध्वा] |
| @deva[छो] | to cut | @deva[छात], @deva[छित] | @deva[छात्वा], @deva[छित्वा] |
| @deva[दृश्] | to see | @deva[दृष्ट] | @deva[दृष्ट्वा] |
| @deva[क्षुध्][^1] | to be hungry | @deva[क्षुधित] | @deva[क्षुधित्वा], @deva[क्षोधित्वा] |
| @deva[वस्][^1] | to dwell | @deva[उषित] | @deva[उषित्वा] |
| @deva[वच्] | to speak | @deva[उक्त] | @deva[उक्त्वा] |
| @deva[वह्] | to carry | @deva[ऊढ] | @deva[ऊढ्वा] |
| @deva[यज्] | to sacrifice | @deva[इष्ट] | @deva[इष्ट्वा] |
| @deva[वप्] | to sow | @deva[उप्त] | @deva[उप्त्वा] |
| @deva[बन्ध्] | to bind | @deva[बद्ध] | @deva[बद्ध्वा] |
| @deva[बुध्] | to know | @deva[बुद्ध] | @deva[बुद्ध्वा] |
| @deva[शास्] | to rule | @deva[शिष्ट] | @deva[शिष्ट्वा] |

[^1]: See @ref[684] (c); @ref[750].

rules.title: Guṇa Substitution When Intermediate @deva[इ] Is Inserted
rules.body:
When the intermediate @deva[इ] is inserted, the preceding vowel takes its Guṇa substitute; @deva[शि]—@deva[शयित्वा], @deva[कु]—@deva[कवित्वा], @deva[जागृ]—@deva[जागरित्वा], &c.

(a) The roots @deva[तृष्], @deva[मृष्], @deva[कृष्] and @deva[ऋत्] take Guṇa optionally; @deva[तृषित्वा] or @deva[तर्षित्वा], @deva[मृषित्वा] or @deva[मर्षित्वा], @deva[कृषित्वा] or @deva[कर्षित्वा], @deva[ऋत्]—@deva[ऋतित्वा] or @deva[अर्तित्वा]

(b) But the roots @deva[मृड्], @deva[मृद्], @deva[गुध्], @deva[कुष्], @deva[मुष्], and @deva[क्लिश्], the roots mentioned at @ref[463] and @deva[विज्], 7 cl. do not take Guṇa; @deva[मृड्]—@deva[मृडित्वा] 'having rejoiced;' @deva[मृद्]—@deva[मृदित्वा], @deva[गुध्]—@deva[गुधित्वा] 'having covered,' @deva[कुषित्वा], @deva[मुषित्वा], @deva[क्लिश्]—@deva[क्लिशित्वा] or @deva[क्लिष्ट्वा]; @deva[कुट्]—@deva[कुटित्वा], @deva[विज्]—@deva[विजित्वा], &c.

rules.title: Roots Admitting Optional @deva[इ] Before @deva[त्वा]
rules.body:
Veṭ roots, except @deva[व्रश्च्] which takes @deva[इ] necessarily, and @deva[स्तृ], @deva[सू] and @deva[धू] which reject @deva[इ], the five roots given under @ref[472] and the roots marked with an indicatory @deva[उ][^1] admit of @deva[इ] optionally before @deva[त्वा] e. g.

| Roots | | Ind. P. Ptc. or Ger. |
|---|---|---|
| @deva[मृज्] | to cleanse | @deva[मार्जित्वा], @deva[मृष्ट्वा] |
| @deva[गाह्] | to enter | @deva[गाहित्वा], @deva[गाढ्वा] |
| @deva[गुह्] | to conceal | @deva[गुहित्वा], @deva[गूहित्वा], @deva[गूढ्वा] |
| @deva[गुप्] | to protect | @deva[गोपायित्वा], @deva[गोपित्वा], @deva[गुपित्वा], @deva[गुप्त्वा] |
| @deva[इष्] | to desire | @deva[एषित्वा] or @deva[इष्ट्वा] |
| @deva[सह्] | to endure | @deva[सहित्वा] or @deva[सोढ्वा] |
| @deva[लुभ्] | to covet | @deva[लोभित्वा] or @deva[लुब्ध्वा] |
| @deva[अञ्च्] | to go, to worship | @deva[अक्त्वा] having gone, @deva[अञ्चित्वा] having worshipped |
| @deva[क्षण्] | to kill | @deva[क्षत्वा], @deva[क्षणित्वा] |
| @deva[खन्] | to dig | @deva[खनित्वा], @deva[खात्वा] |
| @deva[तन्] | to stretch | @deva[तनित्वा], @deva[तत्वा] |
| @deva[दम्] | to tame | @deva[दमित्वा], @deva[दान्त्वा] |
| @deva[शम्] | to pacify | @deva[शमित्वा], @deva[शान्त्वा] |
| @deva[क्रम्] | to go &c. | @deva[क्रमित्वा], @deva[क्रन्त्वा], @deva[क्रान्त्वा][^2] |
| @deva[वस्] 4 P. | to be straight, &c. | @deva[वसित्वा], @deva[वस्त्वा] |
| @deva[वृत्] 1 A. | to be | @deva[वर्तित्वा] or @deva[वृत्त्वा] &c. &c. |

But @deva[व्रश्च्]—@deva[व्रश्चित्वा], @deva[स्तृ]—@deva[स्तृत्वा], @deva[सू]—@deva[सूत्वा], @deva[धू]—@deva[धूत्वा].

[^1]: The following are the more important of the roots marked with @deva[उ]; @deva[अच्] 1 P A. @deva[अञ्च्] 1. 10. P. A. @deva[अस्] 4 P. @deva[ऋण्], @deva[कम्] 5. P. 1. A. @deva[कुज्], @deva[क्रम्] 1. P. @deva[क्लम्] 4. P. @deva[क्षण्] 8. P. A. @deva[क्षिण्] 8. P A. @deva[क्षिव्] 1. 4. P. @deva[क्षीव्] 1. P. @deva[क्षेद्] 1. P. @deva[खन्] 1. P. A. @deva[गृध्] 4 P. @deva[ग्रस्] 1. A. @deva[ग्रुच्] 1. P. @deva[ग्लुच्] 1. P. @deva[ग्लुञ्च्] 1. P. @deva[घृण्] 8. P. A. @deva[घृष्] 1 P. @deva[चञ्च्] 1. P. @deva[चम्] 1. 5. P. @deva[छृद्] 7. 5. A. @deva[जभ्] 1. P @deva[जस्] 4. P. 10 P. A. @deva[तञ्च्] 1. P. @deva[तन्] 8. P. A. 1. P. A. 10 P. @deva[तृण्] 8. P. A @deva[दम्भ्] 5. P. @deva[दम्] 4. P. @deva[दिश्] 4. P. 10. A. @deva[धाव्] 1. P. A. @deva[ध्वंस्] 1. A. @deva[पूष्] 1 P. @deva[प्लुष्] 1. P. @deva[बस्] 4. P. @deva[भृश्] 4. P. @deva[भ्रम्] 1. 4. P. @deva[भ्रंश्] 1. A. 4. P. @deva[भ्रंस्] 1. A. @deva[मन्] 8. A. @deva[मृष्] 1. P. @deva[म्रुच्], @deva[म्रुञ्च्], @deva[म्लुच्], @deva[म्लुञ्च्], 1. P. @deva[यस्], @deva[युप्], @deva[रुप्], @deva[लुप्], all of the 4th cl. P. @deva[वञ्च्], 1 P. A. @deva[वन्] 8. P. @deva[वस्]. 4 P. @deva[विष्] 1. P. @deva[वृत्] 1. 4 A. 10. P. A. @deva[वृध्] 1 A. 10. P. A @deva[वृष्] 1. P. @deva[शम्] 4. P. A. @deva[शस्] 1. P. @deva[शंस्] 1. P @deva[शास्] 1. P. 2. P. A. @deva[शृध्] 1. P. A. @deva[श्रम्भ्] 1. P. @deva[श्रस्] 4. P. @deva[श्रिष्] 1. 4. P. @deva[श्लिष्] 1. P. @deva[सन्] 1. P. 8. P. A. @deva[ष्ठिव्] 1. 4 P. @deva[सिध्] 1. 4. rules.title: Seṭ Roots, 10th Class, and Derivative Verbs Admitting @deva[इ]
rules.body: The roots @deva[श्वि], @deva[डी], @deva[शी], @deva[पू] and @deva[जॄ], Seṭ roots ending in consonants, roots of the 10th class and all derivative verbs, admit @deva[इ] before @deva[त्वा]; roots of the 10th cl. preserve their @deva[अय्] before @deva[त्वा]; @deva[श्वि]—@deva[श्वयित्वा], @deva[डी]—@deva[डयित्वा], @deva[जॄ]—@deva[जरीत्वा] or @deva[जरित्वा], @deva[नृत्]—@deva[नर्तित्वा], @deva[व्यच्]—@deva[विचित्वा], @deva[लज्ज्]—@deva[लजित्वा], @deva[जीव्]—@deva[जीवित्वा], &c., @deva[चुर्]—@deva[चोरयित्वा]; @deva[कथ्]—@deva[कथयित्वा], @deva[बुध्]—cau. @deva[बोधयित्वा]; desi. @deva[बुबोधिषित्वा]; Ātm. fre. @deva[बोबुधित्वा], &c.

rules.title: Nasal Dropping Rules Before @deva[त्वा]
rules.body:
(a) The roots @deva[स्कन्द्] and @deva[स्यन्द्] do not drop their nasal; @deva[स्कन्द्]—@deva[स्कन्त्वा]; @deva[स्यन्द्]—@deva[स्यन्त्वा], @deva[स्यन्दित्वा].

(b) The penultimate nasal of roots ending in @deva[थ्] or @deva[फ्] and that of @deva[वञ्च्] 'to roam abroad,' 'to deceive' and @deva[लुञ्च्] 'to tear out,' are optionally dropped, @deva[ग्रन्थ्]—@deva[ग्रन्थित्वा], @deva[ग्रथित्वा], @deva[गुम्फ्]—@deva[गुम्फित्वा], @deva[गुफित्वा]; @deva[वञ्च्]—@deva[वञ्चित्वा], @deva[वचित्वा], @deva[वक्त्वा]; @deva[लुञ्च्]—@deva[लुञ्चित्वा], @deva[लुचित्वा].

(c) Roots ending in @deva[ज्] such as @deva[भञ्ज्], @deva[रञ्ज्], @deva[सञ्ज्], @deva[स्वञ्ज्] &c. and the root @deva[तञ्च्] optionally drop their nasal before @deva[त्वा]; @deva[भञ्ज्]—@deva[भंक्त्वा] or @deva[भक्त्वा], @deva[रञ्ज्]—@deva[रंक्त्वा] or @deva[रक्त्वा]; @deva[अञ्ज्]—@deva[अञ्जित्वा], @deva[अङ्क्त्वा] or @deva[अक्त्वा].

(b) @deva[मस्ज्] and @deva[नश्] insert a nasal optionally; @deva[मक्त्वा] or @deva[मंक्त्वा]; @deva[नशित्वा], @deva[नंष्ट्वा] or @deva[नष्ट्वा].

rules.title: Optional Guṇa for Penultimate @deva[इ] and @deva[उ]
rules.body: Guṇa is optionally substituted for the penultimate @deva[इ] and @deva[उ], roots beginning with any consonant and ending in any except @deva[य्] or @deva[व्] when @deva[त्वा] has @deva[इ] prefixed to it; @deva[लिख्]—@deva[लिखित्वा] or @deva[लेखित्वा]; @deva[क्लिद्]—@deva[क्लिदित्वा] or @deva[क्लेदित्वा] (also @deva[क्लिन्त्वा]); @deva[लुभ्]—6. P. @deva[लुभित्वा] or @deva[लोभित्वा]; @deva[द्युत्]—@deva[द्युतित्वा], @deva[द्योतित्वा]; @deva[रिष्]—@deva[रिषित्वा], @deva[रेषित्वा] and @deva[रिष्ट्वा]; so @deva[रुष्], &c., but @deva[दिव्]—@deva[देवित्वा], @deva[द्युत्वा].

rules.title: Gerund Formation with @deva[य] for Compounded Roots
rules.body:
## 2. Indeclinable Participles formed with @deva[य].

When a root is compounded with one or more prepositions or words prefixed to verbs like prepositions, the indeclinable participle is formed by affixing @deva[य] immediately to it; the @deva[य] is changed to @deva[त्य] after a short radical vowel (even when it combines with the final vowel of a preposition to a long vowel); e. g.

| | |
|---|---|
| @deva[दा] with @deva[आ]—@deva[आदाय] | @deva[इ] with @deva[प्र]—@deva[प्रेत्य] |
| @deva[चि] with @deva[निस्]—@deva[निश्चित्य] | @deva[कृ] with @deva[सम्]—@deva[संस्कृत्य] |
| @deva[जि] with @deva[परा]—@deva[पराजित्य] | @deva[कृ] with @deva[द्विधा]—@deva[द्विधाकृत्य] |
| @deva[नी] with @deva[वि]—@deva[विनीय] | @deva[भिद्] with @deva[निस्]—@deva[निर्भिद्य] |
| @deva[भू] with @deva[अनु]—@deva[अनुभूय] | @deva[प्लुत्] with @deva[उत्]—@deva[उत्प्लुत्य] |
| @deva[इ] with @deva[अधि]—@deva[अधीत्य] | &c. &c. &c. |

rules.title: Application of Earlier Rules to Gerunds in @deva[य]
rules.body:
The rules given at @ref[394], @ref[395], @ref[459], @ref[502] and @ref[587] apply to the roots also in the gerund in @deva[य]:—

| | |
|---|---|
| @deva[दिव्] with @deva[प्र]—@deva[प्रदीव्य] | @deva[वच्] with @deva[प्र]—@deva[प्रोच्य] |
| @deva[कॄ] with @deva[अव]—@deva[अवकीर्य] | @deva[वस्] with @deva[प्र]—@deva[प्रोष्य] |
| @deva[पॄ] with @deva[आ]—@deva[आपूर्य] | @deva[ग्रह्] with @deva[वि]—@deva[विगृह्य] |
| @deva[बन्ध्] with @deva[नि]—@deva[निबध्य] | @deva[ह्वे] with @deva[आ]—@deva[आहूय] |
| @deva[मि], @deva[मी], @deva[मा] and | @deva[दी] with @deva[उप]—@deva[उपदाय] |
| @deva[मे][^1] with @deva[अनु]—@deva[अनुमाय] | @deva[ली] with @deva[वि]—@deva[विलीय] or @deva[विलाय] |
| @deva[त्रै] with @deva[परि]—@deva[परित्राय] | &c. &c. &c. |
| @deva[दे] with @deva[आ]—@deva[आदाय] | |

[^1]: @deva[मे] changes its final to @deva[इ] optionally; so @deva[अनुमित्य] also.

rules.title: Nasal Dropping in 8th Class Roots
rules.body: Roots of the 8th class ending in a nasal, except @deva[सन्] and the roots @deva[मन्], @deva[वन्] and @deva[हन्], drop their nasal necessarily; @deva[गम्], @deva[नम्], @deva[यम्] and @deva[रम्] do it optionally; @deva[तन्] with @deva[वि]—@deva[वितत्य]; @deva[मन्] with @deva[अव]—@deva[अवमत्य]; @deva[यम्] with @deva[नि]—@deva[नियम्य] or @deva[नियत्य]; @deva[रम्] with @deva[वि]—@deva[विरम्य] or @deva[विरत्य]; @deva[नम्] with @deva[प्र]—@deva[प्रणम्य] or @deva[प्रणत्य], &c

rules.title: Special Forms for @deva[खन्], @deva[जन्] and @deva[सन्]
rules.body: The roots @deva[खन्], @deva[जन्] and @deva[सन्] have respectively @deva[निखन्य]—@deva[निखाय]; @deva[प्रजन्य]—@deva[प्रजाय]; and @deva[प्रसन्य]—@deva[प्रसाय].

rules.title: Special Rules for @deva[क्षि] and @deva[जागृ]
rules.body: @deva[क्षि] lengthens its @deva[इ] before the affix @deva[य] and @deva[जागृ] changes its final vowel to Guṇa; @deva[प्रक्षीय]; @deva[प्रजागर्य].

rules.title: Samprasāraṇa Rules for @deva[वे], @deva[ज्या] and @deva[व्ये]
rules.body: @deva[वे], @deva[ज्या] and @deva[व्ये] do not take Samprasāraṇa; @deva[प्रवाय]; @deva[प्रज्याय] 'having become old;' @deva[उपव्याय] 'having covered;' but @deva[व्ये] with @deva[परि] or @deva[सम्], takes Samprasāraṇa optionally; @deva[परिव्याय] or @deva[परिवीय]; @deva[संव्याय] or @deva[संवीय].

rules.title: @deva[आ] Not Changing to @deva[ई] in Certain Roots
rules.body: The roots mentioned under @ref[486] do not change their @deva[आ] to @deva[ई]; @deva[प्रयाय], @deva[प्रधाय], @deva[प्रमाय], &c.

rules.title: 10th Class and Causals Preserving @deva[अय्] Before @deva[य]
rules.body: Roots of the Tenth class and Causals preserve their @deva[अय्] before @deva[य], if it be preceded by a short penultimate vowel; if not, it is dropped; @deva[चोरय]—@deva[प्रचोर्य]; @deva[बोधय]—@deva[प्रबोध्य]; @deva[कॄ]—cau. @deva[विकार्य]; @deva[नी] cau. with @deva[आ]—@deva[आनाय्य], &c.; but @deva[गण्]—@deva[विगणय्य], @deva[प्रणमय्य], @deva[प्रकथय्य]; @deva[प्रबेभिदय्य] 'having again and again caused to be broken.'

rules.title: @deva[आप्] Causative with Optional @deva[अय्] Retention
rules.body: (a) @deva[आप्] cau. may retain its @deva[अय्] optionally—@deva[प्राप्य] or @deva[प्रापय्य].

rules.title: Desiderative and Frequentative Bases with @deva[य]
rules.body: Desiderative bases add @deva[य] immediately and Freq. bases add it after dropping their @deva[य], when it is preceded by a consonant and dropping the final @deva[अ] when it is preceded by a vowel; @deva[बुध्]—@deva[प्रबुबोधिष्य]; Fre. @deva[प्रबोबुध्य]; @deva[भू] Fre. @deva[प्रबोभूय्य] &c.

rules.title: Introduction to the Gerund in @deva[अम्]
rules.body:
**(b) The Adverbial Indeclinable Participle**

**or**

**The Gerund in @deva[अम्].**

---

There is another Indeclinable Participle having the same sense as that in @deva[त्वा], formed with the affix @deva[अम्]. Before this the root or the derivative verbal base generally undergoes the same changes as it does before the @deva[इ] of the Pass. Aorist 3rd sing.; @deva[नी]—@deva[नायम्] 'having carried or led'; @deva[दा]—@deva[दायम्] 'having given'; @deva[भू]—@deva[भावम्], @deva[भिद्]—@deva[भेदम्], @deva[ग्रह्]—@deva[ग्राहम्], @deva[गम्]—@deva[गमम्], &c.

rules.title: Usage of the Gerund in @deva[अम्] at End of Compounds
rules.body: This Participle is generally used at the end of compounds; @deva[स लोष्टघातं हतः] 'he was pelted to death;' @deva[बन्दिग्राहं गृहीता] (Vik. I.) 'She was taken a captive;' @deva[स मूलघातं न्यवधीदरींश्च] (Bhaṭṭi. I. 2.) 'He totally exterminated his enemies, &c.'

rules.title: Repetition of Participles for Repeated Action
rules.body:
The participles in @deva[त्वा] and @deva[अम्][^1] when repeated yield the sense of repetition of the action or condition expressed by the verb; @deva[स्मृत्वा स्मृत्वा] or @deva[स्मारं स्मारम्] 'having repeatedly remembered;' @deva[पीत्वा पीत्वा] or @deva[पायं पायम्] 'having drunk again and again;' similarly @deva[भुज्]—@deva[भुक्त्वा भुक्त्वा] or @deva[भोजं भोजम्], @deva[श्रु]—@deva[श्रुत्वा श्रुत्वा] or @deva[श्रावं श्रावम्], @deva[गम्]—@deva[गत्वा गत्वा] or @deva[गामं गामम्] or @deva[गमं गमम्], @deva[लभ्]—@deva[लब्ध्वा लब्ध्वा] or @deva[लम्भं लम्भम्] or @deva[लाभं लाभम्], @deva[प्रलम्भं प्रलम्भम्], @deva[जागृ]—@deva[जागरं जागरम्],[^2] &c.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[आभीक्ष्ण्ये णमुल्] । Pāṇ. III. 4. 22.

[^2]: At the end of compounds this may not be repeated and yet have the sense of repetition; as in

'@deva[लतानुपातं कुसुमान्यगृह्णात्स नद्यवस्कन्दमुपास्पृशच्च ।]

@deva[कुतूहलाच्चारुशिलोपवेशं काकुत्स्थ ईषत्स्मयमान आस्त ॥]' Bhaṭṭi. II. 11

The descendant of Kakutstha, smiling gently, repeatedly bending down the creepers would pluck their flowers, wading through every stream (that he came across), would sip the waters, and seating himself on every charming slab would remain there (in admiration of the scenery).

rules.title: Gerund in @deva[अम्] Without Repetition Sense
rules.body: The Gerund @deva[अम्] does not, in many instances, express the notion of repetition.

rules.title: Gerunds Used with @deva[अग्रे], @deva[प्रथमम्], and @deva[पूर्वम्]
rules.body: This gerund or the one in @deva[त्वा] is used with the words @deva[अग्रे], @deva[प्रथमं] and @deva[पूर्वं], used as prepositions, although the notion of repetition is not present in these compounds; @deva[अग्रेभोजं]-@deva[भुक्त्वा वा व्रजति] 'having first eaten he goes out.' so @deva[प्रथमंभोजं] or @deva[भुक्त्वा पूर्वभोजं] or @deva[भुक्त्वा व्रजति].

rules.title: Special Uses of the Gerund of @deva[कृ] in @deva[अम्]
rules.body:
The gerund in @deva[अम्] of the root @deva[कृ] is used[^1]

(a) with the noun governed by it, if it be compounded with it prepositionally when censure is implied; @deva[चौरकारं आक्रोशति] (@deva[चौरशब्दं उच्चार्येत्यर्थः]) 'cries out (he is) a thief, a thief.' In this case @deva[म्] is added to the noun governed.

(b) with the words @deva[स्वादु], @deva[लवण], and @deva[संपन्न], @deva[म्] being added to these as before; @deva[अस्वादुं स्वादुं कृत्वा भुंक्ते] @deva[स्वादुं-लवणं-सम्पन्नं—कारं भुंक्ते] 'he eats having sweetened or seasoned his food.'

(c) with the words @deva[अन्यथा], @deva[एवं], @deva[इत्थं], and @deva[कथं], provided the root @deva[कृ] loses its sense; @deva[अन्यथाकारं ब्रूते] 'he speaks in a different manner;' @deva[एवंकारं भुंक्ते] 'he eats thus;' similarly @deva[इत्थंकारं], @deva[कथंकारम्], but @deva[शिरोन्यथा कृत्वा भुंक्ते].

(d) with the particles @deva[यथा] and @deva[तथा] when an angry reply is given; @deva[यथाकारं भोक्ष्ये तथाकारं भोक्ष्ये किं तवानेन] (Sid. Kau.); 'I will eat in this manner, I will eat in that manner, what have you to do with that?'

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[कर्मण्याक्रोशे कृञः खमुञ् । स्वादुमि णमुल् । अन्यथैवङ्कथमित्थंसु सिद्धाप्रयागश्चेत् । यथायथयोरसूयाप्रतिवचने ।] Pāṇ. III. 4. 25—28.

rules.title: Gerunds of @deva[दृश्] and @deva[विद्] Expressing Totality
rules.body:
The Gerund of the roots @deva[दृश्] and @deva[विद्][^1] is compounded with their objects and express totality; @deva[कन्यादर्शं वरयति] 'chooses as many girls as he sees, i. e. all of them;' @deva[ब्राह्मणवेदं भोजयति, यं यं ब्राह्मणं जानाति लभते विचारयति वा तं सर्वे भोजयति इत्यर्थः] (Sid. Kau.) 'he feeds every Brāhmaṇa that he knows or comes across or remembers i. e. all of them.'

(a) [^2]The gerunds of @deva[विद्] 'to get' and @deva[जीव्] 'to live' are joined with @deva[यावत्] in the same sense; @deva[यावद्वेदं भुंक्ते] 'eats what he gets.'

(b) [^3]With the words @deva[चर्मन्] and @deva[उदर] the gerund of @deva[पूर्] is used; @deva[चर्मपूरं स्तृणाति]; @deva[उदरपूरं भुंक्ते] 'eats so as to fill his belly.'

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[कर्मणि दृशिविदोः साकल्ये ।] Pāṇ. III. 6. 29.

[^2]: @deva[यावति विन्दजीवोः ।] Pāṇ. III. 4. 30.

[^3]: @deva[चर्मोदरयोः पूरेः ।] Pāṇ. III. 4. 31.

rules.title: Gerund of @deva[पिष्] with @deva[शुष्क], @deva[चूर्ण], and @deva[रूक्ष]
rules.body:
This gerund of @deva[पिष्] is used with @deva[शुष्क], @deva[चूर्ण] and @deva[रूक्ष];[^1] @deva[शुष्कपेषं पिनष्टि शुष्कं पिनष्टीत्यर्थः] (Sid. Kau.); so @deva[चूर्णपेषं पिनष्टि] 'he grinds to powder;' @deva[रूक्षपेषम्].

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[शुष्कचूर्णरूक्षेषु पिषः ।] Pāṇ. III. 4. 35.

rules.title: Special Uses of Gerunds with Various Words
rules.body:
[^1]With the words @deva[समूल], @deva[अकृत] and @deva[जीव] are used respectively the gerunds in @deva[अम्] of the roots @deva[हन्], @deva[कृ] and @deva[ग्रह्] in a cognate sense; @deva[समूलघातं हन्ति] 'kills destroying the roots i e totally;' @deva[अकृतकारं करोति] 'does what ought not to have been done;' @deva[जीवग्राहं गृह्णाति] 'captures him so as to preserve him i e. alive.'

(a) The gerund of @deva[हन्] and @deva[पिष्] is used with words signifying instruments (of action); @deva[पादघातं हन्ति]=@deva[पादेन हन्ति] 'strikes (kicking) with foot;' @deva[उदपेषं पिनष्टि]=@deva[उदकेन पिनष्टि] 'grinds with (using) the water.'

(b) Similarly the gerund of @deva[वृत्] and @deva[ग्रह्] is used with @deva[हस्त] and its synonyms, and that of @deva[पुष्] with @deva[स्व]; @deva[हस्तवर्तं वर्तयति]; so @deva[करवर्तम्], @deva[हस्तेन गुलिकां करोतीत्यर्थः ।] Sid. Kau.; @deva[हस्तग्राहं गृह्णाति]; similarly @deva[पाणिग्राहम्], @deva[करग्राहम्], &c.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[समूलाकृतजीवेषु हन्कृञ्ग्रहः । करणे हनः । स्नेहने पिषः । हस्ते वर्तिग्रहोः । स्वे पुषः ।] Pāṇ. III. 4. 36—40.

rules.title: Gerund of @deva[बन्ध्] with Stanza Arrangements
rules.body:
[^1]The gerund of @deva[बन्ध्] is used with words denoting peculiar arrangements of stanzas, &c., @deva[चक्रबन्धं बध्नाति], @deva[क्रौञ्चबन्धं बद्धः], @deva[मुरजबन्धं बद्धः], @deva[मयूरिकाबन्धम्], @deva[अट्टालिकाबन्धम्], &c.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[अधिकरणे बन्धः । संज्ञायाम्] Pāṇ. III. 4. 41. 42.

rules.title: Gerunds of @deva[नश्] and @deva[वह्] with @deva[जीव] and @deva[पुरुष]
rules.body:
[^1]With the words @deva[जीव] and @deva[पुरुष] used subjectively the gerunds of @deva[नश्] and @deva[वह्] are used; @deva[जीवनाशं नश्यति जीवो नश्यतीत्यर्थः]. @deva[पुरुषवाहं वहति पुरुषो वहतीत्यर्थः]

(a) [^2]The gerunds of @deva[शुष्] and @deva[पूर्] are used with @deva[ऊर्ध्व] similarly; @deva[ऊर्ध्वशोषं शुष्यति]. @deva[वृक्षादिरूर्ध्व एव तिष्ठन् शुष्यतीत्यर्थः ।] @deva[ऊर्ध्वपूरं पूर्यते, ऊर्ध्वमुख एव घटादिर्वर्षोदकादिना पूर्णो भवतीत्यर्थः ।] Sid. Kau.

(b) [^3]Sometimes the Gerund in @deva[अम्] is used with words denoting a standard of comparison; @deva[घृतनिधायं निहितं जलं] 'the water was kept with as much care as ghee;' @deva[अजकनाशं नष्टः अजक इव नष्ट इत्यर्थः ।]

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[कर्त्रोर्जीवपुरुषयोर्नशिवहोः ।] Pāṇ. III. 4. 43.

[^2]: @deva[ऊर्ध्वे शुषिपूरोः ।] Pāṇ. III. 4. 44.

[^3]: @deva[उपमाने कर्मणि च ।] Pāṇ. III. 4. 45.

rules.title: Gerunds of Roots Meaning @deva[हिंस्] with Instruments
rules.body:
[^1]The gerund in @deva[अम्] of roots having the sense of @deva[हिंस्] 'to strike,' &c. are used with words denoting the instrument when the object of the gerund and of the principal verb is the same; @deva[दण्डोपघातं गाः कालयति] i. e. @deva[दण्डेनोपघातं] 'he collects together cows beating (them) with a stick;' @deva[दण्डताडम्]; but @deva[दण्डेन चोरमाहत्य गाः कालयति].

(a) The gerunds of @deva[पीड्], @deva[रुध्] and @deva[कर्ष्], with @deva[उप], are used with nouns having the sense of the Loc. or the Inst.; @deva[पार्श्वोपपीडं शेते] i. e. @deva[पार्श्वाभ्यां उपपीडम्]; @deva[व्रजोपरोधं गाः स्थापयति] i. e. @deva[व्रजेन व्रजे उपरोधं वा]; @deva[पाण्युपकर्षं धानाः संगृह्णाति] i. e. @deva[पाणावुपकर्षं पाणिनोपकर्षं वा ।] Sid. Kau.

(b) Similarly @deva[केशग्राहं युध्यन्ते] i. e. @deva[केशेषु गृहीत्वा]; @deva[हस्तग्राहं] i. e. @deva[हस्तेन गृहीत्वा]; @deva[द्व्यङ्गुलोत्कर्षं खण्डिकां छिनत्ति] i. e. @deva[द्व्यङ्गुलेन द्व्यङ्गुले वा उत्कर्षम् ।]

(c) Nouns having the sense of the Ablative and the Accusative are used with this gerund of a root when haste or hurry is intended; @deva[शय्योत्थायं धावति] 'runs having quickly got up from the bed;' @deva[यष्टिग्राहं युध्यन्ते]; @deva[लोष्टग्राहम्], &c.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[हिंसार्थानां च समानकर्मकाणाम् । सप्तम्यां चोपपीडरुधकर्षः । समासत्तौ । प्रमाणे च । अपादाने परीप्सायाम् । द्वितीयायां च ।] Pāṇ. III. 4. 48-53.

rules.title: Gerunds with Body Parts That Can Be Severed
rules.body:
[^1]A root may be used in its gerundive form in @deva[अम्] with its object prefixed to it if that object be a part of the body which can be severed without fatal effects; @deva[भ्रूविक्षेपं कथयति] 'narrates contracting the eyebrows; but @deva[शिर उत्क्षिप्य] (not @deva[शिरउत्क्षेपम्]) as the severance of the head would cause death.

(a) Similarly when a part of the body is completely hurt or pressed in the action, the gerund in @deva[अम्] is used with that part; @deva[उर-प्रतिपेषं युध्यन्ते] i. e. @deva[कृत्स्नमुरः पीडयन्तः] 'afflicting the whole bosom;' @deva[उरोविदारं प्रतिचस्करे नखैः ।]

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[स्वाङ्गेध्रुवे ।] (@deva[येन विना न जीवनं तद्ध्रुवम् ।] Sid Kau.) @deva[परिक्लिश्यमाने च ।] Pāṇ. III. 4. 54, 55.

rules.title: Gerunds of @deva[विश्], @deva[पत्], @deva[पद्], and @deva[स्कन्द्] for Complete Occupation
rules.body:
[^1]The roots @deva[विश्], @deva[पत्], @deva[पद्], and @deva[स्कन्द्] are used in their gerundive forms in @deva[अम्] in the sense of 'complete occupation or pervasion or repetition' with nouns which if not compounded would have stood in the Acc.; @deva[गेहानुप्रवेशमास्ते गेहं गेहमनुप्रवेशम् ।] @deva[गेहमनुप्रवेशमनुप्रवेशम् ।] so @deva[गेहानुप्रपातम्], @deva[गेहानुप्रपादम्], @deva[गेहानुस्कन्दम्], &c.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[विशिपतिपदिस्कन्दां व्याप्यमानासेव्यमानयोः] Pāṇ. III. 4. 56. @deva[गेहादिद्रव्याण विश्यादिक्रियाभिः साकल्येन संबन्धो व्याप्तिः । क्रियायाः पौनःपुन्यमासेवनम् ।] Sid. Kau.

rules.title: Gerunds of @deva[अस्] and @deva[तृष्] with Time Intervals, and Special Uses
rules.body:
(a) [^1]The gerunds of @deva[अस्] and @deva[तृष्] are used with nouns denoting a period of time intervening between the repetition or performance of the action; @deva[द्व्यहात्यासं] or @deva[द्व्यहमत्यासं गाः पाययति] 'he makes the cows drink water allowing two days to intervene, i. e every third day' @deva[अद्य पाययित्वा द्व्यहमतिक्रम्य पुनः पाययतीत्यर्थः ।] (Sid. Kau.); similarly @deva[द्व्यहतर्षम्] or @deva[द्व्यहंतर्षम्].

(b) [^2]Similarly the gerunds of @deva[दिश्] with @deva[आ], and @deva[ग्रह्] are used with @deva[नामन्] and in the sense of the Acc.; @deva[नामदेशमाचष्टे]; @deva[नामग्राहं मामाह्वयति], &c.

(c) The gerund of @deva[भू] may optionally be used after @deva[तूष्णीं] and @deva[अन्वच्]; @deva[तूष्णींभूय]-@deva[भूत्वा]-@deva[भावं]; @deva[अन्वग्भूय], @deva[अन्वग्भूत्वा], @deva[अन्वग्भावम्].

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[अस्यतितृषोः क्रियान्तरे कालेषु ।]

[^2]: @deva[नाम्न्यादिशिग्रहोः ।] Pāṇ. III. 4. 57. 58.

rules.title: The Infinitive Formation with @deva[तुम्]
rules.body:
**(c) The Infinitive.**

---

The Infinitive is formed by the affix @deva[तुम्] with the same effect as the @deva[ता] of the Future; e. g.

| Roots | Infinitive | Roots | Infinitive |
|---|---|---|---|
| @deva[इ] to go | @deva[एतुम्] | @deva[ग्रन्थ्] to compose | @deva[ग्रन्थितुम्] |
| @deva[एध्] to grow | @deva[एधितुम्] | @deva[पच्] to cook | @deva[पक्तुम्] |
| @deva[दा] to give | @deva[दातुम्] | @deva[व्रश्च्] to cut | @deva[व्रश्चितुम्] or @deva[व्रष्टुम्] |
| @deva[नी] to carry | @deva[नेतुम्] | @deva[गुह्] to cover | @deva[गूहितुम्] or @deva[गोढुम्] |
| @deva[कृ] to do | @deva[कर्तुम्] | @deva[सह्] to bear | @deva[सहितुम्] or @deva[सोढुम्] |
| @deva[भू] to be | @deva[भवितुम्] | @deva[चुर्] to steal | @deva[चोरयितुम्] |
| @deva[धू] to shake | @deva[धवितुम्] or @deva[धोतुम्] | @deva[बुध्] Cau. | @deva[बोधयितुम्] |
| @deva[वृ] to choose | @deva[वरितुम्] or @deva[वरीतुम्] | Desi. | @deva[बुबोधिषितुम्] |
| @deva[गै] to sing | @deva[गातुम्] | Ātm. Freq. | @deva[बोबुधितुम्] |
| @deva[गम्] to go | @deva[गन्तुम्] | &c. | &c. |

rules.title: Comprehensive Alphabetical List of Kṛt Affixes
Introduction to Syntax
rules.body:
**CHAPTER XV.**

---

**SYNTAX.**

---

Syntax deals with the mode of arranging words in sentences. Of the three divisions of Syntax—Concord, Government and Order, the Syntax of Sanskrit is mainly concerned with the first two. Syntax in English depends principally upon the last. In Sanskrit and other cognate Languages which are rich in inflection, the relation, which one word bears to another in a sentence is determined by its grammatical form, and no change occurs in the meaning of the sentences, how-so-ever the order of words be changed. But in English and other languages, deficient in inflection, 'order' is everything. Change the order of words and there is a corresponding change in the meaning. In Sanskrit, therefore, the mere order of words is not of material importance, though a perfect arbitrariness in that respect is not allowable. Sanskrit Syntax also takes further into account the meaning and use of participles, the various tenses and moods, and participles.[^1] These will be treated of in their proper order.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: As the great bulk of Sanskrit literature is thrown in the form of verse, the laws of Syntax will be found not to be always observed by the poets. In ordinary prose writings the usual order of words in a sentence is, first the subject with its adjuncts, then the object with its adjuncts, then the adverbs and other indeclinables (extensions of the predicate) and lastly the predicate. The chief characteristics of Sanskrit style are, in the words of Prof. Max Müller, 'the predominance of co-ordination, the use of the Locative Absolute, a fondness for compounds and indeclinable participles supplying the place of subordinate clauses, the frequent employment of the Past Participle instead of the finite verb, a predilection for passive forms, and the absence of the indirect construction and of the subjunctive mood. For the latter reason the use of the tenses and moods is comparatively simple, on the other hand, the use of the cases, being much less definite than in Latin and Greek presents some difficulties.' M. Williams' Grammar for Beginners.

rules.title: Articles in Sanskrit
rules.body:
**THE ARTICLE.**

There are no articles in Sanskrit corresponding to the English Definite and Indefinite articles. The words @deva[कश्चित्] and @deva[एक], however, are often used in the sense of 'a certain' and the pron. @deva[तद्] m. f. n as equivalent to 'the;' @deva[कश्चित् नरः] a certain man; @deva[एकः पान्थः] a traveller, @deva[स राजा] the king, &c.

rules.title: Number in Sanskrit Grammar
rules.body:
As already remarked (See @ref[54]) there are three numbers in Sanskrit: a singular number, denoting a single individual, a dual number denoting two, and a plural number denoting more than two. Besides these general senses—

(a) The singular may be used to denote a class; @deva[सिंहः श्वापदराजः] the lion is the king of beasts; @deva[बुद्धिमत्सु नरः श्रेष्ठः] &c.

(b) The dual sometimes denotes a male and a female of the same class; @deva[पितरौ] parents; @deva[चटकौ] a male and a female of sparrow.

(1) Note:—Words like @deva[द्वय], @deva[द्वितीय], @deva[युग], @deva[द्वंद्व], &c. meaning 'a pair,' &c which are dual in sense but singular in form ought to be always used in the singular, except when several pairs are meant.

(2) Note:—Words like @deva[हस्तौ], @deva[नेत्रे], @deva[पादौ], &c. should always be used in the dual in Sanskrit.

(c) The plural, like the singular, may represent a class, @deva[ब्राह्मणाः पूज्याः] (or @deva[ब्राह्मणः पूज्यः]) Brāhmaṇas (i. e. the Brāhmaṇa class) are adorable.

(1) The plural is not unfrequently used as a mark of respect or reverence. @deva[इति श्रीशंकराचार्याः]; so (says) the venerable Shankarāchārya; @deva[इति आचार्यपादाः] this is the opinion of the revered preceptor, &c.

(2) In the first person, great personages and writers sometimes use the plural instead of the singular; @deva[वयमपि भवत्यौ किमपि पृच्छामः] we (i. e. I,) too ask you something; @deva[इति तु वयं] but we (i. e. I, the writer) hold this opinion; @deva[वयमपि च गिरामीश्महे] we rule over speech (i. e. language).

(3) Words like @deva[दाराः], @deva[गृहाः], @deva[अक्षताः], @deva[सिकताः], @deva[आपः], @deva[प्राणाः], @deva[लाजाः], &c. are always used in the plural, though some of them are singular in sense.

(4) Names of countries which are really the names of the people inhabiting them, must be used in the plural; @deva[स विदेहान् उपाययौ] he went to Videha, &c.

But in the case of compounds ending in words denoting a country, such as @deva[देश], @deva[विषय], &c. the sing. must be used; @deva[अस्ति मगधदेशे पाटलिपुत्रं नाम नगरम्] there is a town called Pāṭaliputra in the country of Magadha.

(5) The plural of proper nouns denotes a family or race as in English; @deva[जनकानां रघूणां च यत्कृत्स्नं गोत्रमङ्गलम्] Utta.

rules.title: Concord: Agreement of Words in Sentences
rules.body:
**SECTION I.**

**CONCORD.**

## Concord: Agreement of Words in Sentences

Concord is the agreement of words in a sentence as regards gender, number, person or tense.

The concords deserving notice in Sanskrit are three:—(1) Concord of the verb with the Subject; (2) Concord of the Adjective with the Substantive; and (3) Concord of the Relative with its Antecedent.

**CONCORD OF THE VERB WITH THE SUBJECT.**

rules.title: Verb Agreement with Subject in Number and Person
rules.body:
## Verb Agreement with Subject in Number and Person

The verb must agree with its subject in number and person; @deva[आसीत् राजा नलो नाम] there was a king, Nala by name; @deva[अहं गच्छामि] I go; @deva[ब्राह्मणौ गच्छतः] two Brāhmaṇas go, &c.

rules.title: Verb Concord with Multiple Subjects (and/or)
rules.body:
## Verb Concord with Multiple Subjects (and/or)

(a) When two or more subjects differing in number are connected by 'and' the verb must be plural; @deva[ततः कुन्ती च राजा च भीष्मश्च सह बन्धुभिः । ददुः श्राद्धं तदा पाण्डोः] &c. Mah. Bhā. Sometimes the verb agrees with the nearest subject in number, @deva[सा च सत्यवती देवी गान्धारी च यशस्विनी । राजदारैः परिवृता गान्धारी चापि निर्ययौ ॥] Mah. Bhā. @deva[अहश्च रात्रिश्च उभे च सन्ध्ये धर्मोपि जानाति नरस्य वृत्तम् ॥]

(b) But when they are connected by 'or' and are all sing. the verb will be singular, and when the subject differ in number the verb will agree with the one nearest to it; @deva[रामः गोविंदो वा व्रजतु] 'Let Rāma or Govinda go,' @deva[स वा इमे बालका वा आम्रं गृह्णन्तु] 'let him or these boys take the mango fruit.'

rules.title: Verb Agreement with Subjects of Different Persons
rules.body:
## Verb Agreement with Subjects of Different Persons

(a) When a verb agrees with two or more subjects of different persons connected by 'and,' the first person has preference over the second or third, and the second over the third; @deva[त्वमहं रामश्चैतत्करिष्यामः] Rāma, you and I shall do this; @deva[त्वं रामश्च पाठशालां गच्छतम्].

(b) But when the subjects are connected by 'or', the verb agrees with the one nearest to it; @deva[स वा वयं वा तत्संपादयामः] he or we accomplish that; @deva[अहं रामोथवा राजा लक्ष्मणो वा मरिष्यति] either I or King Rāma or Lakṣmaṇa will perish.

rules.title: Predicate Forms: Participle, Adjective, or Noun
rules.body:
## Predicate Forms: Participle, Adjective, or Noun

The predicate may not always be a finite verb; but a participle, or an adjective or a noun may take its place.

(a) When a participle is used as the predicate it must agree with the subject in number and gender; @deva[स तदुक्तवान्] he said that, @deva[सा तदुक्तवती] she said that, @deva[तेषां बन्धनानि छिन्नानि] their bonds were cut off, @deva[कार्यं कृतं] the work is done, @deva[लता छिन्ना] the creeper is cut; &c.

(b) When an adjective or a noun is used as the predicate, a form of the roots @deva[अस्] or @deva[भू] may be used with it or may be omitted; the adjective used predicatively agrees with the subject in number and gender; words like @deva[आस्पद], @deva[पात्र], @deva[भाजन], @deva[स्थान], @deva[पद] &c. retain their gender and number; @deva[सुभृत्यः दुर्लभः] a good servant is difficult to be obtained, @deva[सुपुत्रः पितुः गर्वास्पदम्] a good son is the object of his father's pride, @deva[सम्पदः पदमापदाम्] riches are the abode of miseries, @deva[स तु तस्या अभिमानभूमिः] &c; in these cases the verb agrees with the subject in number and not with the noun used predicatively; @deva[सम्पदः आपदां पदं सन्ति] and not @deva[अस्ति], &c.

rules.title: Predicative Agreement with Verbs of Incomplete Predication
rules.body:
## Predicative Agreement with Verbs of Incomplete Predication

When a substantive or an adjective is used predicatively with verbs of incomplete predication such as 'to grow, to seem, to be, to appear,' &c. the substantive or adjective so used must agree with the subject in case; @deva[एष मे निश्चयः] this is my resolve; @deva[स भूपतिः प्रजागरकृशः लक्ष्यते] that king seems emaciated through wakefulness; @deva[प्रभुर्बुभूषुर्भुवनत्रयस्य] desirous of being the lord of the three worlds.

(a) The same applies to transitive roots of incomplete predication used passively; @deva[तेन मुनिना स मूषकः बिडालः कृतः] by that sage the mouse was made (transformed into) a cat, &c.; @deva[नृपो हि विष्णुः मन्यते] a king is thought to be Vishnu.

rules.title: Nominative Case with Indeclinables Used Adjectivally
rules.body:
## Nominative Case with Indeclinables Used Adjectivally

When an indeclinable used with an adjectival force takes the place of the verb, the object governed by it is put in the Nominative case.[^1] @deva[विषवृक्षोपि संवर्ध्य स्वयं छेत्तुमसांप्रतम्] (Kum. II. 55.) it is not fit to cut down even a poisonous tree having first reared it up; here the indeclinable @deva[असांप्रतं] is equivalent to @deva[न युज्यते] and the whole sentence to @deva[वृक्षं संवर्ध्य तं छेत्तुं असाम्प्रतं] (@deva[न युज्यते]) @deva[योपि विषवृक्षः स्यात्।]

**Concord of the Adjective with the Substantive.**

---

[^1]: @deva[निपातेनाभिहिते कर्माणि न विभक्तिपरिगणनस्य प्रायिकत्वात्।] Vāman.

rules.title: Adjective Agreement with Substantives
rules.body:
## Adjective Agreement with Substantives

An adjective, participial or qualitative, must agree with the substantive it qualifies in gender, number and case; @deva[रूपवान् पुरुषः] a handsome man; @deva[रूपवती स्त्री] a beautiful woman; @deva[महत्संकटम्] a great calamity; @deva[एते मयूराः], @deva[तानि पुस्तकानि]; @deva[गच्छन्ती नारी], &c.

But numeral adjectives of fixed gender and number remain unchanged:—@deva[शतं ब्राह्मणाः] a hundred Brāhmaṇas; @deva[शतं स्त्रियः] a hundred women, @deva[विंशति बालकानि] twenty children.

rules.title: Adjective Agreement with Multiple Substantives
rules.body:
## Adjective Agreement with Multiple Substantives

When an adjective qualifies two or more substantives it agrees with them in their combined number; when the substantives differ in gender, the adjective will be masculine when the substantives are masculine and feminine; and neuter when they are masculine, feminine and neuter; @deva[राजा राज्ञी च स्तुत्यचरितौ स्तः] the king and his queen are of laudable conduct; @deva[धर्मः कामश्च दर्पश्च हर्षः क्रोधः सुखं वयः । अर्थादेतानि सर्वाणि प्रवर्तन्ते न संशयः] fulfilment of duty, satisfaction of desires, pride, anger, happiness and long life, all these proceed undoubtedly from wealth.

(a) Sometimes the adjective takes the gender of the majority of the substantives; @deva[वृद्धौ च मातापितरौ साध्वी भार्या सुतः शिशुः । अप्यकार्यशतं कृत्वा भर्तव्या मनुरब्रवीत् ॥] aged parents, a good wife and a young son should be maintained even by doing a hundred foul deeds; so has Manu spoken (laid down).

(b) And sometimes it takes the gender and number of the substantive nearest to it when the particle @deva[च] is used; @deva[उद्वेगः कलहः कण्डूः सेव्यमाना च वर्धते] dejection, quarrel and an itching sensation prevail all the more they are attended to; @deva[यस्य वीर्येण कृतिनो वयं च भुवनानि च] (@deva[कृतीनि]) by whose valour we have become happy and so have the three worlds.

rules.title: Predicate Participle Agrees with the Subject
rules.body:
## Predicate Participle Agrees with the Subject

When a past or potential passive participle is used as predicate with a noun in apposition to the subject, the participle agrees with the subject; @deva[कृताः शरव्यं हरिणा तवासुराः] (S'ak. VI.) the demons are made the marks of your arrows by Hari.

**Concord of Relative with its Antecedent.**

rules.title: Relative Agrees with its Antecedent
rules.body:
## Relative Agrees with its Antecedent

The relative agrees with its antecedent in gender, number and person, the cases of the relative and its antecedent being determined by their relation to their respective clauses; @deva[यस्यास्ति वित्तं स नरः कुलीनः] he who has wealth has a noble family; @deva[यस्य बुद्धिर्बलं तस्यः यधेन युज्यते लोके बुधस्तत्तेन योजयेत्] what, which is fit to be united with anything, a wise man should unite with it &c.

rules.title: Relative with a Predicate Noun of Different Gender
rules.body:
## Relative with a Predicate Noun of Different Gender

When the relative has for its predicate a noun differing in gender from the antecedent the relative generally takes the gender of the antecedent noun, the demonstrative pronoun following that of the noun it qualifies; @deva[परगुणासहिष्णुत्वं हि यत्स दुर्जनानां स्वभावः]—non-endurance of the merits of another is but the nature of the wicked; @deva[शैत्यं हि यत्सा प्रकृतिर्जलस्य].

rules.title: Relative Pronoun यत् Introducing a Clause
rules.body:
## Relative Pronoun यत् Introducing a Clause

The relative pronoun @deva[यत्] neu. sing. is used like the English 'that' to introduce a clause, the gender of the demonstrative pronoun being the same as that of the antecedent noun; @deva[यद्विद्वान् अपि नरः अन्यान् विगणयति स धनमद एव] it is the pride of wealth that even a learned man slights another; @deva[सत्योयं जनप्रवादः यत्संपत्संपदमनुबध्नातीति] it is a true saying that one good fortune follows another.

*Obs*:—Sometimes the antecedent noun or pronoun is omitted and has to be inferred from the gender and number of the relative; e. g. @deva[धनेन किं यो न ददाति याचके] i. e. @deva[तस्य धनेन], &c. what is the use of wealth to him who does not bestow it on mendicants, &c.

rules.title: Section II. Government: the Kārakas
rules.body:
**SECTION II.**

**GOVERNMENT.**

## Section II. Government: the Kārakas

The only portion of Syntax treated separately in Sanskrit grammars is the Kārakaprakaraṇa or the chapter on Government. Kāraka is the name given to the relation subsisting between a noun and a verb in a sentence. There are six Kārakas in Sanskrit belonging to the first seven cases, except the Genitive, which is, therefore, not a Kāraka case. These are @deva[कर्ता], @deva[कर्म], @deva[करण], @deva[संप्रदान], @deva[अपादान] and @deva[अधिकरण].

rules.title: Upapadavibhaktis and Kārakavibhaktis
rules.body:
## Upapadavibhaktis and Kārakavibhaktis

There are several indeclinables in Sanskrit which also govern cases. Cases governed by indeclinables are called Upapadavibhaktis, as distinguished from those governed by verbs which are called Kārakavibhaktis. In cases where both are possible the latter predominates over the former (@deva[उपपदविभक्तेः कारकविभक्तिर्बलीयसी]); as in @deva[मुनित्रयं नमस्कृत्य] although @deva[नमस्] alone would govern the Dative.

rules.title: The Nominative Case
rules.body:
## The Nominative Case

The Nominative, as in English and other languages is simply the naming case, its office, when used by itself, is to express the crude form of a word, gender, measure and number and nothing more.[^1] When used with a verb it forms its subject.

**The Accusative Case.**

---

[^1]: @deva[प्रातिपदिकार्थलिङ्गपरिमाणवचनमात्रे प्रथमा] Pāṇ. II. 3. 46.

rules.title: Accusative Case Denotes the Object
rules.body:
## Accusative Case Denotes the Object

The Accusative denotes the object i. e. the person or thing upon whom or which the effect of an action takes place; @deva[हरिं सेवते] he worships Hari; @deva[ग्रामं गच्छन् तृणं स्पृशति] going to a village he touches grass.[^1]

---

[^1]: But when the relation of object and verb is expressed by the passive termination the noun forming the object is put in the nominative case; @deva[हरिः सेव्यते].

rules.title: Transitive Verbs Govern Accusative Case
rules.body:
## Transitive Verbs Govern Accusative Case

All transitive verbs govern an Accusative; @deva[पुष्पाण्यवचिनोति] collects flowers; @deva[अप एव ससर्जादौ] (the creator) created water first, &c. Several transitive verbs govern what is called in English a factitive object besides a direct object; @deva[त्वामामनन्ति प्रकृतिं त्वामेव पुरुषं विदुः] Kum. II. 13 they consider thee to be Prakriti, they know thee to be Purusha; @deva[कुमारं नेतारं कृत्वा] having made Kumāra the leader (of the forces); @deva[नाम्ना तमात्मजन्मानं अजं चकार] made his son Aja by name.

rules.title: Intransitive Verbs with Accusative of Space and Time
rules.body:
## Intransitive Verbs with Accusative of Space and Time

[^1] Intransitive roots govern the Accusative nouns denoting space or country, or duration of time and distance; @deva[कुरून् स्वपिति] he sleeps in the country of the Kurus; @deva[तत्र कतिपयान् दिवसान् अवसत्] there he dwelt for some days; @deva[गोदोहमास्ते] he sits down till a cow is milked; @deva[कोशं प्रतिष्ठते] he walks for a Kosa; @deva[कोशं कुटिला नदी] the course of the river is winding for a Kosa; but @deva[मासस्य द्विरधीते] studies twice a month; @deva[कोशस्यैकदेशे पर्वतः] the hill is situated in a part of a Kosa.

---

[^1]: @deva[कालाध्वनोरत्यन्तसंयोगे ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 5.

rules.title: Verbs of Motion Govern Accusative of Destination
rules.body:
## Verbs of Motion Govern Accusative of Destination

Roots having the sense of motion, real or metaphorical govern the Accusative of the place to which it is directed. @deva[ग्रामं गच्छति] goes to a village; @deva[अधिज्यधन्वा विचचार दावम्] with his bow strung he roamed all over the forest; @deva[आनन्दस्य परां कोटिमध्यगच्छन्] they reached the highest point of joy; @deva[मनसा कृष्णमेति] goes to Krishna (thinks of him) mentally; @deva[इति चिन्तयन्नेष स निद्रां ययौ] while thus pondering he sank into sleep.

(a) When the motion is real, the Dative may also be used; @deva[ग्रामाय ग्रामं वा गच्छति]; but not of words denoting 'a road;' @deva[पन्थानं गच्छति] only; but @deva[उत्पथेन पथे गच्छति] he reaches the main road by taking a by-path.

rules.title: Roots शी, स्था, आस् with अधि Govern Accusative
rules.body:
## Roots @deva[शी], @deva[स्था], @deva[आस्] with @deva[अधि] Govern Accusative

The roots[^1] @deva[शी], @deva[स्था] and @deva[आस्], with @deva[अधि], govern the Accusative of the place where the action takes place; @deva[अधिशेते अधितिष्ठति अध्यास्ते वा वैकुण्ठं हरिः]; @deva[शिलापट्टमधिशयाना] reclining on a stone-slab; @deva[अर्धासनं गोत्रभिदोधितस्थौ] occupied half of Indra's seat; @deva[अध्यास्त सर्वर्तुसुखामयोध्याम्] lived in Ayodhyā delightful in all seasons.

---

[^1]: @deva[अधिशीङ्स्थासां कर्म ।] Pāṇ. I. 4. 46.

rules.title: Root विश् with अभिनि: Accusative and Locative
rules.body:
## Root @deva[विश्] with @deva[अभिनि]: Accusative and Locative

@deva[विश्][^1] with @deva[अभिनि] governs the Accusative; @deva[अभिनिविशते सन्मार्गम्] he pursues the path of goodness; @deva[धन्या सा गणिकादारिका यामेव भवन्मनोऽभिनिविशते] happy is that harlot girl on whom you have fixed your mind (see Bhatti. VIII. 80.). Rarely this governs the Loc. @deva[अभिनिविशते पापे] fondly resorts to sin. @deva[विश्] with a preposition governs the Acc. but with @deva[उप] meaning 'to sit' takes the Loc. @deva[आसनेऽस्मिन्नुपविश] sit on this seat.

---

[^1]: @deva[अभिनिविशश्च] Pāṇ. I. 4. 47.

rules.title: Root वस् with Prepositions Governs Accusative
rules.body:
## Root @deva[वस्] with Prepositions Governs Accusative

The root @deva[वस्][^1] preceded by the prepositions @deva[उप], @deva[अनु], @deva[अधि] and @deva[आ] governs the Accusative case; @deva[उप-अनु-अधि-आ-वसति वैकुंठं हरिः]. Hari dwells in Vaikuntha; @deva[शून्यमन्ववसद्वनं] he dwelt in a dreary forest; but @deva[वस्] with @deva[उप] meaning 'to abstain from food' is used with the Loc; @deva[उपवसति वने रामः] Rāma observes a fast in the forest.

---

[^1]: @deva[उपान्वध्याङ्वसः ।] Pāṇ. I. 4. 48.

rules.title: Particles and Prepositions Governing Accusative
rules.body:
## Particles and Prepositions Governing Accusative

The particles[^1] @deva[उभयतः], @deva[सर्वतः], @deva[उपर्युपरि], @deva[अधोधः], @deva[अध्यधि] and @deva[धिक्]; @deva[अभितः], @deva[परितः], @deva[समया], @deva[निकषा], @deva[हा] and @deva[प्रति] meaning 'to,' and @deva[अन्तरा] 'between,' and @deva[अन्तरेण] 'without,' 'regarding to,' govern the Accusative; @deva[उभयतः कृष्णं गोपाः] the cowherds are on both sides of Krishna—@deva[सर्वतः प्रासादं जाग्रति दण्डधारिणः] guards keep vigil on all sides of the palace; @deva[उपर्युपरि लोकं हरिः] Hari is over all the worlds; @deva[अधोधो लोकं पातालः] Pātāla is below the world. @deva[अध्यधि लोकम्]; @deva[धिग्वो जाल्मान्] fie upon you rogues; @deva[धिक्सानुजं कुरुपतिं] fie upon the lord of the Kurus, with all his brothers; (@deva[धिक्]) is used sometimes with the Nom. and sometimes with the Voc. @deva[धिगर्थाः कष्टसंश्रयाः] fie upon wealth which is attended with troubles; @deva[धिङ् मूर्ख] fie upon thee fool; @deva[रक्षांसि वेदिं परितो निरास्थदङ्गान्ययाक्षीदभितः प्रधानम्] (Bhatti I. 12) he dispelled the demons from around the altar and offered sacrifices to the minor deities arranged round the principal one. @deva[अभितस्तं पृथासूनुः स्नेहेन परितस्तरे] Kir. XI. 8. @deva[ग्रामं समया-निकषा व्रजति] goes near to the village. Vide Sis. I. 68, VI. 73. @deva[हा कृष्णाभक्तं] woe to him who is not a devotee of Krishna; @deva[मन्दौत्सुक्योऽस्मि नगरगमनं प्रति] I have but a faint desire to go to the town; @deva[अन्तरा त्वां मां हरिः]; @deva[हरिमन्तरेण न सुखं] happiness is not possible without Hari; @deva[देवीं वसुमतीमन्तरेण] with reference to queen Vasumati.

Some of the indeclinables given above are used with the Genitive; e. g. @deva[उपर्युपरि सर्वेषामादित्य इव तेजसा] (he stood) very high above all by his lustre, like the sun, &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[उभसर्वतसो कार्या धिगुपर्यादिषु त्रिषु । द्वितीयाम्रेडितान्तेषु ततोन्यत्रापि दृश्यते । अभितः परितः समया निकषा हा प्रतियोगेपि ।] Vārtikas on Pāṇ. I. 4. 48. @deva[अन्तरान्तरेण युक्ते] Pāṇ. II. 3. 4.

rules.title: Prepositions Used with Accusative: अति, अनु, अभि, उप, परि, प्रति
rules.body:
## Prepositions Used with Accusative: @deva[अति], @deva[अनु], @deva[अभि], @deva[उप], @deva[परि], @deva[प्रति]

The following prepositions are used with the Accusative.[^1]

(a) @deva[अति] 'superior to, higher than,' @deva[अनु] 'just after, after, by the side of, inferior to,' @deva[अभि] 'close to' and @deva[उप] 'near, inferior to;' e. g. @deva[अति देवान् कृष्णः] Krishna excels gods in might; @deva[अतिरामं गोविन्दः] Govinda is superior to Rāma; @deva[जपमनु प्रावर्षत्] it rained just after the muttering of prayers; @deva[सर्वं मामनु ते] every thing of thee is after mine; @deva[अनु पितरं गच्छति सुतः] the son imitates his father; @deva[न भवान् अनु रामं चेत्] if you are not inferior to Rāma; so @deva[अनु हरि सुराः], @deva[भक्तो हरिं अभि] the devotee is close to Hari; @deva[उपशूरं न ते वृत्तं] your act is not like that of a hero (lit. is inferior to his); @deva[उपहरिं सुराः] &c.

(b) The prepositions @deva[अभि], @deva[अनु], @deva[परि] and @deva[प्रति] are used with the Accusative when they refer to particular things; @deva[गिरि-अभि-अनु-परि-प्रति-वियोतते विद्युत्] the lightning flashes towards the mountain; also when they mean 'to every one,' &c. @deva[वृक्षं वृक्षमभि-अनु-परि-प्रति-सिंचति] waters each and every tree; so @deva[अभि-अनु-परि-प्रति स्त्रीं स्त्रीं जातमन्मथः ।]

(c) @deva[अनु], @deva[परि] and @deva[प्रति] also govern the Accusative when they imply 'one's own share;' @deva[लक्ष्मीः हरिमनु-परि-प्रति] Lakshmi is the proper share (property) of Hari.

---

[^1]: @deva[कर्मप्रवचनीययुक्ते द्वितीया] Pāṇ. II. 3. 8. Prepositions used by themselves and governing nouns are called Karmapravachanīya. @deva[तृतीयार्थे । हीने । उपोधिके च । लक्षणेत्थंभूताख्यानभागवीप्सासु प्रतिपर्यनवः । अभिरभागे ।] Pāṇ. I. 4. 85–87, 90, 91.

rules.title: Roots Governing Double Accusative
Passive Construction with Double Accusative Roots
rules.body:
## Passive Construction with Double Accusative Roots

When these verbs are used in the passive,[^1] the secondary object in the case of the first twelve roots and the principal one in that of the last four is put in the Nominative case, the other Accusative remaining as before; @deva[धेनुः पयो दुह्यते], @deva[दशरथः रामं ययाचे कौशिकेन], @deva[उदधिः सुधां ममन्थे देवैः] &c, @deva[तेन गावः ग्रामं नीयन्ते ह्रियन्ते कृष्यन्ते उह्यन्ते वा], &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[गौणे कर्मणि दुह्यादेः नीहृकृष्वहाम् * * * लादयो मताः] Sid. Kau. on Pāṇ. VII. 1. 69.

rules.title: Causative Verbs: Subject in Accusative Case
rules.body:
## Causative Verbs: Subject in Accusative Case

In the case of the causals of roots implying 'motion,' 'knowledge,' 'eating,' roots having some literary work for their object, intransitive roots and the roots @deva[दृश्] and @deva[जल्प्], @deva[भाष्] with @deva[आ]; @deva[लप्] with @deva[वि], @deva[ग्रह्] and @deva[श्रु], their subject in the primitive sense is put in the Accusative case.[^1]

@deva[शत्रूनगमयत्स्वर्गं वेदार्थं स्वानवेदयत् ।]
@deva[आशयच्चामृतं देवान्वेदमध्यापयद्विधिम् ।]
@deva[आसयत्सलिले पृथ्वीं यः स मे श्रीहरिर्गतिः ॥] Sid. Kau.

That venerable Hari is my refuge who despatched the enemies (of gods) to the next world, explained the meaning of the Vedas to his (followers), made the gods drink nectar, taught Veda to the Creator and seated the earth (made it rest) on waters.

@deva[दर्शयति हरिं भक्तान्] he makes the devotees see Hari; @deva[जल्पयति भाषयति विलापयति धर्मं पुत्रं देवदत्तः; पुत्रं विद्यामग्राहयत्] (cf. Kum. I. 52); @deva[अश्रावयत्परिषदान्कथाम्]. But when the double causal is used the subject ceases to be the subject of the root in the primitive sense and therefore takes the Instrumental; @deva[गमयति देवदत्तः यज्ञदत्तं], @deva[गमयति देवदत्तेन यज्ञदत्तं विष्णुमित्रः]

*Obs*:—@deva[दृश्] is sometimes found used with the Dative; @deva[प्रत्यभिज्ञानरत्नं च रामायादर्शयन्कृती] Rag. XII. 54.

(a) The causals of @deva[नी], and @deva[वह्] when it has for its subject a noun other than one denoting a driver, govern the Instrumental of the primitive subject;[^2] @deva[नाययति वाहयति वा भारं भृत्येन] he makes his servant carry a load; but @deva[वाहयति रथं वाहान् सूतः] the charioteer makes the horses draw the chariot.

(1) The same holds good in the case of the causal of @deva[अद्] and @deva[खाद्];[^3] @deva[आदयति खादयति वा अन्नं बटुना] he makes the boy eat his food.

(2) @deva[भक्ष्][^4] when it has not the sense of @deva[हिंसा] 'pain or injury to a sentient thing' does the same; @deva[भक्षयत्यन्नं बटुना]; but @deva[भक्षयति बलीवर्दान् सस्यम्] (when the loss of corn causes pain to the mind).

(b) @deva[स्मृ] and @deva[ज्ञा] which denote a kind of knowledge are construed with the Instrumental, though the former when meaning 'to remember with pain' is sometimes found used with the Accusative also; @deva[स्मारयति ज्ञापयति वा देवदत्तेन]; @deva[अयि चंद्रगुप्तदोषा अतिक्रान्तपार्थिवगुणान् स्मारयन्ति प्रकृतीः ।] Vide also Śis. VI. 56.
