(c) The causal of the denominative @deva[शब्दाय][^5] also is construed with the Instrumental; @deva[शब्दाययति देवदत्तेन] he causes Devadatta to make a sound.

Note:—[^6] By intransitive roots are meant such roots as are not capable of governing an object other than one denoting space, time, &c. and not such as, though transitive, may be used without their object being actually expressed; @deva[मासं आसयति देवदत्तं]; but @deva[देवदत्तेन पाचयति] and not @deva[देवदत्तं] though the object of @deva[पच्] is not actually expressed.

---

[^1]: @deva[गतिबुद्धित्यवसानार्थशब्दकर्माकर्मकाणामणि कर्ता स णौ ।] Pāṇ. I. 4. 52. @deva[जल्पतिप्रभृतीनामुपसंख्यानम् । दृशेश्च] Vārtikas.
[^2]: @deva[नीवह्योर्न । नियन्तृकर्तृकस्य वहेरनिषेधः ।] Vārtikas.
[^3]: @deva[आदिखाद्योर्न ।] Vārtika.
[^4]: @deva[भक्षेरहिंसार्थस्य न ।] Vārt.
[^5]: @deva[शब्दायतेर्न] Vārt.
[^6]: @deva[येषां देशकालादिभिन्नं कर्म न संभवति तेऽत्राकर्मकाः । न त्वविवक्षितकर्मणोपि] Sid. Kau.

rules.title: Causative: Roots हृ, कृ, अभिवद्, दृश् in the Ātmanepada
rules.body:
## Causative: Roots @deva[हृ], @deva[कृ], @deva[अभिवद्], @deva[दृश्] in the Ātmanepada

The primitive subject of the verbs @deva[हृ] and @deva[कृ],[^1] of @deva[अभिवद्], and @deva[दृश्] when used in the Atm. is either put in the Accusative or the Instrumental; @deva[हारयति कारयति वा भृत्यं भृत्येन वा कटम्] he causes the servant to take or weave a mat; @deva[अभिवादयते दर्शयते देवं भक्तं भक्तेन वा] he makes the devotee bow down to, or see, God.

---

[^1]: @deva[हृक्रोरन्यतरस्याम्] Pāṇ. I. 4. 43. @deva[अभिवादिदृशोरात्मनेपदं वेति वाच्यम् ।] Vārt.

rules.title: Passive Construction with Causative Verbs
rules.body:
## Passive Construction with Causative Verbs

When the causal forms are used in the passive,[^1] the principal object (i. e. the primitive subject) is put in the Nominative case; but in the case of roots implying 'knowledge or eating' and roots having a literary work for their object the principal object is put in the Nominative case and the secondary object in the Accusative or *vice versa*; @deva[देवदत्तः कटं करोति] Devadatta prepares a mat—@deva[देवदत्तं देवदत्तेन वा कटं कारयति]; @deva[देवदत्तः कटं कार्यते] he makes Devadatta prepare a mat, @deva[देवदत्तः ग्रामं गच्छति] Dev. goes to a village; @deva[देवदत्तं ग्रामं गमयति] causes Dev. to go to a village; @deva[देवदत्तः ग्रामं गम्यते]; Devadatta is made to go, &c.; @deva[माणवकं धर्मं बोधयति] he makes Māṇavaka know his duty; @deva[बोध्यते माणवकं धर्मः, माणवको धर्मं इति वा] Māṇavaka is made to know, &c.; @deva[बटुमोदनं भोजयति] he makes the child eat food; @deva[बटुरोदनं भोज्यते] or @deva[बटुमोदनो भोज्यते] the boy is made, &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[बुद्धिभक्षार्थयोः शब्दकर्मणां च निजेच्छया । प्रयोज्यकर्मण्यन्येषां ण्यन्तानां लादयो मताः ॥] Sid. Kau. on Pāṇ. VII. 1. 69.

rules.title: Causative Verbs with Double Accusative Roots
rules.body:
## Causative Verbs with Double Accusative Roots

As regards the causal of roots governing two Accusatives the general rules given at @ref[808] hold good; @deva[कौशिकः दशरथं रामं अयाचत]; (@deva[देवाः]) @deva[कौशिकेन दशरथं राममयाचयन्], @deva[गोपोऽजां ग्रामं हरति], (@deva[स्वामी]) @deva[गोपेन अजां ग्रामं हारयति], &c.

## THE INSTRUMENTAL CASE

rules.title: Instrumental Case: Agent and Instrument
rules.body:
## Instrumental Case: Agent and Instrument

The Instrumental case[^1] primarily expresses either the agent (when the construction is passive) or the instrument or means by which an action is done; @deva[तव महिमानं अजानता मया असत्कृतोसि] thou wast disrespected by me, not knowing thy greatness; @deva[रामेण बाणेन हतो वाली] Vāli was killed by Rāma with an arrow (here @deva[रामेण] is the agent; @deva[बाणेन] the instrument).

(a) The Instrumental is also used in the following senses.[^2] @deva[प्रकृत्या दर्शनीयः] lovely *by nature*, @deva[प्रायेण याज्ञिकः] he is *almost* a ritualist; @deva[गोत्रेण गार्ग्यः] Gārgya *by family name*; @deva[सुखेन याति] goes with *ease*; so @deva[समेनैति], @deva[विषमेणैति], &c @deva[द्विद्रोणेन धान्यं क्रीणाति] he buys two *dronas* of corn at a time; @deva[साहस्रेण पशून् क्रीणाति] he buys one *thousand* beasts at a time, &c.

(1) In the case of numerals and words expressive of measure the Acc. may also be used; @deva[द्विद्रोणं क्रीणाति धान्यं], @deva[शतेन शतेन शतं शतं वत्सान् पाययति पयः]; &c

(b) *Obs.*—[^3] The root @deva[दिव्] 'to play,' however, governs the Accusative or the Instrumental of the instrument used; @deva[अक्षैः अक्षान् वा दीव्यति] he plays at dice.

(c) [^4] The root @deva[ज्ञा] with @deva[सम्] also governs the Accusative or the Instrumental; @deva[पित्रा पितरं वा संजानीते] he recognises or lives in peace with his father; but @deva[विष्णु संजानीध्व] remember Vishnu.

---

[^1]: @deva[कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 18.
[^2]: @deva[प्रकृत्यादिभ्य उपसंख्यानम् ।] Vārt.
[^3]: @deva[दिवः कर्म च ।] Pāṇ. I. 4. 43.
[^4]: @deva[संज्ञोन्यतरस्यां कर्मणि ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 22.

rules.title: Instrumental with Time/Space for Accomplishment
rules.body:
## Instrumental with Time/Space for Accomplishment

When the accomplishment of an object is to be expressed,[^1] the Instrumental of words expressing the length of time or space is used; @deva[अह्ना क्रोशेन वाऽनुवाकोधीतः] the section (of the Veda) was studied by him in a day, or a Kosa (i. e. by going over it); but @deva[मासमधीतो नायातः] as the accomplishment does not take place.

---

[^1]: @deva[अपवर्गे तृतीया ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 6. @deva[अपवर्गः फलप्राप्तिः । तस्यां द्योत्यायां कालाध्वनोरत्यन्तसंयोगे तृतीया स्यात् ।]

rules.title: Instrumental with Defective Limbs
rules.body:
## Instrumental with Defective Limbs

Words expressing some defect in a limb of the body govern the Instrumental of the defective limb;[^1] @deva[अक्ष्णा काणः] blind of one eye; so @deva[पादेन खञ्जः] &c

---

[^1]: @deva[येनाङ्गविकारः ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 20.

rules.title: Instrumental with Characteristic Attributes
rules.body:
## Instrumental with Characteristic Attributes

A characteristic attribute indicative of the existence of a particular state or condition is put in the Instrumental;[^1] @deva[जटाभिः तापसः] he is an ascetic (which is apparent) from his matted hair (@deva[जटाज्ञाप्यतापसत्वविशिष्ट इत्यर्थ] Sid. Kau.).

---

[^1]: @deva[इत्थंभूतलक्षणे ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 21.

rules.title: Instrumental for Cause, Motive, and Purpose
rules.body:
## Instrumental for Cause, Motive, and Purpose

The Instrumental is also used to express the cause or motive or the object of purpose of an action as distinguished from the mere instrument of it;[^1] @deva[पुण्येन दृष्टो हरिः] Hari was seen by (virtue of) merit; @deva[तेनापराधेन दण्ड्योसि] thou art to be punished for that fault; @deva[अध्ययनेन वसति] dwells for the purpose of studying; also when the object to be accomplished is simply implied; @deva[अलं श्रमेण] away with your efforts i. e. they will not succeed; @deva[श्रमेण साध्यं नास्ति इत्यर्थः] (Sid. Kau).

---

[^1]: @deva[हेतौ ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. @deva[फलमपि इह हेतुः । द्रव्यादिसाधारणं निर्व्यापारसाधारणं च हेतुत्वम् । करणत्वं तु क्रियामात्रविषयं व्यापारनियतं च ।] Sid. Kau.

rules.title: Instrumental: Excelling, Resemblance, Swearing, Rejoicing, Motion, Price
rules.body:
## Instrumental: Excelling, Resemblance, Swearing, Rejoicing, Motion, Price

The Instrumental is used with words expressing the idea of—

(a) excelling; @deva[पूर्वान् महाभाग तयातिशेषे] Oh fortunate one, you excel your ancestors in that (devotion); @deva[धाम्नातिशाययति धाम सहस्रधाम्नः] (Mu 3. 17) he surpasses by his lustre, the lustre of the sun; @deva[दूरीकृता खलु गुणैरुद्यानलता वनलताभिः ।] Ś'ak. I.

(b) resemblance, likeness, equality; @deva[स्वरेण पितरमनुहरति] resembles his father in voice; @deva[देहबन्धने स्वरेण च रामभद्रमनुहरति] (Utta. 4.); @deva[अस्य मुखं मातुः मुखेन संवदति] his face resembles that of his mother; @deva[विष्णुना सदृशो वीर्ये] equal to Vishnu in valour.

(c) swearing; @deva[भरतेनात्मना चाहं शपे] I swear by Bharata and myself; @deva[शापितासि मम जीवितेन] I conjure thee by my life.

(d) rejoicing, being pleased; @deva[भक्त्या गुरौ मय्यनुकम्पया च प्रीतास्मि] I am pleased with thee by thy devotion to your preceptor and compassion upon me; @deva[कापुरुषः स्वल्पकेनापि तुष्यति] a low person is satisfied with little.

(e) motion (the conveyance or the part of the body on which a thing is carried being put in the Instrumental case); @deva[रथेन संचरते] 'he moves about in a chariot.'

(f) price (real or metaphorical) at which a thing is bought; @deva[शतेन क्रीतः] bought for a hundred (rupees, etc.), @deva[स्वप्राणव्ययेनापि रक्षणीयाः सुहृदसवः] 'the life of a friend ought to be saved even at the cost of one's life.'

rules.title: Instrumental: Use, Need, Accompaniment, Possession
rules.body:
## Instrumental: Use, Need, Accompaniment, Possession

The following words also govern the Instrumental case:—

(a) Words expressing the idea of use or need, such as @deva[किं], @deva[कार्यं], @deva[अर्थः], @deva[प्रयोजनं] and the like, and the root @deva[कृ] with @deva[किं] used in the same sense; @deva[धनेन किं यः] &c what is the use of his wealth who &c; @deva[तृणेन कार्यं भवतीश्वराणाम्]—'even the rich sometimes stand in need of grass,' similarly @deva[कोर्थः पुत्रेण जातेन यो न विद्वान्न धार्मिकः], @deva[न स्वामिपादानां मया किमपि प्रयोजनम्], &c.

(b) The particles @deva[अलं] and @deva[कृतं] meaning 'enough,' @deva[अलं रुदितेन] 'enough of your weeping (do not weep):' @deva[कृतं अत्यादरेण] 'away with overpressing'; @deva[अलं] is also used with a gerund @deva[अलं अन्यथा संभाव्य] 'away with misunderstanding.'

(c) Particles expressing 'accompaniment' such as @deva[साकं], @deva[सार्धं], @deva[समं], @deva[सह], &c.; @deva[आस्व साकं मया सौधे] (Bh. VIII. 70.); @deva[वनं मया सार्धमसि प्रपन्नः] Rag. XIV. 63; @deva[आहो निवत्स्यति समं हरिणाङ्गनाभिः ।] Ś'ak I. 27. &c.

(d) Words meaning 'having or destitute of,' @deva[समायुक्तोप्यर्थैः] (@deva[परिभवपदं याति कृपणः]) 'though possessed of wealth,' &c; @deva[अर्थेन हीनः] 'destitute of wealth.'

*N. B.* For the optional use of the Instrumental see the Abl., the Gen. and the Loc. cases.

## THE DATIVE CASE

rules.title: Dative Case: Sampradāna (Indirect Object)
rules.body:
## Dative Case: Sampradāna (Indirect Object)

The primary sense of the Dative case is Sampradāna (@deva[संप्रदानं]).[^1] The indirect object of the root @deva[दा] is called Sampradāna; also the person or thing with reference to whom or which an action is done; @deva[विप्राय गां ददाति] 'he gives a cow to a Brāhmaṇa;' @deva[युद्धाय संनह्यते] 'prepares for battle;' @deva[न शूद्राय मतिं दद्यात्] 'The Śūdra should not be instructed in the Veda, &c'

But in the case of the root @deva[यज्][^2] the proper object is put in the Instrumental case and the indirect object in the Accusative; @deva[पशुना रुद्रं यजते] 'he sacrifices a bull to Rudra.'

Note:—Though the root @deva[दा] ought to govern the Dat. of the indirect object, it is sometimes found used with the Gen. or the Loc. @deva[राज्यं शिबीनां ऋद्धं वै ददामि तव खेचर] 'Oh sky-wanderer, I will give you the prosperous kingdom of the Sibis;' @deva[यस्त्वं रामे पृथिवीं दातुमिच्छासि] 'thou who art thinking of bestowing the earth upon Rāma,' &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[चतुर्थी संप्रदाने] Pāṇ. II. 3. 13. @deva[कर्मणा यमभिप्रैति स संप्रदानम्] Pāṇ. I. 4. 32. @deva[क्रियया यमभिप्रैति सोपि संप्रदानम्] Vārt.
[^2]: @deva[यजेः कर्मणः करणसंज्ञा संप्रदानस्य च कर्मसंज्ञा ।] Vārt.

rules.title: Dative with रुच् and Roots of Pleasing
rules.body:
## Dative with @deva[रुच्] and Roots of Pleasing

The roots @deva[रुच्][^1] and others having the same sense govern the Dative of the person or thing pleased or satisfied; @deva[हरये रोचते भक्तिः] 'Hari likes devotion;' @deva[अपां हि तृप्ताय न वारिधारा स्वादुः सुगन्धिः स्वदते तुषारा] 'a stream of sweet water, cool and perfumed, is not liked by one who has already drunk enough of water.'

---

[^1]: @deva[रुच्यर्थानां प्रीयमाणः] Pāṇ. I. 4. 33.

rules.title: Dative with श्लाघ्, ह्नु, स्था, शप्
rules.body:
## Dative with @deva[श्लाघ्], @deva[ह्नु], @deva[स्था], @deva[शप्]

The roots @deva[श्लाघ्][^1] 'to praise,' @deva[ह्नु] 'to hide,' @deva[स्था] 'to stand,' and @deva[शप्] 'to swear,' govern the Dative of the person to whom some object or feeling is to be conveyed; @deva[गोपी स्मरात् कृष्णाय श्लाघते-ह्नुते-तिष्ठते-शपते वा] 'a cowherdess being incited by love flatters Krishna or apparently conceals her feeling from him or waits for him or swears before him;' (Vide Bhatti. VII. 73. 74.): but @deva[राजानं श्लाघते मन्त्री] 'a minister praises his king.'

---

[^1]: @deva[श्लाघह्नुङ्स्थाशपां ज्ञीप्स्यमानः ।] Pāṇ. I. 4. 34.

rules.title: Dative with धृ (Debt) and स्पृह् (Desire)
rules.body:
## Dative with @deva[धृ] (Debt) and @deva[स्पृह्] (Desire)

The creditor (or the person to whom something is due) in the case of the root @deva[धृ][^1] 'to owe;' and the person or thing desired in the case of @deva[स्पृह्], are put in the Dative case; @deva[वृक्षसेचने द्वे धारयसि मे] 'you owe me two sprinklings of trees' (Sa'k.); @deva[भक्ताय धारयति मोक्षं हरिः]; (Sid. Kau.) @deva[तस्यै स्पृहयमाणोसौ] 'he longing for her (Bhatti VIII. 15.);' @deva[पुष्पेभ्यः स्पृहयति] 'he longs for flowers;' but @deva[पुष्पाणि स्पृहयति] where no longing is implied.

---

[^1]: @deva[धारेरुत्तमर्णः । स्पृहेरीप्सितः ।] Pāṇ. I. 4 35, 36.

rules.title: Dative with क्रुध्, द्रुह्, ईर्ष्य्, असूय् (Anger, Hatred, Jealousy)
rules.body:
## Dative with @deva[क्रुध्], @deva[द्रुह्], @deva[ईर्ष्य्], @deva[असूय्] (Anger, Hatred, Jealousy)

The roots @deva[क्रुध्],[^1] @deva[द्रुह्], @deva[ईर्ष्य्], and @deva[असूय्], and others having the same sense govern the Dative of the person against whom the feeling of anger, hatred, &c. is directed; @deva[हरये क्रुध्यति द्रुह्यति-ईर्ष्यति-असूयति वा] (Sid Kau) 'he is angry with Hari, or bears hatred towards him, or is jealous of him or finds fault with him;' @deva[सीतायै नाक्रुध्यन्नाप्यसूयत] (Bhatt. VIII 75.) 'he did neither get angry with Sītā nor find fault with her;' but @deva[भार्यामीर्ष्यति] 'he keeps a jealous watch over his wife' (that others may not see her @deva[मैनामन्योऽद्राक्षीदिति] Sid. Kau)

(a) [^2] But @deva[क्रुध्] and @deva[द्रुह्] preceded by a preposition govern the Accusative case; @deva[किं मां संक्रुध्यसि] 'why do you get angry with me?' @deva[नित्यमस्मच्छरीरमभिद्रोग्धुं यतते] (Mud. I.) 'he always endeavours to do harm to my body.'

*Obs*:—@deva[द्रुह्] with @deva[अभि] is also found used with the Dat.; @deva[मया पुनरेभ्य एवाभिद्रुग्धमजेन] (Utta. VII).

---

[^1]: @deva[क्रुधद्रुहेर्ष्यासूयार्थानां यं प्रति कोपः ।] Pāṇ. I. 4. 37. @deva[क्रोधोऽमर्षः द्रोहोऽपकारः ईर्ष्याऽक्षमा असूया गुणेषु दोषाविष्करणं । द्रुहादयोपि कोपप्रभवा एव गृह्यन्ते । अतो विशेषणं सामान्येन ।] Sid. Kau.
[^2]: @deva[क्रुधद्रुहोरुपसृष्टयोः कर्म ।] Pāṇ. I. 4. 38.

rules.title: Dative with राध् and ईक्ष् (Fortune Inquiry)
rules.body:
## Dative with @deva[राध्] and @deva[ईक्ष्] (Fortune Inquiry)

The roots @deva[राध्][^1] and @deva[ईक्ष्] both meaning 'to determine the good or bad fortune of,' govern the Dative of the person with reference to whom the inquiry is made; @deva[कृष्णाय राध्यति ईक्षते वा । पृष्टो गर्गः शुभाशुभं पर्यालोचयतीत्यर्थः ।] Sid. Kau.

---

[^1]: @deva[राधीक्ष्योर्यस्य विप्रश्नः ।] Pāṇ. I. 4. 39.

rules.title: Dative with श्रु (Promise)
rules.body:
## Dative with @deva[श्रु] (Promise)

@deva[श्रु][^1] with @deva[प्रति] and @deva[आ] meaning 'to promise,' governs the Dative of the person to whom a promise is made after solicitation; @deva[विप्राय गां प्रतिशृणोति आशृणोति वा । विप्रेण मह्यं देहीति प्रवर्तितः प्रतिजानीति इत्यर्थः ।] Sid. Kau.

---

[^1]: @deva[प्रत्याङ्भ्यां श्रुवः पूर्वस्य कर्ता ।] Pāṇ. 4. 40.

rules.title: Dative/Instrumental with परि+क्री (Hire)
rules.body:
## Dative/Instrumental with @deva[परि]+@deva[क्री] (Hire)

The root @deva[क्री][^1] with @deva[परि] 'to hire, as a servant,' &c., optionally governs the Dative (and optionally the Inst.) of the price at which he is hired; @deva[शतेन शताय वा परिक्रीतः ।] Sid. Kau.

---

[^1]: @deva[परिक्रयणे संप्रदानमन्यतरस्याम् ।] Pāṇ. 4. 44. @deva[नियतकालभृत्यास्वीकरणं परिक्रयणं ।] Sid. Kau.

rules.title: Dative for Purpose, Result, Evil Portent, Benefit
rules.body:
## Dative for Purpose, Result, Evil Portent, Benefit

[^1] (a) A noun expressive of the purpose for which anything is done, or the result to which anything leads or the effect for which anything exists, is put in the Dative case; @deva[मुक्तये हरिं भजति] 'worships Hari for final beatitude;' @deva[भक्तिर्ज्ञानाय कल्पते सम्पद्यते जायते वा] 'devotion leads to knowledge;' @deva[मूत्राय कल्पते जायते सम्पद्यते यवागूः] (Mb.) 'water gruel tends to (produce) urine,' @deva[कुण्डलाय हिरण्यं] (Mah. Bhās.) 'gold for Kundala (a kind of ornament);' @deva[यूपाय दारु] 'wood for a sacrificial post,' &c.

*N. B.* The roots @deva[भू] or @deva[अस्] are often omitted after a Dative used in this sense @deva[काव्यं यशसे] (@deva[भवति]), poetry is for fame.'

(d) [^2] An evil foreboded by a portentous phenomenon is also put in the Dative case; @deva[वाताय कपिला विद्युत्] 'the tawny lightning forebodes a storm.'

(c) [^3] The word @deva[हित] is used with the Dative; @deva[ब्राह्मणाय हितं] 'good for a Brāhmaṇa.'

---

[^1]: @deva[तादर्थ्ये चतुर्थी वाच्या । क्लृपि संपद्यमाने च ।] Vārtika.
[^2]: @deva[उत्पातेन ज्ञापिते च ।] Vārt. @deva[वाताय कपिलाविद्युदातपायातिलोहिनी । पीता वर्षाय विज्ञेया दुर्भिक्षाय सिता भवेत् ।] Mah. Bhās.
[^3]: @deva[हितयोगे च ।] Vārt.

rules.title: Dative with Implied Infinitive
rules.body:
## Dative with Implied Infinitive

The object governed by an infinitive mood not actually used but implied, is put in the Dative;[^1] @deva[फलेभ्यो याति] i. e. (@deva[फलानि आहर्तुं]) 'goes for (in order to bring) fruits;' @deva[नृसिंहाय नमस्कुर्मः] (i. e @deva[नृसिंहमनुकूलयितुं]) 'We bow down to Nrisimha (to propitiate him)'

(a) The Dative of an abstract noun formed from a root may be used to express the sense of the infinitive of the same root; @deva[यागाय याति] 'goes to perform a sacrifice;' @deva[त्यागाय संभृतार्थानां] (Rag. I. 7.) 'who had amassed wealth in order to give it away,' &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[क्रियार्थोपपदस्य च कर्माणि स्थानिनः । तुमर्थाच्च भाववचनात् ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 14, 15.

rules.title: Dative with नमः, स्वस्ति, स्वाहा, स्वधा, अलं, वषट्
rules.body:
## Dative with @deva[नमः], @deva[स्वस्ति], @deva[स्वाहा], @deva[स्वधा], @deva[अलं], @deva[वषट्]

The particles[^1] @deva[नमः], @deva[स्वस्ति], @deva[स्वाहा] and @deva[स्वधा] (exclamations used in offering oblations to gods and manes respectively), @deva[अलं] meaning 'equal to, a match for' and @deva[वषट्] (an exclamation accompanying an oblation to a deity) govern the Dative case; @deva[तस्मै नमः शंभवे] 'bow to that Śambhu;' @deva[प्रजाभ्यः स्वस्ति] 'may it be well with the subjects;' @deva[स्वस्त्यस्तु ते] (Rag. V. 17.) 'Farewell to thee;' @deva[अग्नये स्वाहा] 'this offering to Agni,' similarly @deva[पितृभ्यः स्वधा]; @deva[दैत्योभ्यो हरिः अलं] 'Hari is a match for the demons;' so @deva[अलं मल्लो मल्लाय] (Mah. Bhās.) 'one wrestler is a match for another; (see Rag. II 39. Bhatti. VIII. 98.); @deva[इन्द्राय वषट्] 'this oblation to Indra.'

(a) But when @deva[कृ] is used with @deva[नमः], it becomes the principal verb [^2] and therefore governs the Accusative case; @deva[नमस्करोति देवान्] 'bows down to gods' (when the sense of an infinitive is suppressed, of course the Dative will be used; see @ref[828]).

(b) Words having the sense of @deva[अलं], such as @deva[प्रभुः], @deva[समर्थः], @deva[शक्तः], &c. and also the verb @deva[प्रभू], are used with the Dative (Sid Kau.) @deva[दैत्योभ्यो हरिः प्रभुः समर्थः शक्तो वा]; @deva[प्रभुः—समर्थः—शक्तः मल्लो मल्लाय]; @deva[प्रभवति मल्लो मल्लाय]; @deva[विधिरपि न येभ्यः प्रभवति] (Bhar. II. 94.); @deva[प्रभु] and the other words may also be used with the Genitive (Sid. Kau.) @deva[प्रभवति निजस्य कन्यकाजनस्य महाराजः] (Māl. Mād. IV) the great king has power over his daughter.

(c) Verbs meaning 'to salute' such as @deva[प्रणम्], @deva[प्रणपत्], &c. may govern the Dative or the Accusative; @deva[न प्रणमन्ति देवताभ्यः] (Kād.) they do not bow down to deities; @deva[तां भक्तिप्रवणेन चेतसा प्रणनाम] saluted her with a mind bowed down with devotion; @deva[प्रणिपत्य सुरास्तस्मै शमयित्रे सुरद्विषां] (Rag. X. 15.) the gods bowed respectfully to him, the annihilator of the enemies of the immortals; @deva[वागीशं] (@deva[वाग्भिरर्थ्याभिः]) @deva[प्रणिपत्य] (Kum. II. 3.) having bowed to the lord of speech &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[नमः स्वस्तिस्वाहास्वधालंवषड्योगाच्च ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 16.
[^2]: @deva[उपपदविभक्तेः कारकविभक्तिर्बलीयसी ।] Vārt.

rules.title: Dative with Verbs of Telling and Sending
rules.body:
## Dative with Verbs of Telling and Sending

With verbs of telling such as @deva[कथ्], @deva[ख्या], @deva[शंस्], @deva[चक्ष्], @deva[निविद्] cau. &c. and of sending such as @deva[हि] with @deva[प्र], @deva[सृज्] with @deva[वि], &c. the Dative of the indirect object is used; @deva[रामभिष्वसनदर्शनोत्सुकं मैथिलाय कथयांबभूव सः ।] (Rag. XI. 37.); He told the king of Mithilā that Rāma was eager to see the bow; @deva[आख्याहि मे को भवानुग्ररूपः] (Bhag. XI. 31.) Tell me, who thou art in this fierce form, &c., @deva[उपस्थितां होमवेलां गुरवे निवेदयामि] (S'ak. IV.) I will tell my preceptor that it is time to offer the morning oblations, @deva[हरिरस्मै सुरांगनां प्रजिघाय] (Rag. VIII. 79.) Indra sent a heavenly damsel against him (i. e. to disturb his contemplations); @deva[रक्षस्तस्मै महोपलं प्रजिघाय] (Rag. XV. 21.)

rules.title: Dative/Accusative with मन् Showing Contempt (Non-Animals)
rules.body:
## Dative/Accusative with @deva[मन्] Showing Contempt (Non-Animals)

The indirect object of the root @deva[मन्] cl. 4. 'to think' if not an animal, may be put in the Accusative or the Dative case when contempt is to be shown;[^1] @deva[न त्वां तृणं मन्ये तृणाय वा] I do not consider thee a straw; but @deva[न त्वां तृणं मन्वे] (@deva[मन्] cl. 8) when mere comparison is meant, the Accusative is used; @deva[त्वां तृणं मन्ये] (Mb.)

---

[^1]: @deva[मन्यकर्मण्यनादरे विभाषाऽप्राणिषु ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 17. On @deva[अप्राणिषु] Kātyāyana remarks '@deva[अप्राणिषु इत्यपनीय नौकाकान्नशुकशृगालवर्ज्येष्विति वाच्यम्]' i. e. "Instead of 'If not an animal' it should be said, 'If not one of a ship, or food or a crow or a parrot or a jackal,'" @deva[न त्वां मन्ये नावं अन्नं वा]; @deva[न त्वां शुने श्वानं वा मन्ये]; in the former case though neither @deva[नौ] nor @deva[अन्न] is an animal, the Accusative ought to be used, in the latter though @deva[श्वन्] is an animal the Dative may be optionally used.

rules.title: Accusative/Dative with Motion Verbs (Actual Motion)
rules.body:
## Accusative/Dative with Motion Verbs (Actual Motion)

The object of roots implying motion (i. e. the place to which the motion is directed), if it be not a road, is put in the Accusative or the Dative, when actual motion is meant;[^1] @deva[ग्रामं ग्रामाय वा गच्छति] 'goes to a village;' but @deva[मनसा हरिं व्रजति], @deva[पन्थानं गच्छति].

## THE ABLATIVE CASE

---

[^1]: @deva[गत्यर्थकर्मणि द्वितीयाचतुर्थ्यौ चेष्टायामनध्वनि ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 12.

rules.title: Ablative Case: Motion Away From (अपादान)
rules.body:
## Ablative Case: Motion Away From (@deva[अपादान])

The principal sense of the Ablative case is @deva[अपादान] or 'motion away from[^1];' hence the noun from which the motion, real or conceived, takes place is put in the Ablative case; @deva[ग्रामादायाति] 'comes from a village;' @deva[धावतोऽश्वात्पतति] 'falls down from a running horse'; @deva[सदाचाराद् भ्रंशते].

(a) [^2] Words having the sense of @deva[जुगुप्सा], @deva[विराम] or 'cessation,' 'pause,' and @deva[प्रमाद] 'swerving from,' also govern the Ablative case; @deva[पापात् जुगुप्सते] 'he hates sin;' @deva[न नवः प्रभुराफलोदयात्स्थिरकर्मा विरराम कर्मणः] (Rag. VIII. 22) the new monarch, steady in action, did not desist from efforts until they bore their fruit'; @deva[धर्मात्प्रमाद्यति] 'swerves from duty'; @deva[स्वाधिकारात्प्रमत्तः] (Meg. I.) 'careless, failing in the discharge of the duties (of his office)'; so @deva[धर्मान्मुह्यति]; @deva[प्रसमीक्ष्य निवर्तेत सर्वमांसस्य भक्षणात्] (Manu Smr. V. 49.), &c.

@deva[मद्] with @deva[प्र] in the sense of 'to be careless about' is used with the Loc. also; @deva[अतोर्थान्न प्रमाद्यन्ति प्रमदासु विपश्चितः ।] (Manu Smr. II. 213) on this account wise men are not careless about their wives.

---

[^1]: @deva[अपादाने पञ्चमी ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 28. @deva[ध्रुवमपाये अपादानम्] Pāṇ. I. 4. 24.
[^2]: @deva[जुगुप्साविरामप्रमादार्थानामुपसंख्यानम् ।] Vārt.

rules.title: Ablative with Fear and Protection
rules.body:
## Ablative with Fear and Protection

In the case of words expressing fear or protection from fear,[^1] that from which or whom the fear proceeds is put in the Ablative case; @deva[चोराद्बिभेति] is afraid of a thief; @deva[भीतो रणे श्वेतवाहात्] I was afraid of the white-horsed one i. e. Arjuna; @deva[स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयाद्] (Bhag. II. 40) even a little of this (kind of) piety saves one from great fear; @deva[कपेरत्रासिषुर्नादात्] (Bhatt. IX. 11.) were afraid of the roar of the monkey.

(a) [^2] That from which one is kept off is also put in the Ablative; @deva[पापान्निवारयति] wards off from sin; @deva[यवेभ्यो गां वारयति] keeps off the cow from barley.

---

[^1]: @deva[भीत्रार्थानां भयहेतुः] Pāṇ. I. 4. 25.
[^2]: @deva[वारणार्थानामीप्सितः ।] Pāṇ. I. 4. 27.

rules.title: Ablative with परा+जि (Disgust)
rules.body:
## Ablative with @deva[परा]+@deva[जि] (Disgust)

In the case of @deva[जि] with @deva[परा][^1] the thing unbearable is put in the Ablative case; @deva[अध्ययनात्पराजयते] finds study unbearable or difficult; @deva[तां पराजयमानां स प्रीतेः] (Bhatti. VIII. 71.) who got disgusted with the love (of Rāvaṇa); but @deva[शत्रून् पराजयते ।]

---

[^1]: @deva[पराजेरसोढः ।] Pāṇ. I. 4. 26.

rules.title: Ablative with Concealment
rules.body:
## Ablative with Concealment

When concealment is to be had recourse to,[^1] that whose sight one desires to avoid is put in the Ablative case; @deva[मातुर्निलीयते कृष्णः] 'Krishna conceals himself from his mother; but @deva[चोरान्न दिदृक्षते].

---

[^1]: @deva[अन्तर्धौ येनादर्शनमिच्छति ।] Pāṇ. I. 4. 28.

rules.title: Ablative with Learning and Origin
rules.body:
## Ablative with Learning and Origin

(a) [^1] The teacher from whom something is learnt regularly is put in the Ablative case; @deva[उपाध्यायादधीते] learns from the preceptor; but @deva[नटस्य गाथां शृणोति].

(b) Similarly the prime or original cause in the case of @deva[जन्] to be born, and the source in the case of @deva[भू] are put in the Ablative; @deva[ब्रह्मणः प्रजाः प्रजायन्ते] the creation proceeds from Brahman; @deva[गोमयाद्वृश्चिको जायते] the scorpion is born from cowdung; @deva[हिमवतो गङ्गा प्रभवति] The Ganges rises from the Himalayas; @deva[कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते] from desire anger is produced.

*Note*:—Verbs meaning 'to be born' or 'to be begotten upon' are often used with the Loc.; @deva[तस्यां शतानन्द आङ्गिरसोऽजायत] from her was born Satananda Angirasa; @deva[मेनकायामुत्पन्नां] begotten upon Menakā; See Manu Smr. 154. I. 9.

---

[^1]: @deva[आख्यातोपयोगे ।] Pāṇ. I. 4. 29. @deva[जनिकर्तुः प्रकृतिः । भुवः प्रभवः ।] Pāṇ. I. 4. 30. 31.

rules.title: Ablative when the Sense of an Indeclinable Participle is Suppressed
rules.body:
## Ablative when the Sense of an Indeclinable Participle is Suppressed

When the sense of an indeclinable participle is suppressed in a sentence[^1] the object governed by that ptc. or the place at or on which the action takes place is put in the Ablative case; @deva[प्रासादात् प्रेक्षते] sees from a palace (@deva[प्रासादमारुह्य प्रेक्षते] Sid. Kau.); similarly @deva[आसनात् प्रेक्षते]=@deva[आसने उपविश्य प्रेक्षते]; @deva[श्वशुराज्जिह्रेति]=@deva[श्वशुरं वीक्ष्य जिह्रेति], Sid. Kau

---

[^1]: @deva[ल्यब्लोपे कर्मण्यधिकरणे च ।] Vārt.

rules.title: Ablative for Distance in Time and Space
rules.body:
## Ablative for Distance in Time and Space

(a) [^1] The place or time from which the distance of another place or point of time is to be expressed is put in the Ablative case; the distance in space being put in the Nominative or the Locative and that in time in the Locative; @deva[वनाद् ग्रामो योजनं योजने वा] (Sid. Kau.) the village is a *yojana* from the forest, @deva[गविधुमतः सांकाश्यं चत्वारि योजनानि चतुर्षु योजनेषु वा] (Mb); @deva[कार्तिक्या आग्रहायणी मासे] (Sid Kau.) the full moonday of Mārgaśīrsha is a month (at the interval of a month) from that of Kārtika; @deva[समुद्रात्परी क्रोशौ].

(b) The Ablative is also used in questions and answers; @deva[कस्मात् त्वं । नद्याः] whence art thou? from the river; @deva[कुतो भवान् । पाटलिपुत्रात्] where do you come from? Pāṭaliputra.

---

[^1]: @deva[यतश्चाध्वकालनिर्माणं तत्र पञ्चमी । तद्युक्ताद्ध्वनः प्रथमासप्तम्यौ । कालात्सप्तमी च वक्तव्या । प्रश्नाख्यानयोश्च ।] Vārtikas.

rules.title: Ablative with अन्य, इतर and Direction Words
rules.body:
## Ablative with @deva[अन्य], @deva[इतर] and Direction Words

The words @deva[अन्य], @deva[इतर] and others having a similar sense, the particles @deva[आरात्] 'near or distant,' @deva[ऋते] 'without,' words expressive of direction used with reference to time or space (except when they refer to the limbs of the body) and those derived from the root @deva[अञ्च्] at the end of compounds, and indeclinables ending in @deva[ओ] and @deva[आहि] are constructed with the Ablative;[^1] @deva[अन्यो भिन्न इतरो वा कृष्णात्] different from Krishna; @deva[इतरो रावणादेष राघवानुचरो यदि] Bhatti. VII. 106. If he be one other than Rāvaṇa and a follower of Rāma; @deva[आराद्वनात्] near or away from the forest; @deva[ऋते क्रौर्यात्समायातः] (Bhatti VII. 105) come without (setting aside) his cruelty; @deva[ग्रामात्पूर्वा उत्तरो वा] to the east or the north of the village; @deva[चैत्रात्पूर्वः फाल्गुनः] the month of Fālguna is prior to that of Chaitra; but @deva[पूर्वं कायस्य] the (forepart) of the body; @deva[प्राक् प्रत्यग् वा ग्रामात्] to the east or to the west of the village; @deva[प्राक्प्रभातात्] (Bhatti. VII. 106) before the day dawned; @deva[दक्षिणा दक्षिणाहि वा ग्रामम्] to the south or in the southern direction of the village; @deva[उत्तरा समुद्रात्] (Bhatti) in the north of the sea.

*Obs*:—@deva[ऋते] is sometimes used with the Accusative, @deva[ऋतेपि त्वां न भविष्यन्ति सर्वे] (Bhag. XI. 32) even without thee all will die.

(a) Words like @deva[प्रभृति], @deva[आरभ्य], @deva[बहिः], @deva[अनन्तरं], @deva[ऊर्ध्वं], @deva[परं] &c. are used with the Ablative; the first word may also be used with adverbs of time; @deva[तस्माद्दिनात्प्रभृति] from that day; @deva[ततः-तदा-प्रभृति] since then; @deva[अद्यप्रभृत्यवनताङ्गि तवास्मि दासः] (Kum. V. 86), @deva[ततः], @deva[तस्माद्दिनादारभ्य], @deva[मालत्याः प्रथमावलोकदिवसादारभ्य]; @deva[ग्रामाद्बहिः] outside the village; @deva[पुरगारुत्मतगोपुराद्बहिः] (@deva[निरगात्]) went out of the emerald gate of the town; @deva[ऊर्ध्वं संवत्सरात्] (M. S. IX. 77) after a year; @deva[अत ऊर्ध्वं] hence forward; @deva[वर्त्मनः परं] (Rag. I. 17) beyond the path; @deva[भाग्यायत्तमतः परं]; @deva[पुराणपत्रापगमादनन्तरं] (Rag. III. 70.) after the dropping of old leaves; see Bhag. XII 12.

---

[^1]: @deva[अन्यारादितरर्तेदिक्शब्दाञ्चूत्तरपदाजाहियुक्ते ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 29.

rules.title: Ablative with अप, परि, आ, प्रति
rules.body:
## Ablative with @deva[अप], @deva[परि], @deva[आ], @deva[प्रति]

The ablative is used with—[^1]

(a) The prepositions @deva[अप] and @deva[परि] meaning 'away from, without' and @deva[आ] meaning 'as far as' or 'including, comprehending'; @deva[यत्संप्रत्यप लोकेभ्यो लंकायां वसतिर्भयात्] (Rām.) now that he dwelt in Lankā, in terror, away from the worlds; @deva[अप हरेः संसारः] *Samsāra* exists outside Hari; @deva[अप त्रिगर्तेभ्यो वृष्टो देवः] it rained everywhere, except in the country of Trigarta. Similarly @deva[परि हरेः संसारः परि त्रिगर्तेभ्यो वृष्टो देवः] (Vop.) &c. @deva[आमुक्ते संसार], @deva[आसकलाद् ब्रह्म] Brahman pervades every thing; @deva[आ परितोषाद् विदुषां] until the learned are satisfied.

(b) @deva[प्रति] meaning 'the representative of, in exchange for or giving in return for;' @deva[प्रद्युम्नः कृष्णात्प्रति] (Sid. Kau.) Pradyumna is the representative of Krishna, @deva[तिलेभ्यः प्रतियच्छति माषान्] gives māshas in return for sesamum.

---

[^1]: @deva[अपपरी वर्जने । आङ्मर्यादावचने ।] Pāṇ. I. 4. 88–89. @deva[पञ्चम्यपाङ्परिभिः] Pāṇ. II. 3. 10 @deva[प्रतिः प्रतिनिधिप्रतिदानयोः ।] Pāṇ I 4. 92. @deva[प्रतिनिधिप्रतिदाने च यस्मात् ।] Pāṇ. II 3. 11.

rules.title: Ablative with Debt as Cause
rules.body:
## Ablative with Debt as Cause

When a word expressive of 'a debt,' is merely intended to be stated as a cause,[^1] it is put in the Ablative case; @deva[शताद्बद्धं द्रव्यं] a thing mortgaged for a hundred rupees, @deva[ऋणाद्बद्ध इव] tied down as it were by the debt he owes.

---

[^1]: @deva[अकर्तर्यृणे पञ्चमी ।] Pāṇ. II. 4. 25.

rules.title: Ablative for Cause, Argument, Comparison
rules.body:
## Ablative for Cause, Argument, Comparison

(a) The Ablative often denotes the cause of an action or condition and may be translated by 'on account of, by reason of,' &c; @deva[मौनान्मूर्खः गण्यते] one is considered a fool by reason of his silence (if he keeps silence); @deva[गोमानुषाणां वधात्] (H.) on account of my killing cows and men.

(b) The Ablative is used to make a causative assertion or to advance an argument; @deva[पर्वतो वह्निमान् धूमात् ।] The mountain is fiery (has fire on it). because there is smoke; @deva[स्मृत्यनवकाशदोषप्रसङ्ग इति चेन्नान्यस्मृत्यनवकाशदोषप्रसंगात्] (Ved. Su. II 1. 1) A disputant says—if you say that our argument is liable to the fault of giving no scope to your smritis then we reply: this your argument will not hold; for in that case other smritis will have no scope given to them.

(c) The Ablative is used with comparatives or words having a comparative sense; @deva[भक्तिमार्गात् ज्ञानमार्गः श्रेयान्] the way of knowledge is more efficient than that of devotion; @deva[अणोरप्यणीयान्] smaller than an atom; @deva[अश्वमेधसहस्रेभ्यः सत्यमेवातिरिच्यते] truth alone is superior to a thousand horse-sacrifices; @deva[चैत्ररथादनूने] not inferior to Chaitraratha.

rules.title: पृथक्, विना, नाना with Ablative/Accusative/Instrumental
rules.body:
## @deva[पृथक्], @deva[विना], @deva[नाना] with Ablative/Accusative/Instrumental

[^1] The indeclinables @deva[पृथक्], @deva[विना] and @deva[नाना] govern the Ablative, the Accusative and the Instrumental cases; @deva[पृथक् रामात्-रामं-रामेण वा] different from or without Rāma; so @deva[नाना रामं] &c. @deva[नाना नारीं निष्फला लोकयात्रा] (Vop.) worldly life is vain without a woman (wife).

---

[^1]: @deva[पृथग्विनानानाभिस्तृतीयान्यतरस्याम् ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 32.

rules.title: Ablative/Instrumental with स्तोक, अल्प, कृच्छ्र, कतिपय
rules.body:
## Ablative/Instrumental with @deva[स्तोक], @deva[अल्प], @deva[कृच्छ्र], @deva[कतिपय]

[^1] The words @deva[स्तोक] 'a little,' @deva[अल्प] 'a little,' @deva[कृच्छ्र] 'difficulty,' and @deva[कतिपय] 'some' when used in an adverbial sense with verbs, are used in the Ablative or the Instrumental; @deva[स्तोकेन स्तोकाद्वा मुक्तः] let off with little; similarly @deva[अल्पेन अल्पान्मुक्तः], @deva[कृच्छ्रेण कृच्छ्राद्वा कृतः] done with difficulty; @deva[कतिपयेन कतिपयाद्वा प्राप्तः], but @deva[स्तोकेन विषेण हतः] killed with a little poison; when used adverbially they take the Accusative also; @deva[स्तोकं गच्छति] goes a little.

(a) @deva[दूर] and @deva[अन्तिक] and others having the same sense, are used in the Ablative, the Accusative and the Instrumental cases; @deva[ग्रामस्य दूरात् दूरं दूरेण वा] away from the village; so @deva[अन्तिकात् अन्तिकं अन्तिकेन वा] near the village.

## THE GENITIVE CASE

---

[^1]: @deva[करणे च स्तोकाल्पकृच्छ्रकतिपयस्यासत्त्ववचनस्य । दूरान्तिकार्थेभ्यो द्वितीया च ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 33. 35.

rules.title: Genitive Case: Introduction and Relation (सम्बन्ध)
rules.body:
## Genitive Case: Introduction and Relation (@deva[सम्बन्ध])

[^1] The Genitive, as already remarked, is not a Kāraka case. It, therefore, expresses simply the relation of one noun to another in a sentence, such as that of a servant and his master (a relation which is other than that expressed by a Kāraka case); @deva[राज्ञः पुरुषः], @deva[पुत्रस्य माता], @deva[द्रव्यस्य गुणः] &c; and even in those cases where the genitive is used in the sense of other cases it expresses simple relation or @deva[सम्बन्ध] only, as in @deva[सतां गतम्]; @deva[सर्पिषो जानीते]; @deva[मातुः स्मरति]; @deva[एध उदकस्य उपस्कुरुते]; @deva[भजे शंभोश्चरणयोः]; @deva[फलानां तृप्तः], &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[षष्ठी शेषे] Pāṇ. II 3. 50 @deva[कारकप्रातिपदिकार्थ] (the sense of the Nominative)@deva[-व्यतिरिक्तः स्वस्वामिभावादिसम्बन्धः शेषः तत्र षष्ठी स्यात् । कर्मादीनामपि सम्बन्धविवक्षाया षष्ठ्येव ।] Sid. Kau.

rules.title: Genitive with हेतु (Purpose, Cause)
rules.body:
## Genitive with @deva[हेतु] (Purpose, Cause)

[^1] When the word @deva[हेतु] (cause, object) is used in a sentence, that which is the object and the word @deva[हेतु] are put in the Genitive case; @deva[अन्नस्य हेतोर्वसति] dwells for the sake of (with the object of getting) food; @deva[रोदिषि कस्य हेतोः] Mark P. 23. 12. @deva[हेतोर्बोधस्य मैथिल्याः प्रास्तावीद्रामसंकथाम्] (Bhatti. VIII. 103.) he began to give her an account of Rāma in order to show her that he (Hanumat) was Rāma's messenger.

(a) [^2] When a pronoun is used with the word @deva[हेतु], the Instrumental and the Genitive may both be used; @deva[कस्य हेतोः], @deva[केन हेतुना], with what object? Why? The Ablative may also be used; @deva[तेन हेतुना], @deva[तस्माद्धेतोः], @deva[तस्य हेतो] ; when a word having the same sense as @deva[हेतु], such as @deva[निमित्त], @deva[कारण], &c, is used with a pronoun it may be used in any case in agreement with the pronoun; @deva[कस्य निमित्तस्य], @deva[कस्य प्रयोजनस्य]; @deva[केन निमित्तेन], @deva[कस्मै निमित्ताय] &c.; but they are generally used in the Accusative used like an adverb; @deva[किं-निमित्तं-कारणं-प्रयोजनं-अर्थं], &c. when a pronoun is not used, any case except the Nominative and the Accusative may be used; @deva[ज्ञानेन निमित्तेन] (@deva[हरिः सेव्यः]), @deva[ज्ञानाय निमित्ताय] with the object of acquiring knowledge.

---

[^1]: @deva[षष्ठी हेतुप्रयोगे ।] Pāṇ II. 3. 27.
[^2]: @deva[सर्वनाम्नस्तृतीया च । निमित्तपर्यायप्रयोगे सर्वासां प्रायदर्शनम् ।] Vārt.

rules.title: Genitive with Words Ending in -तस् and Direction Words
rules.body:
## Genitive with Words Ending in @deva[-तस्] and Direction Words

[^1] Words ending in the termination @deva[तस्] and showing direction and others having the same sense, such as @deva[उपरि], @deva[उपरिष्टात्], @deva[अधः], @deva[अधस्तात्], @deva[पुरः], @deva[पुरस्तात्], @deva[पश्चात्], @deva[अग्रे], &c. are used with the Genitive; @deva[ग्रामस्य दक्षिणतः उत्तरतः] &c. to the south or to the north of the village, &c; @deva[अर्कस्योपरि] (S'ak. II 8.) on the Arka plant; @deva[तरूणामधः] (S'ak. I.) under the trees; @deva[तस्य स्थित्वा कथमपि पुरः] (Meg.) standing before him with great difficulty, &c.

(a) [^2] Words ending in @deva[एन] such as @deva[दक्षिणेन], @deva[उत्तरेण], &c. are used with the Genitive or the Accusative; @deva[दक्षिणेन ग्रामं ग्रामस्य वा] to the south of the village; @deva[उत्तरेण स्रवन्तीं] (Māl. Mād IX. 24.) to the north of the river; @deva[दण्डकान्दक्षिणेनाहं] (Bhatti. VIII.108.); @deva[धनपतिगृहानुत्तरेण] (Meg. 80) to the north of Kubera's palace.

---

[^1]: @deva[षष्ठ्यतसर्थप्रत्ययेन] Pāṇ. II. 3. 30.
[^2]: @deva[एनपा द्वितीया । ] Pāṇ. II. 3. 31. @deva[एनपेति योगविभागात्षष्ठ्यपि ।] Sid. Kau.

rules.title: Genitive/Ablative with दूर, अन्तिक and Synonyms
rules.body:
## Genitive/Ablative with @deva[दूर], @deva[अन्तिक] and Synonyms

[^1] The words @deva[दूर] and @deva[अन्तिक] and their synonyms govern either the Genitive or the Ablative; @deva[ग्रामात् ग्रामस्य वा वनं दूरं—निकटं—समीपं वा] the forest is distant from or near the village. @deva[रामाद्रुद्रस्य यो दूरं पापाद्दुःखस्य सोन्तिकं] he who is away from Rāma or Śiva is near sin. @deva[प्रत्यासन्नो माधवीमण्डपस्य] close to the bower of the Mādhavī creeper; @deva[तस्य सकाशं], &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[दूरान्तिकार्थैः षष्ठ्यन्यतरस्याम् ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 34.

rules.title: Genitive with Verbs of Incorrect Knowledge, Memory, Control, Compassion
rules.body:
## Genitive with Verbs of Incorrect Knowledge, Memory, Control, Compassion

The root @deva[ज्ञा][^1] meaning 'to have an incorrect knowledge of' governs the Genitive; @deva[तैलं सर्पिषो जानीते] supposes oil to be ghee; but @deva[सर्पिर्जानीते].

(a) Verbs implying 'to think of, to remember,' such as @deva[स्मृ], @deva[इ] with @deva[अधि], 'to be master of,' such as @deva[ईश्], @deva[भू] with @deva[प्र], &c. and to have compassion on such as @deva[दय्] &c., govern the genitive of their object; @deva[कच्चिद्भर्तुः स्मरसि] (Meg. 90) dost thou remember the lord? @deva[स्मरन् राघवबाणानां विव्यथे राक्षसेश्वरः] Rām. VI. 60. 3. @deva[अध्येति तव लक्ष्मणः] (Bhatti VIII. 119.) Lakshmana remembers thee; @deva[प्रभवति निजस्य कन्यकाजनस्य महाराजः] (Māl. Mād. 4.) the great king has mastery over his daughter; @deva[यदि तं प्रेक्षमाणा आत्मनः प्रभविष्यामि] (Uttar.) if after I see him I shall have control over myself; @deva[गात्राणामनीशोऽस्मि संवृत्तः] (S'ak. II.) I have lost all power over my limbs; @deva[कथंचिदीशा मनसां बभूवुः] (Kum. III. 34.) with great difficulty they could control their minds; @deva[शौवस्तिकत्वं विभवा न येषां व्रजन्ति तेषां दयसे न कस्मात्] (Bhatt. II. 33.) why dost thou feel no compassion for those whose wealth does not see the morrow? @deva[रामस्य दयमानः] (Ibid. VIII 119) taking pity on Rāma.

(b) @deva[कृ] meaning 'to impart additional properties' governs the Genitive; @deva[एधोदकस्य उपस्कुरुते] 'fuel imparts heat to water.' @deva[मा कस्यचिदुपस्कृथाः] Bhatti. VIII. 119.

---

[^1]: @deva[ज्ञोऽविदर्थस्य करणे । अधिगर्थदयेशां कर्मणि । कृञः प्रतियत्ने ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 51–53.

rules.title: Genitive with Verbs of Affliction (Disease)
rules.body:
## Genitive with Verbs of Affliction (Disease)

[^1] Verbs meaning 'to be afflicted with a disease' govern the Genitive of their object when used impersonally or when they have for their subject names of diseases; @deva[चौरस्य ज्वरस्य रुजा] the thief is afflicted with the pain of fever; @deva[पुरुषस्य रुजयत्यतिसारः] dysentery inflicts pain on the man; except when @deva[ज्वर] and @deva[संताप] are used as subjects; (vide Bhatti. VIII. 120;) @deva[तं रुजयति ज्वरः] or @deva[संतापः] fever or affliction pains him.

---

[^1]: @deva[रुजार्थानां भाववचनानामज्वरेः ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 54. @deva[अज्वरिसंताप्योरिति वाच्यम्] ; Vārt.

rules.title: Genitive with नाथ् (to wish) in Benedictions
rules.body:
## Genitive with @deva[नाथ्] (to wish) in Benedictions

[^1] @deva[नाथ्] meaning 'to wish' governs the Genitive when the idea of a benediction is implied; @deva[धृत्या नाथस्व] wish to have patience; @deva[धनस्य नाथते] desires to have wealth. So @deva[सर्पिषः नाथनम्].

---

[^1]: @deva[आशिषि नाथः] Pāṇ. II. 3. 55.

rules.title: Genitive with Verbs Meaning 'to Injure, Punish'
rules.body:
## Genitive with Verbs Meaning 'to Injure, Punish'

[^1] The roots @deva[जस्], @deva[हन्] with @deva[नि] or @deva[प्र] or with both, @deva[नट्], @deva[क्राथ्] and @deva[पिष्] govern the Genitive when meaning to injure, to punish, &c; @deva[चौरस्योज्जासयति राजा] a king punishes a thief; @deva[निजौजसोज्जासयितुं जगद्रुहां] (Sis. I. 37.) to kill the enemies of the world (the demons) by his own power; @deva[मन्योरुज्जासयात्मनः] kill (drive away) your anger; @deva[राक्षसानां निहनिष्यति] or @deva[प्रहणिष्यति] or @deva[निप्रहणिष्यति] or @deva[प्रणिहनिष्यति रामः] Rāma will kill the Rākshasas; @deva[वृषलस्य—उन्नाटयति—क्राथयति] does injury to a Vrishala; @deva[साहसिकस्य पिनष्टि गजः] &c; in other senses they govern the Accusative; @deva[धानाः पिनष्टि] he grinds fried rice.

---

[^1]: @deva[जासिनिप्रहणनाटक्राथपिषां हिंसायाम् ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 56.

rules.title: Genitive with Verbs of Business/Gambling
rules.body:
## Genitive with Verbs of Business/Gambling

[^1] The roots @deva[व्यवह्] (i. e. @deva[ह्] with @deva[वि] and @deva[अव]), @deva[पण्] and @deva[दिव्] when they all mean to transact business, or to stake in gambling, govern the Genitive of their object; @deva[शतस्य व्यवहरति] invests a hundred rupees in business; @deva[प्राणानामपणिष्टासौ] he staked his life; @deva[अदेवीद् बन्धुभोगानां] lost his brothers and pleasures in gambling, &c; but when @deva[दिव्] is preceded by a preposition, the Accusative may also be used; @deva[शतस्य शतं वा प्रतिदीव्यति] (Sid. Kau.)

---

[^1]: @deva[व्यवहृपणोः समर्थयोः । दिवस्तदर्थस्य । विभाषोपसर्गे ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 57–59.

rules.title: Genitive with Words Denoting Frequency of Time
rules.body:
## Genitive with Words Denoting Frequency of Time

[^1] Words having the senses of @deva[कृत्वः] i. e denoting frequency of time, such as @deva[द्विः], @deva[त्रिः], @deva[पञ्चकृत्वः] &c. govern the Genitive of the time in the sense of the Locative; @deva[पञ्चकृत्वोह्नो भोजनम्] taking food five times a day; @deva[द्विरह्नो भुङ्क्ते], &c.

---

[^1]: @deva[कृत्वोर्थप्रयोगे कालेऽधिकरणे ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 64.

rules.title: Genitive Subjective and Objective with Kṛidantas
rules.body:
## Genitive Subjective and Objective with Kṛidantas

[^1] The Genitive is used subjectively and objectively with Kridantas or Primary Nominal Bases derived by means of the Krit affixes (i. e. is used in the sense of the subject or the object of the action denoted by the Kridantas); @deva[कृष्णस्य कृतिः] an act of Krishna i. e. of which Krishna is the agent; @deva[जगतः कर्ता] the Creator of the world, which is the object of the action denoted by the noun @deva[कर्तृ]; similarly @deva[सतां पालकः] the protector of the good; @deva[पयसः पानं] the drinking of milk; @deva[तस्य कवेः क्रिया] a work of that poet; @deva[साधारणी सृष्टिरियं न धातुः] (Rāmacharita XII. 117.). This is not a common creation of Brahman.

(a) [^2] In the case of verbs governing two Accusatives the secondary object of the Kridanta may be put in the Genitive or in the Accusative; @deva[नेताश्वस्य स्रुघ्नं स्रुघ्नस्य वा] (Sid. Kau.) the taker of the horse to Srughna.

(b) [^3] When the agent and the object of the bases derived by means of Krit affixes are used in a sentence, the object is put in the Genitive case and not the agent, @deva[आश्चर्यो गवां दोहोऽगोपेन] the milking of cows by one who is not a cowherd is a wonder.

Exceptions.—This rule does not apply to Krit nouns ending in the affixes @deva[अक] and @deva[अ] when *feminine*; @deva[विभित्सा भेदिका वा रुद्रस्य जगतः] (Sid. Kau.) the desire of Rudra to split the universe or the splitting of the universe by Rudra. According to some when the Krit affixes are of *feminine* gender, and according to others when they are of any gender, and the agent and the object are both used, the agent is put in the Instrumental or Genitive case; @deva[विचित्रा जगतः कृतिः हरेर्हरिणा वा] wonderful is the creation of the world by Hari; @deva[शब्दानामनुशासनमाचार्येणाचार्यस्य वा] (Sid. Kau.); @deva[शोभना खलु पाणिनेः] (@deva[पाणिनिना वा]) @deva[सूत्रस्य कृतिः ।] (Mb.).

---

[^1]: @deva[कर्तृकर्मणोः कृति ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 65.
[^2]: @deva[गुणकर्मणि वेष्यते ।] Vārt.
[^3]: @deva[उभयप्राप्तौ कर्मणि ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 66. @deva[स्त्रीप्रत्यययोरकाकारयोर्नायं नियमः । शेषे विभाषा ।] Vārt. @deva[स्त्रीप्रत्यय इत्येके । केचिदविशेषेण विभाषामिच्छन्ति ॥] Sid. Kau.

rules.title: Genitive with Past Passive Participles in Present Sense
rules.body:
## Genitive with Past Passive Participles in Present Sense

[^1] When past passive participles are used in the sense of the present tense the Genitive is used; @deva[राज्ञां मतो बुद्धः पूजितो वा] respected, known or honoured by kings; @deva[यो धर्मः स सतां मतः रामस्य संमतं] Bhatti. VIII. 124.

(a) Past participles showing the place of an action, as well as those used as abstract nouns are used with the Genitive; @deva[मुकुन्दस्यासितमिदमिदं यातं रमापतेः । भुक्तमेतदनंतस्येत्यूचुर्गोप्यो दिदृक्षवः ॥] @deva[मयूरस्य नृत्तं, कोकिलस्य व्याहृतं, नटस्य भुक्तं, छात्रस्य हसितं], &c. (Mb.) See Bhatt. VIII. 125.

---

[^1]: @deva[क्तस्य च वर्तमाने । अधिकरणवाचिनश्च ।] Pāṇ II. 67–68.

rules.title: Exceptions: When Genitive is NOT Used
rules.body:
## Exceptions: When Genitive is NOT Used

[^1] The Genitive is not used with present participles except that of @deva[द्विष्], verbal derivatives ending in @deva[उ] and @deva[उक] except that derived from @deva[कम्], verbal indeclinables, past participles, passive and active, nouns formed with the affix @deva[खल्] (see p. 456) and with such as mean 'in the habit of, or having the properties of or doing any thing well'; @deva[कर्म कुर्वन्] or @deva[कुर्वाणः]; but @deva[मुरं मुरस्य वा द्विषन् हरिः] Hari, the enemy of Mura; @deva[हरिं दिदृक्षुः] desirous of seeing Hari; @deva[हरिं अलङ्करिष्णुः], @deva[दैत्यान् घातुको हरिः] Hari is the killer of demons; @deva[लक्ष्म्याः कामुकः], @deva[जगत्स्रष्टा], @deva[सुखं कर्तुं] &c. @deva[विष्णुना हता दैत्याः], @deva[दैत्यान् हतवान्]; @deva[ईषत्करः प्रपञ्चो हरिणा] worldly life goes easy with Hari; @deva[आत्मानं अलङ्करिष्णुः] in habit of decorating oneself; @deva[अन्नं भिक्षुः] a habitual beggar; @deva[कर्ता कटं] one who prepares a mat; [^2] also in the case of nouns derived by means of the terminations @deva[अक] showing futurity and @deva[इन्] showing necessary payment; @deva[हरिं दर्शको याति] he goes desiring to see Hari; @deva[शतं दायी] one who has to pay a hundred (rupees.).

---

[^1]: @deva[न लोकाव्ययनिष्ठाखलर्थतृनाम् ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 69. @deva[कमेरनिषेधः] Vārt.
[^2]: @deva[अकेनोर्भविष्यदाधमर्ण्ययोः ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 70.

rules.title: Genitive/Instrumental with Potential Passive Participles
rules.body:
## Genitive/Instrumental with Potential Passive Participles

[^1] In the case of Potential passive participles the agent of the action is put in the Genitive or in the Instrumental case; @deva[मया मम वा सेव्यो हरिः] Hari ought to be served by me; @deva[राक्षसेन्द्रस्य संरक्ष्यं मया लव्यमिदं वनं] (Bhatti. VIII. 129.) this forest which the lord of the demons ought to preserve must be destroyed by me; @deva[गन्तव्या ते वसतिरलका] &c. (Meg.) Thou should go to Alakā.

---

[^1]: @deva[कृत्यानां कर्तरि वा ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 71.

rules.title: Genitive with Words of Equality/Likeness
rules.body:
## Genitive with Words of Equality/Likeness

[^1] In the case of words denoting equality or likeness, such as @deva[तुल्य], @deva[सदृश], &c., the person or thing with whom or which any object is compared is put in the Genitive case, except in the case of @deva[तुला] and @deva[उपमा]; @deva[तुल्यः सदृशः समो वा कृष्णस्य कृष्णेन वा] equal to or like Krishna; @deva[कोन्योस्ति सदृशो मम] who else is equal to me? but @deva[कृष्णस्य तुला उपमा वा नास्ति] (Sid. Kau.)

*Obs.*—The words @deva[तुला] and @deva[उपमा], however, are found used by good authors with the Instrumental against Pāṇini's rule; @deva[तुलां यदारोहति दन्तवाससा] (Kum. V. 34.) which rises to the high position of being compared with your lip; @deva[स्फुटोपमं भूतिसितेन शंभुना] (Sis. I. 4.) clearly deserving to be compared with Śambhu white with ashes; see Rag. VIII. 15.

---

[^1]: @deva[तुल्यार्थैरतुलोपमाभ्यां तृतीयान्यतरस्याम् ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 72.

rules.title: Genitive/Dative with Benediction Words
rules.body:
## Genitive/Dative with Benediction Words

[^1] The words @deva[आयुष्यं], @deva[मद्रं], @deva[भद्रं], @deva[कुशलं], @deva[सुखं], @deva[अर्थः] and @deva[हितं] and words having the same sense, when used in a sentence containing a benediction, govern the Dative or the Genitive case; @deva[आयुष्यं चिरंजीवितं कृष्णाय कृष्णस्य वा भूयात्] (Sid. Kau.); may Krishna live long; similarly @deva[मद्रं], @deva[भद्रं], @deva[कुशलं], @deva[निरामयं], @deva[सुखं], @deva[शं], @deva[अर्थः], @deva[प्रयोजनं], @deva[हितं], @deva[पथ्यं वा भूयात्] (Sid. Kau.).

---

[^1]: @deva[चतुर्थी चाशिष्यायुष्यमद्रभद्रकुशलसुखार्थहितैः ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 73.

rules.title: Genitive with Certain Indeclinables
rules.body:
## Genitive with Certain Indeclinables

The Genitive is used with indeclinables like @deva[मध्ये], @deva[पारे], @deva[कृते], &c.; @deva[गङ्गाया मध्ये परे वा] in the middle or on the other side of the Ganges; @deva[अमीषां प्राणानां कृते] for the sake of this life.

rules.title: Genitive with Superlatives; Ablative with Comparatives
rules.body:
## Genitive with Superlatives; Ablative with Comparatives

With superlatives, and words having the sense of the superlative, the Genitive is used; @deva[नृणां ब्राह्मणः श्रेष्ठः]; @deva[अग्रणीर्मन्त्रकृतामृषीणाम्] (Rag. V. 4.) the chief of sages, the authors to the *Mantras*.

*Note*:—Words having the sense of comparatives are used with the Ablative and sometimes with the Instrumental; @deva[अयमस्माद् बलेन हीनः] or @deva[अधिकः] this person is superior or inferior to him in strength; similarly @deva[देवदत्तो यज्ञदत्तात्पटुः मूर्खो वा]; @deva[को नु स्वन्ततरो मया] who will have a happier end than I? The word @deva[अधिक] is used with the Genitive, the Locative or the Instrumental; @deva[सुतैर्हि तासामधिकोपि सोऽभवत्] he was more (i. e. dearer) to them than their sons; @deva[तेषामप्यधिका मासाः पञ्च च द्वादश क्षपाः] they passed five months and twelve nights more than (those years); @deva[कुडवेऽधिकः प्रस्थः] *A Prastha is larger than a Kudava*.

## THE LOCATIVE CASE

rules.title: Locative Case: Adhikaraṇa (Place and Time)
rules.body:
## Locative Case: Adhikaraṇa (Place and Time)

The place where an action takes place with reference to the subject or object is called Adhikarana (@deva[अधिकरण]) and is put in the Locative case;[^1] @deva[स्वपिति गिरिगर्भे] (Bham. 1. 50); @deva[वासो नन्दनकानने] (*Ibid* 64); @deva[स्थाल्यां ओदनं पचति] cooks food in a cooking utensil; @deva[कर्णे कथयति] tells (something) into the ear; @deva[मोक्षे इच्छा अस्ति], &c. The Locative also denotes the time when an action takes place; @deva[तस्मिन् विप्रकृताः काले दिवौकसः] (Kum. II. 1.) the gods being harassed at that time; @deva[दिनान्ते निलयाय गन्तुं] (Rag. II. 15.)

(a) [^2] Verbal derivatives in @deva[इन्] and having the sense of the p. p. participle govern the Locative of their object; @deva[अधीती व्याकरणे] one by whom grammar is studied; @deva[गृहीती षट्स्वङ्गेषु] by whom the six *Angas* were mastered, &c.

The words @deva[साधु] and @deva[असाधु] govern the Locative of that with reference to which they are used; @deva[साधुः कृष्णो मातरि] well behaved towards his mother; @deva[असाधुर्मातुले] ill-behaved towards his maternal uncle.

(b) [^3] The object or purpose for which any thing is done is put in the Locative case when the thing desired is intimately connected with that on which the action takes place; @deva[चर्मणि द्वीपिनं हन्ति दन्तयोर्हन्ति कुञ्जरम् । केशेषु चमरीं हन्ति सीम्नि पुष्कलको हतः ॥] (Mb). (Man) kills the tiger for his skin, the elephant for his tusks, the *Chamary* deer for her hair and the musk-deer for his musk. If there is no intimate union the Dative is used.

*Obs.*—Sometimes the Instrumental is used to denote the object for which any thing is done; @deva[वेतनेन] (for wages) @deva[धान्यं लुनाति]. Sometimes the Loc. is used to denote the object in general; @deva[यथा सृष्टोसि धात्रा कर्मसु तत्कुरु] since you are created by the creator to do duty, fulfil it.

---

[^1]: @deva[आधारोधिकरणम् । सप्तम्यधिकरणे च ।] Pāṇ. I. 4. 45; II. 3. 36.
[^2]: @deva[क्तस्येन्विषयस्य कर्मण्युपसंख्यानम् । साध्वसाधुप्रयोगे च ।] Vārtikas.
[^3]: @deva[निमित्तात्कर्मयोगे ।] Vārt. @deva[निमित्तमिह फलम् । योगः संयोगः समवायात्मकः ।] Sid. Kau. @deva[समवायः नित्यसंबन्धः] (constant, inseparable union). Tark. Kau.

rules.title: Locative/Genitive with स्वामी, ईश्वर and Related Words
rules.body:
## Locative/Genitive with @deva[स्वामी], @deva[ईश्वर] and Related Words

[^1] The Locative or the Genitive is used with the words @deva[स्वामी] a master, @deva[ईश्वर], @deva[अधिपति] a lord, @deva[दायाद] a heir, @deva[साक्षिन्], @deva[प्रतिभू] a bail, and @deva[प्रसूत] born for; @deva[गवां गोषु वा स्वामी] the master of kine; @deva[पृथिव्याः] or @deva[पृथिव्यां ईश्वरः] the lord of the earth; @deva[ग्रामाणां] or @deva[ग्रामेषु अधिपतिः] the lord of villages, similarly @deva[पित्र्यंशस्य पित्र्यंशे वा दायादः], @deva[व्यवहारे व्यवहारस्य वा साक्षी], @deva[दर्शने दर्शनस्य वा प्रतिभूः] (surety for appearance in a court); @deva[गोषु गवां वा प्रसूतः गोपः] a cowherd is born for cows.

---

[^1]: @deva[स्वामीश्वराधिपतिदायादसाक्षिप्रतिभूप्रसूतैश्च ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 39.

rules.title: Locative/Genitive with आयुक्त and कुशल (appointed/devoted)
rules.body:
## Locative/Genitive with @deva[आयुक्त] and @deva[कुशल] (appointed/devoted)

[^1] The words @deva[आयुक्त] and @deva[कुशल] meaning 'appointed or devoted to' are construed with the Locative or the Genitive; @deva[आयुक्तः कुशलो वा हरिपूजने हरिपूजनस्य वा] appointed to worship Hari; @deva[कुशलोन्वेषणस्याहमायुक्तो दूतकर्मणि ।] (Bhatti. VIII. 115.) In other senses they are construed with the Locative; @deva[आयुक्तो गौः शकटे] a bull harnessed to the yoke of a carriage; @deva[कर्मणि कुशलः] expert in the performance of an act.

---

[^1]: @deva[आयुक्तकुशलाभ्यां चासेवायाम् ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 40.

rules.title: Locative/Genitive for Distinguishing from a Class
rules.body:
## Locative/Genitive for Distinguishing from a Class

[^1] When an object or an individual is to be distinguished from a whole class, the Locative or the Genitive is used; @deva[नृणां नृषु वा ब्राह्मणः श्रेष्ठः] (see Manu S. I. 96.), @deva[गोषु गवां वा कृष्णा बहुक्षीरा]; @deva[गच्छतां गच्छत्सु वा धावन् शीघ्रः], @deva[छात्राणां छात्रेषु वा मैत्रः पटुः ।] (Sid. Kau.)

---

[^1]: @deva[यतश्च निर्धारणम् ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 41. @deva[जातिगुणक्रियासंज्ञाभिः समुदायादेकदेशस्य पृथक्करणं निर्धारणम् ।] Sid. Kau.

rules.title: Locative with साधु and निपुण (adoration sense)
rules.body:
## Locative with @deva[साधु] and @deva[निपुण] (adoration sense)

[^1] The words @deva[साधु] and @deva[निपुण], not preceded by the prepositions @deva[अनु], @deva[परि] and @deva[प्रति], are used with the Loc. when the sense of adoration is to be conveyed; @deva[मातरि साधुर्निपुणो वा] reverentially disposed towards his mother; but @deva[निपुणः राज्ञः भृत्यः] a clever servant of the king. When preceded by the prepositions @deva[अनु], @deva[परि] and @deva[प्रति] these are used with the Accusative; @deva[साधुर्निपुणो वा मातरं प्रति पर्यनु वा].

---

[^1]: @deva[साधुनिपुणाभ्यामर्चायां सप्तम्यप्रतेः ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 43. @deva[अप्रत्यादिभिरिति वक्तव्यम् ।] Vārt.

rules.title: Locative/Instrumental with प्रसित and उत्सुक
rules.body:
## Locative/Instrumental with @deva[प्रसित] and @deva[उत्सुक]

[^1] With the words @deva[प्रसित] and @deva[उत्सुक], the Locative or the Instrumental is used; @deva[प्रसित उत्सुको वा हरिणा हरौ वा] intent upon Hari; @deva[पत्या प्रस्थितेन पत्यौ प्रस्थिते वा योषिदुत्सुका], a woman gets anxious (or restless) when her husband goes out; @deva[तेजस्विभिरुत्सुकानाम्] Kir. XVI. 7

---

[^1]: @deva[प्रसितोत्सुकाभ्यां तृतीया च ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 44. @deva[विषयविवक्षया सप्तमी । करणत्वविवक्षया तृतीया ।] Bharata on Bhatti. VIII. 117.

rules.title: Locative/Instrumental with Nakshatra Names (Time)
rules.body:
## Locative/Instrumental with Nakshatra Names (Time)

[^1] When the names of *Nakshatras* are used as showing a particular time the Locative or the Instrumental is used; @deva[मूलेनावाहयेद्देवीं श्रवणेन विसर्जयेत् । मूले श्रवणे इति वा ।] (Sid. Kau.)

---

[^1]: @deva[नक्षत्रे च लुपि ।] Pāṇ. II 3. 45.

rules.title: Ablative/Locative for Interval of Time or Space
rules.body:
## Ablative/Locative for Interval of Time or Space

[^1] Words expressive of the interval of time or space are used with the Ablative or the Locative; @deva[अद्य भुक्त्वायं द्व्यहे द्व्यहाद्वा भोक्ता] having dined to-day he will dine again after two days; @deva[इहस्थोयं क्रोशात् क्रोशे वा लक्ष्यं विध्येत्] standing here he will hit a mark two miles distant.

---

[^1]: @deva[सप्तमीपञ्चम्यौ कारकमध्ये ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 5.

rules.title: Locative with उप (exceeding) and अधि (master of)
rules.body:
## Locative with @deva[उप] (exceeding) and @deva[अधि] (master of)

[^1] The prepositions @deva[उप] in the sense of 'exceeding' and @deva[अधि] in that of 'the master of' govern the Locative; @deva[उपपरार्धे हरेर्गुणाः] the merits of Hari exceed a parārdha; @deva[अधि भुवि रामः] or @deva[अधि रामे भूः] Rāma is the lord of the earth; in other senses these prepositions are used with the Accusative, for which see @ref[805].

---

[^1]: @deva[यस्मादधिकं यस्य चेश्वरवचनं तत्र सप्तमी ।] Pāṇ. II 3. 9.

rules.title: दूर and अन्तिक with Locative Also
rules.body:
## @deva[दूर] and @deva[अन्तिक] with Locative Also

The words @deva[दूर] and @deva[अन्तिक] and others having the same sense are used in the Locative also; @deva[ग्रामस्य दूरे—दूरं—दूरेण—दूरात् वा]; @deva[तस्याः समीपे—समीपेन—समीपात् गत्वा].

rules.title: Locative with Verbs of Love and Attachment
rules.body:
## Locative with Verbs of Love and Attachment

Verbs having the sense of 'love, regard for, attachment to' such as @deva[स्निह्], @deva[अनुरञ्ज्], @deva[अभिलष्], @deva[रम्], &c. and their derivatives generally govern the Locative; @deva[पिता पुत्रे स्निह्यति] a father loves his son; @deva[अस्ति मे सोदरस्नेहोपि एतेषु] (S'ak. I) I have a sisterly affection for them also; @deva[न खलु तापसकन्यकायां ममाभिलाषः] I do not, indeed, love the ascetic's daughter, @deva[अशुद्धप्रकृतौ राज्ञि जनता नानुरज्यते] people do not love a king whose ministers are corrupt; @deva[भ्रातुर्मृतस्य भार्यायां योनुरज्येत कामतः] (Manu. S. III. 179). @deva[रहसि रमते] (Māl. Mād. III. 2.) takes pleasure in solitude; @deva[रतः श्रेयसि] (Bhatt. I.) devoted to his welfare.

*Note*:—@deva[अनुरञ्ज्] and @deva[अभिलष्] are sometimes used with the Accusative also; @deva[समस्थमनुरज्यन्ति] (Rāma.); @deva[मानुषानभिलषन्ती] (Bhatt. IV. 22.)

rules.title: Locative with Verbs of Acting/Behaving and Throwing
rules.body:
## Locative with Verbs of Acting/Behaving and Throwing

Verbs of acting, behaving towards, &c. such as @deva[वृत्], @deva[व्यवह्], &c and of throwing, such as @deva[अस्], @deva[मुच्], @deva[क्षिप्], &c. govern the Locative; @deva[गुरुषु विनयेन वृत्तिः कार्या] one should act modestly towards respectable persons, @deva[कुरु प्रियसखीवृत्तिं सपत्नीजने] (S'ak. IV.); @deva[ते तस्मिन् शरान् मुमुचुः चिक्षिपुर्वा]; @deva[न खलु न खलु बाणः संनिपात्योयमस्मिन् मृदुनि मृगशरीरे ।] (S'ak. I.); @deva[तस्मिन्नास्थादिषीकास्त्रम्] (Rag. VII. 23.).

rules.title: Locative/Genitive with अपराध् (to offend)
rules.body:
## Locative/Genitive with @deva[अपराध्] (to offend)

The root @deva[राध्] with @deva[अप] 'to offend' is generally construed with the Locative and sometimes with the Genitive; @deva[कस्मिन्नपि पूजार्हे अपराद्धा शकुन्तला] Śakuntalā has offended some one deserving respect; @deva[न तु ग्रीष्मस्यैवं सुभगमपराद्धं युवतिषु] (Śak. III. 9.), @deva[किंपुनरसुरावलेपेन भवतीनामपराद्धं ।] Vik. I.

rules.title: Introduction to Genitive and Locative Absolute Constructions
rules.body:
## THE GENITIVE AND THE LOCATIVE ABSOLUTES

## Introduction to Genitive and Locative Absolute Constructions

"When the participle agrees with a subject different from the subject of the verb, the phrase is said to be in the absolute construction." Bain.

In English, the Nominative is used as an Absolute case; in Sanskrit the Genitive and the Locative are so used. The English Nominative Absolute ought, therefore, to be translated by the Sanskrit Locative Absolute. When the Absolute Construction is to be used, the subject of the participle must be put in the Genitive or the Locative case and the participle made to agree with it in gender, number and case.

*N. B.* When the subject or object of the principal sentence is the same as that of the participial phrase, the absolute construction should not be used; as @deva[अयोध्यां निवृत्तो रामो राज्यमकरोत्] and not @deva[अयोध्यां निवृत्ते रामे स] &c.; @deva[आगतेभ्यो विप्रेभ्यो दक्षिणामयच्छत] and not @deva[आगतेषु विप्रेषु तेभ्यः] &c.

rules.title: Locative Absolute: Simultaneous or Indicative Actions
rules.body:
## Locative Absolute: Simultaneous or Indicative Actions

[^1] When the action done or suffered by a person or thing indicates another action i. e. when the time of the happening of the one action which is known indicates that of the second action, the Locative Absolute be used; @deva[गोषु दुह्यमानासु गतः] he went away while the cows were being milked; @deva[अवसन्नायां रात्रौ] the night being ended; @deva[कुतो धर्मक्रियाविघ्नः सतां रक्षितरि त्वयि] whence can there be obstacles to our religious rites when thou art the protector of the good.

---

[^1]: @deva[यस्य च भावेन भावलक्षणम् ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 37. @deva[यस्य क्रियया क्रियान्तरं लक्ष्यते ततः सप्तमी स्यात् ।] Sid. Kau.

rules.title: Locative/Genitive Absolute for 'when, while, since, although'
rules.body:
## Locative/Genitive Absolute for 'when, while, since, although'

The locative or Genitive Absolute may be used to express the sense of the English particles 'when, while, since, although,' &c. (and may thus supply the place of a pluperfect tense); @deva[एवं तयोः परस्परं वदतोः] while they two were thus talking; @deva[दृष्टे सूर्ये पुनरपि भवान्वाहयेदध्वशेषम्] (Meg. 40); Thou wilt accomplish the rest of thy journey when the sun rises again.

rules.title: Genitive/Locative Absolute for Contempt, Disregard ('in spite of')
rules.body:
## Genitive/Locative Absolute for Contempt, Disregard ('in spite of')

[^1] When 'contempt or disregard' is to be shown, the Genitive or the Locative Absolute is used; @deva[रुदति रुदतो वा पुत्रे पुत्रस्य वा प्राव्राजीत्] he turned out a recluse disregarding his weeping son i. e. in spite of the weeping of his son. In this sense the Genitive Absolute is used more often. The Locative or the Genitive absolute may thus have the sense of 'in spite of,' 'notwithstanding,' &c. in English.

(a) The Locative Absolute be made to express the idea of 'as soon as,' 'no sooner than,' 'the moment that' &c. by compounding it with the word @deva[एव] or @deva[मात्र]; @deva[तस्मिन्...संहितमात्र एव] (Rag. XVI. 78.) no sooner was the arrow fixed, &c. @deva[अनवसितवचन एव मयि] scarcely had I finished my speech when.

---

[^1]: @deva[षष्ठी चानादरे ।] Pāṇ. II. 3. 38.

rules.title: Syntax of Pronouns Reference
rules.body:
## Section III. PRONOUNS.

The chief peculiarities in the Syntax of pronouns have been already noticed in chapter IV.

rules.title: Gender in First and Second Person Pronouns
rules.body: The pronouns of the first and second person viz. @deva[अस्मद्] and @deva[युष्मद्] have no gender. The other pronouns follow the gender of the nouns they refer to. For the uses of the shorter forms of @deva[अस्मत्] and @deva[युष्मत्] see chapter IV.

rules.title: Usage of भवत् as Honorific Second Person
rules.body:
@deva[भवत्] is used in the second person like 'you' in English as a courteous form of address though it is to be regarded as a pronoun of the third person and ought to be treated as such, @deva[भवान् अत्र प्रष्टव्यः] you ought to be asked here; @deva[भवान् अपि तत्र गच्छतु] you may also go there.

(a) When respect is to be shown, @deva[अत्र] and @deva[तत्र] are prefixed to @deva[भवत्] according as the person with reference to whom it is used is near, or at a distance or absent; @deva[अत्रभवान् काश्यपः] the venerable Kāshyapa (who is near); @deva[इदमासनं अलङ्करोत्वत्रभवान्] may you occupy (lit. ornament) this seat; @deva[तत्रभवती इरावती] lady Irāvatī (who is not present). Sometimes @deva[तद्] is used with @deva[भवत्] to show respect; as @deva[यन्मां विधेयविषये स भवान् नियुङ्क्ते।] Māl. Mād. I.

rules.title: Special Senses of Pronoun तद्
rules.body:
The pronoun @deva[तद्] has often the sense of 'well known, renowned,' &c. @deva[तौ पार्वतीपरमेश्वरौ] those (well-known) Pārvatī and Parameśvara; @deva[तान्येव वनस्थलानि] those well-known forest sites.

(a) When repeated, this pronoun has the sense of 'various, several;' @deva[तेषु तेषु रम्यतरेषु स्थानेषु] in those various highly delightful spots; @deva[कृतैरपि तैस्तैः प्रयत्नैः] notwithstanding several efforts–@deva[कामैस्तैस्तैर्हृतज्ञानाः] &c (Bhag. VII. 20).

rules.title: एक and अपर/अन्य for 'Some—Others'
rules.body: The pronouns @deva[एक] and @deva[अपर] or @deva[अन्य] are used in the plural in the sense of 'some—others;' @deva[विधवायाः पुनरुद्वाहः सशास्त्र इत्येके शास्त्रप्रतिषिद्ध इत्यन्ये कलौ निषिद्ध इत्यपरे] some think that widow-remarriage is sanctioned by the Ś'astras, some say that it is prohibited by them, while others hold that it is not allowed in the Kali age. @deva[केचित्] may take the place of @deva[एके].

rules.title: Combination of Pronouns
rules.body: The pronouns @deva[अस्मत्], @deva[युष्मत्], @deva[यत्] and @deva[किम्] are often used in combination with other pronouns; @deva[सोहं—रघूणामन्वयं वक्ष्ये] that I will describe the race of the Raghus; @deva[सोहं सर्वाधमो लोके] that I am the most degraded of all the people; @deva[स त्वं प्रशस्ते महिते मदीये—अग्न्यगारे—वसन्] that thou dwelling in my fire-sanctuary; &c.; @deva[ते वयं दमयन्त्यर्थे चरामः पृथिवीमिमाम्] we, of this description, roam over the earth for (in search of) Damayantī; sometimes @deva[अस्मत्] and @deva[युष्मत्] may be understood; @deva[सा क्षिप्रमातिष्ठ रथं गजं वा] i. e. @deva[सा त्वं] that thou quickly sit in a chariot or mount an elephant. @deva[सोयं पुत्रस्तव मदस्रुचां वारणानां विजेता] this is that son of thine, the subduer of elephants shedding ichor; @deva[तथा विनाकृतः पुत्रैर्योहमिच्छामि जीवितुम्] I, who wish to live still, even though deprived of my sons in that manner, &c. &c.

rules.title: Comparatives with Ablative or Instrumental
rules.body:
## COMPARATIVE AND SUPERLATIVE DEGREES.

Adjectives in the Comparative degree are used with the Ablative; @deva[वर्धनाद्रक्षणं श्रेयः] protection (of one's subjects) is better than aggrandizement. @deva[अर्जुनाद्युधिष्ठिरो ज्यायान्] Udhisthira was older than Arjuna.

(a) Sometimes the comparative is used with the Instrumental; @deva[प्राणैः प्रियतरः] dearer than life. See also @ref[863] *Note*.

rules.title: Superlatives with Genitive or Locative
rules.body: The superlative may either be construed with the Genitive or Locative; @deva[अयमेतेषां एतेषु वा गरिष्ठः गुरुतमो वा].

rules.title: Comparative and Superlative Sense Through Case Usage
rules.body: The sense of the comparative and the superlative may also be expressed by the particular case used; @deva[अस्य हृदयं पाषाणात्कठिनं] his heart is harder than stone; @deva[छात्राणां छात्रेषु वा चैत्रः पटुः] Chaitra is the cleverest of all students.

rules.title: Special Usage of वर and प्रवर
rules.body: The words @deva[वर] and @deva[प्रवर] when used in the sense of the superlative govern the Genitive or the Locative; @deva[पुत्र स्पर्शवतां वरः] 'a son is the best of things possessed of touch;' @deva[चतुष्पदां गोः प्रवरा लोहानां काञ्चनं वरं] 'the cow is the best of quadrupeds and gold of metals'; the neu. sing. of @deva[वर] is used (with a word expressive of negation) in the sense of 'better and not, or but not;' @deva[अकरणान्मन्दकरणं वरं] doing any thing slowly is better than not doing it at all; @deva[अजातमृतमूर्खाणां वरमाद्यौ न चान्तिमः] of (the three kinds of) sons—not born, born and dead, and foolish, the first two are better, but not the last. @deva[याच्ञा मोघा वरमधिगुणे नाधमे लब्धकामा।] Meg. I. 6. @deva[वरं प्राणैः वियोगः न तु मानहानिः] better death than disgrace.

rules.title: Declinable Participles as Adjectives and Verbs
rules.body:
## Section IV. PARTICIPLES.

All declinable participles in Sanskrit partake of the nature of adjectives i. e. they agree with the nouns they qualify in gender, number, and case. The participles often discharge the functions of verbs. They are largely employed to take the place of the Past and Future tenses and more especially of passive verbs. When so employed they follow the same rules of syntax as are laid down for the roots from which they are derived.

rules.title: Present Participle for Contemporaneous Action
rules.body:
## PRESENT PARTICIPLES.

The present participle is to be used when contemporaneity of action is to be indicated. It is often idiomatically used to express the sense of 'while' or 'whilst' in English; @deva[अरण्ये चरन्] while wandering in the forest; @deva[विवाहकौतुकं बिभ्रत एव] while he yet wore the marriage string.

Vide 670 (b).

rules.title: Present Participle for Manner, Cause, or Object
rules.body:
[^1] The present participle is used to denote the manner in which an action is done or the cause or object of an action; @deva[शयाना भुञ्जन्ते यवनाः] the Yavanas dine by lying down; @deva[हरिं पश्यन् मुच्यते] a man is absolved by (reason of his) seeing Hari; similarly @deva[तिष्ठन् मूत्रयति, गच्छन् भक्षयति] (Mb.).

---

[^1]: @deva[लक्षणहेत्वोः क्रियायाः] Pāṇ. III. 2. 126 @deva[हेतुः फलं कारणं च।] Sid. Kau.

rules.title: आस् and स्था with Present Participles for Continuity
rules.body: The roots @deva[आस्] and @deva[स्था] are generally used with present participles to show the continuity of the action denoted by them; @deva[पशूनां वधं कुर्वन् आस्ते] used to kill (always kept on killing) animals; @deva[तं प्रतिपालयन् तस्थौ] remained waiting for him.

rules.title: Limited Use of Perfect Participles
rules.body:
## THE PERFECT PARTICIPLES.

The use of the perfect participles is very limited; it is used in the sense of 'who or what has done &c.'; @deva[तं तस्थिवांसं नगरोपकण्ठे] (Rag. V. 61.) him who had halted in the vicinity of the city; @deva[श्रेयांसि सर्वाण्यधिजग्मुषस्ते] (Rag. V. 34.) of thee who hast obtained all good things, @deva[स शुश्रुवांस्तद्वचनं] (Bhaṭṭi. I. 20) when he heard his words; &c.

rules.title: Past Passive Participle as Verb Substitute
rules.body:
## THE PAST PASSIVE PARTICIPLES.

The past passive participle is very frequently used to supply the place of a verb; sometimes in conjunction with the auxiliary verbs @deva[अस्] and @deva[भू]. The past passive participle agrees adjectivally with the object in gender, number and case, the agent being put in the Instrumental, while the past active participle is treated exactly like the verb in the past tense; @deva[तेन कार्यं कृतं] by him the work was done; @deva[तेन बन्धनानि छिन्नानि] by him the bonds were cut; @deva[आदिष्टास्मि देव्या धारिण्या] I am commanded by queen Dhāriṇī; @deva[स कार्यं कृतवान्] he did the work; @deva[रामः दैत्यान् हतवान्] Rāma killed the Rākshasas; @deva[कृतवत्यासि नावधीरणां] thou didst never despise me, &c.

rules.title: Intransitive Past Passive Participles with Nominative Agent
rules.body: In the case of past passive participles of intransitive roots the agent is put in the Nominative case; @deva[तदा प्ररुदितो राजा रक्षसां] then the king of demons wept; @deva[सत्यं मृतोयं पापः] &c.

rules.title: Impersonal Use of Past Passive Participles
rules.body: The past passive participles are often used impersonally, the agent being put in the Instrumental case; @deva[प्रद्युतितं] or @deva[प्रद्योतितं सूर्येण] it is shone by the sun; @deva[जितं पुत्रप्रेम्णा] victorious (all powerful) is the affection for sons; @deva[पण्डितायितं तत्रभवता] he showed his learning; @deva[प्रमुदितं] or @deva[प्रमोदितं साधुना], &c.

rules.title: Past Passive Participles of @deva[मन्], @deva[बुध], and @deva[पूज्] in Present Sense
rules.body:
The past passive participles of the roots @deva[मन्], @deva[बुध] and @deva[पूज्] and their synonyms are used in the sense of the Present tense and are construed with the Genitive. (See @ref[857].)

For further particulars vide @ref[705]—@ref[707].

rules.title: Active Use of Past Passive Participles
rules.body: Many past passive participles are used actively in which case they may govern the Accusative case, like a Perfect tense active; @deva[आरूढमद्रीन्] (Rag. VI. 77.) which had ascended the mountains; similarly @deva[गगनमध्यमारूढः सविता]; @deva[आपादमुत्तीर्णः] crossed i. e. got over the calamity; @deva[यमुनाकच्छमवतीर्णः] descended to the bank of the Yamunā, &c.

rules.title: Past Passive Participle as Neuter Substantive
rules.body: The past passive participle is used as a *neuter* substantive; @deva[गतं] departure; @deva[दत्तं] a gift, @deva[खातं] an excavation, @deva[भुक्तं, सुप्तं], &c.

rules.title: Past Passive Participles with Auxiliary Verbs @deva[अस्] and @deva[भू]
rules.body: The past passive participle active and passive, may be used with the auxiliaries @deva[अस्] and @deva[भू] in any tense, the meaning of the participle changing accordingly; @deva[गतोस्मि] or @deva[गतवानस्मि] I have or am gone; so @deva[गतवानभवं] or @deva[गतवानासं] or @deva[गतोभवं] I had or was gone; so @deva[कृतवानस्मि]. @deva[गतो वनं श्वो भवितेति रामः] that Rāma is to go to the forest to-morrow; @deva[संप्राप्तः कीर्तिमतुलां भविष्यसि] thou wilt obtain great glory, &c.

rules.title: Future Participle Meaning
rules.body:
## THE FUTURE PARTICIPLES.

The future participle denotes that a person or thing is doing, or is about to do the action or to undergo the condition, expressed by the root; @deva[करिष्यन्] going or about to do; @deva[करिष्यमाण] about to do or what is about to be done.

rules.title: Future Participle Expressing Intention or Purpose
rules.body: Besides showing simple futurity participle expresses intention or purpose; @deva[अनुयास्यन् मुनितनयाम्] wishing to follow the daughter of the sage; @deva[दास्यन्] wishing to give, @deva[वन्यान् विनेष्यन्निव दुष्टसत्त्वान्] wishing, as it were, to tame the wild beasts.

rules.title: Potential Passive Participle: Obligation and Necessity
rules.body:
## POTENTIAL PASSIVE PARTICIPLES.

The Potential passive participle is used in the sense of 'what should or ought to be done;' besides this, this participle yields the sense of 'fitness, obligation, necessity, capacity,' &c., the agent being put in the Instrumental case; @deva[विमर्शमकरोच्चित्ते किं कर्तव्यं मयाधुना] (Devi Bhāg. IV. 7. 1.) he considered in his mind what he ought to do; @deva[धर्मः अनुसरणीयः] religious duty ought to be followed; @deva[त्वया भारो वहनीयः] thou art able to bear this burden; @deva[हन्तव्योयं शठः] this rogue deserves to be killed; @deva[गन्तव्या ते वसतिरलका नाम यक्षेश्वराणां] thou will have to go to Alakā, the habitation of the lords of Yakshas, &c.

*Obs.*—Sometimes the agent is put in the Genitive case; @deva[मम सेव्यो हरिः] Hari is to be served by me; @deva[द्विजातीनां भक्ष्यं अन्नं] boiled rice to be eaten by Brāhmaṇas.

rules.title: Impersonal Use of Potential Passive Participle
rules.body: Occasionally this participle is used impersonally in the *neuter* gender and singular number; @deva[तत्रभवता तपोवनं गन्तव्यम्] his honour should go to the penance grove; @deva[मया चाण्डालैः सह स्थातव्यं] I should have to dwell in the company of Chāṇḍālas &c.

rules.title: Impersonal @deva[भवितव्य] and @deva[भाव्य] for Probability
rules.body: The *neuter* forms @deva[भवितव्यं] and @deva[भाव्यं] are used impersonally in the sense of 'being,' or 'what must be or in all probability is,' the noun denoting the agent being put in the Instrumental case: @deva[अत्र केनापि कारणेन भवितव्यं] there must be some cause; @deva[अस्य शब्दानुरूपेण पराक्रमेण भवितव्यं] or @deva[भाव्यम्] in all probability his strength must be corresponding to his sound; @deva[आर्यया प्रवाहणमारूढया भवितव्यम्] the lady must (in all likelihood) be seated in the carriage, &c.

rules.title: Potential Passive Participle as Noun
rules.body: This participle is sometimes used as a noun; @deva[प्रष्टव्यं पृच्छतस्तस्य] to him who asked what was to be asked; @deva[भवितव्यं भवत्वेव] let that, which is to happen, happen.

rules.title: Gerunds Denoting Prior Action
rules.body:
## INDECLINABLE PAST PARTICIPLES OR GERUNDS.

The past indeclinable participle in Sanskrit denotes the prior of two actions done by the same agent and corresponds to the perfect participle in English; @deva[इति उक्त्वा विरराम] having said this he stopped; @deva[तान् पृष्ठमारोप्य जलाशयं नीत्वा भक्षयति] having seated them on his back, he carried them to the lake and ate them up.

As the past indeclinable participles or gerunds serve the purpose of carrying on the action of the verb and act as connecting links between sentences, they account for the sparing use made in Sanskrit composition of relative pronouns, conjunctions and connecting particles. When several gerunds are used in a sentence they should be translated by verbal tenses and copulative conjunctions; @deva[प्रवृत्ते प्रदोषसमये चन्द्रापीडः चरणाभ्यामेव राजकुलं गत्वा पितुः समीपे मुहूर्तं स्थित्वा दृष्ट्वा च विलासवतीं आगत्य स्वभवनं शयनतलमधिशिश्ये] when the evening time approached, Chandrāpīda went to the royal palace on foot, remained in the presence of his father for an hour, saw Vilāsavatī, &c.
