rules.title: Gerunds Used Prepositionally
rules.body: A few gerunds are used prepositionally in Sanskrit; @deva[विहाय, मुक्त्वा] except, @deva[आदाय] with, @deva[उद्दिश्य, अधिकृत्य, अनुरुध्य] with reference to, &c.

rules.title: Infinitive Expressing Purpose
rules.body:
## THE INFINITIVE MOOD.

The infinitive in Sanskrit generally expresses the purpose or that for which an action is done and thus corresponds to the infinitive of purpose or gerund in English. The infinitive in Sanskrit thus involves the sense of the Dative and may, if desired, be replaced by the Dative of the verbal noun derived from the root; @deva[पानीयं पातुं यमुनाकच्छं अवततार] descended to the bank of the Yamunā to drink water; here @deva[पातुं] may be replaced by @deva[पानाय] (@deva[पानीयस्य पानाय]); @deva[शब्दादीन्विषयान् भोक्तुं] (Rag. X. 25.) where @deva[भोक्तुं]=@deva[भोगाय].

"The infinitive (formed with @deva[तुम्] tum) in Sanskrit" remarks Prof. Monier Williams, "cannot be employed with the same latitude as in other languages. Its use is very limited corresponding to that of the Latin supines, as its termination tum indicates."

(a) "Let the student, therefore, distinguish between the infinitive of Sanskrit and that of Latin and Greek. In these latter languages we have the infinitive made the subject of a proposition; or, in other words, standing in the place of a Nominative and an Accusative case often admissible before it. We have it also assuming different forms, to express present, past, or future time, and completeness or incompleteness in the progress of the action. The Sanskrit infinitive, on the other hand, can never be made the subject of a verb, admits of no Accusative before it, and can only express indeterminate time and incomplete action. Wherever it occurs, it must be considered as the object, and never the subject of some verb expressed or understood. As the object of the verb, it may be regarded as equivalent to a verbal substantive, in which the force of two cases, an Accusative and Dative, is inherent and which differs from other substantives in its power of governing a case. Its use as a substantive, with the force of the *Accusative* case, corresponds to our use of the Latin infinitive; thus @deva[तत् सर्वं श्रोतुं इच्छामि] 'I desire to hear all that,' '*id audire capio*,' where @deva[श्रोतुम्] and *audire* are both equivalent to Accusative. Similarly, @deva[रोदितुं प्रवृत्ता] 'she began to weep,' and @deva[महीं जेतुं आरभे], he began to conquer the earth, where @deva[महीजयं आरभे], he began the conquest of the earth, would be equally correct."

(b) "Bopp considers the termination of the infinitive to be the Accusative of the suffix *tu* (@ref[458] *Obs.*), and it is certain that in the veda other cases of nouns formed with this suffix in the sense of infinitives occur; *e. g.* a Dative in *tave or tavai*, as from *han* comes *hantave* 'to kill;' fr. *anu-i* *anvetave*, 'to follow;' fr. *man*, *mantavai*, 'to think;' there is also a form in *tos* generally in the sense of an Ablative; *e. g.* fr. *i.* comes *etos* 'from going;' fr. *han*, *hantos*, as in *pura hantos*, 'before killing;' and a form in *tvi* corresponding to the indeclinable participle in *tvā* of the classical language; *e. g.* fr. *han*, *hatvi* 'killing;' fr. *bhū bhūtvi* 'being,' &c &c." Sanskrit Grammar.

rules.title: Infinitive Cannot be Subject or Object
rules.body: The infinitive cannot be used as the subject or object of a verb, abstract nouns supplying its place in this case. Where, therefore, the infinitive occurs in English as the subject or the object in a sentence, the abstract noun derived from the root must be used in Sanskrit; @deva[स्वधर्माचारणं हितावहं] to do one's duty is beneficial and not @deva[स्वधर्ममाचारितुं].

rules.title: Infinitive with Verbs of Wishing
rules.body:
[^1]The infinitive is used with verbs and verbal nouns meaning 'to wish or desire' provided the agent of it is the same as that of the verb; @deva[को हर्तुमिच्छति हरेः दंष्ट्राम्] (Mud. I.) who wishes to snatch away the jaws of the lion; @deva[माधुर्यं मधुबिन्दुना रचयितुं क्षाराम्बुधेरीहते;] Bhartṛ. II. 6. But @deva[तमेतत्कर्तुमहमिच्छामि] I wish him to do this, is wrong.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[समानकर्तृकेषु तुमुन्] Pān. III. 3. 158.

rules.title: Infinitive with Verbs of Ability, Knowledge, and Time
rules.body:
[^1]The infinitive is also used with:—

(a) verbs meaning to be able, to make bold, to know, to be wearied, to strive, to begin, to set about, to bear, to be pleased and to be; @deva[न शक्नोति शिरोधरां धारयितुं] (Kād.) is not able to support his neck; @deva[जानासि कोपं निग्रहीतुं] you know how to restrain anger; @deva[अङ्गदेन समं योद्धुमघटिष्ट] (Bhaṭṭi. XV. 77) he strove to fight with Angada; @deva[गन्तुं व्यवस्येद्भवान्] (Meg. 22) thou wilt try to go; @deva[वक्तुं प्रक्रमेथाः] (Meg. 103.) begin to speak; @deva[अस्ति-भवति-विद्यते वा भोक्तुमन्नं] (Sid. Kau) there is food to eat, &c.

(b) [^2]words like @deva[अलं] and others meaning sufficient or able, proficient or skilled in, &c.; @deva[पर्याप्तोसि प्रजाः पातुं] (Rag. X. 25) thou art able to protect the creation; @deva[कः समर्थो दैवमन्यथा कर्तुं] who is able to change destiny; @deva[प्रासादास्त्वां तुलयितुमलं] (Meg. 66) the palaces are able to stand comparison with thee; @deva[भोक्तुं प्रवीणः कुशलः पटुर्वा] (Sid. Kau.) skilled in eating.

(c) [^3]words having the sense of 'it is time to do anything;' @deva[कालः समयो वेला अनेहा वा भोक्तुम्] (Sid. Kau.) it is time to take food.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[शकधृषज्ञाग्लाघटरभलभक्रमसहार्हास्त्यर्थेषु तुमुन्।] Pāṇ. III. 4. 65. Vide Apte's Guide § 176 and note thereon.

[^2]: @deva[पर्याप्तिवचनेष्वसमर्थे।] Pāṇ. III. 4. 66.

[^3]: @deva[कालसमयवेलासु तुमुन्।] Pāṇ. III. 3. 167.

rules.title: Infinitive Has No Passive Form
rules.body: The infinitive in Sanskrit has no passive form. In turning, therefore, an active construction involving an infinitive into a passive one, the verb should be changed into the passive, the infinitive and the words governed by it remaining unaffected—@deva[स ग्रामं गन्तुं इच्छति, तेन ग्रामं गन्तुं इष्यते]—except where the object of the infinitive and the verb is the same, @deva[स भारं वोढुमिच्छति, तेन भारो वोढुमिष्यते].

rules.title: @deva[अर्ह्] with Infinitive for Request or Ability
rules.body: The root @deva[अर्ह्] 'to deserve' when used (in the second person) in combination with the infinitive expresses 'a request, a respectful entreaty,' and is generally, equivalent to the English 'I pray, be pleased, &c.;' @deva[अग्निं शमयितुमर्हसि] (Meg. 55) please put out the fire; @deva[न चेद्रहस्यं प्रतिवक्तुमर्हसि] (Kum V. 40) if you have nothing to conceal from me, please answer me: @deva[द्वित्राण्यहान्यर्हसि सोढुमर्हन्] (Rag. V. 25) pray wait for two or three days, O respectable one! &c. Sometimes it is equivalent to a gentle command: @deva[इमां प्रसादयितुमर्हसि] (Rag. I. 89) you ought to please her; @deva[न तं शोचितुमर्हसि] you ought not to bewail him. In the third person and under the same circumstances it expresses power or ability and can be translated by 'can:' @deva[द्रोणं हि समरे कोऽन्यो योद्धुमर्हति फाल्गुनाद्] Mah. Bhar. IV. 58. 27. @deva[दैवं प्रज्ञाविशेषेण को निवर्तितुमर्हति] Ibid I. 1. 246.

rules.title: Infinitive Compounds with @deva[काम] and @deva[मनस्]
rules.body:
[^1]The infinitive with the final @deva[म्] dropped is joined with the nouns @deva[काम] and @deva[मनस्] to form an adjectival compound meaning 'wishing or having a mind to do any thing;' @deva[एतावदुक्त्वा प्रतियातुकामं शिष्यं महर्षेः] &c. (Rag. V. 18) the disciple of the great sage was desirous of returning &c.; @deva[अयं जनः प्रष्टुमनास्तपोधने] (Kum. V. 40) this person has a mind to ask you a question.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[तुङ्काममनसोरपि।]

rules.title: Present Tense for Current Action
rules.body:
## TENSES AND MOODS.

## THE PRESENT TENSE.

The Present tense shows that an action is taking place at the present time; @deva[अयमागच्छति तव पुत्रः] here comes (is coming) thy son. [^1]It is the Present progressive, which expresses the continuance of an action which is begun over sometime and is, remarks Prof. Bain, a true or strict Present tense. It is only by means of a special adverb or the context that the sense of the present tense can be limited to that of a present act solely; @deva[अधुना स इमां पुरीं अधिवसति] now he dwells in this city.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: "The principal use of the Present Indefinite is to express what is true at all times; 'the sun gives light; twice two is four \* \* \*.' Hence a more suitable name would be the Universal tense. It expresses present time only as representing all time. The permanent arrangements and laws of nature, the peculiarities, habits and propensities of living beings and whatever is constant, regular and uniform, have to be represented by the Present Indefinite. \*\* It is only by a special adverb or by the context that we can confine this tense to mean a present act solely." Bain, Higher English Grammar.

rules.title: Special Uses of Present Tense
rules.body:
Besides the general sense given above the Present tense in Sanskrit has the following senses:—

(a) [^1]It is sometimes used in the sense of 'immediate futurity;' @deva[कदा गमिष्यसि] when wilt thou go? @deva[एष गच्छामि] Here I go (i. e. shall go); @deva[ऊर्ध्वं म्रिये मुहूर्ताद्धि] I shall die an hour after.

(b) It may also be used to denote an action which is recently completed; @deva[कदा त्वं नगरादागतोसि—अयमागच्छामि] when didst thou come from the city? Here I come (have come just now).

(c) In narrations it is used for the Past tense; @deva[गृध्रो ब्रूते कस्त्वं] the vulture says, 'who art thou'?

(d) Sometimes it is used to denote a habitual or repeated action; @deva[पशुवधेनासौ जीवति।]

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: Pān. III. 3. 131. See p. 525.

rules.title: Present for Past with @deva[ननु] Particle
rules.body:
[^1]When a question is asked and an answer is given to it, the Present is used in the sense of the Past tense when the particle @deva[ननु] is used; @deva[कटं अकार्षीः किम्—ननु करोमि भोः] where @deva[करोमि] is equivalent to @deva[अकार्षम्]; when the particles @deva[न] and @deva[नु] are used the Present may be optionally used; @deva[कटमकार्षीः किम्—न करोमि] or @deva[नाकार्षम्—नु करोमि] or @deva[न्वकार्षम्].

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[ननौ पृष्टप्रतिवचने। नन्वोर्विभाषा।] Pān. III. 2. 120, 121.

rules.title: Present for Future with Interrogatives and Conditionals
rules.body:
[^1]With interrogatives the Present is often used in the sense of the Future when thought or desire is implied; @deva[किं करोमि] i. e. (@deva[करिष्यामि]), @deva[क्व गच्छामि] i. e. (@deva[गमिष्यामि]) What shall I do? Whither shall I go? @deva[एतयोः कतरं] or @deva[एतेषां कतमं भोजयसि] (i. e. @deva[भोजयिष्यसि] or @deva[भोजयितासि]) which of these persons will you feed? so @deva[कं नु पृच्छामि दुःखार्ता], &c.; but @deva[कः ग्रामं गमिष्यति।]

(a) It is also used in the sense of the Future in conditional sentences as implying a condition and the fulfilment of the desired object; @deva[योन्नं ददाति] (@deva[दाता दास्यति वा]) @deva[स स्वर्गं याति] (@deva[याता यास्यति वा]) he, who offers (or will offer) food, goes (or will go) to heaven i. e. if one offers &c.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[किंवृत्ते लिप्सायाम्। लिप्स्यमानसिद्धौ च।] Pān. III. 3. 6. 7.

rules.title: Present for Future Perfect with @deva[यावत्], @deva[तावत्]; and Certainty with @deva[पुरा]
rules.body:
With the words @deva[यावत्], @deva[तावत्] and others having a similar sense, the Present is sometimes used in the sense of the Future perfect; @deva[यावत्स त्वां न पश्यति तावद्दूरमपसर] before he sees you, move away (before he shall have seen you, &c.).

(b) [^1]With the particles @deva[पुरा] and @deva[यावत्] the Present has the sense of the Future when certainty is indicated; @deva[यावद्यते साधयितुं त्वदर्थम्।] (Rag. V. 25.) I will endeavour to accomplish your object. @deva[पुरा सप्तद्वीपां जयति वसुधाम्] (S'ak. VII. 33) he will conquer the earth consisting of seven continents. @deva[पुरानुशेते तव चञ्चलं मनः।] Kir. VIII. 8.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[यावत्पुरानिपातयोर्लट्] Pān. III. 3. 4. @deva[निपातावेतौ निश्चयं द्योतयतः।] Sid. Kau.

rules.title: Present for Past with @deva[स्म] Particle
rules.body:
[^1]The particle @deva[स्म] when used with the Present converts it into a Past tense; @deva[कस्मिंश्चिदधिष्ठाने मित्रशर्मा नाम ब्राह्मणः प्रतिवसति स्म] in a certain village there dwelt a Brāhmaṇa Mitraśarmā by name; @deva[पौराः शतशोभिधावन्ति स्म] the citizens ran in hundreds. The particle @deva[स्म] may not necessarily be joined with it; @deva[त्वं स्म वेत्थ महाराज यत्स्माह न विभीषणः, मन्त्रे स्म हितमाचष्टे], &c.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[लट् स्मे।] Pān. III. 2. 118.

rules.title: Present for All Tenses with @deva[जातु] and @deva[आत्]
rules.body:
[^1]When @deva[जातु] or @deva[अपि] is used in a sentence and condemnation or censure is implied, the Present may be used in the sense of the three tenses; @deva[अपि जायां त्यजसि जातु गणिकामादत्से] where @deva[त्यजसि] and @deva[आदत्से] may have also the sense of the Past or the Future tense; @deva[जातु तत्रभवान् वृषलान् याजयति] (you will even make a S'udra perform a sacrifice).

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[गर्हायां लडपिजात्वोः।] Pān. III. 3. 142.

rules.title: Three Past Tenses: Original and Current Usage
rules.body:
## IMPERFECT, PERFECT AND AORIST.

In Sanskrit there are three tenses denoting a past action, viz. the Imperfect, the Perfect, and the Aorist. Originally each of these three tenses had a signification of its own and was used in its proper sense in ancient writings.[^1] After Sanskrit ceased to be a spoken language the exact senses of these tenses were lost sight of and writers began to use them promiscuously, so that now any of these may be used to denote past time with certain limitations. The original senses of these as well as their other peculiarities are noticed below.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: For a further explanation of the difference between these three tenses the student is referred to Dr. Bhandārkar's preface to the 1st Edition of his 2nd Book of Sanskrit.

rules.title: Imperfect for Past Action Not Done Today
rules.body:
## IMPERFECT.

[^1]The Imperfect according to Pāṇini denotes past action not done to-day i. e. done at some time prior to the current day, @deva[तानभाषत पौलस्त्यः] (Bhaṭṭi.) Bibhīshaṇa spoke to them.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[अनद्यतने लङ्।] Pān. III. 2. 111.

rules.title: Imperfect Optional with @deva[ह] and @deva[शश्वत्]; Questions of Recent Time
rules.body:
[^1]The Imperfect is optionally used for the Perfect when the particles @deva[ह] and @deva[शश्वत्] are used in a sentence, @deva[इति ह अकरोत्] or @deva[चकार] @deva[शश्वदकरोत्] or @deva[चकार].

(a) [^2]It may also be optionally used in asking questions referring to a very recent time; @deva[अगच्छत् किं] (*Qu.*) (*Ans*) @deva[अगच्छत्] or @deva[जगाम किं? जगाम]; but when the question refers to a very remote time the Perfect alone ought to be used; @deva[कृष्णः कंसं जघान किं? जघान।]

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[हशश्वतोर्लङ् च।]

[^2]: @deva[प्रश्ने चासन्ने काले।] Pān III. 2. 116, 117.

rules.title: Augment Dropped with @deva[मा] and @deva[स्म] for Imperative
rules.body: When the particle @deva[मा] in combination with @deva[स्म] is used with the Imperfect in the sense of the Imperative, the augment @deva[अ] is dropped; @deva[मा स्म भवः, मा स्म करोत्, मा स्म प्ररुदितं युवाम्।]

rules.title: Perfect for Remote Past Not Witnessed
rules.body:
## PERFECT.

[^1]The Perfect denotes an action done before the current day and not witnessed by the speaker. It has reference to a very remote time and should, therefore, be used in narrating events of the remote past; @deva[तां ताटकाख्यां निजघान रामः।] Rāma killed her whose name was Tāṭakā. @deva[प्रययाविन्द्रजित्प्रत्यक्] (Bhaṭṭi. XIV. 16.).

(a) In the 1st person the Perfect shows that the speaker was in a distracted state of mind or was unconscious when the event took place, or that he wants utterly to deny something that he has done, @deva[बहु जगद पुरस्तात्तस्य मत्ताङ्किलाहम्] (S'is. XI. 39) being frenzied I prattled much, I am told, before him; @deva[कलिङ्गेष्ववात्सीः किं।] didst thou dwell in the country of the Kalingas? @deva[नाहं कलिङ्गाञ्जगाम] I never went to Kalingas. With these exceptions the Perfect should not be used in the 1st person.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[परोक्षे लिट्] Pān. III. 2. 115. @deva[उत्तमपुरुषे चित्तविक्षेपादिना पारोक्ष्यम्।] (Sid. Kau.); @deva[अत्यन्तापह्नवे लिङ् वक्तव्यः।] Vārt.

rules.title: Aorist for Indefinite Past and Today's Actions
rules.body:
## AORIST.

[^1]The Aorist simply expresses past action indefinitely i. e. without reference to any particular time (@deva[भूतसामान्ये लुङ्]); @deva[सोध्यैष्ट वेदांस्त्रिदशानयष्ट पितॄनपारीत्समममंस्त बन्धून्। व्यजेष्ट षड्वर्गमरंस्त नीतौ समूलघातं न्यवधीदरींश्च] (Bhaṭṭi. I. 2.) 'He studied the Vedas, offered sacrifices to the gods, satisfied his departed ancestors, honoured his relatives, subdued the collection of six (i. e. the six passions), took delight in politics and totally annihilated his enemies. The Aorist, however, properly denotes a recent action or one done during the course of the present day. "It is similar to the English present Perfect," remarks Dr. Bhandārkar[^2], "which the student will remember defines an action as having happened in a portion of time which is not yet expired; it brings past action in connection with the present time," @deva[अभूद्वृष्टिरद्य] it rained to-day.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[लुङ्] Pān. III. 2. 110.

[^2]: Second Book of Sanskrit, P. 154.

rules.title: Aorist for Continuous or Near Actions
rules.body:
[^1]The Aorist ought to be used when the idea of the continuousness or nearness of an action is to be implied; @deva[यावज्जीवमन्नमदात्] (Sid. Kau.) gave food throughout his life; @deva[येयं पौर्णमातिक्रान्ता तस्यामग्नीनाधित सोमेनायष्ट] (Sid. Kau) he consecrated the fire on the last Purṇimā day (the full-moon day) and offered Soma, &c.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: Pān. III. 3. 135. See next Page.

rules.title: Multiple Tenses with @deva[पुरा] Particle
rules.body:
[^1]With the particle @deva[पुरा] not joined with @deva[स्म], the Aorist, the Imperfect, the Perfect or the Present may be used; @deva[वसन्तीह पुरा छात्रा अवात्सुरवसन्नूषुर्वा।] (Sid. Kau.) here formerly dwelt pupils. But when @deva[स्म] is used with @deva[पुरा] the present alone can be used; @deva[यजति स्म पुरा] he formerly sacrificed.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[पुरि लुङ् चास्मे।] Pān. III. 2. 122. @deva[पुराशब्दयोगे भूतानद्यतने विभाषया लुङ् चाल्लट् न तु स्मयोगे।] Sid. Kau.

rules.title: Aorist with @deva[मा] for Prohibition
rules.body: The Aorist is used with the prohibitive particle @deva[मा] (@deva[माङ्]) or @deva[मा स्म], with the temporal augment @deva[अ] cut off, and has then the sense of the Imperative; @deva[इति ते संशयो मा भूत्] Ma. Bhā V. 132. 16. have no doubt &c. @deva[मा स्म प्रतीपं गमः] do not go against. Rarely in ancient works the augment is retained @deva[मा निषाद प्रतिष्ठां त्वमगमः शाश्वतीः समाः] may you not live, oh Nishāda for many years. When a root is preceded by a preposition, the @deva[अ] is sometimes not dropped; @deva[मा मन्युवशमन्वगा] do not submit to sorrow or anger (here the @deva[अ] is not dropped); sometimes it is dropped; as in @deva[मावमंस्थाः स्वमात्मानं] do not despise your soul (conscience). Some explain these anomalies by considering the particle to be @deva[मा] and not @deva[माङ्].

rules.title: Difference Between First and Second Futures
rules.body:
## THE TWO FUTURES.

The difference between the Two Futures is the same as that between the Imperfect and the Aorist, the only difference being that the former refers to a future time and the latter to a past one. The First or Periphrastic expresses futurity definitely but not of this day; the Second or Simple Future expresses futurity indefinitely as also that of to-day; it is also employed to denote recent and future continuous time; as @deva[अयोध्यां श्वः प्रयातासि कपे भरतपालिताम्] (Bhaṭṭi XXII,) oh monkey, to-morrow you will go to Ayodhyā governed by Bharata; @deva[आनन्दितारस्त्वां दृष्ट्वा प्रष्टारश्चावयोः शिवम्। मातरः सह मैथिल्या तोष्टा च भरतः परम्] (Bhaṭṭi. XXII. 14.) they will be delighted on seeing you and will ask you questions about the welfare of us two and Sītā; and Bharata also will be greatly pleased; @deva[एते…उन्मूलितारः कपिकेतनेन] (Kir. III. 22) they will be extirpated by the monkey-bannered one (Arjuna); @deva[यास्यत्यद्य शकुन्तला] (S'ak. IV.) Śakuntalā will go (goes) to-day; @deva[मरिष्यामि विजेष्ये वा हताश्चेत्तनया मम] (Bhaṭṭi XVI. 13) if my sons are killed I will die or kill the enemy, &c.

rules.title: When First Future Must Not Be Used
rules.body:
## THE FIRST FUTURE OR PERIPHRASTIC FUTURE.

*Obs.* [^1]When the continuousness of an action or nearness of time (i. e. the non-intervention of the same period between the two points of time referred to) is to be expressed the First Future must not be used; @deva[यावज्जीवमन्नं दास्यति] he will give food throughout his life; and not @deva[दाता], @deva[या इयं अमावास्या आगामिनी तस्यां अग्नीनाधास्यते सोमेन च यक्ष्यते] he will consecrate the fires and offer a Soma sacrifice on the coming Amāvāsyā day; and not @deva[आधाता] and @deva[यष्टा]; also when limit of time or place is expressed and the word @deva[अवर] is used in a sentence; @deva[यः अयमध्वा गन्तव्यः आपाटलिपुत्रात् तस्य यदवरं कौशाम्ब्याः तत्र सक्तून् पास्यामः] and not @deva[पातास्मः]; @deva[यः अयं संवत्सरः आगामी तस्य यदवरं आग्रहायण्याः तत्र युक्ता अध्येष्यामहे] and not @deva[अध्येतास्महे]; but when the word @deva[रात्र] is used the First Future may be used; @deva[योयं मासः आगामी तस्य यः अवरः पञ्चदशरात्रः तत्र अध्येतास्महे] we will study in the earlier fortnight of the coming month. When the period of time meant lies beyond a certain point of time, the First or the Second Future may be used; @deva[योऽयं संवत्सरः आगामी तस्य यत्परमाग्रहायण्यास्तत्राध्येष्यामहे] or @deva[अध्येतास्महे], &c.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[नानद्यतनवत्क्रियाप्रबन्धसामीप्ययोः। भविष्यति मर्यादावचनेऽवरस्मिन्। कालविभागे चानहोरात्राणाम्। परस्मिन्विभाषा।] Pān. III. 3. 135-138.

rules.title: Second Future or Present for Immediate Future
rules.body:
## THE SECOND OR SIMPLE FUTURE.

[^1]When the close proximity of a future action is intended, the Second Future or the Present may be used; @deva[कदा गमिष्यसि] when will you go? @deva[एष गच्छामि] or @deva[गमिष्यामि] I shall just go.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[वर्तमानसामीप्ये वर्तमानवद्वा।] Pān. III. 3. 131.

rules.title: Multiple Tenses in Conditional with Hope
rules.body:
[^1]When there is the idea of hope implied in a conditional form, the Aorist, the Present or the Simple Future may be used in both the clauses to denote a future time; @deva[देवश्चेदवर्षीत् वर्षति वर्षिष्यति वा धान्यमवाप्स्म वपामः वप्स्यामः वा।] (Sid. Kau). if it were to rain we would sow corn.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[आशंसायां भूतवच्च।] Pān. III. 3. 132.

rules.title: Simple Future for Courteous Command
rules.body: The Simple Future is sometimes used as a courteous way of command; @deva[पश्चात्सरं प्रति गमिष्यसि] (Vik. IV.) then you will go (i. e. please then go) to the lake, &c.

rules.title: Simple Future with @deva[क्षिप्र] for Hope
rules.body:
[^1]The Simple Future is alone used when the idea of hope is conveyed by @deva[क्षिप्र] and words having the sense of @deva[क्षिप्र]; @deva[वृष्टिश्चेत्क्षिप्रं आशु त्वरितं वा यास्यति शीघ्रं वप्स्यामः] if a shower were to come quickly we would at once sow corn.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[क्षिप्रवचने लृट्।] Pān. III. 3. 133.

rules.title: Second Future for Imperfect with Verbs of Remembering
rules.body: When the word @deva[यत्] is not used with roots meaning 'to remember,' such as @deva[स्मृ], &c. the Second Future is used in the sense of the Imperfect; @deva[स्मरसि कृष्ण गोकुले वत्स्यामः] Krishna, do you remember that we dwelt in Gokula?

rules.title: Simple Future for Disbelief or Intolerance
rules.body:
[^1]When disbelief in or intolerance of an action is intended to be expressed, and especially in the form of a question, the Simple Future is used optionally in the sense of the Potential; @deva[न संभावयामि] or @deva[न मर्षये भवान् हरि निन्देत्] or @deva[निन्दिष्यति] I never believe, or cannot tolerate it, that you would or should speak ill of Hari; @deva[कः] or @deva[कतरः कतमः हरिं निन्देत्] or @deva[निन्दिष्यति] who will speak ill of Hari (I do not believe that any body will, &c.); @deva[कं वृषलं भवान् याजयेत्] or @deva[याजयिष्यति], &c.; when the word @deva[किङ्किल] [^2](a particle, showing great anger) and roots having the sense of 'to be' precede, the Simple Future only should be used; @deva[न संभवामि] or @deva[मर्षये भवान् किङ्किल वृषलं याजयिष्यति] I do not believe or like that you should make a S'udra perform a sacrifice; so @deva[अस्ति भवति विद्यते वा भवान् वृषलं याजयिष्यति।]

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[किंवृत्ते लिङ्लृटौ। अनवक्लृप्त्यमर्षयोरकिंवृत्तेऽपि।] Pān. III. 3. 144, 145.

[^2]: @deva[किंकिलास्त्यर्थेषु लृट्।] Pān. III. 3. 146.

rules.title: Simple Future for Wonder, Doubt, and Certainty
rules.body:
When the idea of wonder is to be expressed and the words @deva[यच्च], @deva[यत्र] and @deva[यदि] do not occur in a sentence, the Simple Future should be used; @deva[आश्चर्यमन्धो नाम कृष्णं द्रक्ष्यति] it is a wonder that a blind man sees Hari.

(a) The Simple Future is also used when the particles @deva[उत] and @deva[अपि] expressing a doubt are used; @deva[उत दण्डः पतिष्यति] will the stick fall? @deva[अपि धास्यति द्वारं] will he close the door?

(b) This Future is also used when the particle @deva[अलं] meaning sure or able is used; @deva[अलं कृष्णो हस्तिनं हनिष्यति] Krishna is sure or able to kill the elephant.

rules.title: Imperative for Command, Entreaty, Blessing, and Advice
rules.body:
## THE MOODS.

## THE IMPERATIVE MOOD

[^1]The Imperative Mood does not express merely command, but also entreaty, benediction, courteous enquiry, gentle advice, ability, &c.

(a) In the second person this Mood is used to express command, entreaty, gentle advice and benedictions or blessings; @deva[गच्छ] (@deva[त्वं]) @deva[कुसुमपुरं] go to Kusumapura; @deva[परित्रायध्वं परित्रायध्वं] help! help! @deva[क्षमस्वापराधं] O God! forgive my faults, &c.; @deva[शुश्रूषस्व गुरून् कुरु प्रियसखीवृत्तिं सपत्नीजने] (S'ak. IV.) serve your elders and treat your co-wives as if they were your friends; @deva[एधि कार्यकरस्त्वं मे गत्वा प्रवद राघवं] be thou my messenger, go to Rāghava, and say to him; @deva[अनन्यभाजं पतिमाप्नुहीति सा तथ्यमेवाभिहता हरेण] she was addressed the truth by Hara when he said 'do thou obtain a husband not devoted to any other lady.'

(b) In the third person it is often used to express a blessing and sometimes gentle command; @deva[विधत्तां सिद्धिं नो…प्रकीर्णः पुष्पाणां हरिचरणयोरञ्जलिरयम्] may this handful of flowers scattered on the feet of Hari give us success; @deva[पर्जन्यः कालवर्षी भवतु] may rain pour down in time; @deva[पश्चात्तिष्ठन्तु वीरा शकनरपतयः] (Mud. V. II.).

(c) In the first person it expresses a question, necessity, ability, &c; @deva[किं करवाणि ते] what should I do for you? @deva[अधुनाहं गच्छानि] I must go now; @deva[करवामैतद्द्वयं देवि प्रियं तव] we will (are able to) do this thing, oh queen, which is agreeable to you; @deva[नहि प्रेष्यवधं घोरं करवाण्यस्तु ते मतिः] (Bhaṭṭi XX. 6.) let your thought be 'I must not commit the horrible murder of an ambassador.'

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[लोट् च।] Pān. III. 3. 162. Vide Pān. III. 3. 161. quoted on the next page.

rules.title: Passive Imperative Third Person for Courtesy
rules.body: The third person singular of the Imperative in the passive voice is often used and sometimes as a courteous form of expression; @deva[आनीयतां राजपुत्रः] the prince should be brought; @deva[श्रूयतां भो पण्डिताः] may you hear, ye Pandits; @deva[एतदासनमास्यतां] take this seat.

rules.title: Imperative After @deva[मुहूर्त] Time Period
rules.body: When time after a @deva[मुहूर्त] (nearly equal to an hour) is expressed, the Imperative is used; @deva[मुहूर्ताद्यजतां स्म] offer the sacrifice after an hour.

rules.title: Imperative with @deva[स्म] for Polite Request
rules.body: The Imperative with the particle @deva[स्म] is used when a request is courteously expressed; @deva[बालमध्यापय स्म] please teach the child.

rules.title: Imperative with @deva[मा] for Present Sense
rules.body: The Imperative has sometimes the force of the present when used in combination with the particle @deva[मा]; @deva[मा भवतु] no, it is not so; @deva[मा च ते नियतः शत्रुन्मन्युर्भवतु पार्थिव।]

rules.title: Imperative with @deva[इच्छामि] for Wishes
rules.body: @deva[इच्छामि भवान्भुञ्जीत] or @deva[भुङ्क्ताम्] I wish you should dine. See @ref[958].

rules.title: Repeated Imperative for Frequency
rules.body:
[^1]There is a peculiar use of the Imperative which ought to be noticed. The Imperative second person singular is repeated when frequency of an act is indicated and the whole used with the root in any tense; @deva[याहि याहि इति याति] (Sid. Kau.) he goes every now and then; so @deva[यात यातेति यूयं याथ; याहि याहीत्ययासीत्; अधीष्वाधीष्वेत्यधीते] he studies steadily. The Imperative second person is also used when several acts are described as done by the same person; @deva[सक्तून् पिब, धानाः खादेत्यभ्यवहरति] (Sid. Kau.) he takes his food, now eating barley, now eating fried rice; similarly @deva[अन्नं भुङ्क्ष्व दाधिकमास्वादयस्वेत्यभ्यवहरते] (Sid. Kau.).

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[क्रियासमभिहारे लोट् लोटो हिस्वौ वा च तध्वमोः। समुच्चयेऽन्यतरस्याम्। यथाविध्यनुप्रयोगः पूर्वस्मिन्। समुच्चये सामान्यवचनस्य।] Pān. III. 4. 1-5. @deva[क्रियासमभिहारे द्वे वाच्ये।] Vārt.

rules.title: Potential Mood for @deva[विधि], @deva[निमन्त्रण], @deva[आमन्त्रण], @deva[अधीष्ट], @deva[संप्रश्न] and @deva[प्रार्थना]
rules.body:
## THE POTENTIAL MOOD.

[^1]The Potential Mood expresses the sense of @deva[विधि] (command, directing a subordinate, &c.), @deva[निमन्त्रण] (pressing invitation), @deva[आमन्त्रण] (giving permission), @deva[अधीष्ट] (telling one to attend to an honorary office or duty), @deva[संप्रश्न] (courteously asking a person a question), and @deva[प्रार्थना] prayer. @deva[यजेत] one should perform a sacrifice; @deva[त्वं ग्रामं गच्छेः] go to the village; @deva[इह भवान् भुञ्जीत] your honour should take food here; @deva[इहासीत भवान्] you may sit here; @deva[पुत्रमध्यापयेद्भवान्] you may teach my son (as an honorary duty); @deva[किं मो वेदमधीयीय उत तर्कम्] what, oh! shall I learn the Veda or logic? @deva[भो भोजनं लभेय] good Sir, can I get food here? i. e. will you kindly give me food? (All these senses are optionally expressed by the Imperative also).

(a) [^2]In the case of the first two senses viz. @deva[विधि] and @deva[निमन्त्रण] and in that of 'proper time', the potential participle may also be used for the Potential; @deva[भवता यष्टव्यम्], &c.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[विधिनिमन्त्रणामन्त्रणाधीष्टसंप्रश्नप्रार्थनेषु लिङ्।] Pān. III. 3. 161

[^2]: @deva[प्रैषातिसर्गप्राप्तकालेषु कृत्याश्च॥] Pān. III. 3. 163.

rules.title: Potential or Participle After @deva[मुहूर्त]
rules.body:
[^1]When the words 'after an hour' are used the Potential (also Imperative) or the Potential participle may be used; @deva[मुहूर्तादूर्ध्वं यजेत, यजतां, यष्टव्यं वा] (Sid. Kau.).

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[लिङ्चोर्ध्वमौहूर्तिके।] Pān. III. 3. 164.

rules.title: Potential with @deva[काल], @deva[समय], and @deva[वेला] for Time
rules.body:
[^1]The Potential is used with the words @deva[काल], @deva[समय] and @deva[वेला], when the word @deva[यत्] is used; @deva[कालः समयः वेला वा यद्भुञ्जीत भवान्] it is time now that you should dine.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[लिङ् यदि।] Pān. III. 3. 168.

rules.title: Potential or Participle for Fitness and Capability
rules.body:
[^1]When the idea of fitness is to be expressed the Potential or the Potential participle may be used; and sometimes the noun in @deva[तृ] also; @deva[त्वं कन्यां वहेः], @deva[त्वं कन्यायाः वोढा] or @deva[त्वया कन्या वोढव्या] you are fit to marry the girl.

(a) The Potential or the Potential participle may be used when the sense of capability is implied; @deva[भारं त्वं वहेः] or @deva[भारस्त्वया वोढव्यः] thou canst (art able to) carry the load.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[अर्हे कृत्यतृचश्च। शकि लिङ् च।] Pān. III. 3. 169, 172.

rules.title: Potential or Future with Interrogatives for Censure and Wonder
rules.body:
[^1]With interrogative words such as @deva[किं], @deva[कतर], @deva[कतम], &c. the Potential or the Simple Future may be used when censure is implied (see @ref[937]); @deva[कः कतरो वा हरि निन्देत् निन्दिष्यति वा।]

(a) When wonder is implied the simple Future is used in preference to the Potential if the word @deva[यदि] be not used; @deva[आश्चर्यं अन्धो नाम कृष्णं द्रक्ष्यति] it is a wonder that a blind man should see Hari, but @deva[आश्चर्यं यदि साध्वधीयीत] it is wonder if he study.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[किंवृत्ते (गर्हायां) लिङ्लृटौ।] Pān. III. 3. 144. (@deva[चित्रीकरणे]) @deva[शेषे लृङ्यदौ।] Pān III 3. 151.

rules.title: Potential for Hope Without @deva[कच्चित्]
rules.body:
[^1]When hope is expressed without the use of the word @deva[कच्चित्] the potential is generally used; @deva[कामो मे भुञ्जीत भवान्] it is my desire (I hope) that you will eat; but @deva[कच्चिज्जीवति] I hope he lives.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[कामप्रवेदने कच्चिति।] Pān III. 3. 153.

rules.title: Potential or Second Future for Expectation Without @deva[यद्]
rules.body:
[^1]When the sense of 'I expect' is implied, the Potential or the 2nd Future may be used provided the word @deva[यद्] is not used; @deva[संभावयामि भुञ्जीत भोक्ष्यते वा भवान्] I expect you will eat; but @deva[संभावयामि यद्भुञ्जीथास्त्वम्] (Sid. Kau).

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[विभाषा धातौ संभावनवचनेऽयदि।] Pān. III. 3. 155.

rules.title: Potential or Simple Future in Conditionals
rules.body:
[^1]When in a conditional sentence one thing is expressed as depending upon another as effect upon a cause, the Potential or the Simple Future may be used; @deva[कृष्णं नमेच्चेत्सुखं यायात्] if he will bow to Krishna he will attain happiness; so @deva[कृष्णं नंस्यति चेत्सुखं यास्यति।]

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[हेतुहेतुमतोर्लिङ्।] Pān III. 3. 156.

rules.title: Potential or Imperative with Verbs of Wishing
rules.body:
[^1]When words having the sense of 'to wish,' such as @deva[इष्], @deva[कम्]. &c. are used, the Potential or Imperative is used; @deva[इच्छामि भवान्भुञ्जीत] or @deva[भुङ्क्ताम्] I wish you should dine; @deva[इच्छामि सोमं पिबेत् पिबतु वा भवान्] (Sid. Kau) I wish Your Honour will drink Soma.

(a) But when the agents of both the actions are the same, the Potential alone is used in the sense of the Infinitive; @deva[भुञ्जीयेतीच्छति] (Sid. Kau.) i. e. @deva[भोक्तुमिच्छति] wishes that he will eat (wishes to eat).

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[इच्छार्थेषु लिङ्लोटौ। लिङ् च।] Pān III. 3. 157. 159.

rules.title: Impersonal Potential for Precepts
rules.body: Sometimes the Potential is used without a subject when it is used in the sense of 'a precept or advice'; @deva[आपदर्थे धनं रक्षेद्दारान् रक्षेद्धनैरपि। आत्मानं सततं रक्षेद्दारैरपि धनैरपि॥] (a man) should save money for adversity, he should save his wife at the cost of his wealth and himself even at the expense of his wife and wealth; @deva[यद्यद्रोचेत विप्रेभ्यस्तत्तद्दद्यादमत्सरः] (one) should serve Brāhmaṇas with all that they like, without being jealous.

rules.title: Benedictive for Blessings and Wishes
rules.body:
## THE BENEDICTIVE MOOD.

The Benedictive Mood is used to confer a blessing or to express the speaker's wish; @deva[चिरं जीव्यात् भवान्] may you live long! @deva[वर्धिषीष्ठाः स्वजातेषु वध्यास्त्वं रिपुसंहतिः। भूयास्त्वं गुणिनां मान्यस्तेषां स्थेया व्यवस्थितौ॥] (Bhaṭṭi. XIX. 26); @deva[कृतार्थः भूयासम्] may I be successful!

rules.title: Conditional for Unfulfilled Conditions
rules.body:
## THE CONDITIONAL.

[^1]The Conditional is used in those conditional sentences in which the Potential may be used when the nonperformance of the action is implied or in which the falsity of the antecedent is involved as a matter of fact. It expresses both future and past time. It must be used in both the antecedent and the consequent clauses; @deva[सुवृष्टिश्चेदभविष्यत्तदा सुभिक्षमभविष्यत्] if there would be plentiful rain there would be an abundance of corn; @deva[यदि सुरभिमवाप्स्यस्तन्मुखोच्छ्वासगन्धं तव रतिरभविष्यत्पुण्डरीके किमस्मिन्] hadst thou obtained (which thou hast not) the sweet fragrance of her breath, wouldst thou have had any liking for this lotus?

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[लिङ्निमित्ते लृङ् क्रियातिपत्तौ।] Pān. III. 3 139 @deva[हेतुहेतुमद्भावादि लिङ्निमित्तं तत्र भविष्यत्यर्थे लृङ् स्यात् क्रियायाः अनिष्पत्तौ गम्यमानायाम्।] Sid. Kau.

rules.title: Conditional Optional for Past Actions
rules.body:
*Obs.* [^1]When a past action is to be indicated the Conditional may be optionally used in the sense of the Potential; @deva[कथं नाम तत्रभवान्धर्ममत्यक्ष्यत्] or @deva[त्यजेः] how could you give up your religion?

(a) Also where the Potential is used in conjunction with the particles @deva[उत, अपि, जातु] &c; @deva[अपि तत्र रिपुः सीतां नार्थयिष्यत दुर्मतिः। क्रूरं जात्ववदिष्यच्च जात्वस्तोष्यच्छ्रियं स्वकाम्॥ संकल्पं नाकरिष्यच्च तत्रेयं शुद्धमानसा। (मृषा) सत्यामर्षमवाप्स्यस्त्वं राम सीतानिबन्धनम्॥] (Bhaṭṭi. XXI. 3. 4.)

(b) When wonder is to be expressed the Conditional is optionally used where the Potential is used in combination with the particles @deva[यच्च], @deva[यत्र] or @deva[यदि] when the action does not take place; @deva[आश्चर्यं यत्र यत्र स्त्री कृच्छ्रेऽवर्त्स्यन्मते तव। प्रासादस्यां विनष्टायां किं किमालप्स्यथाः फलम्॥] (Bhaṭṭi XXI. 8).

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[भूते च] Pān. III. 3 140

rules.title: Neuter Singulars as Adverbs; @deva[विधा] and @deva[पूर्वम्]
rules.body:
## SECTION V. Indeclinables.

## ADVERBS.

The *neu.* singulars of the Nominative and other cases of several nouns are used as adverbs; @deva[चिरं] or @deva[चिरेण] or @deva[चिराद्ध्यात्वा] having contemplated for a long time; @deva[दुःखं] or @deva[दुःखेन तिष्ठति] he is in distress; so @deva[सुखं] or @deva[सुखेन] &c.

(a) The word @deva[विधा] is used adverbially in combination with several words such as @deva[बहु, नाना], &c.; @deva[बहुविधं, नानाविधं] in various ways. The word @deva[पूर्वं] is also used adverbially as the latter member of a compound when some action is to be expressed as having happened before; @deva[सान्त्वपूर्वं] having said something by way of consolation; @deva[बुद्धिपूर्वम्] thoughtfully, (*i. e.* thought preceding a certain action); @deva[अबुद्धिपूर्वं भगवन्धेनुरेषा हता मया] O venerable Sir, I killed this cow unwittingly; @deva[शपथपूर्वं अकथयत] &c.

rules.title: Reference to Previous Discussion of Prepositions
rules.body:
## PREPOSITIONS.

The use of Prepositions has already been explained at @ref[365]-@ref[371]. The Prepositions governing cases are already noticed under the various cases.

rules.title: General Note on Conjunctions
rules.body:
## CONJUNCTIONS.

The use of Conjunctions has not many syntactical Peculiarities and needs no special notice here. They are used in their proper senses in sentences.

rules.title: Special Uses of @deva[च] Conjunction
rules.body:
The most important of these conjunctions and the one very frequently used is @deva[च]. It can never stand first in a sentence; nor can it be used like 'and' in English. It is used with such of the words or assertions it connects or is placed after the last of the words or assertions it joins together; @deva[रामश्च लक्ष्मणश्च] or @deva[रामः लक्ष्मणश्च]; @deva[कामश्च जृम्भितगुणो नवयौवनं च] love with its excellences expanded, and fresh youth; @deva[कुलेन कान्त्या वयसा नवेन गुणैश्च तैस्तैर्विनयप्रधानैः।]

(a) Sometimes this particle has a disjunctive force; @deva[शान्तमिदमाश्रमपदं स्फुरति च बाहुः]—the hermitage is tranquil yet my arm throbs.

(b) Rarely this particle is used in the sense of 'if'; @deva[जीवितुं चेच्छसि मूढ हेतुं मे गदतः शृणु] oh fool, if you wish to live, &c.

(c) Sometimes it is used as an expletive; @deva[भीमः पार्थस्तथैव च].

(d) Sometimes it is used to connect a subordinate fact with a main one @deva[भिक्षामट गां चानय] wander for alms and bring a cow: @deva[कुट्टिनी च शासिता गोपी च निःसारिता कंदर्पकेतुश्च पुरस्कृतः] the procuress was chastised, the cowherdess was expelled and Kandarpaketu was honoured.

(e) When the particle is repeated it has sometimes the sense of 'on the one hand,' 'on the other hand,' 'and yet,' @deva[क्व च हरिणकानां जीवितं चातिलोलं क्व च निशितनिपाता वज्रसाराः शरास्ते] where, on the one hand, is the extremely frail life of fawns, and where, on the other, are thy arrows hard like adamant and falling sharply; @deva[न सुलभा सकलेन्दुमुखी च सा किमपि चेदमनङ्गविचेष्टितम्।] on the one hand the full moon-faced lady is not easy to obtain and yet there is this unaccountable sport of love.

(f) Sometimes the repetition of @deva[च] shows the simultaneous or undelayed occurrence of two events; @deva[ते च प्रापुरुदन्वन्तं बुबुधे चादिपूरुषः] they reached the ocean and at the same time the primeval Being also awoke.

rules.title: @deva[तथा] as Substitute for @deva[च]
rules.body: @deva[तथा] 'likewise' often supplies the place of @deva[च]; @deva[रामस्तथा लक्ष्मणश्च] Rāma and Lakshmaṇa; @deva[अनागतविधाता च प्रत्युत्पन्नमतिस्तथा] both Anāgatavidhāta and Pratyutpannamati, @deva[तथा हि] means 'for instance, to be more plain;' @deva[तथा च] 'likewise;' both are often used introducing quotations.

rules.title: @deva[तु], @deva[हि], and @deva[वा] Excluded from the First Place
rules.body: @deva[तु] but, @deva[हि] for, because, and @deva[वा] are also excluded from the first place in a sentence. @deva[आत्मा पुत्रः सखा भार्या कृच्छ्रं तु दुहिता किल] the son is one's own self, the wife one's friend, but the daughter a source of anxiety; @deva[अप्याज्ञया शासितुरात्मना वा प्राप्तोसि संभावयितुं वनान्माम्। कालो ह्ययं संक्रमितुं द्वितीयं सर्वोपकारक्षममाश्रमं ते।] (V. 10.); @deva[अस्त्राणि वा शरीरं वा वरय] choose either the missiles or your person.

rules.title: @deva[यदि] and @deva[चेत्] with Potential and Conditional
rules.body: @deva[यदि] and @deva[चेत्] 'if' are usually used with the Potential or the Conditional; as @deva[यदि सोत्र सन्निहितो भवेत् तर्हि मम साहाय्यं कुर्यात्] if he were here he would assist me; @deva[यदि देवदत्तोत्राभविष्यन्नूनमेतदकरिष्यत्] had Devadatta been here, he would have undoubtedly done this; but they are also construed with the Present Indicative; @deva[यदि जीवति भद्राणि पश्यति] if he lives he will see prosperity; @deva[यदि मया देवपादानां प्रयोजनमस्ति] if Your Majesty has any thing to do with me, &c; @deva[शापितोसि मम जीवितेन यदि वाचा न कथयसि] I conjure you by my life if you will not tell it in words. @deva[चेत्] is never used at the beginning of a sentence; @deva[तं चेत्सहस्रकिरणो धुरि नाकरिष्यत्] (S'ak. VII. 4) if the thousand-rayed one (sun) did not place him at the yoke of his car, @deva[अयि रोषमुरीकरोषि] (have recourse to) @deva[नो चेत्] &c Bha. V. I. 44.

rules.title: Six Uses of @deva[अथ] Particle
rules.body:
## The Particles @deva[अथ] and @deva[इति].

[^1]@deva[अथ] is used in the following senses:—(1) as a sign of auspiciousness [^2]; @deva[अथातो ब्रह्मजिज्ञासा] now begins the inquiry about Brahma; *cf.* the Bhāṣya on this sūtra (2) marks the beginning or commencement of a work; @deva[अथेदमारभ्यते प्रथमं तन्त्रम्] now is begun the 1st Tantra; so @deva[अथ योगानुशासनम्], &c; (3) 'then' after that,' &c; @deva[अथ प्रजानामधिप.] &c. (Rag. II. 1.) After that i. e. passing of the night) the lord of the earth, &c. (4) asks a question @deva[अथ भगवान् लोकानुग्रहाय कुशली काश्यपः] is the venerable Kashyapa all right that he may oblige the world? @deva[अथ शक्नोषि भोक्तुं] are you able to eat? (5) 'and, including'; @deva[भीमः अथ अर्जुनः] Bhīma and also Arjuna; (6) 'if;' @deva[अथ मरणमवश्यमेव जन्तोः] if death is sure to befall a creature, &c.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: @deva[मङ्गलानन्तरारम्भप्रश्नकात्स्न्येष्वथो अथ।] Amara

[^2]: Properly speaking this is not the sense of @deva[अथ]. The mere utterance or hearing of this word if considered as auspicious as the word is supposed to have emanated from the throat of Brahmā

rules.title: Six Uses of @deva[इति] Particle
rules.body:
As @deva[अथ] marks the beginning, so @deva[इति] marks the close of a composition. This particle is used in the following senses; (1) to quote the exact words spoken by some one, thus taking the place of the quotation marks and being used generally after the words quoted; [^1]@deva[देव काचिच्चण्डालकन्यका शुकमादाय देवं विज्ञापयति…देवपादमूलमागताहमिच्छामि देवदर्शनसुखमनुभवितुमिति।] O lord a certain *Chandāla* girl requests Your Majesty (saying)……" I who have come to your majesty's feet wish to enjoy the happiness of the sight of Your Majesty;' @deva[ब्राह्मणाः ऊचुः कृतकृत्याः स्म इति] the Brāhmaṇas said " we have accomplished our objects; " (2) cause (rendered in English because, since &c.); @deva[वैदेशिकोस्मीति पृच्छामि] I ask you because I am a foreigner; @deva[पुराणमित्येव न साधु सर्वं] every thing is not good simply because it is old; (3) purpose or motive; @deva[मा भूदाश्रमपीडेति परिमेयपुरःसरः] they two took a limited number of servants with them that there should be no disturbance, &c.; (4) so, thus; as follows; @deva[रामाभिधानो हरिरित्युवाच।] (5) in the capacity of, as regards; @deva[पितेति स पूज्यः गुरुरिति निन्द्यः] as a father he ought to be respected, as a teacher ought to be censured; (6) to state an opinion; @deva[इति आश्मरथ्यः] this is the opinion of Āśmarathya. It is often used by commentators in the sense of 'according to the rule'; @deva[इति शक्यार्थे लिङ्] &c. &c.

---

## Footnotes

[^1]: In Sanskrit there is no indirect construction, so that in translating indirect constructions the actual words of the speaker followed by @deva[इति] must be used.

rules.title: Illustration of Interjections from Bhaṭṭi Kāvya
rules.body:
## INTERJECTIONS.

The following stanza from the Bhaṭṭi Kāvya illustrates the uses of some of these interjections:—

@deva[आः कष्टं बत ही चित्रं हूं मातर्देवतानि धिक्।
हा पितः कासि हे सुष्ठु बह्वेवं विललाप सः॥]

rules.title: Prose and Verse in Sanskrit Poetry
rules.body:
## Prose and Verse in Sanskrit Poetry

This appendix treats of **Prosody**.[^1]

Poetical composition in Sanskrit may be in the form of @deva[गद्य] prose, or '@deva[पद्य]' verse or metrical composition.[^2]

[^1]: The earliest writer on Prosody is Pingalāchārya. His work is known as "The Pingalachhandas-s'āstra." It is written in Sūtras and is divided into eight books. The Agni Purāṇa also deals with the subject very fully. The present chapter, however, is chiefly based on the Vṛttaratnākar and Chhandomañjarī.

[^2]: @deva[काव्यं गद्यं च पद्यं च तद्द्विधैव व्यवस्थितम्] । Dandin. Kāv. Pr. I.

rules.title: Definition and Basis of Sanskrit Prosody
rules.body:
## Definition and Basis of Sanskrit Prosody

Prosody treats of the laws of versification or metrical composition. Sanskrit verse is regulated by quantity, not by accent.

rules.title: Structure of a Stanza: Pāda, Syllable, and Mātrā
rules.body:
## Structure of a Stanza: Pāda, Syllable, and Mātrā

A @deva[पद्य] or stanza consists of four lines each called a pāda or quarter. A pāda is regulated either by the number of syllables (@deva[अक्षर]) or by the number of syllabic instants (@deva[मात्रा]).

(a) A syllable is as much of a word as can be uttered distinctly by one effort of the voice i. e. a single vowel with or without one or more consonants.

(b) A mātrā (@deva[मात्रा]) is the measure of time required to pronounce a short vowel.

rules.title: Light and Heavy Syllables
rules.body:
## Light and Heavy Syllables

A syllable is @deva[लघु] 'light,' or @deva[गुरु] 'heavy' according as its vowel is short or long.

(a) The vowels @deva[अ], @deva[इ], @deva[उ], @deva[ऋ] and @deva[लृ] are short; and the vowels @deva[आ], @deva[ई], @deva[ऊ], @deva[ॠ], @deva[ए], @deva[ऐ], @deva[ओ] and @deva[औ] are long.[^1] When a short vowel is followed by an Anuswāra or Visarga or by a conjunct consonant, it is converted into what is called 'a prosodially long vowel;' as @deva[गन्ध], @deva[अच्छ], &c.

[^1]: @deva[सानुस्वारश्च दीर्घश्च विसर्गी च गुरुर्भवेत् ।]

rules.title: Treatment of Final Syllable in a Pāda
rules.body:
## Treatment of Final Syllable in a Pāda

The last syllable of a pāda is either heavy or light according as the exigence of the metre requires it, whatever be its natural length; [^1]as in @deva[वक्षस्थली रक्षतु सा जगन्ति], &c. (Vik. I.); @deva[तस्याः खुरन्यासपवित्रपांसुम्] (Rag. II. 2.)

[^1]: Vide Vṛttaratnākara I. 9. @deva[वर्णः संयोगपूर्वश्च तथा पादान्तगोपि वा ॥] Chhandomañjarī.

rules.title: Eight Gaṇas (Syllabic Feet)
Five Mātrā Gaṇas
Vṛtta and Jāti: Two Types of Metrical Stanzas
rules.body:
## Vṛtta and Jāti: Two Types of Metrical Stanzas

A *padya* or stanza may be either a @deva[वृत्त] or a @deva[जाति].

(a) A Vṛtta is a stanza the metre of which is regulated by the number and position of syllables in each pāda or quarter.

(b) A Jāti is a stanza the metre of which is regulated by the number of syllabic instants in each Pāda or quarter.

rules.title: Three Types of Vṛtta
rules.body:
## Three Types of Vṛtta

A Vṛtta again is of three kinds;[^1] (1) @deva[समवृत्त] or that in which all the quarters are similar; (2) @deva[अर्धसमवृत्त] or that in which the alternate quarters are similar; and (3) @deva[विषम] or that in which the quarters are all dissimilar.

[^1]: @deva[सममर्धसमं वृत्तं विषमं च यथा परम् ॥ अङ्घ्रयो यस्य चत्वारस्तुल्यलक्षणलक्षिताः । तच्छंदःशास्त्रतत्त्वज्ञाः समं वृत्तं प्रचक्षते ॥ प्रथमांघ्रिसमो यस्य तृतीयश्चरणो भवेत् । द्वितीयस्तुर्यवद्वृत्तं तदर्धसममुच्यते ॥ यस्य पादचतुष्केपि लक्ष्म भिन्नं परस्परम् । तदाहुर्विषमं वृत्तं छन्दःशास्त्रविशारदाः ॥]

rules.title: Twenty-Six Classes of Samavṛttas
rules.body:
## Twenty-Six Classes of Samavṛttas

There are 26 classes of Samavṛttas or regular metres generally accepted. This classification rests on the number of syllables in each quarter which may very from one to twenty-six. Each of these classes comprises a variety of metres all differing from one another according to the combination of the various ganas.

rules.title: Yati (Caesura)
rules.body:
## Yati (Caesura)

Yati (@deva[यति]) is the Sanskrt name for the cæsura or pause which may be made in reciting a quarter or verse.

rules.title: Scope of Metres Covered
rules.body:
## Scope of Metres Covered

Only the metres in common use with their schemes in Gaṇas will be given here; all unimportant metres, as well as Vedic and Prākṛta metres will be ignored.

rules.title: Comprehensive Catalogue of Samavṛttas (Section I)
rules.body:
## Section I. Samavṛttas

*Metres with 8 Syllables to a Pāda.*

### (1) @deva[अनुष्टुभ्] or @deva[श्लोक].

This is the commonest of all Sanskrt metres; it forms the chief metre of the great epics and many of the Purāṇas, There are many Varieties of this metre; but that in common use has eight syllables in a Pāda the fifth being short (though occasional variations from these rules occur in the Mahābhārata and the Rāmāyaṇa):—

Ex.:—Vide Ist canto of Rag.

### (2) @deva[गजगति] (4. 4.)

Def. @deva[नभलगा गजगतिः ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[न भ ल ग] ⏑ ⏑ ⏑ | – ⏑ ⏑ | ⏑ –

Ex. @deva[रविसुतापरिसरे विहरतो दृशि हरेः ।]
@deva[व्रजवधूगजगतिर्मुदमलं व्यतनुत ॥]

### (3) @deva[प्रमाणिका] (4. 4.)

Def. @deva[प्रमाणिका जरौ लगौ ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[ज, र, ल, ग.] ⏑ – ⏑ | – ⏑ – | ⏑ –

Ex. @deva[पुनातु भक्तिरच्युता सदा च्युतांघ्रिपद्मयोः ।]
@deva[श्रुतिस्मृतिप्रमाणिका भवांबुराशितारिका ॥]

### (4) @deva[माणवक] (4. 4.)

Def. @deva[भात्तलगा माणवकम् ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[भ, त, ल, ग,] – ⏑ ⏑ | – – ⏑ | ⏑ –

Ex. @deva[चंचलचूडं चपलैर्वत्सकुलैः केलिपरम् ।]
@deva[ध्याय सखे स्मेरमुखं नन्दसुतं माणवकम् ॥]

### (5) @deva[विद्युन्माला] (4. 4.)

Def. @deva[मो मो गो गो विद्युन्माला ।]

Sch. G. @deva[म, म, ग. ग,] – – – | – – – | – –

Ex. @deva[वासोवल्ली विद्युन्माला बर्हश्रेणी शक्रश्चापः ।]
@deva[यस्मिन्नास्तां तापोच्छित्त्यै गोमध्यस्थः कृष्णांभोदः ॥]

### (6) @deva[समानिका] (4. 4.)

Def. @deva[ग्लौ रजौ समानिका तु ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[र, ज, ग, ल] – ⏑ – | ⏑ – ⏑ | ⏑ –

Ex. @deva[यस्य कृष्णपादपद्ममस्ति हृत्तडागसद्म ।]
@deva[धीः समानिका परेण नोचितात्र मत्सरेण ॥]

---

*Metres with 9 Syllables in a quarter.*

(@deva[बृहती])

### (1) @deva[भुजगशिशुभृता] (7. 2)

Def. @deva[भुजगशिशुभृता नौ मः ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[न, न. म.] ⏑ ⏑ ⏑ | ⏑ ⏑ ⏑ | – – –

Ex. @deva[हृदतटनिकटक्षौणी भुजगशिशुभृता याऽसीत् ।]
@deva[मुरिपुदलिते नागे व्रजजनसुखदा साभूत् ॥]

### (2) @deva[भुजंगसंगता] (3. 6)

Def. @deva[सजरैर्भुजंगसंगता ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[स, ज, र,] ⏑ ⏑ – | ⏑ – ⏑ | – ⏑ –

Ex. @deva[तरलतरंगिरिंगितैर्यमुना भुजगसंगता ।]
@deva[कथमेति वत्सचारकश्चपलः सदैव तां हरिः ॥]

### (3) @deva[मणिमध्यं] (5. 4)

Def. @deva[स्यान्मणिमध्यं चेद्भमसाः ॥]

Sch. of G. @deva[भ, म, स,] – ⏑ ⏑ | – – – | ⏑ ⏑ –

Ex. @deva[कालियभोगाभोगगतस्तन्मणिमध्यस्फीतरुचा ।]
@deva[चित्रपदाभो नंदसुतश्चारु ननर्त स्मेरमुखः ॥]

---

*Metres with 10 Syllables in a quarter.*

(@deva[पंक्तिः])

### (1) @deva[त्वरितगतिः] (5. 5)

Def. @deva[त्वरितगतिश्च नजनगैः ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[न, ज, न, ग.] ⏑ ⏑ ⏑ | ⏑ – ⏑ | ⏑ ⏑ ⏑ | –

Ex. @deva[त्वरितगतिर्व्रजयुवतिस्तरणिसुता विपिनगता ।]
@deva[मुरिपुणा रतिगुरुणा परिरमिता प्रमदमिता ।]

### (2) @deva[मत्ता] (4. 6)

Def. @deva[ज्ञेया मत्ता मभसगमृष्टा ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[म, भ, स, ग.] – – – | – ⏑ ⏑ | ⏑ ⏑ – | –

Ex. @deva[पीत्वा मत्ता मधु मधुपाली कालिंदीये तटवनकुंजे ।]
@deva[उद्दीव्यंतीर्व्रजजनरामाः कामासक्ता मधुजिति चक्रे ॥]

### (3) @deva[रुक्मवती] (5. 5.)

(Also called @deva[चंपकमाला])

Def. @deva[रुक्मवती सा यत्र भमस्गाः ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[भ, म, स, ग.] – ⏑ ⏑ | – – – | ⏑ ⏑ – | –

Ex. @deva[कायमनोवाक्यैः परिशुद्धैर्यस्य सदा कंसद्विषि भक्तिः ।]
@deva[राज्यपदे हर्म्यालिरुदारा रुक्मवती विघ्नः खलु तस्य ॥]

---

*Metres with 11 Syllables in a quarter.*

(@deva[त्रिष्टुभ्])

### (1) @deva[इंद्रवज्रा] (5. 6.)

Def. @deva[स्यादिन्द्रवज्रा यदि तौ जगौ गः ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[त, त, ज, ग. ग.] – – ⏑ | – – ⏑ | ⏑ – ⏑ | – –

Ex. @deva[गोष्ठे गिरिं सव्यकरेण धृत्वा रुष्टेन्द्रवज्राहतिमुक्तवृष्टौ ।]
@deva[यो गोकुलं गोपकुलं च सुस्थं चक्रे स नो रक्षतु चक्रपाणिः ॥]

### (2) @deva[उपेन्द्रवज्रा] (5. 6)

Def. @deva[उपेन्द्रवज्रा जतजास्ततो गौ ।]

Sch of G. @deva[ज, त, ज, ग, ग,] ⏑ – ⏑ | – – ⏑ | ⏑ – ⏑ | – –

Ex. @deva[उपेन्द्रवज्रादिमणिच्छटाभिर्विभूषणानां छुरितं वपुस्ते ।]
@deva[स्मरामि गोपीभिरुपास्यमानं सुरद्रुमूले मणिमण्डपस्थम् ॥]

### (3) @deva[उपजाति.]

Def. @deva[अनन्तरोदीरितलक्ष्मभाजौ पादौ यदीयावुपजातयस्ताः ।]
@deva[इत्थं किलान्यास्वपि मिश्रितासु वदंति जातिष्विदमेव नाम ॥]

Sch. of G.—A mixture of @deva[इन्द्रवज्रा] and @deva[उपेन्द्रवज्रा] gives rise to the metre called @deva[उपजाति]. It is said to have fourteen different varisties. For examples see Rag. II. &c, Kum. III. Kir. XVII. Bhaṭṭi. II. &c.

When other two metres are mixed in one stanza, the mixture is still called Upajāti, as in the following verse from the S'isupālavadha which is a combination of @deva[वंशस्थविल] and @deva[इन्द्रवंशा]—

@deva[इत्थं रथाश्वेभनिषादिनां प्रगे गजो नृपाणामथ तोरणाद्बहिः ।]
@deva[प्रस्थानकालक्षमवेशकल्पनाकृतक्षणक्षेपमुदैक्षताच्युतम् ॥]

### (4) @deva[दोधकम्.] (6. 5)

Def. @deva[दोधकमिच्छति भत्रितयाद्गौ ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[भ, भ, ग, ग,] – ⏑ ⏑ | – ⏑ ⏑ | – ⏑ ⏑ | – –

Ex. @deva[देव सदोध कदम्बतलस्थ श्रीधर तावक नामपदं ते ।]
@deva[कण्ठतले सुविनिर्गमकाले स्वल्पमणिक्षणमेष्यति योगम् ॥]

### (5) @deva[भ्रमरविलसितम्] (5. 7)

Def. @deva[म्भौ न्लौ गः स्याद्भ्रमरविलसितम् ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[म, भ, न, ल, ग,] – – – | – ⏑ ⏑ | ⏑ ⏑ ⏑ | ⏑ –

Ex. @deva[मुग्धे मानं परिहर न चिरात्तारुण्यं ते सफलयतु हरिः ।]
@deva[फुल्ला वल्ली भ्रमरविलसिताभावे शोभां कलयतु किमु ताम् ॥]

### (5) @deva[रथोद्धता] (3. 8 or 4. 7)

Def. @deva[रान्नराविह रथोद्धता लगौ ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[र न र ल ग.] – ⏑ – | ⏑ ⏑ ⏑ | – ⏑ – | ⏑ –

Ex. @deva[राधिका दधिविलोडनास्थिता कृष्णवेणुनिनदैरथोद्धता ।]
@deva[यामुनं तटनिकुञ्जमञ्जसा सा जगाम सलिलाहृतिच्छलात् ॥]

### (6) @deva[शालिनी] (4. 7)

Def. @deva[शालिन्युक्ता म्तौ तगौ गोऽब्धिलोकैः ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[म, त, त, ग, ग.] – – – | – – ⏑ | – – ⏑ | – –

Def. @deva[अंधो हन्ति ज्ञानवृद्धिं विधत्ते धर्मं दत्ते काममर्थं च सूते ।]
@deva[मुक्तिं दत्ते सर्वदोपास्यमाना पुंसां श्रद्धाशालिनी विष्णुभक्तिः ॥]

### (6) @deva[स्वागता] (3. 8)

Def. @deva[स्वागता रनभगैर्गुरुणा च ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[र, न, भ, ग, ग.] – ⏑ – | ⏑ ⏑ ⏑ | – ⏑ ⏑ | – –

Ex. @deva[यस्य चेतसि सदा मुरवैरी बल्लवीजनविलासविलोलः ।]
@deva[तस्य नूनममरालयभाजः स्वागतादरकरः सुरराजः ॥]

---

*Metres with 12 Syllables in a quarter.*

(@deva[जगती])

### (1) @deva[वंशस्थविल] also called @deva[वंशस्थ] and @deva[वंशस्तनित] (5. 7)

Def. @deva[वदन्ति वंशस्थविलं जतौ जरौ]

Sch. of G. @deva[ज, त. ज. र.] ⏑ – ⏑ | – – ⏑ | ⏑ – ⏑ | – ⏑ –

Ex. @deva[विलासवंशस्थविलं मुखानिलैः प्रपूर्य यः पञ्चमरागमुद्गिरन् ।]
@deva[व्रजाङ्गनानामपि गानशालिनां जहार मानं स हरिः पुनातु नः ॥]

### (2) @deva[इन्द्रवंशा]

Def. @deva[तथेन्द्रवंशा प्रथमाक्षरे गुरौ] i. e. the same as the Vams'asthavila except that its first syllable is long.

Sch. of G. @deva[त त ज र.] – – ⏑ | – – ⏑ | – ⏑ – | – ⏑ –

Ex. @deva[दैत्येन्द्रवंशाभिरुदीर्णदीधितिः पीताम्बरोसौ जगतां तमोपहः ।]
@deva[यस्मिन्ममज्जुः शलभा इव स्वयं ते कंसचाणूरमुखा मखद्विषः ॥]

### (3) @deva[चन्द्रवर्त्म] (4. 8.)

Def. @deva[चन्द्रवर्त्म निगदन्ति रनभसैः ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[र, न, भ, स.] – ⏑ – | ⏑ ⏑ ⏑ | ⏑ ⏑ | ⏑ ⏑ –

Ex. @deva[चन्द्रवर्त्म पिहितं घनतिमिरैः राजवर्त्म रहितं जनगमनैः ।]
@deva[इष्टवर्त्म तदलंकुरु सरसे कुंजवर्त्मनि हरिस्तव कुतुकी ॥]

### (4) @deva[जलधरमाला] (4. 8)

Def. @deva[मो भस्मौ चेज्जलधरमालाब्ध्यन्त्यैः ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[म. भ. स. म.] – – – | – ⏑ ⏑ | ⏑ ⏑ – | – – –

Ex. @deva[या भक्तानां कलिदुरितोत्तप्तानां तापच्छेदे जलधरमाला नव्या ।]
@deva[भव्याकारा दिनकरपुत्रीकूले केलीलोला हरितनुर्व्यात्सा वः ॥]

### (5) @deva[जलोद्धतगतिः] (6. 6)

Def. @deva[जसौ जसयुतौ जलोद्धतगतिः ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[ज, स, ज, स.] ⏑ – ⏑ | ⏑ ⏑ – | ⏑ – ⏑ | ⏑ ⏑ –

Ex. @deva[यदीयहलतो विलोक्य विपदं कलिन्दतनया जलोद्धतगतिः ।]
@deva[विलासविपिनं विवेश सहसा करोतु कुशलं हरिः स जगताम् ॥]

### (6) @deva[तामरसम्] (5. 7)

Def. @deva[इह वद तामरसं ननजा यः ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[न न ज य.] ⏑ ⏑ ⏑ | ⏑ – ⏑ | ⏑ – ⏑ | ⏑ – –

Ex. @deva[स्फुटसुषमामकरन्दमनोज्ञं व्रजललनानयनालिनिपीतम् ।]
@deva[तव मुखतामरसं मुरशत्रो हृदयतडागविकाशि ममास्तु ॥]

### (7) @deva[तोटकम्] (4. 4.)

Def. @deva[वद तोटकमब्धिसकारयुतम् ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[स, स, स, स.] ⏑ ⏑ – | ⏑ ⏑ – | ⏑ ⏑ – | ⏑ ⏑ –

Ex. @deva[यमुनातटमच्युतकेलिकलालसदङ्घ्रिसरोरुहसङ्गरुचिम् ।]
@deva[मुदितोऽट कलरपनेतुमघ यदिचेच्छासि जन्म निज सफलम् ॥]

### (8) @deva[द्रुतविलम्बितम्] (4. 8 or 4. 4. 4)

Def. @deva[द्रुतविलम्बितमाह नभौ भरौ ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[न, भ, भ, र.] ⏑ ⏑ ⏑ | – ⏑ ⏑ | – ⏑ ⏑ | – ⏑ –

Ex. @deva[तरणिजापुलिने नवबल्लवीपरिषदा सह केलिकुतूहलात् ।]
@deva[द्रुतविलम्बितचारुविहारिणं हरिमहं हृदयेन सदा वहे ॥]

### (9) @deva[मन्दाकिनी] or @deva[प्रभा] (7. 5)

Def. @deva[ननररघाटिता तु मन्दाकिनी ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[न, न, र, र.] ⏑ ⏑ ⏑ | ⏑ ⏑ ⏑ | – ⏑ – | – ⏑ –

Ex. @deva[बलिदमनविधौ बभौ संगता पदजलरुहि यस्य मन्दाकिनी]
@deva[सुरनिहितसिताम्बुजस्रङ्निभा हरतु जगदघं स पीताम्बरः ॥]

### (10) @deva[प्रमिताक्षरा] (5. 7)

Def. @deva[प्रमिताक्षरा सजससैः कथिता ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[स, ज, स, स.] ⏑ ⏑ – | ⏑ – ⏑ | ⏑ ⏑ – | ⏑ ⏑ –

Ex. @deva[अमृतस्य शीकरमिवोद्गिरती रदमौक्तिकांशुलहरीच्छुरिता ।]
@deva[प्रमिताक्षरा मुररिपोर्भणितीर्व्रजसुभ्रुवामधिजहार मनः ॥]

### (11) @deva[भुजंगप्रयातम्] (6. 6)

Sch. of G. @deva[य, म, न, स, भ ल, म.]

Ex. @deva[करादस्य भ्रष्टे ननु शिखरिणी दृश्यति शिशो-]
@deva[र्विलीनाः स्मः सत्यं नियतमवधेयं तदखिलैः ।]

@deva[इति त्रस्यद्गोपानुचितनिभृतालापजनितं]
@deva[स्मित बिभ्रद्देवो जगदवतु गोवर्धनधरः ॥]

### (6) @deva[हरिणी] (6. 4. 7)

Def. @deva[नसमरसला गः षड्वेदैर्हयैर्हरिणी मता ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[न, स, म, र, स, ल, ग.]

Ex. @deva[व्यधित स विधिर्नेत्रं नीत्वा ध्रुवं हरिणीगणा-]
@deva[द्व्रजमृगदृशां संदोहस्योल्लसन्नयनश्रियम् ।]
@deva[यदयमनिशं दूर्वाश्यामे मुरारिकलेवरे]
@deva[व्यकिरदधिकं बद्धाकांक्षे विलोलविलोचनम् ॥]

---

*Metree with 18 syllable in a quarter.*

(@deva[धृतिः])

### (1) @deva[चित्रलेखा] (4. 7. 7.)

Def. @deva[मन्दाक्रान्ता नपरलघुयुता कीर्तिता चित्रलेखा ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[म, भ, न, य, य, य.]

Ex. @deva[शङ्केऽमुष्मिञ् जगति मृगदृशां साररूपं यदासी-]
@deva[दाकृष्येदं व्रजयुवतिसभा वेधसा सा व्यधायि ।]
@deva[नैतादृक्चेत्कथमुदधिसुतामन्तरेणाच्युतस्य]
@deva[प्रीतं तस्यां नयनयुगमभूच्चित्रलेखाद्भुतायाम् ॥]

### (2) @deva[नन्दनम्] (11. 7)

Def. @deva[नजभजरैस्तु रेफसहितैःशिवैर्हयैर्नन्दनम् ॥]

Sch. of G. @deva[न, ज, भ, ज, र, र.]

Ex. @deva[तरणिसुतातरङ्गपवनैः सलीलमान्दोलितं]
@deva[मधुरिपुपादपङ्कजरजःसुपूतपृथ्वीतलम् ।]
@deva[मुरहरचित्रचेष्टितकलाकलापसंस्मारकं]
@deva[क्षितितलनन्दनं व्रज सखे सुखाय वृन्दावनम् ॥]

### (3) @deva[नाराचम्] (8. 5. 5)

Def. @deva[इह ननरचतुष्कसृष्टं तु नाराचमाचक्षते]

Sch. of G. @deva[न, न, र, र, र, र.]

Ex. @deva[दिनकरतनयातटीकानने चारु संचारिणी]
@deva[श्रवणनिकटकृष्टमेणेक्षणा कृष्ण राधा त्वयि ।]
@deva[ननु विकिरति नेत्रनाराचमेषातिहृच्छेदनं]
@deva[तदिह मदनविभ्रमोद्भ्रान्तचित्तां विधत्स्व द्रुतम् ॥]

---

*Metres with 19 Syllables in a quarter.*

@deva[अतिधृति]

### (1) @deva[मेघविस्फूर्जिता] (6. 6. 7)

Def. @deva[रसर्त्वश्वैर्म्नौ न्सौ ररगुरुयुतो मेघविस्फूर्जिता स्यात् ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[य, म, न, स, र, र, ग.]

Ex. @deva[कदम्बमोदाढ्या विपिनपवनाः केकिनः कान्तकेकाः]
@deva[विनिद्राः कन्दल्यो दिशिदिशि मुदा दर्दुरा दृप्तनादाः ।]
@deva[निशान्तृत्यद्विद्युद्विलसितलसन्मेघविस्फूर्जिता चेत्]
@deva[प्रियः स्वाधीनोऽसौ दनुजदलनो राज्यमस्मात्किमन्यत् ॥]

### (2) @deva[शार्दूलविक्रीडितम्] (12. 7)

Def. @deva[सूर्याश्वैर्यदि मः सजौ सततगाः शार्दूलविक्रीडितम् ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[म, स, ज, स, त, त, ग.]

Ex. @deva[गोविन्दं प्रणमोत्तमाङ्ग रसने तं घोषयाहर्निशं]
@deva[पाणी पूजयतं मनः स्मर पदे तस्यालयं गच्छतम् ।]
@deva[एवं चेत्कुरुताखिलं मम हितं शीर्षादयस्तद्वुधं]
@deva[न प्रेक्षे भवतां कृते भवमहाशार्दूलविक्रीडितम् ॥]

### (3) @deva[सुमधुरा] (7. 6. 6)

Def. @deva[म्रौ भ्नौ मो नो गुरुश्चेद् हयऋतुरसैरुक्ता सुमधुरा ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[म, र, भ, न, म, न, ग.]

Ex. @deva[वेदार्थान्प्राकृतस्त्वं वदसि न च ते जिह्वा निपतिता]
@deva[मध्याह्ने वीक्षसेऽर्कं न तव सहसा दृष्टिर्विचालिता ।]
@deva[दीप्ताग्नौ पाणिमन्तः क्षिपासि स च ते दग्धो भवति नो]
@deva[चारित्र्याचारुदत्तं चलयसि न ते देहं हरति भूः ॥]

---

*Metres with 20 syllables in a quarter.*

(@deva[कृतिः])

### (1) @deva[गीतिका] (5. 7. 8)

Def. @deva[सजजाभरौ सलगा यदा कथिता तदा खलु गीतिका ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[स, ज, ज, भ, र, स, ल, ग.]

Ex. @deva[करतालचंचलकङ्कणस्वनामिश्रणेन मनोरमा]
@deva[रमणीयवेणुनिनादरङ्गिमसङ्गमेन सुखावहा ।]
@deva[बहुलानुरागनिवासरासमुद्भवा तव रागिणं]
@deva[विदधौ हरिं खलु वल्लवीजनचारुचामरगीतिका ॥]

### (2) @deva[सुवदना] (7. 7. 6)

Def. @deva[ज्ञेया सप्ताश्वषभिर्मरभनययुता म्लौ गः सुवदना ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[म, र, भ, न, य, म, ल, ग.]

Ex. @deva[प्रत्याहृत्येन्द्रियाणि त्वदितरविषयान्नासाग्रनयना]
@deva[त्वां ध्यायन्ती निकुञ्जे परतरपुरुषं हर्षोत्थपुलका ।]
@deva[आनन्दाश्रुप्लुताक्षी वसति सुवदना योगैकरसिका]
@deva[कामार्तिं त्यक्तकामा ननु नरकरिपो राधा मम सखी ॥]

---

*Metres with 21 syllables in a quarter.*

(@deva[प्रकृतिः])

### (1) @deva[सरसी] (also called @deva[पञ्चकावली], @deva[धृतश्रीः])

Def. @deva[नजभजजा जरौ यदि तदा गदिता सरसी कवीश्वरैः ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[न, ज, भ, ज, ज, ज, र.]

Ex. @deva[चिकुरकलापैवलङ्कृतप्रमदासु लसद्रसोर्मिषु]
@deva[स्फुटवदनाम्बुजासु विलसद्भुजबालमृणालवल्लिषु ।]
@deva[कुचयुगचक्रवाकमिथुनानुगतासु कलाकुतूहली]
@deva[व्यरचयदच्युतो व्रजमृगीनयनासरसीषु विभ्रमम् ॥]

### (2) @deva[स्रग्धरा] (7. 7. 7)

Def. @deva[म्रभ्नैर्यानां त्रयेण त्रिमुनियतियुता स्रग्धरा कीर्तितेयम् ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[म, र, भ, न, य, य, य.]

Ex. @deva[व्याकोषेन्दीवराभा कनककषलसत्पीतवासाः सुहासा]
@deva[बर्हैश्चन्द्रकान्तैर्वलयितचिकुरा चारुकर्णावतंसा ।]
@deva[अंसव्यासक्तवंशीध्वनिसुखितजगद्वल्लवीभिर्लसन्ती]
@deva[मूर्तिर्गोपस्य विष्णोरवतु जगति नः स्रग्धरा हारिहारा ॥]

---

*Metres with 22 syllabes in a quarter.*

(@deva[आकृती])

### (1) @deva[मदिरा.]

Def. @deva[सप्तभकारयुतेकगुरुर्गदितेयमुदारतरा मदिरा]

Sch. of G. @deva[भ, भ, भ, भ, भ, भ, भ, ग.]

Ex. @deva[माधवमासिपिकस्वकेसरपुष्पलसन्मदिरामुदितै-]
@deva[र्भृङ्गकुलैरुपगीतवने वनमालिनमालि कलानिलयम् ।]
@deva[कुञ्जगृहोदरपल्लवकल्पिततल्पमनल्पमनोजरसं]
@deva[तं भजमाधविकामृदुनर्तनयामुनवातकृतोपगमा ॥]

### (2) @deva[हंसी] (8. 14)

Def. @deva[मौ गौ नाश्वत्वारो गो गो वसुभुवनयतिरिति भवति हंसी ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[म, म, त, न, न, न, स, ग.]

Ex. @deva[सार्धं कान्तेनैकान्तेऽसौ विकचकमलमधु सुरभि पिबन्ती]
@deva[कामक्रीडाकूतस्फीतप्रमदसरसतरमलघु रसन्ती ।]

@deva[कालिन्दीये पद्मारण्ये पवनपतनपरितरलपरागे]
@deva[कंसाराते पश्य स्वेच्छं सरभसगतिरिह विलसति हंसी ॥]

---

*Metres with 23 syllables in a quarter.*

(@deva[विकृतिः])

### (1) @deva[अद्रितनया] (also called @deva[अश्वललित]).

Def. @deva[नजभजभा जभौ, लघुगुरु बुधैस्तु गदितेयमद्रितनया ।]

Sch. of G. @deva[न, ज, भ, ज, भ, ज, भ, ल ग.]

Ex. @deva[खरतरशौर्यपावकशिखापतङ्गनिभभग्नदृप्तदनुजो]
@deva[जलधिसुताविलासवसतिः सतां गतिरशेषमान्यमहिमा ॥]
@deva[भुवनहितावतारचतुरश्वराचरधरोऽवतीर्ण इह हि]
@deva[क्षितिवलयेस्ति कंस शमनस्तवेति तमवोचदद्रितनया ॥]

---

Metres with 24, 25, 26, syllables in a *pāda* are omitted as they are very rare.

### @deva[दण्डक]

Metres with 27 syllabes or more in each *pāda* are designated by the general name *Daṇḍaka*. Many varieties of this are mentioned (as the number of syllables in each *pāda* may sometimes reach 999), such as @deva[चंडवृष्टिप्रयात], @deva[प्रचितक], @deva[मत्तमातंगलीलाकर], @deva[सिंहविक्रान्त], @deva[कुसुमस्तवक], @deva[अनंगशेखर], @deva[संग्राम] &c.; Māl. Mād. V. 23. is an instance of the species last named, having 54 letters to a *pāda*.

rules.title: Ardhasamavṛttāni and Viṣamavṛttāni: Metres with Alternate or Unequal Quarters
Jāti: Metres Regulated by Syllabic Instants
rules.body:
## @deva[जाति] or Metres regulated by the number of syllabic instants.

The most common variety of metres regulated by syllabic instants is @deva[आर्या]. It is of nine kinds:—

@deva[पथ्या विपुला चपला मुखचपला जघनचपला च ।]
@deva[गीत्युपगीत्युद्गीतय आर्यागीतिश्च नवधार्या ॥]

Of these the last four are generally used and deserve notice here.

### @deva[आर्या]

Def. @deva[यस्याः पादे प्रथमे द्वादश मात्रास्तथा तृतीयेऽपि ।]
@deva[अष्टादश द्वितीये चतुर्थके पञ्चदश सार्या ॥]

The first and third quarters have each 12 mātrās or syllabic instants, the second 18 and the fourth 15.

Ex. @deva[येनामन्दमरन्दे दलदरविन्दे दिनान्यनायिषत ।]
@deva[कुटजे खलु तेनेहा तेनेहा मधुकरेण कथम् ॥]

### @deva[गीतिः]

Def. @deva[आर्याप्रथमार्धसमं यस्या परार्थमीरिता गीतिः ।]

i. e. the third and fourth quarters of this metre are respectively similar to the first and second quarters of an Ārya.

Ex. @deva[पाटीर तव पटीयान्कः परिपाटीमिमामुरीकर्तुम् ।]
@deva[यत्पिषतामपि नृणां पिष्टोपि तनोषि परिमलैः पुष्टिम् ॥]

### @deva[उपगीतिः]

Def. @deva[आर्यापरार्धतुल्ये दलद्वये प्राहुरुपगीतिम् ।]

i. e. the first and second quarters of this metre are like those of an Ārya while the second and third quarters contain 15 mātrās each.

Ex. @deva[नवगोपसुन्दरीणां लासोल्लासे मुरारातिम् ।]
@deva[अस्मारयदुपगीतिः स्वर्गकुरङ्गीदृशां गीतेः ॥]

### @deva[उद्गीतिः]

Def. @deva[आर्याशकलद्वितये विपरीते पुनरिहोद्गीतिः ।]

i. e. the first and third quarters of this metre contain 12 syllabic instants respectively.

Ex. @deva[नारायणस्य सततमुद्गीतिः संस्मृतिर्भक्त्या ।]
@deva[अर्चीयामासक्तिर्दुस्तरसंसारसागरे तरणिः ॥]

### @deva[आर्यागीतिः]

Def. @deva[आर्या प्राग्दलनन्तेऽधिकगुरुतादृग्परार्धमार्यागीतिः ।]

i. e. the first and third quarters of this metre, as also the second and the fourth quarters must contain 12 and 20 syllabic instants respectively.

Ex. @deva[चारुसमीरणविपिने हरिणकलङ्ककिरणावली सविलासा ।]
@deva[आबद्धराममोहा वेलामूले विभावरी परिहीना ॥]

### (१) @deva[वैतालीयम्]

Def. @deva[षाड्विषमेऽष्टौ समे कलास्ताश्च समे स्युर्निरन्तराः ।]
@deva[न समात्र पराश्रिता कला वैतालीयेन्ते रलौ गुरुः ॥]

The first and third quarters of this metre should contain fourteen syllabic instants, and the second and fourth sixteen each of these the last eight mātrās should consist of a @deva[रगण] (– ⏑ –) followed by a short and a long syllable (⏑ –); the syllabic instants in the even quarters should not be at all composed of short syllables or long syllables; and the even syllabic instant in each quarter (i. e. the 2nd, 4th and 6th) should not be formed conjointly with the next (i. e. 3rd, 5th and 9th.)

Ex. @deva[कुशलं खलु तुभ्यमेव तत् वचनं कृष्णयदभ्यधामहम् ।]
@deva[उपदेशपराः परेष्वपि स्वविनाशाभिमुखेषु साधवः ॥]

### (२) @deva[औपच्छन्दसिकम्]

Def. @deva[पर्यन्तेर्यौ तथैव शेषमौपच्छन्दसिकं सुधीभिरुक्तम् ।]

This is the same as Vaitālīya except that at the end of each quarter there must be a @deva[र] Gaṇa followed by a @deva[य] Gaṇa instead of @deva[ल] and @deva[ग] i. e. it is the same as Vaitālīya with a long syllable added at the end of each quarter.

Ex. @deva[आतन्वानं सुरारिकान्तास्वौपच्छन्दासिकं हृदो विनोदम् ।]
@deva[कंसं यो निर्जघान देवो वन्दे तं जगतां स्थितिं दधानम् ॥]
